root.title: Optimality and Active-Set Theory for Constrained NLP
root.top_down_role: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear-programming optimality, constraint regularity, second-order geometry, classical sensitivity, active-set identification, and working-set interfaces. Full duality, quadratic-programming solvers, SQP globalization, interior-point methods, and variational-analysis foundations remain in their owning chapters.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained NLP Optimality-Active-Set Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional KKT conditions and second-order geometry for smooth equality- and inequality-constrained nonlinear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(E\) and \(I\) be finite index sets, and consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(h_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in E\) and \(g_i(x)\ge 0\) for \(i\in I\). For a feasible point \(x^*\), set \(\mathcal A(x^*)=\{i\in I:g_i(x^*)=0\}\), and assume LICQ holds there. With \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)-\sum_{i\in E}\lambda_i h_i(x)-\sum_{i\in I}\mu_i g_i(x)\), if \(x^*\) is a local minimizer, then there are unique multipliers \((\lambda^*,\mu^*)\in\mathbb R^E	imes\mathbb R^I\) satisfying \(\mu_i^*\ge0\), \(
abla_xL(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)=0\), and \(\mu_i^*g_i(x^*)=0\) for every \(i\in I\). Define \(\mathcal C(x^*,\mu^*)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:
abla h_i(x^*)^	op d=0\ 	ext{for all }i\in E,\ 
abla g_i(x^*)^	op d=0\ 	ext{for }i\in\mathcal A(x^*)	ext{ with }\mu_i^*>0,\ 
abla g_i(x^*)^	op d\ge0\ 	ext{for }i\in\mathcal A(x^*)	ext{ with }\mu_i^*=0\}\). Then \(d^	op
abla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)d\ge0\) for every \(d\in\mathcal C(x^*,\mu^*)\). Conversely, if a feasible \(x^*\) and multipliers \((\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) satisfy these KKT conditions and \(d^	op
abla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)d>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\mathcal C(x^*,\mu^*)\), then there exist \(c>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(f(x)\ge f(x^*)+c\lVert x-x^*Vert^2\) for every feasible \(x\) with \(\lVert x-x^*Vert<\varepsilon\); hence \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice continuously differentiable finite-dimensional nonlinear program, LICQ at a local minimizer yields unique KKT multipliers and nonnegative Lagrangian curvature on the associated critical cone. Conversely, a feasible KKT point with strictly positive Lagrangian curvature on every nonzero critical-cone direction satisfies quadratic growth and is a strict local minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(E\) and \(I\) are finite, and \(f\), every \(h_i\), and every \(g_i\) are twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(x^*\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
LICQ holds at \(x^*\): \(\{\nabla h_i(x^*):i\in E\}\cup\{\nabla g_i(x^*):i\in\mathcal A(x^*)\}\) is linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At a local minimizer, the KKT multipliers are unique and \(d^\top\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)d\ge0\) on \(\mathcal C(x^*,\mu^*)\); at a feasible KKT point, strict positivity on \(\mathcal C(x^*,\mu^*)\setminus\{0\}\) implies quadratic growth and strict local optimality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible-Geometry Regime of a Finite-Dimensional NLP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be closed. Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)\in K\), with feasible set \(\Omega=c^{-1}(K)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic nonlinear programming; the definition classifies local feasible geometry independently of objective optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathcal G(\bar x):=(\Omega,\bar x,T_\Omega(\bar x),\widehat N_\Omega(\bar x),N_\Omega(\bar x))\] is the feasible-geometry regime at \(\bar x\in\Omega\), where \(T_\Omega(\bar x)\) is the contingent tangent cone, \(\widehat N_\Omega(\bar x)=T_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ\) is the regular normal cone, and \(N_\Omega(\bar x)\) is the limiting normal cone. The regime is bound-constrained when \(K\) is a box, affine-polyhedral when \(c\) is affine and \(K\) is polyhedral, smooth nonlinear when the constraint functions defining \(c(x)\in K\) are continuously differentiable, and general nonlinear otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, the feasible-geometry regime is the feasible set together with its contingent tangent, regular normal, and limiting normal cones. Bounds, affine-polyhedral constraints, smooth nonlinear constraints, and general nonlinear constraints define distinct specializations according to the form of the set and constraint mapping.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is closed, so local tangent and normal constructions are well posed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G(\bar x)\) records the first-order primal and dual local geometry relevant to feasible directions, multipliers, and active-set analysis.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Any closed feasible set \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) can be represented directly by taking \(c(x)=x\) and \(K=\Omega\).
special_cases_latex: For simple bounds, \(\Omega=[\ell,u]\).
For affine constraints, \(\Omega=\{x:Ax=b,\;Cx\le d\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The polar relation \(\widehat N_\Omega(\bar x)=T_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ\) supplies the regular dual geometry.
When \(\Omega\) is convex, regular and limiting normal cones coincide.
boundary_notes: The classification does not assert a constraint qualification or equality between the tangent and linearized cones.
Infinite-dimensional feasible geometry and nonclosed feasible sets are outside this scope.

notation.meaning: Contingent tangent cone to the feasible set at the reference point.
Negative polar cone \(\{v:\langle v,d\rangle\le0\ \forall d\in C\}\).

review_flags: The supplied locators were not independently inspected; an exact source covering the combined regime classification is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Geometry Regime of a Finite-Dimensional NLP

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic, continuously differentiable NLP with finitely many equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A smooth NLP is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=0,\qquad g(x)\le0,\] where \(f,h,g\) are continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of the feasible set \(\Omega:=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}\). At \(\bar x\in\Omega\), the active inequality index set is \(I(\bar x):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\). A \(C^r\) smooth regime requires \(f,h,g\in C^r\) locally, with \(r=1\) for first-order and ordinarily \(r=2\) for Hessian-based analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth nonlinear program minimizes a differentiable objective over points satisfying finitely many differentiable equalities and inequalities. An inequality is active at a feasible reference point precisely when its value is zero there.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h,g\) are defined on an open subset of \(\mathbb R^n\).
All component functions are at least continuously differentiable near the reference feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set and activity map are \(\Omega=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}\) and \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The constraints can be written \(c(x)\in K\) with \(c=(h,g)\) and \(K=\{0\}^p\times\mathbb R_-^q\).
special_cases_latex: With \(q=0\), the program is equality constrained.
With \(p=0\), it is inequality constrained.
Affine components give a linearly constrained smooth program.
immediate_consequences_latex: Inactive constraints satisfy \(g_i(\bar x)<0\) and impose no first-order equality at \(\bar x\).
The Jacobians \(\nabla h(\bar x)\) and \(\nabla g_{I(\bar x)}(\bar x)\) determine the linearized constraints.
boundary_notes: Smoothness alone does not imply any constraint qualification.
Nonsmooth, stochastic, semi-infinite, and integer constraints are excluded.

notation.meaning: Set of inequality constraints active at \(\bar x\).

review_flags: A precise inspected source locator for the canonical smooth-NLP formulation is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Equality-Inequality Nonlinear Program
Rank Deficiency Can Overestimate Equality Tangency
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality x-squared equals zero has a zero Jacobian at its sole feasible point, so its linearization admits every direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h(x)=x^2\) and \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R:h(x)=0\}=\{0\}\), \(Dh(0)=0\) and hence \(\ker Dh(0)=\mathbb R\), whereas \(T_F(0)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_F(0)=\{0\}\subsetneq\ker Dh(0)=\mathbb R.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate equality whose Jacobian null space exceeds the true tangent cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Regular Level-Set Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-row-rank equality system defines a local manifold whose tangent and normal spaces are the Jacobian null space and transpose range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x:h(x)=0\}\), where \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in F\). If \(Dh(\bar x)\) has full row rank \(m\), then \(F\) is locally a \(C^1\) manifold of dimension \(n-m\), \(T_F(\bar x)=\ker Dh(\bar x)\), and its normal space is \(\operatorname{range}Dh(\bar x)^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_F(\bar x)=\ker Dh(\bar x),\qquad N_F(\bar x)=\operatorname{range}Dh(\bar x)^\top.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local manifold and tangent-space structure of a regular equality-constrained feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-constrained NLP minimizes a smooth objective over the common zero set of smooth constraint functions; its linearized feasible directions lie in the Jacobian null space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable. The equality-constrained nonlinear program is
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=0,
\]
with feasible set \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:h(x)=0\}\). At a feasible point \(\bar x\), the first-order linearized feasible subspace is \(L_F(\bar x)=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:Dh(\bar x)d=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=h^{-1}(0)\) and \(L_F(\bar x)=\ker Dh(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth optimization with equality constraints only.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the equality-constraint mapping at \(\bar x\)

knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Feasible Points Are Locally Unconstrained
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every inequality is strict, continuity makes the point interior and no first-order direction is restricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x:g_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,p\}\), with each \(g_i\) continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in F\). If \(g_i(\bar x)<0\) for every \(i\), then \(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}F\), and consequently \(T_F(\bar x)=L_F(\bar x)=\mathbb R^n\).
assumptions_latex: Every \(g_i\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\in\operatorname{int}F,\qquad T_F(\bar x)=L_F(\bar x)=\mathbb R^n.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local geometry when every inequality is inactive.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative-Slack Reformulation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonpositive inequality system has an equivalent equality-plus-bound representation using a uniquely determined nonnegative slack vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\), \(g(x)\le0\) is equivalent to the existence of \(s\in\mathbb R_+^p\) satisfying \(g(x)+s=0\). The slack is unique: \(s=-g(x)\). Thus minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\le0\) is equivalent in \(x\) to minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)+s=0\) and \(s\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g(x)\le0\iff\exists!s\ge0:\ g(x)+s=0,\quad s=-g(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent equality-plus-bound representation of componentwise inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Constrained Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality-constrained NLP minimizes a smooth objective where every constraint value is nonpositive; constraints attaining zero at a feasible point form its active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) be continuously differentiable. Under the convention \(g_i(x)\le 0\), the inequality-constrained nonlinear program is
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_i(x)\le0\quad(i=1,\ldots,p).
\]
Its feasible set is \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g(x)\le0\}\), and the active index set at \(\bar x\in F\) is \(I(\bar x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g(x)\le0\}\) and \(I(\bar x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth optimization with inequality constraints only.

notation.meaning: active inequality index set at \(\bar x\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Squared-Slack Reformulation Is Degenerate at Activity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder claim rejected because its asserted constraint-qualification failure does not follow from the vanishing slack derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proposed claim asserted that \(g_i(x)+z_i^2=0\) can create artificial equality-Jacobian rank deficiency merely because \(2z_i=0\) at an active inequality. That inference is invalid: the corresponding equality row still contains \(\nabla g_i(\bar x)\), and full row rank of the squared-slack equality Jacobian is equivalent to linear independence of the active inequality gradients after inactive slack columns are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero squared-slack derivative at activity does not by itself destroy equality-Jacobian regularity; the builder's claimed failure boundary was overstated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 2\bar z_i=0\text{ alone does not imply rank deficiency of the full equality Jacobian}.
knowledge_statements.title: Squared-Slack Reformulation Is Degenerate at Activity

intermediate_metadata.reason: The accepted local inventory comprises the inequality-only formulation, active set, componentwise feasibility test, strictly feasible interior regime, and exact nonnegative-slack representation. The builder's squared-slack rank-failure claim was deferred because its inference is false. KKT duality, active-set and SQP algorithms, barrier methods, and the equality and mixed sibling regimes were excluded.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Equality–Inequality Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed NLP combines equality equations with componentwise inequalities; every equality is active, while an inequality is active exactly when it holds at equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) be continuously differentiable. A mixed constrained nonlinear program has the form
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=0,\qquad g(x)\le0.
\]
Thus \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}\). At \(\bar x\in F\), all equalities and precisely the inequalities in \(I(\bar x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\) are active.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}\), with active inequalities indexed by \(I(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonlinear programs containing both equality and inequality constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deferred locally because this is primarily a constraint-qualification failure statement, not a defining property of the mixed-regime leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equality \(h_j(x)=0\) is feasible-set equivalent to \(h_j(x)\le0\) and \(-h_j(x)\le0\). At a feasible point the replacement gradients are opposite, so their all-inequality representation fails LICQ and admits no direction strictly decreasing both constraints, hence fails MFCQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Paired opposite inequalities preserve an equality's feasible set but force LICQ and MFCQ failure in that representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The paired-inequality representation fails LICQ and MFCQ at \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R^n\), let \(Y=\mathbb R^m\), let \(F:X\to Y\), and let \(K\subseteq Y\) be closed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional set-constrained formulation encompassing bounds, affine-polyhedral systems, and nonlinear inverse-image constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structured constraint specialization is a feasible set of inverse-image form \[\Omega:=\{x\in X:F(x)\in K\}=F^{-1}(K),\] together with the declared structural class of \(F\) and \(K\). It is a bound specialization if \(F\) is the identity and \(K=[\ell,u]\); an affine-polyhedral specialization if \(F(x)=Ax-b\) and \(K\) is polyhedral; and a nonlinear specialization if \(F\) is nonlinear. At \(\bar x\in\Omega\), first-order linearization replaces \(F(\bar x+d)\in K\) by \(F(\bar x)+F'(\bar x)d\in T_K(F(\bar x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured constraint system is the inverse image of a declared closed set under a mapping. Bounds, affine-polyhedral constraints, and nonlinear constraints arise from specific choices of the mapping and target set.
assumptions_latex: For first-order linearization, \(F\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\in F^{-1}(K)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structural pair \((F,K)\) defines \(\Omega=F^{-1}(K)\) and the linearized cone \(\{d:F'(\bar x)d\in T_K(F(\bar x))\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Equality and inequality constraints use \(F=(h,g)\) and \(K=\{0\}^p\times\mathbb R_-^q\).
special_cases_latex: A box is obtained from \(F(x)=x\).
A conic system has \(K\) equal to a closed convex cone.
immediate_consequences_latex: Structure in \(K\) determines activity, faces, and target-space normals.
Affine \(F\) removes linearization error.
boundary_notes: No regularity condition ensuring an exact inverse-image tangent or normal formula is included.
Disjunctive or nonclosed target sets require separate treatment.
review_flags: The combined structural taxonomy requires an inspected supporting locator.
knowledge_statements.title: Set-Constrained Structured NLP
Projection onto a Box
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a box clamps each coordinate to its interval, and normal membership is equivalent to a projection fixed-point identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B=[\ell,u]=\{x:\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\}\), where \(\ell_i\le u_i\), the Euclidean projection is separable: \[[P_B(y)]_i=\min\{u_i,\max\{\ell_i,y_i\}\}.\] For \(x\in B\) and \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), \[v\in N_B(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=P_B(x+v).\] Moreover, \(\operatorname{dist}(y,B)^2=\sum_i(y_i-[P_B(y)]_i)^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coordinatewise clamping gives \(P_B\), exact distance to \(B\), and the normal-cone fixed-point test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise Euclidean projection and its normal-cone characterization.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Constraint Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a box boundary, tangent directions point inward coordinatewise, while normal vectors have the opposite signs and vanish on free coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\}\), where \(\ell_i<u_i\), and let \(\bar x\in B\). Its tangent and convex-analysis normal cones are
\[
T_B(\bar x)=\{d:d_i\ge0\text{ if }\bar x_i=\ell_i,\ d_i\le0\text{ if }\bar x_i=u_i\},
\]
\[
N_B(\bar x)=\{v:v_i\le0\text{ if }\bar x_i=\ell_i,\ v_i\ge0\text{ if }\bar x_i=u_i,\ v_i=0\text{ if }\ell_i<\bar x_i<u_i\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed coordinatewise formulas characterize \(T_B(\bar x)\) and \(N_B(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent and normal geometry of a finite box at a feasible point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Geometry of a Box Constraint
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\ell,u\in(\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\})^n\) satisfy \(\ell_i<u_i\), and define \(B=[\ell,u]:=\{x:\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\ \forall i\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional box constraints, allowing one-sided or free coordinates through infinite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\bar x\in B\), define \(L(\bar x)=\{i:\bar x_i=\ell_i\}\), \(U(\bar x)=\{i:\bar x_i=u_i\}\), and \(F(\bar x)=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus(L(\bar x)\cup U(\bar x))\). Then \[T_B(\bar x)=\{d:d_i\ge0\ (i\in L(\bar x)),\ d_i\le0\ (i\in U(\bar x)),\ d_i\in\mathbb R\ (i\in F(\bar x))\},\] and \[N_B(\bar x)=\{v:v_i\le0\ (i\in L(\bar x)),\ v_i\ge0\ (i\in U(\bar x)),\ v_i=0\ (i\in F(\bar x))\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a point in a box, tangent directions must point inward at active lower and upper bounds and are unrestricted at interior coordinates. Normal vectors have the opposite coordinatewise signs and vanish on free coordinates.
assumptions_latex: No coordinate has coincident finite lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tangent and normal cones are the coordinatewise cones displayed above, with \(N_B(\bar x)=T_B(\bar x)^\circ\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(d\in T_B(\bar x)\) iff \(d_i\in T_{[\ell_i,u_i]}(\bar x_i)\) for every coordinate.
special_cases_latex: If \(\bar x\) is interior, then \(T_B(\bar x)=\mathbb R^n\) and \(N_B(\bar x)=\{0\}\).
For nonnegativity constraints, \(B=\mathbb R_+^n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Projection onto \(B\) separates by coordinate.
The minimal face containing \(\bar x\) is obtained by fixing coordinates in \(L(\bar x)\cup U(\bar x)\).
boundary_notes: Fixed coordinates with \(\ell_i=u_i\) require \(d_i=0\) and unrestricted normal components.
Coupled inequalities are not box constraints.

notation.meaning: Active-lower, active-upper, and free coordinate sets.

review_flags: An inspected source locator for the exact tangent and normal formulas is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Geometry of a Box Constraint

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^q\). Define \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Cx\le d\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed convex polyhedra represented by finitely many affine equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\bar x\in P\), let \(I(\bar x)=\{i:C_i\bar x=d_i\}\). The affine-polyhedral tangent and normal cones are \[T_P(\bar x)=\{w:Aw=0,\ C_iw\le0\ \forall i\in I(\bar x)\}\] and \[N_P(\bar x)=\{A^Ty+C_{I(\bar x)}^Tz:y\in\mathbb R^p,\ z\in\mathbb R_+^{|I(\bar x)|}\}.\] A face is any nonempty set \(F=P\cap\{x:a^Tx=\beta\}\) where \(a^Tx\le\beta\) is valid for \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine-polyhedral feasible set is an intersection of finitely many affine hyperplanes and halfspaces. At a feasible point, only active inequalities enter its tangent and normal cone formulas; faces are intersections with supporting hyperplanes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local geometry is polyhedral and is determined by \(A\) and the active rows \(C_{I(\bar x)}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A polyhedron is equivalently a finite intersection of closed affine halfspaces and affine hyperplanes.
special_cases_latex: A polyhedral cone has \(b=0\) and \(d=0\).
A box is a polyhedron with coordinate inequalities.
immediate_consequences_latex: The tangent cone equals the linearized constraint cone without an additional constraint qualification.
The normal cone is generated by equality normals and nonnegative combinations of active inequality normals.
boundary_notes: The multiplier representation may be nonunique when active normals are dependent.
Curved nonlinear constraints are not affine-polyhedral even if their local tangent approximation is polyhedral.

notation.meaning: The \(i\)-th row of the inequality matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Polyhedral Feasible Geometry
Projection and Distance to an Affine Constraint Set
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a nonempty affine equality set removes the row-space correction determined by the residual; the pseudoinverse formula remains valid with dependent rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\), and let \(A^\dagger\) be the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse. For every \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), \[P_F(y)=y-A^\dagger(Ay-b),\qquad \operatorname{dist}(y,F)=\|A^\dagger(Ay-b)\|.\] Equivalently, \(P_F(y)\) is the unique \(z\in F\) satisfying \(y-z\in\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\).
assumptions_latex: Projection and distance use the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_F(y)=y-A^\dagger(Ay-b)\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(y,F)=\|A^\dagger(Ay-b)\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric geometry of a nonempty affine equality set, including rank-deficient representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Constraint Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty affine feasible set is a translate of the constraint matrix null space; this null space is its tangent space, and the row space is its normal space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b\}\) be nonempty, with \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). For every \(\bar x\in F\),
\[
F=\bar x+\ker A,\qquad T_F(\bar x)=\ker A,
\]
and, using the convex-analysis normal convention,
\[
N_F(\bar x)=(\ker A)^\perp=\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T}).
\]
These identities remain valid when the rows of \(A\) are linearly dependent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\bar x+\ker A\), \(T_F(\bar x)=\ker A\), and \(N_F(\bar x)=\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible, tangent, and normal geometry for affine equalities.

notation.meaning: tangent cone, here a linear subspace

knowledge_statements.title: Local Exactness of the Polyhedral Tangent Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near any point of a polyhedron, translating the tangent cone reproduces the feasible set exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Cx\le d\}\) and \(\bar x\in P\). There exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \[P\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar x)=\bigl(\bar x+T_P(\bar x)\bigr)\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar x).\] Thus the active affine constraints determine the exact feasible set in a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) and \(\bar x+T_P(\bar x)\) coincide locally at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact local reconstruction of a polyhedron from its tangent cone.

notation.meaning: open Euclidean ball centered at the reference point

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Feasible Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedron, the tangent cone linearizes active constraints exactly, and the normal cone is generated by equality normals and nonnegative combinations of active inequality normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^p\). Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ Cx\le d\}\), and fix \(\bar x\in P\). Define \(I(\bar x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:C_i\bar x=d_i\}\). Then
\[
T_P(\bar x)=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:Av=0,\ C_i v\le0\ \text{for all }i\in I(\bar x)\},
\]
and
\[
N_P(\bar x)=\{A^{\mathsf T}\lambda+C_{I(\bar x)}^{\mathsf T}\mu:\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m,\ \mu\in\mathbb{R}^{|I(\bar x)|}_+\}.
\]
Thus only active inequalities determine the local first-order geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed active-constraint formulas give \(T_P(\bar x)\) and \(N_P(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local tangent and normal cones of a linearly constrained polyhedron.

notation.meaning: indices of inequalities active at \(\bar x\)
nonnegative vectors indexed by the active inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Nonpolyhedral Faces Need Not Be Exposed
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact nonpolyhedral convex set can have an extreme singleton face that no supporting functional exposes by itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\|x\|\le1\}\), \(q=(2,0)\), and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(D\cup\{q\})\). At either tangency point \(z=(1/2,\pm\sqrt3/2)\), the singleton \(\{z\}\) is an extreme face of \(C\), but its unique supporting line also contains the segment \([z,q]\). Hence \(\{z\}\) is not exposed.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is the convex hull of the closed unit disk and \((2,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extreme face \(\{z\}\) is not exposed, so polyhedrality is essential to the exposed-face theorem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the exposed-face equivalence outside the polyhedral class.

notation.meaning: a tangency point from q to D

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Definitions of a Polyhedral Face
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A face contains both endpoints of every feasible segment whose relative interior meets it; for polyhedra this is equivalent to exposure by a supporting linear functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex. A convex subset \(F\subseteq P\) is a face of \(P\) if \[x,y\in P,\quad t\in(0,1),\quad tx+(1-t)y\in F\ \Longrightarrow\ x,y\in F.\] If \(P\) is a polyhedron, every nonempty face equivalently has the form \[F=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in P}c^{\mathsf T}x\] for a vector \(c\) whose maximum over \(P\) is finite.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is convex for the segment definition.
\(P\) is a polyhedron for the exposed-face equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The segment property defines faces, and for polyhedra it is equivalent to a supporting-functional representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic segment definition and the polyhedral supporting-functional equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Lattice Operations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedral faces form a finite inclusion lattice; intersections are meets, minimal containing faces are joins, and proper inclusion strictly increases dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polyhedron \(P\), intersections of faces are faces, with the empty intersection interpreted as \(P\) and an empty resulting intersection allowed as the empty face. Including \(\varnothing\) and \(P\), the finitely many faces ordered by inclusion form a lattice: the meet is intersection, and the join of \(F_1,F_2\) is the unique minimal face containing \(F_1\cup F_2\). If \(F\subsetneq G\), then \(\dim F<\dim G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The face family of \(P\), including \(\varnothing\) and \(P\), is a finite lattice ordered by inclusion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion and intersection structure of the faces of a polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.title: Face Structure of Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty polyhedral face is the maximizer set of a linear functional. Each feasible point belongs to the relative interior of one unique minimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. Every nonempty face \(F\) of \(P\) is exposed: there exist \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\) such that
\[
F=P\cap\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:c^{\mathsf T}x=\alpha\},\qquad c^{\mathsf T}x\le\alpha\quad\text{for all }x\in P.
\]
For each \(x\in P\), the intersection of all faces containing \(x\) is the unique minimal face containing \(x\), and \(x\) lies in its relative interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) has the displayed exposing-hyperplane representation, and every \(x\in P\) determines a unique minimal face.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exposed-face representation and minimal faces of finite-dimensional polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Tangent–Linearized Cone Inclusion without Regularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the constraint x squared at most zero, every direction is linearly feasible even though the true feasible set contains only zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R:x^2\le0\}=\{0\}\) and \(\bar x=0\). Since \(g'(0)=0\), \[L_F(0)=\mathbb R,\] whereas isolation of the feasible point gives \[T_F(0)=\{0\}.\] Hence \(T_F(0)\subsetneq L_F(0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F(0)=\{0\}\subsetneq\mathbb R=L_F(0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth inequality showing failure of linearization exactness.

knowledge_statements.title: MFCQ Gives Exact First-Order Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under MFCQ, every direction satisfying the linearized active constraints is a genuine tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}\), with \(h,g\) continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in F\). Suppose \(Dh(\bar x)\) has full row rank and there exists \(d\) such that \[Dh(\bar x)d=0,\qquad \nabla g_i(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}d<0\quad(i\in I(\bar x)).\] Then \[T_F(\bar x)=L_F(\bar x).\]
assumptions_latex: \(h\) and \(g\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F(\bar x)=L_F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-cone exactness for a smooth mixed constraint system under MFCQ.

knowledge_statements.title: General Nonlinear-Constraint Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth nonlinear constraints produce a linearized cone from equality Jacobians and active inequality gradients. The true tangent cone is contained in it, with equality requiring regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) be continuously differentiable, and define \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}\). Let \(\bar x\in F\) and \(I(\bar x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\). The linearized cone is
\[
L_F(\bar x)=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:Dh(\bar x)d=0,\ \nabla g_i(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}d\le0\ \text{for every }i\in I(\bar x)\}.
\]
Always \(T_F(\bar x)\subseteq L_F(\bar x)\); equality requires an appropriate constraint qualification and need not hold otherwise.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F(\bar x)\subseteq L_F(\bar x)\), with the displayed formula for \(L_F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order local geometry of a smooth mixed nonlinear feasible set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Geometry of Smooth Nonlinear Constraints
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) be continuously differentiable, and let \(\Omega=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth but potentially nonconvex nonlinear constraints; no constraint qualification is built into the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(\bar x\in\Omega\), with \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\), the nonlinear feasible geometry consists of the contingent cone \[T_\Omega(\bar x)=\{d:\exists t_k\downarrow0,\ d_k\to d,\ \bar x+t_kd_k\in\Omega\},\] and the linearized cone \[L_\Omega(\bar x)=\{d:\nabla h(\bar x)^Td=0,\ \nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td\le0\ \forall i\in I(\bar x)\}.\] Always \(T_\Omega(\bar x)\subseteq L_\Omega(\bar x)\); equality is a regularity property, not part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For differentiable nonlinear constraints, the contingent cone records limits of feasible displacements, while the linearized cone is obtained from active constraint gradients. Every tangent direction is linearized-feasible, but the reverse inclusion can fail.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) and \(g\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((T_\Omega(\bar x),L_\Omega(\bar x))\) distinguishes actual first-order feasible geometry from its gradient linearization.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The tangent definition is equivalent to \(d=\lim_k(x_k-\bar x)/t_k\) for \(x_k\in\Omega\), \(x_k\to\bar x\), and \(t_k\downarrow0\).
special_cases_latex: For affine constraints, \(T_\Omega(\bar x)=L_\Omega(\bar x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Failure of equality between the cones signals first-order degeneracy.
The polar \(L_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ\) has a gradient-multiplier representation.
boundary_notes: The inclusion may be strict without a constraint qualification.
Nonsmooth constraint functions require generalized derivatives.

notation.meaning: Linearized constraint cone at the reference point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order Primal and Dual Geometry of a Feasible Set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and let \(\bar x\in\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional variational geometry for an arbitrary closed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The first-order feasible geometry at \(\bar x\) is the triple \[\bigl(T_\Omega(\bar x),\widehat N_\Omega(\bar x),N_\Omega(\bar x)\bigr),\] where \[T_\Omega(\bar x)=\{d:\exists t_k\downarrow0,\ d_k\to d,\ \bar x+t_kd_k\in\Omega\},\qquad \widehat N_\Omega(\bar x)=T_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ,\] and \[N_\Omega(\bar x)=\{v:\exists x_k\to\bar x,\ x_k\in\Omega,\ v_k\to v,\ v_k\in\widehat N_\Omega(x_k)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-order feasible geometry comprises the contingent tangent cone, its polar regular normal cone, and the outer limit of nearby regular normals, called the limiting normal cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat N_\Omega(\bar x)=T_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ\) and \(\widehat N_\Omega(\bar x)\subseteq N_\Omega(\bar x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(T_\Omega(\bar x)=\operatorname*{Limsup}_{t\downarrow0}(\Omega-\bar x)/t\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\Omega\) is closed and convex, then \(\widehat N_\Omega(\bar x)=N_\Omega(\bar x)=\{v:\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle\le0\ \forall x\in\Omega\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A differentiable objective has no feasible first-order descent direction at a local minimizer.
Regular normals support polar stationarity formulations.
boundary_notes: The proximal normal cone is a different, generally smaller construction.
For nonclosed sets, closure conventions must be stated separately.
review_flags: The exact variational definitions require an inspected authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible Directions and the Contingent Tangent Cone
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\bar x\in\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local feasible geometry; exact closure correspondence is stated for convex feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The radial feasible-direction cone is \[D_\Omega(\bar x):=\{d:\exists\varepsilon>0\ \text{such that}\ \bar x+td\in\Omega\ \forall t\in[0,\varepsilon]\}.\] The contingent tangent cone is \[T_\Omega(\bar x):=\{d:\exists t_k\downarrow0,\ d_k\to d,\ \bar x+t_kd_k\in\Omega\}.\] One always has \(D_\Omega(\bar x)\subseteq T_\Omega(\bar x)\). If \(\Omega\) is convex, then \[T_\Omega(\bar x)=\overline{D_\Omega(\bar x)}=\overline{\operatorname{cone}(\Omega-\bar x)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A radial feasible direction remains feasible along a sufficiently short line segment. A contingent tangent direction is a limit of scaled feasible displacements. Every radial direction is tangent, and for a convex feasible set the tangent cone is exactly the closure of the radial cone.
assumptions_latex: For the equality with the closure of radial directions, \(\Omega\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_\Omega(\bar x)\subseteq T_\Omega(\bar x)\), with \(T_\Omega(\bar x)=\overline{D_\Omega(\bar x)}\) when \(\Omega\) is convex.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(d\in T_\Omega(\bar x)\) iff there are \(x_k\in\Omega\) and \(t_k\downarrow0\) such that \((x_k-\bar x)/t_k\to d\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}\Omega\), both cones equal \(\mathbb R^n\).
For a polyhedron, the radial cone is already closed, so \(D_\Omega(\bar x)=T_\Omega(\bar x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Polarizing the tangent cone produces the regular normal cone.
Convexity eliminates curved-path tangent directions not approximable by radial directions.
boundary_notes: For nonconvex sets, \(\overline{D_\Omega(\bar x)}\) can be strictly smaller than \(T_\Omega(\bar x)\).
Alternative texts may use “feasible direction” for the contingent definition itself.
review_flags: The hinted tangent-cone source was not inspected; exact terminology and correspondence need source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Directions and the Contingent Tangent Cone
Sharp Boundaries for Feasible-Direction Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disconnected feasible set makes persistent directions strictly fewer than radial directions, while conical feasible sets furnish nonclosed and nonconvex examples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(\bar x=0\), let \(F_1=\{0,1\}\subset\mathbb R\). Then \(D_{F_1}(0)=\{0\}\subsetneq R_{F_1}(0)=[0,\infty)\). If \(F_2=\{0\}\cup\{(u,v):v>0\}\subset\mathbb R^2\), then \(D_{F_2}(0)=R_{F_2}(0)=F_2\), which is not closed. If \(F_3=(\mathbb R\times\{0\})\cup(\{0\}\times\mathbb R)\), then \(D_{F_3}(0)=R_{F_3}(0)=F_3\), which is not convex.
assumptions_latex: The base point is the origin in each example.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_F(\bar x)\subseteq R_F(\bar x)\text{ can be strict, and either family can be nonclosed or nonconvex}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary sets exhibiting strict inclusion, nonclosedness, and nonconvexity of radial and persistent feasible-direction cones.

notation.meaning: the three feasible sets in the statement

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Direction Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Radial directions reach another feasible point along a ray; persistent feasible directions keep an initial ray segment feasible. These cones may be nonclosed and nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\bar x\in F\). The radial feasible-direction cone and the locally persistent feasible-direction cone are
\[
R_F(\bar x)=\{d:\exists t>0,\ \bar x+td\in F\},
\]
\[
D_F(\bar x)=\{d:\exists\varepsilon>0,\ \bar x+td\in F\text{ for every }t\in[0,\varepsilon]\}.
\]
Both contain \(0\), are closed under multiplication by nonnegative scalars, and satisfy \(D_F(\bar x)\subseteq R_F(\bar x)\); neither must be closed or convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_F(\bar x)\subseteq R_F(\bar x)\), and both sets are positively homogeneous cones.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radial and locally persistent feasible directions for an arbitrary feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Clarke–Bouligand Tangent Inclusion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the crossing of the coordinate axes, every axial direction is Bouligand tangent, but only zero is robustly Clarke tangent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=(\mathbb R\times\{0\})\cup(\{0\}\times\mathbb R)\subseteq\mathbb R^2\) and \(\bar x=(0,0)\). Then \(T_F(\bar x)=F\), whereas \(T_F^C(\bar x)=\{0\}\). Hence \(T_F^C(\bar x)\subsetneq T_F(\bar x)\), and the Bouligand tangent cone need not be convex.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the union of the coordinate axes in \(\mathbb R^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_F^C(0)=\{0\}\subsetneq T_F(0)=F.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary nonregular set showing strict inclusion and Bouligand nonconvexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent-Cone Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Bouligand cone uses feasible secant limits. The Clarke cone requires robust feasibility from every nearby feasible sequence and is a closed convex subcone of the Bouligand cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally closed at \(\bar x\in F\). The Bouligand tangent cone is
\[
T_F(\bar x)=\{d:\exists x_k\in F,\ t_k\downarrow0,\ (x_k-\bar x)/t_k\to d\}.
\]
The Clarke tangent cone is
\[
T_F^C(\bar x)=\{d:\forall x_k\to\bar x\text{ in }F,\ \forall t_k\downarrow0,\ \exists d_k\to d\text{ with }x_k+t_kd_k\in F\}.
\]
Both are closed cones, \(T_F^C(\bar x)\) is convex, and \(T_F^C(\bar x)\subseteq T_F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F^C(\bar x)\subseteq T_F(\bar x)\); both are closed cones and \(T_F^C(\bar x)\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bouligand and Clarke tangent cones for a locally closed feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Failure of Persistent-Direction Closure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonconvex discrete set accumulating at the base point, tangent directions exist although no nonzero ray segment remains feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{0\}\cup\{1/n:n\in\mathbb N\}\subset\mathbb R\) and \(\bar x=0\). With \(x_n=1/n\) and \(t_n=1/n\), \((x_n-\bar x)/t_n=1\), so \(1\in T_F(0)\). No \(d>0\) is a persistent feasible direction because every interval \(\{td:0<t<\varepsilon\}\) contains points outside \(F\). Thus \(D_F(0)=\{0\}\), whereas \(T_F(0)=[0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline{D_F(0)}=\{0\}\ne[0,\infty)=T_F(0).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed nonconvex set whose Bouligand tangent contains directions not approximable by persistent feasible directions.

notation.meaning: nonconvex feasible set accumulating at zero

knowledge_statements.title: Direction–Cone Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex feasible set, radial and persistent feasible directions coincide, and their closure is exactly the Bouligand tangent cone. The correspondence generally fails without convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(\bar x\in F\). With
\[
R_F(\bar x)=\{\lambda(x-\bar x):\lambda\ge0,\ x\in F\},
\]
the Bouligand tangent cone satisfies
\[
T_F(\bar x)=\overline{R_F(\bar x)}=\overline{\operatorname{cone}(F-\bar x)}.
\]
Moreover, convexity makes every radial direction locally persistent, so \(D_F(\bar x)=R_F(\bar x)\) and consequently \(T_F(\bar x)=\overline{D_F(\bar x)}\). Without convexity, these equalities can fail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_F(\bar x)=R_F(\bar x)\) and \(T_F(\bar x)=\overline{D_F(\bar x)}=\overline{R_F(\bar x)}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure correspondence between feasible directions and tangents for convex sets.

notation.meaning: nonnegative conical hull of displacements from \(\bar x\)

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Linearization Can Overestimate Tangency
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero gradient of the active squared constraint makes every direction linearized-feasible although the feasible set is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R:x^2\le0\}\) and \(\bar x=0\). Then \(F=\{0\}\), so \(T_F(0)=\{0\}\); however, \(g'(0)=0\) and therefore \(L_F(0)=\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_F(0)=\{0\}\subsetneq\mathbb R=L_F(0).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional failure of tangent–linearization equality.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convexity and Tangent Inclusion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linearized cone is closed, convex, and polyhedral and always contains the true Bouligand tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the smooth feasible set and linearized cone \(L_F(\bar x)\) in the seed, \(L_F(\bar x)\) is a closed convex polyhedral cone and the Bouligand tangent cone always satisfies \(T_F(\bar x)\subseteq L_F(\bar x)\). Equality can fail without a constraint qualification.
assumptions_latex: The equality and inequality constraints are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_F(\bar x)\text{ is closed, convex, and polyhedral, and }T_F(\bar x)\subseteq L_F(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal properties of the active-constraint linearization.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized Constraint Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linearized constraint cone consists of directions satisfying the linearized equalities and the nonpositive linearizations of exactly the active inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) be continuously differentiable, and define \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}\). Let \(\bar x\in F\). If \(I(\bar x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\), the linearized constraint cone is
\[
L_F(\bar x)=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:Dh(\bar x)d=0,\ \nabla g_i(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}d\le0\text{ for every }i\in I(\bar x)\}.
\]
Inactive inequalities impose no first-order restriction in this definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar Cone and Regular Normal Duality
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a cone. Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and \(\bar x\in\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Euclidean polarity and regular normal geometry; limiting normals are distinguished explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The negative polar of \(C\) is \[C^\circ:=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\langle v,d\rangle\le0\ \forall d\in C\}.\] The regular normal cone to \(\Omega\) at \(\bar x\) is defined by \[\widehat N_\Omega(\bar x):=T_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ.\] Consequently, \(\widehat N_\Omega(\bar x)\) is always closed and convex. If \(T_\Omega(\bar x)\) is closed and convex, bipolarity gives \[T_\Omega(\bar x)=\widehat N_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative polar contains vectors making nonpositive inner product with every vector of a cone. The regular normal cone is, by definition, the negative polar of the tangent cone; when that tangent cone is closed and convex, polarity recovers it exactly.
assumptions_latex: For exact bipolar recovery, \(T_\Omega(\bar x)\) is convex as well as closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat N_\Omega(\bar x)=T_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ\), and \(T_\Omega(\bar x)=\widehat N_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ\) under closed convex tangent geometry.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For any cone \(C\), \(C^{\circ\circ}=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}C\).
special_cases_latex: For closed convex \(\Omega\), \(N_\Omega(\bar x)=\{v:\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle\le0\ \forall x\in\Omega\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: First-order feasible descent exclusions have an equivalent regular-normal form.
Normal vectors define supporting halfspaces for the tangent cone.
boundary_notes: The limiting normal cone need not be convex and is not generally the polar of the contingent tangent cone.
Using the positive-polar convention reverses all displayed inequalities.
review_flags: A precise inspected source for the polarity convention and normal-cone distinction is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Polar Cone and Regular Normal Duality
Normal Cones Separate at a Crossing
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a crossing, the regular normal is zero, limiting normals lie on either axis, and Clarke convexification gives the whole plane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=(\mathbb R\times\{0\})\cup(\{0\}\times\mathbb R)\) at \(\bar x=0\), \(\widehat N_F(0)=\{0\}\), \(N_F(0)=F\), and \(N_F^C(0)=\mathbb R^2\).
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the union of the coordinate axes in \(\mathbb R^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat N_F(0)=\{0\}\subsetneq N_F(0)\subsetneq N_F^C(0)=\mathbb R^2.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonregular set separating regular, limiting, and Clarke normals.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Normal Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal normals admit a local quadratic supporting inequality and form a subcone of the regular and limiting normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) locally closed at \(\bar x\in F\), the proximal normal cone is \[N_F^P(\bar x)=\{v:\exists\sigma,\delta>0\text{ such that }v^\top(x-\bar x)\le\sigma\|x-\bar x\|^2\ \forall x\in F\cap B_\delta(\bar x)\}.\] It satisfies \(N_F^P(\bar x)\subseteq\widehat N_F(\bar x)\subseteq N_F(\bar x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_F^P(\bar x)\subseteq\widehat N_F(\bar x)\subseteq N_F(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-support normal family and its relation to regular and limiting normals.

knowledge_statements.title: Regular, Limiting, and Clarke Normal Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regular normals satisfy a first-order support condition, limiting normals arise as nearby regular-normal limits, and Clarke normals convexify the limiting cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be locally closed at \(\bar x\in F\). Define \(\widehat N_F(\bar x)=\{v:\limsup_{x\to\bar x,\ x\in F,\ x\ne\bar x}v^\top(x-\bar x)/\|x-\bar x\|\le0\}\), \(N_F(\bar x)=\{v:\exists x_k\to\bar x,\ v_k\to v,\ v_k\in\widehat N_F(x_k)\}\), and \(N_F^C(\bar x)=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}N_F(\bar x)\). Then \(\widehat N_F(\bar x)\subseteq N_F(\bar x)\subseteq N_F^C(\bar x)\); the regular and Clarke cones are closed and convex, while the limiting cone need not be convex.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat N_F(\bar x)\subseteq N_F(\bar x)\subseteq N_F^C(\bar x)=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}N_F(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical first-order normal-cone families for a locally closed set.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Set Normal Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed convex set, all standard normal cones coincide with the global supporting-normal cone and tangent polar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed and convex and \(\bar x\in F\), then the proximal, regular, limiting, and Clarke normal cones coincide and equal \[N_F(\bar x)=\{v:v^\top(x-\bar x)\le0\text{ for every }x\in F\}=T_F(\bar x)^\circ.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_F^P(\bar x)=\widehat N_F(\bar x)=N_F(\bar x)=N_F^C(\bar x)=T_F(\bar x)^\circ.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-hyperplane representation for a closed convex feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under LICQ, the feasible-set normal cone consists exactly of nonnegative combinations of active inequality gradients plus arbitrary combinations of equality gradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C(\bar x)=T_C(\bar x)^\circ=\operatorname{cone}\{\nabla g_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\}+\operatorname{span}\{\nabla h_j(\bar x):1\le j\le p\}\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional constraint representation under LICQ.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent and Linearized Polars Can Differ
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero active gradient makes the linearized polar trivial even though the true tangent polar is the whole line.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R:x^2\le0\}=\{0\}\) at \(\bar x=0\), \(L_F(0)=\mathbb R\) and \(T_F(0)=\{0\}\). Hence \(L_F(0)^\circ=\{0\}\), while \(T_F(0)^\circ=\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_F(0)^\circ=\{0\}\subsetneq\mathbb R=T_F(0)^\circ.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate inequality separating the tangent and linearized polars.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar of the Linearized Constraint Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Farkas polarity gives the constraint-gradient formula for the linearized cone without regularity; regularity is needed to transfer it to the true tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_F(\bar x)=\{d:Dh(\bar x)d=0,\ \nabla g_i(\bar x)^\top d\le0\ (i\in I(\bar x))\}\). Then, without a constraint qualification, \[L_F(\bar x)^\circ=\left\{Dh(\bar x)^\top\mu+\sum_{i\in I(\bar x)}\lambda_i\nabla g_i(\bar x):\mu\in\mathbb R^m,\ \lambda_i\ge0\right\}.\]
assumptions_latex: The constraint derivatives exist at the feasible point \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_F(\bar x)^\circ=\operatorname{range}Dh(\bar x)^\top+\operatorname{cone}\{\nabla g_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-gradient representation requiring no constraint qualification.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar Calculus for Closed Convex Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polarity converts a cone sum into an intersection of polars and an intersection into the closed sum of polars.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For closed convex cones \(K_1,K_2\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \((K_1+K_2)^\circ=K_1^\circ\cap K_2^\circ\) and \((K_1\cap K_2)^\circ=\operatorname{cl}(K_1^\circ+K_2^\circ)\). If \(K_1\) and \(K_2\) are polyhedral, the closure in the second formula is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (K_1+K_2)^\circ=K_1^\circ\cap K_2^\circ,\qquad (K_1\cap K_2)^\circ=\operatorname{cl}(K_1^\circ+K_2^\circ).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sum and intersection rules under the negative-polar convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Moreau Decomposition for Polar Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every vector splits uniquely into orthogonal projections onto a closed convex cone and its negative polar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty closed convex cone. Every \(z\in\mathbb R^n\) has the unique decomposition \(z=P_Kz+P_{K^\circ}z\), with \(\langle P_Kz,P_{K^\circ}z\rangle=0\). Equivalently, \(z=u+v\), \(u\in K\), \(v\in K^\circ\), and \(u^\top v=0\) if and only if \(u=P_Kz\) and \(v=P_{K^\circ}z\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone in \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z=P_Kz+P_{K^\circ}z,\qquad (P_Kz)^\top P_{K^\circ}z=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal projection decomposition for a closed convex cone and its negative polar.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Polarity Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative polarity reverses inclusion, and applying it twice to a cone yields its closed convex hull. Consequently, two closed convex cones are mutual negative polars whenever either one is the negative polar of the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), define its negative polar by \[K^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:y^\top x\le0\ \text{for every }x\in K\}.\] The set \(K^\circ\) is a closed convex cone, and polarity reverses inclusion: if \(K_1\subseteq K_2\), then \(K_2^\circ\subseteq K_1^\circ\). Moreover, \[K^{\circ\circ}=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{conv}K).\] Hence \(K^{\circ\circ}=K\) whenever \(K\) is closed and convex. In particular, if \(T\) and \(N\) are closed convex cones in \(\mathbb R^n\), then \[N=T^\circ\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T=N^\circ.\] Thus, whenever a feasible-set tangent cone and the selected normal cone are closed convex cones and one is defined or established as the negative polar of the other, they determine each other by polarity.
assumptions_latex: For the mutual-polar equivalence, \(T,N\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) are closed convex cones
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K^{\circ\circ}=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{conv}K)\), and for closed convex cones \(T,N\), \(N=T^\circ\iff T=N^\circ\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional negative-polar, bipolar, and mutual-polar relations for closed convex cones.

notation.meaning: a pair of closed convex cones, such as suitably defined tangent and normal cones

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the active-set map \(I(x)=\{i:g_i(x)=0\}\). The activity-dependent linearized geometry at \( ar x\) is \[L( ar x)=\{d:
abla h( ar x)^Td=0,\ 
abla g_i( ar x)^Td\le0\  orall i\in I( ar x)\},\] with lineality subspace \[\operatorname{lin}L( ar x)=\{d:
abla h( ar x)^Td=0,\

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activity-dependent geometry is the linearized cone and its lineality space indexed by constraints that are tight at the reference point. Inactive inequalities do not enter the local first-order cone.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active set \(I(\bar x)\) selects exactly the inequality gradients appearing in \(L(\bar x)\) and \(\operatorname{lin}L(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Indexed Local Constraint Geometry

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) and let \(\Omega=\{x:g(x)\le0\}\). Fix \(\bar x\in\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite systems of inequality constraints under the convention \(g_i(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constraint activity partition at \(\bar x\) is \[I(\bar x):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}:g_i(\bar x)=0\},\qquad J(\bar x):=\{i:g_i(\bar x)<0\}.\] Feasibility implies \[\{1,\ldots,q\}=I(\bar x)\mathbin{\dot\cup}J(\bar x).\] The activity stratum associated with an index set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,q\}\) is \[S_I:=\{x\in\Omega:g_i(x)=0\ (i\in I),\ g_j(x)<0\ (j\notin I)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, every inequality is either active, meaning tight, or inactive, meaning strictly satisfied. Points having exactly the same active index set form an activity stratum.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is feasible, so \(g_i(\bar x)\le0\) for all \(i\).
The constraint index set is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(\bar x)\) and \(J(\bar x)\) form a disjoint exhaustive partition, and \(\bar x\in S_{I(\bar x)}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(I(\bar x)=\{i:-g_i(\bar x)=0\}\) is the zero set of the nonnegative slack vector \(-g(\bar x)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(I(\bar x)=\varnothing\), \(\bar x\) is strictly feasible for all inequalities.
If \(J(\bar x)=\varnothing\), all inequalities are tight.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only indices in \(I(\bar x)\) appear in the linearized inequality cone.
The sets \(S_I\), including empty ones, describe the activity stratification of \(\Omega\).
boundary_notes: Equality constraints are always tight and are normally indexed separately.
Approximate activity based on a tolerance is algorithmic and is not this exact partition.

knowledge_statements.title: Active–Inactive Constraint Partition
Active Constraint Subsets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active subset contains precisely the inequality constraints attained at equality at the current feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider inequality constraints \(g_i(x)\le0\) indexed by the finite set \(\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(x\) be feasible. The active constraint subset at \(x\) is \[\mathcal A(x)=\{i\in\mathcal I:g_i(x)=0\}.\] An index belongs to \(\mathcal A(x)\) exactly when its inequality boundary contains \(x\). Equality constraints, if present, hold at every feasible point and are not included in this inequality-activity partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\in\mathcal A(x)\iff g_i(x)=0\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active inequalities at a feasible point.

knowledge_statements.title: Inactive Constraint Subsets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inactive subset consists of strictly satisfied inequalities and is the complement of the active subset among inequality indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inequality constraints \(g_i(x)\le0\) indexed by \(\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the inactive constraint subset at a feasible point \(x\) is \[\mathcal N(x)=\{i\in\mathcal I:g_i(x)<0\}=\mathcal I\setminus\mathcal A(x).\] Thus \(\mathcal A(x)\) and \(\mathcal N(x)\) are disjoint and form a partition of \(\mathcal I\). Equality constraints are excluded from this partition because they cannot be strictly satisfied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I=\mathcal A(x)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal N(x)\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly satisfied inequalities at a feasible point.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Local Inactivity Stability Without Continuity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discontinuous inequality can be active at every nearby feasible point while strictly inactive at the limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define one inequality on \(\mathbb R\) by \[g(0)=-1,\qquad g(x)=0\quad(x\ne0),\] and impose \(g(x)\le0\). Every point is feasible. For \(x_k=1/k\to0\), \(\mathcal A(x_k)=\{1\}\) for every \(k\), whereas \(\mathcal A(0)=\varnothing\). Thus eventual containment \(\mathcal A(x_k)\subseteq\mathcal A(0)\) fails without continuity at the limit.
assumptions_latex: Continuity at the limiting point is not imposed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\to0,\qquad \mathcal A(x_k)=\{1\}\not\subseteq\mathcal A(0)=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of eventual active-set containment for an inequality discontinuous at the limiting feasible point.

knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Partition Transitions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a feasible point, strictly inactive continuous inequalities stay inactive; only constraints active at the limit can appear in nearby active sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and let \(x_k\to\bar x\) be feasible points. Every constraint inactive at \(\bar x\) remains inactive eventually: for each \(i\in\mathcal N(\bar x)\), there exists \(k_i\) such that \(i\in\mathcal N(x_k)\) whenever \(k\ge k_i\). Equivalently, because the index set is finite, \[\mathcal A(x_k)\subseteq\mathcal A(\bar x)\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }k.\] Therefore a local transition can remove indices from the active set, but an index strictly inactive at the limit cannot become active arbitrarily near that limit.
assumptions_latex: The inequality index set is finite
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(x_k)\subseteq\mathcal A(\bar x)\) for all sufficiently large \(k\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local stability and switching of inequality activity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For one inequality on \(\mathbb R\), define \[g(0)=-1,\qquad g(x)=0\quad(x\ne0),\] and impose \(g(x)\le0\). Every point is feasible. With \(x_k=1/k\to0\), one has \(\mathcal A(x_k)=\{1\}\) for every \(k\), whereas \(\mathcal A(0)=\varnothing\). Hence \(\mathcal A(x_k)\nsubseteq\mathcal A(0)\), showing that the seed’s eventual-containment conclusion can fail without continuity at the limit.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly and Weakly Active Constraint Partition
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(h(x)=0\), \(g(x)\le0\), and a feasible point \(\bar x\) with a KKT multiplier pair \((\lambda,\mu)\), where \(\mu\ge0\) and \(\mu_i g_i(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite NLP at a specified KKT multiplier; the partition may depend on the chosen multiplier when multipliers are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The multiplier-weighted activity partition is \[I^+(\bar x,\mu):=\{i\in I(\bar x):\mu_i>0\},\qquad I^0(\bar x,\mu):=\{i\in I(\bar x):\mu_i=0\},\] together with the inactive set \(J(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)<0\}\). Complementarity gives \(\mu_i=0\) for every \(i\in J(\bar x)\), and \[\{1,\ldots,q\}=I^+(\bar x,\mu)\mathbin{\dot\cup}I^0(\bar x,\mu)\mathbin{\dot\cup}J(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a KKT multiplier, active inequalities split into strongly active indices with positive multipliers and weakly active indices with zero multipliers. Inactive constraints necessarily have zero multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \((\lambda,\mu)\) satisfies dual feasibility and complementarity: \(\mu\ge0\) and \(\mu_i g_i(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The positive-multiplier, zero-multiplier active, and inactive index sets form a disjoint exhaustive partition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Strict complementarity at \((\bar x,\mu)\) is equivalent to \(I^0(\bar x,\mu)=\varnothing\).
special_cases_latex: If the KKT multiplier is unique, the weighted partition is intrinsic to \(\bar x\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Indices in \(I^+\) are forced to satisfy equality in the associated critical-cone conditions.
Weakly active indices retain one-sided linearized inequalities.
boundary_notes: With nonunique multipliers, different multipliers may produce different weighted partitions.
Positive multipliers should not be conflated with numerically large approximate multipliers.

notation.meaning: Positive- and zero-multiplier subsets of the active inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly and Weakly Active Constraint Partition
Strongly Active Constraints
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strongly active inequality is active and has a strictly positive component in the selected KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a KKT pair \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) for inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), using multipliers \(\bar\lambda_i\ge0\). The strongly active subset relative to \(\bar\lambda\) is \[\mathcal A_+(\bar x,\bar\lambda)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0,\ \bar\lambda_i>0\}.\] By complementary slackness, positive multiplier already implies activity, so equivalently \(\mathcal A_+(\bar x,\bar\lambda)=\{i:\bar\lambda_i>0\}\). This classification is attached to the selected KKT multiplier and need not be intrinsic to \(\bar x\) when multipliers are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A_+(\bar x,\bar\lambda)=\{i\in\mathcal A(\bar x):\bar\lambda_i>0\}=\{i:\bar\lambda_i>0\}\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-relative strong activity for KKT inequalities.

notation.meaning: selected KKT multiplier vector for inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Active Constraints
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly active inequality is attained at equality but has zero component in the selected KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a KKT pair \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) associated with inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), the weakly active subset relative to the selected multiplier is \[\mathcal A_0(\bar x,\bar\lambda)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0,\ \bar\lambda_i=0\}.\] It contains constraints lying on their boundaries but contributing no normal vector through that multiplier. Together with the strongly active subset, it partitions the active inequalities: \[\mathcal A(\bar x)=\mathcal A_+(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal A_0(\bar x,\bar\lambda).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A_0(\bar x,\bar\lambda)=\mathcal A(\bar x)\setminus\mathcal A_+(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-relative weak activity for KKT inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Active Constraints with Multiplier-Dependent Support
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate active inequalities yield a segment of multipliers whose selected positive supports differ, demonstrating multiplier-dependent activity classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}-x\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_1(x)=x\le0,\qquad g_2(x)=x\le0.\] At the solution \(\bar x=0\), \(\mathcal A(\bar x)=\{1,2\}\), and the KKT inequality multipliers satisfy \[\mu_1+\mu_2=1,\qquad \mu_1,\mu_2\ge0.\] Hence \((1,0)\), \((0,1)\), and \((1/2,1/2)\) are valid multipliers with different positive supports, although the geometric active set is unchanged.
assumptions_latex: KKT stationarity is written \(\nabla f(\bar x)+\sum_i\mu_i\nabla g_i(\bar x)=0\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary nonunique-multiplier example exhibiting different strong–weak partitions of the same geometric active set.

notation.meaning: Active indices having positive components in the selected multiplier.

knowledge_statements.title: Possible Positive Support and Relative-Interior Multipliers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active indices split into those positive for some multiplier and those zero for every multiplier; every relative-interior multiplier realizes the entire possible-positive support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Lambda(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\) consist of multiplier pairs \((\lambda,\mu)\), and define \[\mathcal A_{\exists+}=\{i\in\mathcal A(\bar x):\exists(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda(\bar x),\ \mu_i>0\},\qquad \mathcal A_{\forall0}=\{i\in\mathcal A(\bar x):\mu_i=0\ \forall(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda(\bar x)\}.\] These sets partition \(\mathcal A(\bar x)\). Every \((\lambda^{\rm ri},\mu^{\rm ri})\in\operatorname{relint}\Lambda(\bar x)\) satisfies \[\{i:\mu_i^{\rm ri}>0\}=\mathcal A_{\exists+},\qquad \{i:\mu_i^{\rm ri}=0\}=\mathcal A_{\forall0}.\] Consequently, a strictly complementary multiplier exists exactly when \(\mathcal A_{\forall0}=\varnothing\), in which case every relative-interior multiplier is strictly complementary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal A(\bar x)=\mathcal A_{\exists+}\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal A_{\forall0},\quad \operatorname{supp}\mu^{\rm ri}=\mathcal A_{\exists+}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical support classification induced by a nonempty convex KKT multiplier set.

notation.meaning: Active indices positive for at least one KKT multiplier.
Active indices zero for every KKT multiplier.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Dependent Activity Classification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active set is geometric, but its positive- versus zero-multiplier partition can change with the chosen KKT multiplier; uniqueness removes this ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) be the set of KKT inequality multipliers at a feasible stationary point \(\bar x\). For every \(\lambda\in\Lambda(\bar x)\), define \(\mathcal A_+(\lambda)=\{i\in\mathcal A(\bar x):\lambda_i>0\}\) and \(\mathcal A_0(\lambda)=\{i\in\mathcal A(\bar x):\lambda_i=0\}\). The geometric active set \(\mathcal A(\bar x)\) is independent of \(\lambda\), but its strong–weak partition may vary. The classification is multiplier-independent exactly when \[\mathcal A_+(\lambda)=\mathcal A_+(\mu)\quad\text{for all }\lambda,\mu\in\Lambda(\bar x).\] In particular, uniqueness of the KKT multiplier implies multiplier-independent classification.
assumptions_latex: All multipliers use the same inequality sign convention
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(\bar x)=\mathcal A_+(\lambda)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal A_0(\lambda)\) for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda(\bar x)\), while the two parts may depend on \(\lambda\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of strong and weak activity on multiplier choice.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Possible Positive Support from a Relative-Interior Multiplier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical support classification induced by a nonempty convex KKT multiplier set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Lambda(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\), and define \[\mathcal A_{\exists+}=\{i\in\mathcal A(\bar x):\exists\lambda\in\Lambda(\bar x)\text{ with }\lambda_i>0\},\qquad \mathcal A_{\forall0}=\{i\in\mathcal A(\bar x):\lambda_i=0\ \forall\lambda\in\Lambda(\bar x)\}.\] Then these sets partition \(\mathcal A(\bar x)\). Moreover, every \(\lambda^{\mathrm{ri}}\in\operatorname{relint}\Lambda(\bar x)\) simultaneously realizes all possibly positive indices: \[\mathcal A_+(\lambda^{\mathrm{ri}})=\mathcal A_{\exists+},\qquad \mathcal A_0(\lambda^{\mathrm{ri}})=\mathcal A_{\forall0}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active indices split into those positive for at least one multiplier and those zero for every multiplier; any relative-interior multiplier realizes this entire possible-positive support at once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal A(\bar x)=\mathcal A_{\exists+}\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal A_{\forall0},\quad \mathcal A_+(\lambda^{\mathrm{ri}})=\mathcal A_{\exists+}\text{ for every }\lambda^{\mathrm{ri}}\in\operatorname{relint}\Lambda(\bar x).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Cx\le d\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex polyhedral geometry; representation-dependent activity is separated from intrinsic face structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in P\), let \(F_P(x)\) be the unique minimal face of \(P\) containing \(x\). The face-stratum correspondence is \[x\in\operatorname{ri}F_P(x),\qquad P=\mathbin{\dot\bigcup}_{F\in\mathcal F(P)}\operatorname{ri}F,\] where \(\mathcal F(P)\) is the family of nonempty faces. For an irredundant inequality representation, each nonempty activity stratum \(S_I=\{x\in P:I(x)=I\}\) is the relative interior of the face obtained by imposing \(C_i x=d_i\) for \(i\in I\), with equalities \(Ax=b\) retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every point of a polyhedron lies in the relative interior of one unique minimal face, and the relative interiors of all nonempty faces partition the polyhedron. Under an irredundant representation, constant-activity strata correspond to these relative interiors.
assumptions_latex: For the direct activity-set correspondence, the inequality description is irredundant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The map \(x\mapsto F_P(x)\) identifies each point with a unique face stratum \(\operatorname{ri}F_P(x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Two points lie in the same face stratum iff they have the same minimal face.
Under an irredundant description, two points share a stratum iff their active inequality sets coincide.
special_cases_latex: The interior stratum is \(\operatorname{ri}P\).
Vertices are zero-dimensional face strata.
immediate_consequences_latex: The tangent and normal cone combinatorial types are constant on each relative-interior face stratum.
Passing to a proper subface can only add active supporting inequalities.
boundary_notes: Redundant or duplicate inequalities can destroy a one-to-one correspondence with raw index sets.
Curved feasible sets generally require a separate manifold or variational stratification.

notation.meaning: Relative interior of \(F\) in its affine hull.
