knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Faces and Relative-Interior Strata
Face Direction Space as Tangent-Cone Lineality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a relative-interior face point, the face direction space is the tangent cone’s lineality space and the null space of all face-active rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\), \(F\), and \(I(F)\) be as in the seed, and let \(x\in\operatorname{relint}F\). Then \[\operatorname{lin}T_P(x)=T_P(x)\cap(-T_P(x))=\{d:a_i^\top d=0\ \forall i\in I(F)\}=\operatorname{span}(F-F).\] Consequently, \[\operatorname{aff}F=x+\operatorname{lin}T_P(x),\qquad \dim F=\dim\operatorname{lin}T_P(x).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{span}(F-F)=\operatorname{lin}T_P(x)=\{d:a_i^\top d=0\ \forall i\in I(F)\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic affine-direction geometry of a polyhedral face.

notation.meaning: Largest linear subspace contained in the tangent cone.
Direction space parallel to the affine hull of F.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Face Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the relative interior of a polyhedral face, the active inequalities and the corresponding tangent and normal cones remain constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^\top x\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) be a polyhedron, let \(F\) be a nonempty face, and define \(I(F)=\{i:a_i^\top x=b_i\text{ for every }x\in F\}\). For every \(x\in\operatorname{relint}F\), the active set equals \(I(F)\), and the local cones are constant along the relative interior: \[T_P(x)=\{d:a_i^\top d\le0\text{ for all }i\in I(F)\},\qquad N_P(x)=\operatorname{cone}\{a_i:i\in I(F)\}.\] Thus a face determines a fixed first-order feasible geometry on its relative interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_P(x)=\{d:a_i^\top d\le0\ (i\in I(F))\}\) and \(N_P(x)=\operatorname{cone}\{a_i:i\in I(F)\}\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent and normal geometry on polyhedral faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Openness, Convexity, and Closure of Activity Strata
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty exact-activity stratum is convex and relatively open in its affine hull; its closure permits additional inequalities to become active.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x:a_i^\top x\le b_i,\ i\in\mathcal I\}\) and \(J\subseteq\mathcal I\), every nonempty activity stratum \[S_J=\{x\in P:a_i^\top x=b_i\ (i\in J),\ a_i^\top x<b_i\ (i\notin J)\}\] is convex and relatively open in its affine hull. Its closure is \[\overline{S_J}=\{x\in P:a_i^\top x=b_i\ \forall i\in J\};\] points in the boundary may have additional active inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_J\text{ is convex and relatively open, and }\overline{S_J}=\{x\in P:a_i^\top x=b_i\ \forall i\in J\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topology and convexity of nonempty exact-activity regions in a polyhedron.

notation.meaning: Polyhedral points having exact active set J.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Activity Strata
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local activity stratum is the set of feasible points having exactly one prescribed active inequality set; nonempty strata partition the polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^\top x\le b_i,\ i\in\mathcal I\}\). For each \(J\subseteq\mathcal I\), the activity stratum indexed by \(J\) is \[S_J=\{x\in P:a_i^\top x=b_i\text{ for }i\in J,\ a_i^\top x<b_i\text{ for }i\in\mathcal I\setminus J\}.\] Equivalently, \(S_J=\{x\in P:\mathcal A(x)=J\}\). The nonempty sets \(S_J\) are pairwise disjoint and partition \(P\); within each stratum, the active-set description and polyhedral tangent-normal geometry are constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\mathop{\dot\bigcup}_{J\subseteq\mathcal I,\ S_J\ne\varnothing}S_J\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-active-set strata of a polyhedral feasible region.

notation.meaning: stratum having exact active set J

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Openness and Convexity of Activity Strata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic topology and convexity of nonempty exact-activity regions in a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x:a_i^\top x\le b_i,1\ i\in\mathcal I\}\) and \(J\subseteq\mathcal I\), every nonempty activity stratum \[S_J=\{x:a_i^\top x=b_i\ (i\in J),\ a_i^\top x<b_i\ (i\notin J)\}\] is convex and relatively open in its affine hull. Its closure in \(P\) is obtained by replacing every strict inequality by a non-strict one: \[\overline{S_J}=\{x\in P:a_i^\top x=b_i\text{ for every }i\in J\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty exact-activity stratum is convex and relatively open in its affine hull; its closure permits additional inequalities to become active.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Openness and Convexity of Activity Strata
General Face–Stratum Bijection and Order Reversal
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty polyhedral face is the closure of one exact-activity stratum, and face inclusion reverses inclusion of the corresponding full active-index sets; irredundancy and full dimensionality are unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^\top x\le b_i,\ i\in\mathcal I\}\ne\varnothing\), with \(\mathcal I\) finite, and define \(I(F)=\{i:a_i^\top x=b_i\ \forall x\in F\}\). For every nonempty face \(F\), \[S_{I(F)}=\{x\in P:\mathcal A(x)=I(F)\}=\operatorname{relint}F,\qquad \overline{S_{I(F)}}=F.\] Conversely, every nonempty exact-activity stratum is the relative interior of one unique face. For nonempty faces \(F,G\), \[F\subseteq G\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad I(F)\supseteq I(G).\] Thus the face lattice is anti-isomorphic to the realizable exact active-index sets, even when the finite inequality description is redundant or \(P\) is not full-dimensional.
assumptions_latex: \(P\ne\varnothing\) is given by finitely many affine inequalities
Only nonempty faces and strata are considered
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\longleftrightarrow S_{I(F)}=\operatorname{relint}F\text{ is a bijection, and }F\subseteq G\iff I(F)\supseteq I(G).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-relative correspondence for an arbitrary finite inequality description of a nonempty polyhedron.

notation.meaning: All represented inequalities active identically on F.

knowledge_statements.title: Face–Stratum Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an irredundant facet description, each face has one relative-interior activity stratum, and every nonempty exact-activity stratum uniquely identifies a face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^\top x\le b_i,\ i\in\mathcal I\}\) be full-dimensional, with an irredundant representation in which every inequality defines a facet. For each nonempty face \(F\), set \(I(F)=\{i:a_i^\top x=b_i\text{ for every }x\in F\}\). Then \[\operatorname{relint}F=\{x\in P:\mathcal A(x)=I(F)\}=S_{I(F)}.\] Conversely, every nonempty activity stratum \(S_J\) is the relative interior of the unique face \[F_J=\{x\in P:a_i^\top x=b_i\text{ for every }i\in J\}.\] Thus faces and nonempty exact-activity strata correspond bijectively.
assumptions_latex: The inequality representation is irredundant and facet-defining
Only nonempty faces and strata are considered
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\longleftrightarrow\operatorname{relint}F=S_{I(F)}\) is a bijection between nonempty faces and nonempty activity strata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence for irredundant facet descriptions of full-dimensional polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\), with continuously differentiable data, and let \(\bar x\) be feasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth NLP; MFCQ is used as the representative regularity condition linking feasible geometry to nonabnormal multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The point \( ar x\) is multiplier-regular in the MFCQ sense if \(
abla h( ar x)\) has full column rank and there exists \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \[
abla h_j( ar x)^Td=0\  orall j,\qquad 
abla g_i( ar x)^Td<0\  orall i\in I( ar x).\] Its KKT multiplier set is \[\Lambda( ar x):=\{(\lambda,\mu):
abla f( ar x)+
abla h( ar x)\lambda+
abla g( ar x)\mu=0,\ \mu\ge0,\ \mu_i g_i( ar x)=0\}.\] A feasible point satisfying this regularity condition and \(\Lambda( ar x)
e\varnothing\) is a multiplier-regular stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFCQ multiplier regularity requires independent equality gradients and one direction tangent to all equalities that strictly decreases every active inequality. The associated multiplier set consists of all equality and nonnegative inequality multipliers satisfying stationarity and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Multiplier regularity is the displayed MFCQ condition; multiplier-regular stationarity additionally requires \(\Lambda(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: MFCQ excludes a nonzero abnormal multiplier \((\lambda,\mu)\) satisfying \(\nabla h(\bar x)\lambda+\nabla g(\bar x)\mu=0\), \(\mu\ge0\), and \(\mu_i=0\) for inactive indices.
special_cases_latex: LICQ implies MFCQ.
With equality constraints only, MFCQ reduces to linear independence of equality gradients.
immediate_consequences_latex: At a local minimizer, MFCQ supports a nonabnormal KKT multiplier representation.
The multiplier set is described by linear equations, nonnegativity, and complementarity at fixed \(\bar x\).
boundary_notes: MFCQ need not make the multiplier unique; LICQ is stronger.
The definition does not state a necessary-optimality theorem or its proof.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth NLP using the inequality convention \(g(x)\le0\) and nonnegative inequality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Lagrangian–multiplier representation pair at a feasible point \(\bar x\) is \[\bigl(L,\Lambda(\bar x)\bigr),\qquad L(x,\lambda,\mu):=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\mu^Tg(x),\] where \[\Lambda(\bar x):=\{(\lambda,\mu):\nabla_xL(\bar x,\lambda,\mu)=0,\ \mu\ge0,\ \mu_i g_i(\bar x)=0\ \forall i\}.\] Equality multipliers \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\) are unrestricted, while inequality multipliers \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^q\) are dual-feasible and complementary to the inequality slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The representation pair consists of the scalar Lagrangian and the set of multiplier vectors that make its gradient with respect to the decision variable vanish while satisfying nonnegativity and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((L,\Lambda(\bar x))\) jointly records the scalar constraint aggregation and all KKT multiplier representations at \(\bar x\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Complementarity is equivalently \(0\le\mu\perp-g(\bar x)\ge0\).

Stationarity is \(
abla f( ar x)+
abla h( ar x)\lambda+
abla g( ar x)\mu=0\).
special_cases_latex: With equality constraints only, \(L=f+\lambda^Th\) and no sign restrictions apply to \(\lambda\).
Under LICQ, \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) contains at most one multiplier pair.
immediate_consequences_latex: Inactive inequalities have zero multipliers.
Positive multipliers can occur only on active inequalities.
boundary_notes: Changing to the convention \(g(x)\ge0\) changes the sign of the inequality term or multiplier restriction.
Nonemptiness of \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) is not guaranteed without stationarity and suitable optimality hypotheses.

notation.meaning: Componentwise nonnegativity and zero inner product, equivalently complementarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian and KKT Multiplier-Set Pair
Lagrangian Dual-Function Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing the Lagrangian over the primal variable produces a concave dual function and the weak-duality lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[q(\lambda,\mu)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}L(x,\lambda,\mu),\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R^p,\quad\mu\ge0.\] The function \(q\) is concave. For every primal-feasible \(x\), \[q(\lambda,\mu)\le L(x,\lambda,\mu)\le f(x),\] and therefore \[\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^p,\mu\ge0}q(\lambda,\mu)\le\inf_{h(x)=0,g(x)\le0}f(x).\]
assumptions_latex: Infima and suprema are interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^\star:=\sup_{\lambda,\mu\ge0}q(\lambda,\mu)\le p^\star.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual lower-bound representation for inequalities written as nonpositive functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Value at Complementary Feasible Pairs
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible complementary pair the Lagrangian equals the objective; feasibility alone only gives a lower value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(h(x)=0\), \(g(x)\le0\), and \(\mu\ge0\), then \[L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\mu^{\mathsf T}g(x)\le f(x).\] If additionally \(\mu_i g_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\), then \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)\) for every equality multiplier \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu_i g_i(x)=0\ \forall i\Rightarrow L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value identity underlying primal-dual certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Inequality Sign Conventions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reversing the inequality orientation reverses the sign of its Lagrangian term while preserving the represented KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing \(g_i(x)\le0\) by \(c_i(x)=-g_i(x)\ge0\) transforms \[L=f+\lambda^{\mathsf T}h+\mu^{\mathsf T}g,\quad\mu\ge0,\] into \[L=f+\lambda^{\mathsf T}h-\mu^{\mathsf T}c,\quad\mu\ge0.\] Stationarity and complementarity remain equivalent after substitution.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian combines the objective and constraints; KKT multipliers represent stationarity using nonnegative, complementary inequality coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem 
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=0,\quad g(x)\le 0,\]
the Lagrangian is 
\[L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}h(x)+\mu^{\mathsf T}g(x).\]
At a feasible point \(x\), a KKT multiplier pair \((\lambda,\mu)\) represents first-order stationarity by 
\[\nabla_x L(x,\lambda,\mu)=0,\qquad \mu\ge0,\qquad \mu_i g_i(x)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\]
Thus inactive inequalities have zero multipliers, while active constraint gradients combine with \(\nabla f(x)\) to give the zero vector.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h_j,g_i\) are continuously differentiable near the feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Lagrangian and KKT system give the local multiplier representation of first-order stationarity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard smooth finite-dimensional NLP with equality constraints and inequalities written as nonpositive functions.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The KKT multiplier set \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) consists of all equality multipliers \(\lambda\) and nonnegative inequality multipliers \(\mu\) satisfying stationarity and complementary slackness at \(\bar x\). Because inactive inequalities have zero multipliers, it is an affine inverse image intersected with the nonnegative orthant on the active coordinates.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\) for \(i=1,\ldots,r\), let \(b_j\in\mathbb R^n\) for \(j=1,\ldots,s\), and let \(q\in\mathbb R^n\). Define \(K=\{\sum_i\mu_i a_i+\sum_j\lambda_j b_j:\mu\geq0,\ \lambda\in\mathbb R^s\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linearized first-order systems. The vectors may represent active inequality gradients, equality gradients, and an objective gradient at a fixed nonlinear-programming point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\text{Exactly one of}\quad \mathrm{(M)}:\ q\in K,\qquad \mathrm{(D)}:\ \exists d\in\mathbb R^n\text{ with }q^Td<0,\ a_i^Td\geq0\ \forall i,\ b_j^Td=0\ \forall j\quad\text{holds}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An alternative-certificate multiplier principle is the mutually exclusive pair consisting of a multiplier representation \(q=\sum_i\mu_i a_i+\sum_j\lambda_jb_j\), with \(\mu_i\geq0\), and a separating direction \(d\) that has negative pairing with \(q\), nonnegative pairing with every inequality generator, and zero pairing with every equality generator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[q\notin K\iff \exists d:\ q^Td<0,\ A^Td\geq0,\ B^Td=0;\qquad q\in K\iff q^Td\geq0\ \forall d\text{ satisfying }A^Td\geq0,\ B^Td=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The multiplier alternative is \(\exists(\mu,\lambda)\in\mathbb R_+^r\times\mathbb R^s\) such that \(q=A\mu+B\lambda\).
The directional alternative supplies a strict separating hyperplane between \(q\) and the closed polyhedral cone \(K\).
special_cases_latex: With no equality generators, this is the conic form of Farkas' lemma.

At a feasible NLP point, taking \(q=-\nabla f(\bar x)\) converts the multiplier alternative into stationarity and the directional alternative into a first-order feasible descent certificate, after matching the constraint sign convention.
immediate_consequences_latex: Failure of every admissible descent direction is equivalent to membership of the objective normal in the cone generated by active constraint normals.
The strict inequality \(q^Td<0\) makes simultaneous validity of both alternatives impossible.
boundary_notes: Closedness is automatic for the finitely generated cone plus linear subspace used here; analogous alternatives for general cones require suitable closedness assumptions.
This definition concerns the linearized system and does not itself establish that linearized directions are genuine tangent directions.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), and \(g\in\mathbb R^n\). Put \(K=\{By+Cw:y\in\mathbb R_+^m,\ w\in\mathbb R^p\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional homogeneous linear equalities and inequalities, including free multipliers through the columns of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathcal A_g:=\{(y,w):y\geq0,\ By+Cw=g\},\qquad \mathcal S_g:=\{d:B^Td\geq0,\ C^Td=0,\ g^Td<0\}.\quad\text{Exactly one of }\mathcal A_g\neq\varnothing\text{ and }\mathcal S_g\neq\varnothing\text{ holds}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear alternative certificate system associates with \((B,C,g)\) a representation system \(By+Cw=g\), \(y\geq0\), and a strict separation system \(B^Td\geq0\), \(C^Td=0\), \(g^Td<0\). Exactly one system is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[g\in K\iff \mathcal A_g\neq\varnothing\iff g^Td\geq0\quad\forall d\text{ with }B^Td\geq0,\ C^Td=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[g\notin K\iff \mathcal S_g\neq\varnothing.\]
Replacing each free component of \(w\) by the difference of two nonnegative variables reduces the system to the nonnegative-generator form of Farkas' lemma.
special_cases_latex: If \(C\) has no columns, \(K=\operatorname{cone}(B)\).
If \(B\) has no columns, the alternative states either \(g\in\operatorname{range}(C)\) or some \(d\in\ker(C^T)\) satisfies \(g^Td<0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any \(d\in\mathcal S_g\) is an explicit certificate that the multiplier equation is infeasible.
Any \((y,w)\in\mathcal A_g\) certifies that no strict separating direction exists.
boundary_notes: The strict inequality belongs only to the separating certificate; weakening it to \(g^Td\leq0\) destroys the exclusive alternative.
Affine systems with nonzero right-hand sides require homogenization or a corresponding affine form of the alternative.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality Feasibility Form of Farkas' Lemma
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite weak linear-inequality system is infeasible exactly when a nonnegative multiplier annihilates its coefficient matrix and pairs negatively with its right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), exactly one of the systems \[Ax\leq b\] and \[y\geq0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0\] is feasible. Equivalently, \(Ax\leq b\) has a solution if and only if every \(y\geq0\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) also satisfies \(b^{\mathsf T}y\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x:Ax\leq b\iff\forall y\geq0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y=0\Rightarrow b^{\mathsf T}y\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative certificate for feasibility of a finite system of weak linear inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Alternative Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Either a vector is a nonnegative combination of the columns of A, or a linear functional strictly separates it from that cone, but not both.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Exactly one of the following systems is solvable:
\[\text{(P)}\qquad Ax=b,\qquad x\ge0,\]
\[\text{(D)}\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0.\]
Consequently, \(b\) belongs to the finitely generated cone \(\{Ax:x\ge0\}\) if and only if every \(y\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\) also satisfies \(b^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\). Equivalent inequality, conic, and homogeneous alternatives follow by introducing slack variables or splitting unrestricted variables into positive and negative parts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(\mathrm{(P)}\) and \(\mathrm{(D)}\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality form of Farkas' lemma for a finite-dimensional nonnegative linear feasibility system.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed-Cone Failure of Strict Certification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point outside a nonclosed convex cone but in its closure need not have a strict dual nonmembership certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:v>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\} and z=(1,0). Then K is a convex cone, z\notin K, and z\in\overline K. Every y\in K^* satisfies \langle y,z\rangle\ge0, so no dual-cone vector strictly separates z from K.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Closedness cannot be omitted from the strict conic alternative.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp closedness boundary for the conic separation alternative.

knowledge_statements.title: Bipolar Membership Characterization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The double dual of a convex cone is its closure, so dual inequalities characterize membership in a closed cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonempty convex cone K\subseteq\mathbb R^n, K^{**}=\overline K. Hence z\in\overline K if and only if \langle y,z\rangle\ge0 for every y\in K^*; when K is closed, this is equivalent to z\in K.
assumptions_latex: K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a nonempty convex cone.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K^{**}=\overline K.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-cone membership formulation underlying the separation alternative.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point outside a nonempty closed convex set is strictly separated from it by an affine hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let C\subseteq\mathbb R^n be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let z
otin C. Then there exist y
e0 and \alpha\in\mathbb R such that \langle y,zangle<\alpha\le\langle y,cangle for every c\in C. Conversely, these inequalities imply z
otin C.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists y\ne0,\alpha:\ \langle y,z\rangle<\alpha\le\inf_{c\in C}\langle y,c\rangle.

knowledge_statements.title: Separating-Hyperplane Alternatives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point either lies in a closed convex cone or is strictly separated from it by a functional nonnegative on the entire cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty closed convex cone and let \(z\in\mathbb R^n\). Exactly one of the following alternatives holds:
\[z\in K,\]
or there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^n\) such that
\[\langle y,k\rangle\ge0\quad\text{for every }k\in K,\qquad \langle y,z\rangle<0.\]
The second alternative supplies a separating hyperplane through the origin. Its normal \(y\) belongs to the dual cone \(K^*=\{y:\langle y,k\rangle\ge0\ \forall k\in K\}\) and certifies that \(z\notin K\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone in \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either \(z\in K\), or some \(y\in K^*\) satisfies \(\langle y,z\rangle<0\), exclusively.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong separation of a point from a closed convex cone in Euclidean space.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Alternative Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero homogeneous alternative certificate can be normalized so its nonnegative inequality multipliers sum to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The certificate system \(H\lambda+G\mu=0\), \(\mu\geq0\), \(\mu\neq0\) is positively homogeneous. Therefore it is feasible if and only if it has a representative satisfying \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\mu=1\). Thus \[H\lambda+G\mu=0,\qquad \mu\geq0,\qquad \mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\mu=1\] is an equivalent nonhomogeneous linear feasibility test for absence of a direction \(d\) with \(H^{\mathsf T}d=0\) and \(G^{\mathsf T}d<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists(\lambda,\mu):H\lambda+G\mu=0,\ \mu\geq0,\ \mu\neq0\iff\exists(\lambda,\mu):H\lambda+G\mu=0,\ \mu\geq0,\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\mu=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-sum normalization of the homogeneous multiplier certificate in the strict-direction alternative.

notation.meaning: All-ones vector having the dimension of \(\mu\)

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative-Certificate Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure of a common strict linearized feasible direction is equivalent to a verifiable nonzero positive dependence among equality and inequality gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\) and \(G\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\). Exactly one of the systems
\[H^{\mathsf T}d=0,\qquad G^{\mathsf T}d<0,\]
and
\[H\lambda+G\mu=0,\qquad \mu\ge0,\qquad \mu\ne0\]
is solvable. Hence a pair \((\lambda,\mu)\) satisfying the second system is a directly checkable certificate that no direction preserves the linearized equalities while strictly decreasing every listed inequality. Conversely, infeasibility of the strict-direction system guarantees such a nonzero multiplier certificate.
assumptions_latex: The inequality \(G^{\mathsf T}d<0\) is componentwise strict.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strict-direction system is infeasible if and only if a certificate \((\lambda,\mu)\) with \(H\lambda+G\mu=0\), \(\mu\ge0\), and \(\mu\ne0\) exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gordan-type correspondence between absence of a common strict feasible direction and nonzero constraint multipliers.

notation.meaning: Equality and nonnegative inequality certificate multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Qualifications Force Normality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any constraint qualification excluding abnormal constraint-only dependencies forces Fritz John multipliers to be normal; MFCQ and LICQ therefore yield KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be a local minimizer satisfying the hypotheses of the Fritz John multiplier principle. If a constraint qualification at \(x\) excludes every nonzero pair \((\lambda,\mu)\) with \(\mu\geq0\), \(\mu_i=0\) for inactive inequalities, and \[\nabla h(x)\lambda+\sum_i\mu_i\nabla g_i(x)=0,\] then every Fritz John multiplier at \(x\) has \(\alpha>0\). In particular, MFCQ, and hence LICQ, forces normality. Dividing the multipliers by \(\alpha\) yields a KKT multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is a local minimizer for which the Fritz John principle applies.
The stated constraint qualification excludes every nonzero abnormal constraint-multiplier pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha>0\), and \((1,\lambda/\alpha,\mu/\alpha)\) satisfies the KKT multiplier conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normality consequence of excluding nontrivial abnormal constraint-gradient dependencies.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Multiplier Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Fritz John multiplier is normal when its objective coefficient is positive; normalization makes that coefficient one and yields the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A Fritz John multiplier triple \((\alpha,\lambda,\mu)\), with \(\alpha\ge0\), is normal when \(\alpha>0\). Because the Fritz John equations are positively homogeneous in the multipliers, a normal triple can be rescaled to \(\alpha=1\). The stationarity and sign conditions then become
\[
abla f(x)+
abla h(x)\lambda+\sum_i\mu_i
abla g_i(x)=0,\qquad \mu\ge0,\qquad \mu_i g_i(x)=0.\]
Thus the normal Fritz John regime is precisely the regime in which the necessary conditions reduce to the KKT multiplier system.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is feasible for differentiable constraints \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\alpha>0\), normalization to \(\alpha=1\) converts the Fritz John system into the KKT system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal branch of the Fritz John first-order multiplier principle for smooth inequality-and-equality constrained NLP.

knowledge_statements.title: MFCQ–Abnormality Alternative
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With independent equality gradients, MFCQ holds exactly when no abnormal constraint-only multiplier certificate exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible point \(x\), let \(H\) collect equality gradients and \(G_A\) collect active inequality gradients. Assume \(H\) has full column rank. Then MFCQ holds, meaning that some \(d\) satisfies \(H^{\mathsf T}d=0\) and \(G_A^{\mathsf T}d<0\), if and only if there is no pair \((\lambda,\mu)\) satisfying \[H\lambda+G_A\mu=0,\qquad \mu\geq0,\qquad \mu\neq0.\] Consequently, under the equality-rank assumption, an abnormal Fritz John multiplier exists exactly when MFCQ fails.
assumptions_latex: The equality-gradient matrix \(H\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MFCQ}(x)\iff\nexists(\lambda,\mu):H\lambda+G_A\mu=0,\ \mu\geq0,\ \mu\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order regularity boundary for existence of an abnormal Fritz John multiplier when equality gradients are independent.

knowledge_statements.title: Abnormal Multiplier Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An abnormal Fritz John multiplier has zero objective coefficient, leaving a nontrivial signed dependence involving only active constraint gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A Fritz John multiplier triple \((\alpha,\lambda,\mu)
e0\) is abnormal when \(\alpha=0\). At a feasible point \(x\), its conditions reduce to
\[
abla h(x)\lambda+\sum_{i\in A(x)}\mu_i
abla g_i(x)=0,\qquad \mu_i\ge0,\qquad (\lambda,\mu)
e0,\]
with \(\mu_i=0\) for \(i
otin A(x)\). The stationarity relation therefore records a nontrivial constraint-gradient dependence and contains no objective gradient. Any constraint qualification excluding such a dependence rules out abnormal multipliers and forces the normal regime.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is feasible for differentiable constraints \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(\alpha=0\), the multipliers give a nontrivial constraint-only stationarity relation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abnormal branch of the Fritz John principle, in which objective information disappears from stationarity.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\Omega=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\subset\mathbb R^n\) with continuously differentiable constraints and \(\bar x\in\Omega\), let \(T_\Omega(\bar x)\) be the Bouligand tangent cone and \(L_\Omega(\bar x)=\{d:\nabla h(\bar x)^Td=0,\ \nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td\leq0\ (i\in I(\bar x))\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programs at a feasible point. A family groups pointwise regularity predicates; it is not a single universally equivalent condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathfrak C(\bar x):=\{\mathrm{LICQ},\mathrm{MFCQ},\mathrm{CRCQ},\mathrm{CPLD},\mathrm{RCPLD},\mathrm{ACQ},\mathrm{GCQ},\mathrm{Slater/linearity}\},\] where each member is a predicate on the local constraint representation whose intended consequence is an exact or dual-exact first-order description of feasible geometry and hence a valid multiplier rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical constraint-qualification family is the collection of named pointwise conditions imposed on active constraint gradients, feasible directions, tangent and linearization cones, or convex structure to ensure that first-order linearization supplies the normal information needed for multiplier optimality conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathrm{LICQ}\Rightarrow\mathrm{MFCQ}\Rightarrow\text{first-order multiplier validity},\qquad \mathrm{ACQ}:T_\Omega(\bar x)=L_\Omega(\bar x),\qquad \mathrm{GCQ}:T_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ=L_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ.\]
special_cases_latex: Gradient-directional qualifications impose rank or strict-direction conditions, such as LICQ and MFCQ.
Tangent-linearization qualifications impose equality of cones or their polars, such as ACQ and GCQ.
Convex-structural qualifications use affine equalities together with strict feasibility of convex inequalities.
immediate_consequences_latex: The family separates conditions by mechanism while retaining their common role in excluding pathological linearizations.
Different qualifications need not be equivalent; the applicable implication hierarchy depends on smoothness and the exact constraint class.
boundary_notes: Membership in this family does not mean that every listed condition holds at the point.
Constraint qualifications are representation-dependent except for formulations stated purely through the feasible-set tangent or normal geometry.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h_j,g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(\bar x\) be feasible for \(h=0\), \(g\leq0\), and let \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise, first-order, finite-dimensional regularity defined solely from equality and active-inequality gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
\[\mathcal R_{\mathrm{GD}}( ar x):=\left\{ egin{array}{l}	ext{rank predicates on }\{
abla h_j( ar x),
abla g_i( ar x):i\in I( ar x)\},\quad	ext{or}\[2pt]	ext{direction predicates asserting }\exists d:
abla h_j( ar x)^Td=0\  orall j,\

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gradient-directional regularity class consists of constraint qualifications expressible at a feasible point through ranks or dependence relations among active gradients, possibly together with a direction tangent to all equalities and strictly decreasing every active inequality. LICQ is the pure independence member; MFCQ combines equality-gradient independence with the strict direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathrm{LICQ}(\bar x)\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{GD}}(\bar x),\qquad \mathrm{MFCQ}(\bar x)\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{GD}}(\bar x),\qquad \mathrm{LICQ}(\bar x)\Rightarrow\mathrm{MFCQ}(\bar x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The MFCQ direction condition says that the relative interior of the linearized inequality system, within \(\ker\nabla h(\bar x)^T\), is nonempty.

The failure of MFCQ is equivalently witnessed by a nonzero abnormal multiplier satisfying \(\sum_j\lambda_j\nabla h_j(\bar x)+\sum_{i\in I(\bar x)}\mu_i\nabla g_i(\bar x)=0\) with \(\mu\geq0\), under equality-gradient independence.
special_cases_latex: With no inequalities, both LICQ and MFCQ reduce to linear independence of the equality gradients.
With no equalities, MFCQ requires a direction strictly decreasing all active inequalities.
immediate_consequences_latex: LICQ gives uniqueness of any KKT multiplier vector.
MFCQ permits KKT necessity at a local minimizer and yields boundedness of the KKT multiplier set.
boundary_notes: This class does not include purely tangent-cone qualifications unless they are additionally represented by gradient conditions.
All conditions are tied to the chosen constraint representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension and Redundancy Boundary for LICQ
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Too many, duplicated, or zero active gradients violate LICQ, but LICQ failure does not itself preclude KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: LICQ at x\in\mathbb R^n requires p+|A(x)|\le n. It fails when the active-gradient family has deficient rank, including duplicated equality constraints, duplicated active inequalities, or a zero active constraint gradient. LICQ failure alone does not imply that KKT multipliers fail to exist.
assumptions_latex: \text{There are }p\text{ equalities and }|A(x)|\text{ active inequalities in }\mathbb R^n.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p+|A(x)|>n\Longrightarrow\neg\operatorname{LICQ}(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate structural obstructions to active-gradient independence.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Stability of LICQ
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With continuous gradients, LICQ persists at all sufficiently nearby feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the constraint gradients are continuous and LICQ holds at a feasible point \bar x, then there is a neighborhood U of \bar x such that LICQ holds at every feasible x\in U.
assumptions_latex: \text{The constraints are continuously differentiable near }\bar x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni\bar x\ \forall x\in U\cap F:\operatorname{LICQ}(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence of active-gradient independence at nearby feasible points.

knowledge_statements.title: LICQ Implies MFCQ
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear independence of all active gradients guarantees an equality-tangent direction strictly decreasing every active inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible point x, if the equality gradients together with all active inequality gradients are linearly independent, then the equality gradients are independent and there exists d satisfying \nabla h_j(x)^{\mathsf T}d=0 for every j and \nabla g_i(x)^{\mathsf T}d<0 for every i\in A(x). Hence LICQ implies MFCQ.
assumptions_latex: \text{The constraints are differentiable at the feasible point }x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{LICQ}(x)\Longrightarrow\operatorname{MFCQ}(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical hierarchy relation within gradient-directional qualifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Independence Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ requires all equality gradients and active inequality gradients to be linearly independent; it excludes abnormal dependencies and ensures multiplier uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a feasible point \(x\), define \(A(x)=\{i:g_i(x)=0\}\). The linear independence constraint qualification holds at \(x\) when the family
\[\{\nabla h_j(x):j=1,\ldots,p\}\cup\{\nabla g_i(x):i\in A(x)\}\]
is linearly independent. Equivalently, the relation
\[\sum_{j=1}^p\lambda_j\nabla h_j(x)+\sum_{i\in A(x)}\mu_i\nabla g_i(x)=0\]
implies \(\lambda=0\) and \(\mu=0\), without imposing signs on \(\mu\). LICQ excludes abnormal constraint-gradient dependencies and, whenever KKT multipliers exist, makes them unique.
assumptions_latex: \(h_j\) and \(g_i\) are differentiable at the feasible point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: LICQ holds exactly when the displayed active-gradient family is linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LICQ for smooth equality and nonpositive inequality constraints at a feasible point.

notation.meaning: Indices of inequalities active at x.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ holds at \(\bar x\) exactly when the gradients of every equality constraint and every active inequality constraint form a linearly independent family.

knowledge_statements.title: MFCQ Does Not Ensure Multiplier Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicated active inequalities can satisfy MFCQ while producing a continuum of KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \min_{x\in\mathbb R}x subject to -x\le0 and -x\le0. At the solution x=0, d=1 strictly decreases both active constraint linearizations, so MFCQ holds. Stationarity is 1-\mu_1-\mu_2=0 with \mu_1,\mu_2\ge0, giving the nonunique multiplier segment \mu_1+\mu_2=1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{MFCQ}(0)\text{ holds, but the KKT multiplier is not unique.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between MFCQ and LICQ.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Error Bound Under MFCQ
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near an MFCQ point, aggregate constraint violation bounds distance to the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the constraints are continuously differentiable and MFCQ holds at \bar x, then there exist \kappa>0 and a neighborhood U of \bar x such that \operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa\bigl(\|h(x)\|+\|g(x)_+\|\bigr) for every x\in U.
assumptions_latex: \text{The constraint functions are continuously differentiable near }\bar x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa\bigl(\|h(x)\|+\|g(x)_+\|\bigr)\quad(x\in U).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric regularity consequence for smooth finite-dimensional constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: MFCQ Consequences for Tangent Geometry and Multipliers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFCQ makes the linearized cone exact and gives a nonempty bounded KKT multiplier set at a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the constraints are continuously differentiable and MFCQ holds at a feasible point \bar x, then T_F(\bar x)=L_F(\bar x). If, additionally, \bar x is a local minimizer of a differentiable objective, its KKT multiplier set is nonempty and bounded, although it need not be a singleton.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the multiplier conclusion, }\bar x\text{ locally minimizes a differentiable objective.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_F(\bar x)=L_F(\bar x),\qquad \varnothing\ne\Lambda(\bar x)\text{ is bounded at a local minimizer.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Principal first-order consequences of MFCQ at a smooth feasible point.

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier set at the reference point.

knowledge_statements.title: Mangasarian–Fromovitz Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFCQ requires independent equality gradients and a direction tangent to all equalities that strictly decreases every active inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a feasible point \(x\), the Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification holds when the equality gradients \(\{
abla h_j(x)\}_{j=1}^p\) are linearly independent and there exists a direction \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying
\[
abla h_j(x)^{\mathsf T}d=0\quad(j=1,\ldots,p),\qquad 
abla g_i(x)^{\mathsf T}d<0\quad(i\in A(x)),\]
where \(A(x)=\{i:g_i(x)=0\}\). Equivalently, no nonzero pair \((\lambda,\mu)\) with \(\mu\ge0\) can satisfy the corresponding constraint-only stationarity relation over the active inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(h_j\) and \(g_i\) are differentiable at the feasible point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: MFCQ holds at \(x\) exactly under the displayed independence and strict-direction conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MFCQ for smooth equality constraints and inequalities represented by nonpositive functions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathcal Q_{TL}(\bar x):=\{Q:Q\text{ asserts either }T_\Omega(\bar x)=L_\Omega(\bar x)\text{ or }T_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ=L_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangent–linearization qualification is a pointwise condition requiring the true tangent cone and the cone obtained by linearizing active constraints to agree, either directly or after taking polar cones. Direct equality is the Abadie form; polar equality is the Guignard form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[T_\Omega(\bar x)\subseteq L_\Omega(\bar x),\qquad \mathrm{ACQ}:T_\Omega(\bar x)=L_\Omega(\bar x),\qquad \mathrm{GCQ}:T_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ=L_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Since \(T_\Omega(\bar x)\subseteq L_\Omega(\bar x)\), ACQ requires the reverse inclusion \(L_\Omega(\bar x)\subseteq T_\Omega(\bar x)\).
GCQ states that linearized and geometric first-order normals coincide even when the primal cones themselves differ.
special_cases_latex: LICQ implies direct tangent–linearization equality.
If every active constraint is affine, direct equality holds without LICQ.
immediate_consequences_latex: ACQ implies GCQ by taking polar cones.
GCQ supplies the normal-cone identity needed to represent first-order optimality by active constraint multipliers.
boundary_notes: The tangent cone used here is the Bouligand or contingent cone, not necessarily a convex cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Gradient Can Destroy Abadie CQ
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared inequality defines a singleton, but its zero gradient makes every direction linearized-feasible, so ACQ fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R:x^2\le0\}=\{0\}, T_\Omega(0)=\{0\}. Since g'(0)=0, the linearized inequality imposes no restriction and L_\Omega(0)=\mathbb R. Therefore ACQ fails at 0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_\Omega(0)=\{0\}\subsetneq\mathbb R=L_\Omega(0).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal smooth inequality where the linearization overestimates the tangent cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Abadie Implies Guignard
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality of the tangent and linearization cones implies equality of their polar cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If T_\Omega(\bar x)=L_\Omega(\bar x), then T_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ=L_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ. Hence ACQ implies GCQ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{ACQ}(\bar x)\Longrightarrow\mathrm{GCQ}(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate relation between the tangent–linearization qualifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Abadie Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Abadie CQ holds when the actual Bouligand tangent cone equals the cone predicted by the first-order linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}\]
and let \(x\in\Omega\). Its linearization cone is
\[L_\Omega(x)=\{d:\nabla h(x)^{\mathsf T}d=0,\ \nabla g_i(x)^{\mathsf T}d\le0\ \text{for all }i\in A(x)\}.\]
The Abadie constraint qualification holds at \(x\) when
\[T_\Omega(x)=L_\Omega(x),\]
where \(T_\Omega(x)\) is the Bouligand tangent cone. Since \(T_\Omega(x)\subseteq L_\Omega(x)\) always holds under differentiability, ACQ asserts the reverse inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: ACQ at \(x\) is the equality \(T_\Omega(x)=L_\Omega(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent–linearization equality form of ACQ for a smooth finite-dimensional feasible set.

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone to the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Abadie Constraint Qualification (ACQ)
Guignard CQ Can Hold While Abadie CQ Fails
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the crossed-quadrant set, the tangent cone is smaller than the full linearization but their polar cones coincide; GCQ holds while ACQ fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \Omega=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1x_2\le0\} and \bar x=(0,0). Since \nabla(x_1x_2)(\bar x)=0, L_\Omega(\bar x)=\mathbb R^2. Its tangent cone is T_\Omega(\bar x)=\{d:d_1d_2\le0\}, so ACQ fails. Because \operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}T_\Omega(\bar x)=\mathbb R^2, both polar cones equal \{0\}, and GCQ holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{GCQ}(\bar x)\quad\text{and}\quad\neg\mathrm{ACQ}(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth inequality proving GCQ is strictly weaker than ACQ.

knowledge_statements.title: Guignard Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Guignard CQ requires the tangent and linearization cones to have identical polar cones; it is weaker than equality of the cones themselves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a feasible point \(x\in\Omega=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}\), let \(T_\Omega(x)\) be the Bouligand tangent cone and \(L_\Omega(x)\) the constraint linearization cone. The Guignard constraint qualification holds at \(x\) when
\[T_\Omega(x)^\circ=L_\Omega(x)^\circ,\]
where the negative polar is \(C^\circ=\{v:\langle v,d\rangle\le0\ \text{for every }d\in C\}\). Equivalently, because taking polars closes convex hulls,
\[(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}T_\Omega(x))=L_\Omega(x)\]
whenever \(L_\Omega(x)\) is closed and convex.
assumptions_latex: \(h_j\) and \(g_i\) are continuously differentiable near the feasible point \(x\).
\(L_\Omega(x)\) is formed from equality gradients and active inequality gradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: GCQ at \(x\) is the polar equality \(T_\Omega(x)^\circ=L_\Omega(x)^\circ\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polar-cone equality form of GCQ for a smooth finite-dimensional feasible set.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Guignard constraint qualification holds when the negative polar of the true tangent cone equals the negative polar of the linearization cone, even if the two primal cones are not equal.

equivalent_formulations_latex: Since \(T_\Omega(\bar x)\subseteq L_\Omega(\bar x)\), one always has \(L_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ\subseteq T_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ\); GCQ requires the reverse inclusion.

For \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\) and \(K\subseteq I(\bar x)\), write \(G_{J,K}(x)=[\nabla h_j(x)]_{j\in J}\,[\nabla g_i(x)]_{i\in K}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming. These qualifications control how rank or signed dependence of selected active-gradient subfamilies persists near a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{RD}}(\bar x):=\left\{Q:\ Q\text{ requires, for specified }(J,K),\text{ local persistence of either }\operatorname{rank}G_{J,K}(x)\text{ or positive linear dependence of its equality/inequality columns}\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rank-dependence qualification family consists of constraint qualifications that inspect selected equality and active-inequality gradients and require their rank or their positive linear dependence pattern at \(\bar x\) to persist throughout a neighborhood. CRCQ uses constant ranks, CPLD uses persistence of positive dependence, and relaxed variants first select a stable basis of equality gradients.

equivalent_formulations_latex: A family \(\{v_j\}_{j\in J}\cup\{w_i\}_{i\in K}\) is positively linearly dependent when there exist coefficients \(\lambda_j\in\mathbb R\), \(\mu_i\geq0\), not all zero, such that \(\sum_{j\in J}\lambda_jv_j+\sum_{i\in K}\mu_iw_i=0\).

CPLD only constrains subfamilies that are positively dependent at the reference point.
RCPLD relaxes the equality portion by fixing a constant-rank basis and testing selected active inequalities relative to it.
immediate_consequences_latex: The family is weaker than LICQ in degenerate representations because it permits dependent active gradients.
Its conditions are local: values of gradients at nearby points are part of the definition.

knowledge_statements.title: CRCQ Implies Abadie Regularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CRCQ makes every linearized feasible direction tangentially realizable, so it implies ACQ and GCQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If CRCQ holds at a feasible point \bar x of a continuously differentiable mixed-constraint system, then T_\Omega(\bar x)=L_\Omega(\bar x). Consequently CRCQ implies ACQ and hence GCQ.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_\Omega(\bar x)=L_\Omega(\bar x)\Longrightarrow T_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ=L_\Omega(\bar x)^\circ.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be feasible for continuously differentiable constraints \(h_j(x)=0\), \(j=1,\ldots,p\), and \(g_i(x)\leq0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Let \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \bar x be a local minimizer of a nonlinear program with a differentiable objective and continuously differentiable equality and inequality constraints. If CPLD holds at \bar x, then there exist unrestricted equality multipliers \lambda and nonnegative inequality multipliers \mu satisfying stationarity, primal feasibility, and complementarity at \bar x.

\text{The constraints are continuously differentiable near }\bar x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\exists(\lambda,\mu),\ \mu\ge0:\ 
abla f( ar x)+\sum_j\lambda_j
abla h_j( ar x)+\sum_i\mu_i

knowledge_statements.title: Constant Positive Linear Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard CPLD condition for equality and reference-active inequality gradient subfamilies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(m,p\in\mathbb N_0\), and let \(g_i,h_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), \(j=1,\ldots,p\), be continuously differentiable near a feasible point \(\bar x\) of the constraints \(g_i(x)\le0\) and \(h_j(x)=0\). Define \(I(\bar x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\). For \(E\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\) and \(J\subseteq I(\bar x)\), the gradients indexed by \((E,J)\) are positively linearly dependent at \(\bar x\) if there exist coefficients \(\nu_j\in\mathbb R\), \(j\in E\), and \(\lambda_i\ge0\), \(i\in J\), not all zero, such that
\[
\sum_{j\in E}\nu_j\nabla h_j(\bar x)+\sum_{i\in J}\lambda_i\nabla g_i(\bar x)=0.
\]
CPLD holds at \(\bar x\) if there exists a neighborhood \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) of \(\bar x\) such that every subfamily positively linearly dependent at \(\bar x\) is linearly dependent at every \(x\in U\). No sign restriction is imposed on coefficients witnessing the nearby linear dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CPLD requires each constraint-gradient subfamily positively dependent at the reference point to remain linearly dependent throughout a neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(m,p\in\mathbb N_0\), and \(g_i,h_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every positively dependent indexed subfamily at \(\bar x\) remains linearly dependent on one common neighborhood \(U\).

notation.meaning: signed equality and nonnegative inequality dependence coefficients

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Constant-Rank Qualifications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxed constant-rank constraint qualification (RCRCQ) for smooth finite-dimensional constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(h_j(x)=0\), \(j\in E\), and \(g_i(x)\le0\), \(i\in I\), let \(\bar x\) be feasible and \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\). RCRCQ holds at \(\bar x\) if there exists a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that, for every subset \(K\subseteq I(\bar x)\), the rank \[\operatorname{rank}\bigl(\{\nabla h_j(x):j\in E\}\cup\{\nabla g_i(x):i\in K\}\bigr)\] is constant as \(x\) ranges over \(U\). Only inequalities active at \(\bar x\) are tested, which distinguishes this relaxed condition from rank requirements involving arbitrary nearby active sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every family formed from all equality gradients and any subset of currently active inequality gradients has locally constant rank.
assumptions_latex: \(h_j,g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) satisfies RCRCQ.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Basis Invariance of RCPLD
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the constant equality-rank requirement, changing the selected equality-gradient basis does not change whether RCPLD holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the equality-gradient rank is constant near \(\bar x\). If the RCPLD positive-dependence condition holds using one index set \(J\) whose gradients form a basis of the equality-gradient span at \(\bar x\), then it holds using every such equality-basis index set \(J'\). Thus RCPLD is a property of the constraint system at \(\bar x\), not of the chosen equality basis.

The equality-gradient rank is constant near \(\bar x\).
Both \(J\) and \(J'\) index bases of the equality-gradient span at \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h_j(x)=0\ (j=1,\ldots,p),\ g_i(x)\leq0\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\}\), where each \(h_j\) is affine and each \(g_i\) is convex and continuously differentiable. Let \(\bar x\in\Omega\) and \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex inequality structure with affine equalities. The local active-set form stated here is the Slater qualification used for multiplier necessity at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathrm{Slater}_{\bar x}\iff \exists x^{\mathrm s}\in\mathbb R^n:\ h_j(x^{\mathrm s})=0\ \forall j,\quad g_i(x^{\mathrm s})\leq0\ \forall i,\quad g_i(x^{\mathrm s})<0\ \forall i\in I(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex-structural Slater qualification holds at \(\bar x\) when the equalities are affine, the inequalities are convex, and there exists a feasible point that satisfies every inequality active at \(\bar x\) strictly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d:=x^{\mathrm s}-\bar x\quad\text{satisfies}\quad \nabla h_j(\bar x)^Td=0\ \forall j,\qquad \nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td<0\ \forall i\in I(\bar x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a global Slater point satisfying \(g_i(x^{\mathrm s})<0\) for every inequality, the local active-set condition holds at every feasible \(\bar x\).
After redundant affine equalities are removed, convexity converts strict feasibility into the MFCQ direction \(d=x^{\mathrm s}-\bar x\).
special_cases_latex: If every constraint is affine, tangent–linearization equality holds at each feasible point even when active gradients are dependent.
For inequality-only convex problems, the qualification is ordinary strict feasibility of the inequalities active at the point.

The qualification excludes abnormal Fritz John multipliers after redundant affine equalities are removed.

knowledge_statements.title: Slater Is Sufficient but Not Necessary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex problem can have an optimum and KKT multipliers even when strict feasibility is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The convex problem \min_x x^2 subject to x^2\le0 has the unique feasible and optimal point x=0, but no strictly feasible point. Slater's qualification fails, although \mu=0 satisfies stationarity, dual feasibility, and complementarity at the optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Slater's qualification is not necessary for KKT solvability.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary preventing strict feasibility from being treated as necessary for KKT solvability.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Valued Slater Strong Duality and Dual Attainment
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-valued finite-dimensional convex program with finite optimum, Slater strict feasibility gives zero duality gap and an optimal dual multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider p^*=\inf\{f_0(x):Ax=b,\ g_i(x)\le0\}, where f_0,g_1,\ldots,g_m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R are convex and p^* is finite. If there exists \hat x with A\hat x=b and g_i(\hat x)<0 for every i, then the Lagrange-dual value equals p^*, and the dual supremum is attained by some (\lambda,\mu) with \mu\ge0.
assumptions_latex: \exists\hat x:\ A\hat x=b,\ g_i(\hat x)<0\ \forall i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^*=p^*\quad\text{and the dual optimum is attained}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precise finite-valued convex-program consequence of Slater qualification.

knowledge_statements.title: Differentiable Slater Implies MFCQ
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For differentiable convex constraints and independent affine equalities, a Slater point supplies an MFCQ direction at every feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the convex inequalities g_i are differentiable at a feasible point x, A has full row rank, and a Slater point \hat x satisfies A\hat x=b and g_i(\hat x)<0 for every i. Then d=\hat x-x satisfies Ad=0 and \nabla g_i(x)^{\mathsf T}d<0 for every active inequality. Hence MFCQ holds at every feasible x.
assumptions_latex: g_i\text{ is convex and differentiable at }x\text{ for every }i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{MFCQ}(x)\text{ holds at every feasible }x.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relation between convex strict feasibility and the local directional qualification.

notation.meaning: Direction from the feasible point toward the Slater point.

knowledge_statements.title: Slater Qualification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slater's qualification holds when a point in the relative interior of the common effective domain satisfies the affine equalities and every convex inequality strictly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and let \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be proper convex functions. Define the common effective domain by \(D=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{dom}g_i\). The system \(Ax=b\), \(g_i(x)\le 0\) satisfies Slater's qualification if there exists \(\hat x\in\operatorname{ri}D\) such that \[A\hat x=b,\qquad g_i(\hat x)<0\quad\text{for every }i=1,\ldots,m.\]
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system satisfies Slater's qualification at the strict feasible point \(\hat x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-interior Slater condition for a finite-dimensional convex inequality system with affine equalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Slater constraint qualification for convex constraints
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X_0\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, let \(g_i:X_0\to\mathbb R\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be convex, and let \(h_j:X_0\to\mathbb R\), \(j=1,\ldots,p\), be affine. The feasible set is \(X=\{x\in X_0:g_i(x)\leq0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ h_j(x)=0\ (j=1,\ldots,p)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex programming with convex inequalities, affine equalities, and an optional convex set constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The constraint system satisfies the Slater qualification if there exists a point \(x^{\mathrm S}\in X_0\) such that
\[
g_i(x^{\mathrm S})<0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\qquad h_j(x^{\mathrm S})=0\quad(j=1,\ldots,p),
\]
and, in the set-constrained formulation requiring interior compatibility, \(x^{\mathrm S}\in\operatorname{int}X_0\) when equality constraints are present. Such an \(x^{\mathrm S}\) is called a Slater point or strictly feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex inequalities \(g_i(x)\leq0\) and affine equalities \(h_j(x)=0\) over a convex set \(X_0\), Slater qualification means that one feasible point \(x^{\mathrm S}\) satisfies every inequality strictly: \(g_i(x^{\mathrm S})<0\) for all \(i\), while satisfying every equality exactly. In the cited set-constrained formulation, \(x^{\mathrm S}\) must also lie in \(\operatorname{int}X_0\) when equalities occur.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists x^{\mathrm S}\in X_0:\quad g(x^{\mathrm S})<0,\quad h(x^{\mathrm S})=0,\quad x^{\mathrm S}\in\operatorname{int}X_0\ \text{when required}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(p=0\) and \(X_0=\mathbb R^n\), the condition is simply \(\exists x^{\mathrm S}\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(g_i(x^{\mathrm S})<0\) for every \(i\).
special_cases_latex: For affine inequalities, strict feasibility is the corresponding polyhedral Slater condition.
For a conic constraint \(G(x)\in-K\), the analogous condition is \(G(x^{\mathrm S})\in-\operatorname{int}K\), provided \(K\) has nonempty interior.
immediate_consequences_latex: Under the cited convex hypotheses, Slater qualification supplies the regularity needed for the standard normal-cone and KKT multiplier representation.
boundary_notes: Strict feasibility concerns inequality constraints; affine equalities are satisfied exactly, not strictly.
Relative-interior variants are needed when the ambient convex domain has empty ordinary interior; that variant is not asserted here.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core convex-duality consequence of the qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[p^*=\inf\{f_0(x):Ax=b,\ g_i(x)\le0\},\] where \(f_0,g_i\) are proper convex functions and the optimal value is finite. If the Slater condition in the seed holds and the standard finite-dimensional closedness hypotheses for the perturbation problem hold, then the Lagrange dual value equals \(p^*\). Moreover, the dual supremum is attained by some \((\lambda,\mu)\) with \(\mu\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Slater regularity and the usual finite-dimensional closedness assumptions, convex primal and Lagrange-dual values agree and an optimal dual multiplier exists.

Affine equalities and the seed's relative-interior Slater point exist.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X_0\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a convex polyhedron and let \(X=\{x\in X_0:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m;\ h_j(x)=0,\ j=1,\ldots,p\}\), where every \(g_i\) and \(h_j\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional systems whose set constraint and scalar constraints are polyhedral; no nonlinear constraint qualification is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An affine-polyhedral regularity class consists of constraint systems for which \(X_0\) is a convex polyhedron and all functions \(g_i\) and \(h_j\) are affine. At every \(\bar x\in X\), with active set \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\), the tangent cone is represented exactly by the linearized constraints:
\[
T_X(\bar x)=\{d\in T_{X_0}(\bar x):\langle\nabla g_i,d\rangle\leq0\ (i\in I(\bar x)),\ \langle\nabla h_j,d\rangle=0\ (j=1,\ldots,p)\}.
\]
This exactness holds without an additional local regularity assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint system is in the affine-polyhedral regularity class when its base set \(X_0\) is a convex polyhedron and all equality and inequality functions are affine. For every feasible point \(\bar x\), the true tangent cone \(T_X(\bar x)\) then equals the cone obtained by linearizing the active inequalities and all equalities within \(T_{X_0}(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[X_0\ \text{polyhedral and }g_i,h_j\ \text{affine}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad T_X(\bar x)=T_X^{\mathrm{lin}}(\bar x)\quad(\bar x\in X).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The feasible set \(X\) itself is a convex polyhedron, being an intersection of finitely many affine halfspaces, affine hyperplanes, and \(X_0\).
special_cases_latex: Linear programs and linearly constrained quadratic programs belong to this class.
If \(X_0=\mathbb R^n\), only the active affine inequalities and affine equalities appear in the tangent-cone formula.
immediate_consequences_latex: The polar of the tangent cone admits the standard multiplier representation, so affine-polyhedral KKT conditions do not require a nonlinear constraint qualification.
boundary_notes: A smooth nonlinear constraint is not affine-polyhedral merely because its first-order approximation is affine.
Redundant affine constraints may cause multiplier nonuniqueness even though tangent-cone exactness holds.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Regularity Does Not Imply LICQ or MFCQ
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine structure preserves ranks and dependencies, but redundant representations can still violate LICQ and MFCQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Constant affine gradients make CRCQ and CPLD automatic, but do not make LICQ or MFCQ automatic for every affine representation. The active system x\le0,\ 2x\le0 at \bar x=0 fails LICQ because its active gradients are dependent. A duplicated affine equality has dependent equality gradients and therefore fails both LICQ and MFCQ, although all ranks and dependence relations remain constant.
assumptions_latex: \text{Constraints are represented by finitely many affine functions.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Automatic CRCQ/CPLD does not imply automatic LICQ/MFCQ.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between automatic persistence qualifications and representation-dependent independence qualifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Constraint Regularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because affine constraint gradients are constant, all selected ranks and dependence relations persist automatically, including under redundant representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every constraint is affine: \(h_j(x)=a_j^{\mathsf T}x-b_j\) and \(g_i(x)=c_i^{\mathsf T}x-d_i\). Their gradients are the constant vectors \(a_j\) and \(c_i\). Consequently, for every feasible \(\bar x\) and every choice of equality and active-inequality indices, the rank and every linear-dependence relation of the selected gradients are independent of \(x\). Thus the constant-rank and constant-positive-linear-dependence requirements hold automatically at \(\bar x\), even when the affine representation contains redundant constraints.
assumptions_latex: All equality and inequality constraints are affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) satisfies CRCQ and CPLD.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Automatic rank-persistence properties of affine equality and inequality systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Dependence of Polyhedral Multipliers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedral tangent and normal cones are intrinsic, while redundant representations can produce nonunique multiplier coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cones T_P(\bar x) and N_P(\bar x) depend only on P, but coefficients (\lambda,\mu) representing a normal as A^{\mathsf T}\lambda+C_I^{\mathsf T}\mu need not be unique when the active affine normals are linearly dependent. Exact polyhedral cone formulas therefore do not imply unique multipliers.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ has a possibly redundant affine representation.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Exact cone formulas do not imply uniqueness of multiplier coefficients.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes intrinsic cones from nonunique coefficients in redundant affine descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Hoffman Error Bound for a Polyhedral System
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to a nonempty polyhedron is globally bounded by a constant times its affine constraint violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Cx\le d\} be nonempty. For fixed finite-dimensional norms there exists H<\infty, depending on A,C and those norms, such that for every x, \operatorname{dist}(x,P)\le H\bigl(\|Ax-b\|+\|(Cx-d)_+\|\bigr).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(x,P)\le H\bigl(\|Ax-b\|+\|(Cx-d)_+\|\bigr)\quad\forall x.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global metric regularity of a fixed feasible affine equality-inequality system.

notation.meaning: Hoffman constant for the represented system and selected norms.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Constraint Regularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedron, the tangent cone is its active linearization and the normal cone is generated by equality normals and nonnegative active inequality normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Cx\le d\}\), and let \(I(\bar x)=\{i:C_i\bar x=d_i\}\) for \(\bar x\in P\). Then the tangent and normal cones are exactly \[T_P(\bar x)=\{v:Av=0,\ C_i v\le0\ \text{for all }i\in I(\bar x)\},\] \[N_P(\bar x)=\{A^{\mathsf T}\lambda+C_{I(\bar x)}^{\mathsf T}\mu:\lambda\in\mathbb R^p,\ \mu\ge0\}.\] Hence the linearized cone equals the tangent cone at every feasible point, without any linear-independence or strict-feasibility assumption on the displayed representation.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is represented by finitely many affine equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_P(\bar x)\) and \(N_P(\bar x)\) have the displayed polyhedral representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Polyhedral Qualification Is Not Automatic LICQ or MFCQ
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedral optimality survives redundancy even when representation-dependent LICQ or MFCQ fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Automatic KKT, Abadie, and Guignard conclusions for a polyhedron do not imply that every affine description satisfies LICQ or MFCQ. Redundant active inequalities can violate LICQ, and dependent equality rows violate both LICQ and MFCQ, while the polyhedral tangent-normal formulas and KKT multiplier existence remain valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Abadie and Guignard Qualifications for Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible point of a polyhedron automatically satisfies Abadie and Guignard qualifications for its affine representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Cx\le d\} and \bar x\in P. For this affine representation, T_P(\bar x)=L_P(\bar x), so Abadie's constraint qualification holds. Consequently T_P(\bar x)^\circ=L_P(\bar x)^\circ, and Guignard's constraint qualification also holds. No independence, irredundancy, or strict-feasibility assumption is required.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is represented by finitely many affine equalities and inequalities.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_P(\bar x)=L_P(\bar x),\qquad T_P(\bar x)^\circ=L_P(\bar x)^\circ.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint qualifications following automatically from polyhedral tangent geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Qualification Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every differentiable local minimum over a polyhedron has KKT multipliers, even for a redundant affine representation, without an extra nonlinear constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Cx\le d\}\), let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable at \(\bar x\in P\), and suppose \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(P\). Then there exist \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb R^m_+\) such that \[\nabla f(\bar x)+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda+C^{\mathsf T}\mu=0,\qquad \mu_i(C_i\bar x-d_i)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] No independent nonlinear constraint qualification is required: the conclusion follows from the exact normal-cone representation of the polyhedron, and it remains valid for redundant affine descriptions.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty polyhedron given by finitely many affine constraints.
\(f\) is differentiable at the local minimizer \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) admits multipliers satisfying stationarity, dual feasibility, and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order optimality over a polyhedron without a separately imposed constraint qualification.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix a class \(\mathcal P\) of finite-dimensional differentiable constrained problems and a feasible-point pair \((P,\bar x)\). Let \(Q(P,\bar x)\) denote a constraint-qualification predicate and let \(C(P,\bar x)\) denote a consequence predicate such as tangent-cone exactness, existence of KKT multipliers, boundedness of the multiplier set, or uniqueness of the multiplier.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal organizational definition for comparing qualifications by the consequences they guarantee; it is not itself a named classical constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a constraint qualification \(Q\), define its guaranteed-consequence set by
\[
\operatorname{Con}(Q)=\{C:\ \forall(P,\bar x)\in\mathcal P,\ Q(P,\bar x)\Rightarrow C(P,\bar x)\}.
\]
The constraint-qualification consequence hierarchy is the preorder \(Q_1\preceq_{\mathrm{con}}Q_2\) defined by
\[
Q_1\preceq_{\mathrm{con}}Q_2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Con}(Q_1)\subseteq\operatorname{Con}(Q_2).
\]
Two qualifications are consequence-equivalent when their guaranteed-consequence sets coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The consequence hierarchy assigns each constraint qualification \(Q\) the set \(\operatorname{Con}(Q)\) of properties that \(Q\) guarantees uniformly over a fixed problem class. Qualification \(Q_2\) is at least as strong in consequence as \(Q_1\) when every consequence guaranteed by \(Q_1\) is also guaranteed by \(Q_2\). Equality of consequence sets defines consequence-equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q_1\preceq_{\mathrm{con}}Q_2\iff\operatorname{Con}(Q_1)\subseteq\operatorname{Con}(Q_2).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The relation \(\preceq_{\mathrm{con}}\) is reflexive and transitive; quotienting by equality of consequence sets yields a partial order.
special_cases_latex: A useful consequence chain is tangent-cone exactness \(\Rightarrow\) KKT multiplier existence at local minimizers; boundedness and uniqueness require additional hypotheses and are separate consequence predicates.
immediate_consequences_latex: Qualifications with the same logical implication strength can still be separated if the problem class or the selected family of consequences changes.
boundary_notes: This formal hierarchy should not be read as asserting any particular implication among LICQ, MFCQ, CRCQ, CPLD, Abadie, or Guignard qualifications.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A curved duplicate constraint gives MFCQ without CRCQ, while opposing affine inequalities give CRCQ without MFCQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Neither MFCQ nor CRCQ implies the other. At \((0,0)\), the inequalities \(g_1(x)=x_1\le0\) and \(g_2(x)=x_1+x_2^2\le0\) satisfy MFCQ with \(d=(-1,0)\), while CRCQ fails because the rank of \(\{
abla g_1,
abla g_2\}\) is one at \((0,0)\) and two at nearby points with \(x_2
e0\). At \(x=0\), the affine inequalities \(x\le0\) and \(-x\le0\) satisfy CRCQ, while MFCQ fails because no direction strictly decreases both active inequalities.
assumptions_latex: All displayed inequalities use the nonpositive convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{MFCQ}\not\Rightarrow\mathrm{CRCQ}\) and \(\mathrm{CRCQ}\not\Rightarrow\mathrm{MFCQ}\).
