knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Active Representation of the Critical Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active inequalities with positive KKT multipliers define equality faces of the critical cone; zero-multiplier active inequalities retain one-sided restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(( ar\lambda, ar\mu)\) be a KKT multiplier at \( ar x\), and define \(I^+( ar\lambda):=\{i\in I( ar x): ar\lambda_i>0\}\). Then \[C( ar x)=\{d:
abla h_j( ar x)^Td=0\  orall j,\ 
abla g_i( ar x)^Td=0\  orall i\in I^+( ar\lambda),\ 
abla g_i( ar x)^Td\leq0\  orall i\in I( ar x)\setminus I^+( ar\lambda)\}.\]
assumptions_latex: \((\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) satisfies KKT conditions under the convention \(g_i\leq0\), \(\bar\lambda_i\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(\bar x)\) has equality restrictions on \(I^+(\bar\lambda)\) and inequality restrictions on the remaining active indices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-cone restrictions separated by positive and zero active multipliers.

notation.meaning: active inequalities with positive KKT multipliers

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Cone Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The critical cone consists of linearized feasible directions that do not increase the objective to first order. At a KKT point their objective derivative is zero, and the cone can be partitioned according to which active inequalities have zero directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) over \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m;\ h_j(x)=0,\ j=1,\ldots,p\}\), and let \(\bar x\in F\) and \(I(\bar x):=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\). Define the linearized cone
\[L_F(\bar x):=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:\nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td\leq0\ \text{for all }i\in I(\bar x),\ \nabla h_j(\bar x)^Td=0\ \text{for }j=1,\ldots,p\}.\]
The critical cone is
\[C(\bar x):=\{d\in L_F(\bar x):\nabla f(\bar x)^Td\leq0\}.\]
If a KKT multiplier exists at \(\bar x\), stationarity implies
\[C(\bar x)=\{d\in L_F(\bar x):\nabla f(\bar x)^Td=0\}.\]
For \(J\subseteq I(\bar x)\), define
\[C_J(\bar x):=\{d\in C(\bar x):\nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td=0\iff i\in J\}.\]
The nonempty sets among \(\{C_J(\bar x):J\subseteq I(\bar x)\}\) partition \(C(\bar x)\) by first-order active-index pattern.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\) are differentiable at the feasible point \(\bar x\).
For the equality characterization, a KKT multiplier exists at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At a KKT point, \(C(\bar x)=L_F(\bar x)\cap\{d:\nabla f(\bar x)^Td=0\}\), and the nonempty sets \(C_J(\bar x)\) partition \(C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearized critical cones for smooth nonlinear programs, partitioned by first-order active-index patterns.

notation.meaning: indices of inequalities active at the reference point
critical-cone vectors having first-order active-index pattern J

knowledge_statements.title: Spurious Linearized Critical Directions Without Abadie Regularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate constraint can make every vector linearly critical even though the feasible set has no nonzero tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R:x^2\leq0\}=\{0\}\), \(\bar x=0\), and \(f\equiv0\). Then \(T_F(0)=\{0\}\), while the linearized cone is \(L_F(0)=\mathbb R\) because \(g'(0)=0\). Hence the geometric critical-direction set contains only zero, whereas the linearized critical cone is \(C(0)=\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F(0)\cap\nabla f(0)^\perp=\{0\}\subsetneq\mathbb R=C(0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of the geometric direction–cone correspondence.

knowledge_statements.title: Critical Direction–Cone Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Abadie regularity and KKT stationarity, geometric critical directions are exactly the nonzero vectors of the linearized critical cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar x\) be feasible and suppose Abadie's constraint qualification holds, namely \(T_F(\bar x)=L_F(\bar x)\). Then the set of critical feasible directions, including the zero direction, satisfies
\[\{d\in T_F(\bar x):\nabla f(\bar x)^Td=0\}=L_F(\bar x)\cap\nabla f(\bar x)^\perp.\]
If KKT stationarity holds, the right-hand side is exactly the critical cone \(C(\bar x)\). Consequently, nonzero critical directions are precisely the nonzero elements of \(C(\bar x)\); without tangent-linearization equality, the linearized cone can contain spurious critical vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\) are differentiable at the feasible point \(\bar x\).
KKT stationarity holds for the final identification with \(C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{d\neq0:d\in T_F(\bar x),\ \nabla f(\bar x)^Td=0\}=C(\bar x)\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality between geometric critical directions and the linearized critical cone under Abadie regularity.

notation.meaning: vectors orthogonal to the objective gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Strictness Without Second-Order Regularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate quadratic inequality admits every formal curvature correction although only the zero correction is realizable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R:x^2\leq0\}=\{0\}\), \(\bar x=0\), and \(d=0\). The formal curvature inequality is \(g'(0)w+d^2g''(0)=0\leq0\), so \(\mathcal W(0;0)=\mathbb R\), whereas \(T_F^2(0;0)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F^2(0;0)=\{0\}\subsetneq\mathbb R=\mathcal W(0;0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the formal constraint-curvature system to characterize realizable corrections.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Constraint-Curvature Formula for Affine Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For affine constraints, the second-order tangent set is exactly the zero-curvature constraint system without a regularity assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose every \(g_i\) and \(h_j\) is affine. For any \( ar x\in F\) and \(d\in T_F( ar x)\), \[T_F^2( ar x;d)=\{w:
abla h_j^Tw=0\  orall j,\ 
abla g_i^Tw\leq0\  orall i\in I( ar x)	ext{ with }
abla g_i^Td=0\}.\] No constraint qualification is required.
assumptions_latex: All equality and inequality constraints are affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F^2(\bar x;d)=\mathcal W(\bar x;d)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconditional exactness when all constraint curvature vanishes.

knowledge_statements.title: Universal Constraint-Curvature Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every realizable second-order correction satisfies the curvature equations and inequalities of constraints remaining active to first order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{x:g_i(x)\leq0,\ h_j(x)=0\}\), with all constraints twice continuously differentiable near \( ar x\in F\). If \(d\in T_F( ar x)\) and \(w\in T_F^2( ar x;d)\), then \[
abla h_j( ar x)^Tw+d^T
abla^2h_j( ar x)d=0\quad orall j,\] and \[
abla g_i( ar x)^Tw+d^T
abla^2g_i( ar x)d\leq0\quad orall i\in I( ar x)	ext{ such that }
abla g_i( ar x)^Td=0.\] Thus \(T_F^2( ar x;d)\subseteq\mathcal W( ar x;d)\), where \(\mathcal W\) denotes the displayed curvature system.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i,h_j\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F^2(\bar x;d)\subseteq\mathcal W(\bar x;d)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary second-order constraint equations requiring no constraint qualification.

notation.meaning: solutions of the directional second-order constraint system

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Curvature Exactness under MFCQ
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under MFCQ, the formal second-order equality and directionally active inequality curvature system exactly describes the realizable parabolic corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{x:g_i(x)\leq0,\ h_j(x)=0\}\), where all constraints are twice continuously differentiable near \( ar x\in F\). Suppose MFCQ holds at \( ar x\): the equality gradients are linearly independent and there exists \(z\) such that \(
abla h_j( ar x)^Tz=0\) for every \(j\) and \(
abla g_i( ar x)^Tz<0\) for every \(i\in I( ar x)\). For \(d\in T_F( ar x)\), let \(I_0( ar x,d)=\{i\in I( ar x):
abla g_i( ar x)^Td=0\}\). Then
\[T_F^2( ar x;d)=\left\{w: egin{array}{ll}
abla h_j( ar x)^Tw+d^T
abla^2h_j( ar x)d=0& orall j,\
abla g_i( ar x)^Tw+d^T
abla^2g_i( ar x)d\leq0& orall i\in I_0( ar x,d)\end{array}ight\}.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F^2(\bar x;d)=\mathcal W(\bar x;d)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact parabolic second-order tangent characterization for a smooth mixed constraint system under MFCQ.

notation.meaning: active inequalities with zero first-order change along d
parabolic second-order tangent set in direction d
directional constraint-curvature system displayed in the statement

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Curvature Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order linearized feasible corrections indexed by first-order feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be twice continuously differentiable near a point \(\bar x\) in
\[
\Omega:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}.
\]
Define \(I(\bar x):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\). Let \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(Dh(\bar x)d=0\) and \(\nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td\le0\) for every \(i\in I(\bar x)\), and set
\[
I_0(\bar x,d):=\{i\in I(\bar x):\nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td=0\}.
\]
The constraint-curvature correction set is
\[
\Gamma(\bar x;d):=\left\{w\in\mathbb R^n:\begin{array}{l}
\nabla h_j(\bar x)^Tw+d^T\nabla^2h_j(\bar x)d=0\quad\text{for every }j\in\{1,\ldots,p\},\\
\nabla g_i(\bar x)^Tw+d^T\nabla^2g_i(\bar x)d\le0\quad\text{for every }i\in I_0(\bar x,d)
\end{array}\right\}.
\]
The sets \(\Gamma(\bar x;d)\), indexed by linearized feasible directions \(d\), form the second-order linearized constraint-curvature family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each linearized feasible direction in a finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear program, the constraint gradients and Hessians define the allowable second-order correction vectors; only inequalities remaining active to first order constrain the correction.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in\Omega\).
\(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies the linearized equality constraints and all active linearized inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Gamma(\bar x;d)\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the second-order linearized feasible-correction set associated with \(d\).

notation.meaning: Indices of inequalities active at the reference point.
Active inequalities having zero first directional derivative along d.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Family of second-order necessary curvature conditions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a local minimizer of a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, let \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) be its KKT multiplier set, let \(C(\bar x)\) be the critical cone, and let \(H(\bar x,y)=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming; the family distinguishes a single-multiplier condition from a direction-dependent multiplier condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The second-order necessary-condition family comprises the following quantified curvature predicates:
\[
\mathrm{FSONC}(\bar x;y):\quad d^TH(\bar x,y)d\geq0
\quad\forall d\in C(\bar x),
\]
for a fixed \(y\in\Lambda(\bar x)\), and
\[
\mathrm{DSONC}(\bar x):\quad
\forall d\in C(\bar x),\quad
\max_{y\in\Lambda(\bar x)}d^TH(\bar x,y)d\geq0.
\]
Equivalently, DSONC says that for each critical direction \(d\), at least one multiplier \(y_d\in\Lambda(\bar x)\), possibly depending on \(d\), satisfies
\[
d^TH(\bar x,y_d)d\geq0.
\]
Under LICQ the multiplier set is a singleton, so the fixed and directional forms coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family consists of nonnegative Lagrangian-curvature tests on critical directions. In the fixed-multiplier form, one KKT multiplier must work for every critical direction. In the directional form, each critical direction may select its own multiplier from the multiplier set. With a unique multiplier, the two quantifier patterns become identical.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Second-order necessity is represented either by \(\exists y\in\Lambda(\bar x)\ \forall d\in C(\bar x)\) nonnegative curvature, or by \(\forall d\in C(\bar x)\ \exists y_d\in\Lambda(\bar x)\) nonnegative curvature, according to the applicable regularity regime.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) is compact, the directional condition can be written with \(\max_{y\in\Lambda(\bar x)}\).
If \(\Lambda(\bar x)=\{\bar y\}\), then DSONC and \(\mathrm{FSONC}(\bar x;\bar y)\) coincide.
special_cases_latex: Under LICQ, the classical necessary condition is \(d^TH(\bar x,\bar y)d\geq0\) for all \(d\in C(\bar x)\), where \(\bar y\) is the unique KKT multiplier.
immediate_consequences_latex: A fixed multiplier satisfying FSONC automatically supplies a valid directional multiplier for every critical direction.
Failure of DSONC produces a critical direction having negative Lagrangian curvature for every admissible multiplier.
boundary_notes: The validity of a particular member of the family depends on its stated constraint qualification.
The directional condition does not assert that one common multiplier works for all directions.

notation.meaning: Set of KKT multipliers at the reference point.
Fixed-multiplier and directional-multiplier second-order necessary conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Multiplier Necessary Conditions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimizer satisfying LICQ, the unique KKT multiplier gives nonnegative Lagrangian curvature in every critical-cone direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program with inequalities \(g_i(x)\leq0\) and equalities \(h_j(x)=0\). Let \(\bar x\) be a local minimizer satisfying LICQ, and let \((\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) be its unique KKT multiplier. With
\[L(x,\lambda,\mu):=f(x)+\sum_i\lambda_i g_i(x)+\sum_j\mu_jh_j(x),\]
one has
\[d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d\geq0\qquad\text{for every }d\in C(\bar x).\]
Thus one fixed multiplier certifies nonnegative Lagrangian curvature simultaneously over the entire critical cone.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d\geq0\) for all \(d\in C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical second-order necessity with the unique multiplier supplied by LICQ.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a KKT point of a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, fix \(\bar y\in\Lambda(\bar x)\), set \(H_{\bar y}=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)\), and let \(C(\bar x,\bar y)\) be the associated critical cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical smooth NLP second-order necessity with a single multiplier fixed before all critical directions are tested.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The fixed-multiplier second-order necessary condition at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is
\[
d^TH_{\bar y}d\geq0
\qquad\forall d\in C(\bar x,\bar y).
\]
Thus the quantifiers are
\[
\exists\,\bar y\in\Lambda(\bar x)\quad
\forall d\in C(\bar x,\bar y):
\quad d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)d\geq0.
\]
In the classical LICQ regime, \(\Lambda(\bar x)=\{\bar y\}\), and every local minimizer satisfies this condition for its unique multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-multiplier necessary condition chooses one KKT multiplier and requires the Hessian of that same Lagrangian to have nonnegative curvature along every associated critical direction. The multiplier cannot be changed after the direction is selected. Under LICQ, the multiplier is unique and this is the classical second-order necessary condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)d\geq0\) for every \(d\in C(\bar x,\bar y)\), with one fixed \(\bar y\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The restriction of \(H_{\bar y}\) to \(C(\bar x,\bar y)\) is positive semidefinite in the quadratic-form sense.
If \(C(\bar x,\bar y)=\operatorname{range}Z\) is a subspace, the condition is equivalent to \(Z^TH_{\bar y}Z\succeq0\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints with full-row-rank Jacobian \(A\), the cone is \(\ker A\), so necessity is \(d^TH_{\bar y}d\geq0\) for all \(d\in\ker A\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A direction \(d\in C(\bar x,\bar y)\) with \(d^TH_{\bar y}d<0\) certifies failure of the fixed-multiplier condition.
When the multiplier is unique, no distinction remains between fixed and directional multiplier selection.
boundary_notes: Without a constraint qualification guaranteeing the relevant multiplier statement, local minimality need not imply this fixed-multiplier form.
Semidefiniteness is required only on the critical cone, not on all of \(\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Lagrangian Hessian evaluated at the fixed multiplier.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional-Multiplier Necessary Conditions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under MFCQ, every critical direction admits some KKT multiplier with nonnegative Lagrangian curvature, although the multiplier may vary by direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar x\) be a local minimizer of a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, suppose MFCQ holds at \(\bar x\), and let \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) be the nonempty compact set of KKT multipliers. Then for every \(d\in C(\bar x)\),
\[\max_{(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda(\bar x)}d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\lambda,\mu)d\geq0.\]
Equivalently, for each critical direction \(d\), there exists a possibly direction-dependent multiplier \((\lambda_d,\mu_d)\in\Lambda(\bar x)\) for which the displayed quadratic form is nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\) are twice continuously differentiable near the local minimizer \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall d\in C(\bar x)\ \exists(\lambda_d,\mu_d)\in\Lambda(\bar x):d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\lambda_d,\mu_d)d\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order necessity allowing the KKT multiplier to depend on the critical direction.

notation.meaning: set of KKT multipliers at the reference point

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a local minimizer of a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, let \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) be its multiplier set, and let \(C(\bar x)\) be the set of first-order critical directions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonlinear programming under a regularity condition that yields a nonempty compact multiplier set; the multiplier may depend on the tested direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The directional-multiplier second-order necessary condition is
\[
\forall d\in C(\bar x),\qquad
\max_{y\in\Lambda(\bar x)}
 d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,y)d\geq0.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\forall d\in C(\bar x)\quad\exists y_d\in\Lambda(\bar x)
\quad d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,y_d)d\geq0.
\]
The choice \(y_d\) is permitted to vary with \(d\); no single multiplier is asserted to satisfy the inequality simultaneously for all critical directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every critical direction, directional-multiplier necessity requires at least one KKT multiplier giving nonnegative Lagrangian curvature in that direction. When the multiplier set is compact, this is expressed by maximizing the directional quadratic form over all multipliers. Unlike the fixed-multiplier condition, different directions may use different maximizing multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each \(d\in C(\bar x)\), there exists \(y_d\in\Lambda(\bar x)\) such that \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,y_d)d\geq0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) is compact, \(\exists y_d\) is equivalent to \(\max_{y\in\Lambda(\bar x)}d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,y)d\geq0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\Lambda(\bar x)=\{\bar y\}\), the condition reduces to \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)d\geq0\) for all critical \(d\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The condition fails exactly when some critical direction has strictly negative Lagrangian curvature for every multiplier in \(\Lambda(\bar x)\).
Any multiplier that works uniformly for all critical directions establishes this directional condition.
boundary_notes: The order \(\forall d\,\exists y_d\) must not be interchanged with \(\exists y\,\forall d\).
Compactness or attainment is needed to use a maximum rather than a supremum.

notation.meaning: A KKT multiplier selected for the critical direction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quantifier-based strength regimes for second-order necessity
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At a KKT point \(\bar x\), let \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) be the multiplier set, \(C(\bar x)\) the critical cone, and \(q_y(d)=d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,y)d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A comparison of second-order necessary conditions by multiplier quantifier order, not by changing the underlying nonlinear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the fixed regime by
\[
\mathrm{F}:\quad \exists y\in\Lambda(\bar x)\ \forall d\in C(\bar x),
\quad q_y(d)\geq0,
\]
and the directional regime by
\[
\mathrm{D}:\quad \forall d\in C(\bar x)\ \exists y_d\in\Lambda(\bar x),
\quad q_{y_d}(d)\geq0.
\]
The fixed regime is at least as strong as the directional regime:
\[
\mathrm{F}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{D}.
\]
If \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) is a singleton, the regimes coincide. With nonunique multipliers, D permits different curvature-supporting multipliers in different directions and therefore need not supply a common multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Necessary-condition strength is organized by the order of the direction and multiplier quantifiers. The fixed regime requires one multiplier to yield nonnegative curvature in all critical directions. The directional regime permits a multiplier chosen separately for each direction. Fixed implies directional, and uniqueness of the multiplier collapses the distinction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\exists y\,\forall d:q_y(d)\geq0)\Rightarrow(\forall d\,\exists y_d:q_{y_d}(d)\geq0)\), with equivalence when \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) is a singleton.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under compactness, regime D is \(\min_{d\in C(\bar x)\cap\mathbb S^{n-1}}\max_{y\in\Lambda(\bar x)}q_y(d)\geq0\).
Regime F is \(\max_{y\in\Lambda(\bar x)}\min_{d\in C(\bar x)\cap\mathbb S^{n-1}}q_y(d)\geq0\).
special_cases_latex: LICQ gives a unique multiplier and hence \(\mathrm{F}\iff\mathrm{D}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A common fixed multiplier is a reusable certificate across all critical directions.
Directional necessity alone cannot identify a single projected Hessian that must be positive semidefinite on the whole critical cone.
boundary_notes: The max-min formulas require nonempty compact indexing sets and omit the vacuous case \(C(\bar x)=\{0\}\).
No converse \(\mathrm{D}\Rightarrow\mathrm{F}\) is part of the definition without additional structure.

notation.meaning: Directional quadratic form of the Lagrangian Hessian for multiplier \(y\).

source_refs.locator: Theorem 12.5, equation (12.57), Section 12.5, pp. 330-332
Theorem 3.46, equation (3.74), Section 3.7.2, pp. 145-147

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Necessary-Condition Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the weak regime, each critical direction may use a different KKT multiplier to obtain nonnegative curvature. The equivalent unit-direction min-max formula applies when the critical cone contains a nonzero direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) be a feasible KKT point, let \(C(\bar x)\) be its critical cone, and let \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) be its nonempty compact KKT multiplier set. The weak second-order necessary-condition regime is the predicate
\[\forall d\in C(\bar x)\quad\exists(\lambda_d,\mu_d)\in\Lambda(\bar x)\quad d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\lambda_d,\mu_d)d\geq0.\]
If \(C(\bar x)\setminus\{0\}\neq\varnothing\), this is equivalently
\[\min_{d\in C(\bar x)\cap\mathbb S^{n-1}}\ \max_{(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda(\bar x)}d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\lambda,\mu)d\geq0.\]
The multiplier selection may vary across critical directions. If \(C(\bar x)=\{0\}\), the quantified predicate holds trivially, while the normalized min-max expression is omitted because its direction set is empty.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) is a feasible KKT point.
The Lagrangian is twice differentiable with respect to \(x\) at \(\bar x\).
For the normalized min-max characterization, \(C(\bar x)\setminus\{0\}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall d\in C(\bar x)\ \exists(\lambda_d,\mu_d)\in\Lambda(\bar x)\) such that \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\lambda_d,\mu_d)d\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier pattern for direction-dependent second-order necessary conditions.

notation.meaning: critical cone at the KKT point
Euclidean unit sphere in n-dimensional space

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Max-Min Form of the Strong Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strong regime is equivalent to a nonnegative max-min curvature value; the zero critical cone is handled directly by the quantified condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(D:=C(\bar x)\cap\mathbb S^{n-1}\neq\varnothing\), \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) is nonempty and compact, and \(q(d,\eta)=d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\eta)d\) is continuous. Then the strong regime is equivalent to \[\max_{\eta\in\Lambda(\bar x)}\min_{d\in D}q(d,\eta)\geq0.\] If \(C(\bar x)=\{0\}\), the original quantified condition holds vacuously and the normalized expression is omitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\eta\in\Lambda(\bar x)\ \forall d\in C(\bar x):q(d,\eta)\geq0\iff\max_{\eta\in\Lambda(\bar x)}\min_{d\in D}q(d,\eta)\geq0.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent scalar formulation of fixed-multiplier nonnegative curvature on the critical cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Necessary-Condition Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strong regime requires one KKT multiplier whose Lagrangian Hessian is nonnegative along every critical direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a feasible KKT point \(\bar x\), critical cone \(C(\bar x)\), and multiplier set \(\Lambda(\bar x)\), the strong second-order necessary-condition regime is the predicate
\[\exists(\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\in\Lambda(\bar x)\quad\forall d\in C(\bar x)\quad d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d\geq0.\]
Equivalently, a single KKT multiplier makes the Lagrangian Hessian copositive on the entire critical cone. This condition is automatic from the fixed-multiplier necessary theorem when LICQ supplies a unique multiplier.
assumptions_latex: The Lagrangian is twice differentiable with respect to \(x\) at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists(\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\in\Lambda(\bar x)\ \forall d\in C(\bar x):d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier pattern requiring one multiplier to work over the whole critical cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth NLP with Directionwise but No Common Curvature Multiplier
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This smooth three-constraint problem has a curvature-valid multiplier for every critical direction, but no single multiplier works for every direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), let \(\phi_k=2\pi k/3\) for \(k=0,1,2\), and define
\[H_k=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\phi_k&\sin\phi_k\\\sin\phi_k&-\cos\phi_k\end{bmatrix}-\varepsilon I_2.\]
For variables \((x,y)\in\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R\), consider \(f(x,y)=-y\) subject to
\[g_k(x,y)=y+\tfrac12x^TH_kx\leq0,\qquad k=0,1,2.\]
The origin is a strict local minimizer: every feasible point satisfies
\[-y\geq\tfrac12\max_k x^TH_kx\geq\tfrac12(1/2-\varepsilon)\|x\|^2,\]
and a feasible point with \(x=0\) has \(-y\geq0\), with objective value zero only at the origin. The KKT multiplier set at the origin is \(\Lambda=\{\lambda\geq0:\sum_k\lambda_k=1\}\), and its critical directions are \((d,0)\). For every nonzero \(d\), some vertex multiplier \(e_k\) satisfies \(d^TH_kd>0\). Conversely, for every fixed \(\lambda\in\Lambda\),
\[\operatorname{tr}\!\left(\sum_k\lambda_kH_k\right)=-2\varepsilon<0,\]
so \(\sum_k\lambda_kH_k\) is not positive semidefinite and fails on some critical direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\( orall d\in C\setminus\{0\}\ \exists\lambda_d\in\Lambda:\ d^T
abla_{xx}^2L(0,\lambda_d)d>0\), but \(
exists\lambda\in\Lambda\  orall d\in C:\ d^T
abla_{xx}^2L(0,\lambda)d\geq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Minimax Characterization of the Regime Gap
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The max-min curvature value does not exceed the min-max value; their signs characterize the strong and weak regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(D:=C(\bar x)\cap\mathbb S^{n-1}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) is nonempty and compact. For \(q(d,\eta):=d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\eta)d\), define \[\alpha:=\max_{\eta\in\Lambda(\bar x)}\min_{d\in D}q(d,\eta),\qquad \beta:=\min_{d\in D}\max_{\eta\in\Lambda(\bar x)}q(d,\eta).\] Then \(\alpha\leq\beta\). The fixed-multiplier regime is equivalent to \(\alpha\geq0\), and the directional-multiplier regime is equivalent to \(\beta\geq0\). Thus \(\alpha<0\leq\beta\) exactly separates the two regimes.
assumptions_latex: The directional curvature is continuous on \(D\times\Lambda(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha\leq\beta\), with the strong regime equivalent to \(\alpha\geq0\) and the weak regime equivalent to \(\beta\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar characterization of the boundary between fixed- and directional-multiplier curvature regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Necessary-Condition Regime Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed multiplier always yields directionwise multipliers; the reverse can fail when acceptable multiplier choices vary and have no common intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q(d,\lambda,\mu):=d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\lambda,
\mu)d\), the fixed-multiplier condition
\[\exists(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda(\bar x)\quad\forall d\in C(\bar x):q(d,\lambda,\mu)\geq0\]
implies the directional-multiplier condition
\[\forall d\in C(\bar x)\quad\exists(\lambda_d,\mu_d)\in\Lambda(\bar x):q(d,\lambda_d,\mu_d)\geq0.\]
The converse is not a logical consequence when \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) is non-singleton: directionwise acceptable multiplier subsets may have empty intersection. If \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) is a singleton, the two regimes coincide.
assumptions_latex: The Lagrangian Hessian exists at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\exists\lambda\,\forall d)\Rightarrow(\forall d\,\exists\lambda_d)\), with equivalence when \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary created by exchanging the multiplier and direction quantifiers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Family of second-order sufficient curvature conditions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((\bar x,y)\) satisfy the KKT conditions of a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, let \(H_y=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,y)\), and let \(C(\bar x,y)\) be the critical cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth NLP sufficiency; the family distinguishes positivity on the critical cone, positivity on multiplier-selected planes, and strong active-manifold positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The second-order sufficient-condition family consists of positive-curvature predicates of the forms
\[
\mathrm{CSOSC}(y):\quad d^TH_yd>0
\quad\forall d\in C(\bar x,y)\setminus\{0\},
\]
\[
\mathrm{SSOSC}(y):\quad d^TH_yd>0
\quad\forall d\in D(y)\setminus\{0\},
\]
where \(D(y)\) imposes equality to zero for equality constraints and for active inequalities selected by positive multipliers, and the strong form
\[
y_i>0\ \forall i\in I(\bar x),\qquad
 d^TH_yd>0\quad\forall d\in\ker A(\bar x)\setminus\{0\},
\]
where \(A(\bar x)\) is the full active-constraint Jacobian. Each predicate includes existence of the stated KKT multiplier. The critical-cone form implies strict local minimality and quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sufficient-condition family requires strict positive Lagrangian curvature on a set of directions left unresolved by first-order conditions. The standard member tests the critical cone. Semi-strong and strong members test multiplier-selected or full active-manifold tangent spaces, with the strong form also requiring positive multipliers for all active inequalities. These forms differ in the direction set and multiplier requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A KKT pair satisfying strict positive Lagrangian curvature on its prescribed nonzero direction set meets the corresponding member of the second-order sufficient-condition family.
equivalent_formulations_latex: On any closed cone \(K\), strict positivity of \(d^TH_yd\) for all \(d\in K\setminus\{0\}\) is equivalent to \(d^TH_yd\geq\sigma\|d\|^2\) on \(K\) for some \(\sigma>0\).
special_cases_latex: Under strict complementarity, the critical cone is the null space of the active Jacobian, so critical-cone and active-manifold curvature tests coincide.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every critical-cone SOSC point is a strict local minimizer.
Uniform positive curvature on the relevant cone yields a local quadratic-growth bound.
boundary_notes: Terminology for semi-strong and strong SOSC varies across sources; the defining direction set and multiplier requirements must be stated explicitly.
Positive definiteness of the full Hessian on \(\mathbb R^n\) is sufficient but generally stronger than required.

notation.meaning: Multiplier-selected tangent plane used by a semi-strong condition.
Jacobian whose rows are all active constraint gradients.

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Cone Sufficiency
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive Lagrangian curvature on every nonzero critical-cone direction implies strict local optimality and a local quadratic-growth bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar x\) be feasible for a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, and suppose \((\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) satisfies the KKT conditions at \(\bar x\). If
\[d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d>0\qquad\text{for every }d\in C(\bar x)\setminus\{0\},\]
then \(\bar x\) is a strict local minimizer with quadratic growth: there exist \(c>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that
\[f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+c\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2\]
for every feasible \(x\) satisfying \(\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<\varepsilon\).
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
\(\bar x\) is feasible and admits the KKT multiplier \((\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\).
The Lagrangian Hessian is positive on \(C(\bar x)\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists c,\varepsilon>0\ \forall x\in F\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar x):f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+c\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical KKT second-order sufficient condition for quadratic growth.

notation.meaning: critical cone at the KKT point
open Euclidean ball of radius epsilon

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be feasible for a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, and suppose \(\bar y\) is a multiplier satisfying the KKT conditions. Let \(C(\bar x,\bar y)\) be the critical cone and \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local sufficiency at a smooth KKT point; no global convexity is assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The critical-cone second-order sufficient condition holds at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) when
\[
d^THd>0
\qquad\forall d\in C(\bar x,\bar y)\setminus\{0\}.
\]
Equivalently, there exists \(\sigma>0\) such that
\[
d^THd\geq\sigma\|d\|^2
\qquad\forall d\in C(\bar x,\bar y).
\]
The condition, together with the KKT system, is a sufficient local optimality certificate: it entails a neighborhood radius \(\delta>0\) and \(\alpha>0\) for which
\[
f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+\alpha\|x-\bar x\|^2
\qquad\forall x\in\Omega\cap B_\delta(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Critical-cone sufficiency requires the Lagrangian Hessian at one KKT pair to have strictly positive curvature along every nonzero critical direction. In finite dimensions this is equivalent to a uniform positive curvature bound on the cone. The condition yields quadratic growth on nearby feasible points and therefore makes the reference point a strict local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict positivity of \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)d\) on \(C(\bar x,\bar y)\setminus\{0\}\) implies quadratic growth and strict local minimality.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\inf\{d^THd:d\in C(\bar x,\bar y),\ \|d\|=1\}>0\).
There exists \(\sigma>0\) with \(d^THd\geq\sigma\|d\|^2\) for all \(d\in C(\bar x,\bar y)\).
special_cases_latex: If strict complementarity holds, the cone is an active-manifold tangent subspace and the condition becomes positive definiteness of the reduced Hessian.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(\bar x\) is an isolated strict local minimizer relative to \(\Omega\).
No nonzero critical direction has zero or negative Lagrangian curvature.
boundary_notes: The condition is local and does not imply global optimality for a nonconvex problem.
A strict local minimizer may fail this condition when growth is flatter than quadratic.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Second-Order Sufficiency
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive Lagrangian curvature on the full linearized cone is a strong sufficient condition for strict local optimality and quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar x\) be feasible for a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, and let \((\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) satisfy the KKT conditions. Assume there exists \(\alpha>0\) such that
\[d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d\geq\alpha\lVert d\rVert^2\qquad\text{for every }d\in L_F(\bar x).\]
Because \(C(\bar x)\subseteq L_F(\bar x)\), the critical-cone sufficient condition holds uniformly. Hence \(\bar x\) is a strict local minimizer with quadratic growth: for some \(c,\varepsilon>0\), \(f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+c\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2\) for every feasible \(x\in B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\) are twice continuously differentiable near the feasible point \(\bar x\).
The displayed uniform curvature bound holds on \(L_F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) satisfies local quadratic growth and is therefore a strict local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform positive curvature on the full linearized feasible cone.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be feasible for a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program and let \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) be the set of multipliers satisfying the KKT system at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth NLP with potentially nonunique multipliers; one multiplier is selected and used consistently in both the cone and Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Multiplier-dependent sufficiency holds at \(\bar x\) if there exists \(\bar y\in\Lambda(\bar x)\) such that
\[
d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)d>0
\qquad\forall d\in C(\bar x,\bar y)\setminus\{0\}.
\]
Both objects in the test depend on the same selected multiplier: \(\bar y\) determines the Lagrangian Hessian and, through its positive and zero inequality components, the displayed multiplier representation of the critical cone. The condition is existential in the multiplier and universal in its nonzero critical directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplier-dependent sufficiency means that at least one KKT multiplier makes the associated Lagrangian Hessian strictly positive on every nonzero direction in the associated critical cone. The same multiplier must be used to form both the Hessian and the cone. Once such a multiplier exists, the point satisfies the standard second-order sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\bar y\in\Lambda(\bar x)\ \forall d\in C(\bar x,\bar y)\setminus\{0\}:d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)d>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: There exist \(\bar y\in\Lambda(\bar x)\) and \(\sigma>0\) such that \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)d\geq\sigma\|d\|^2\) for all \(d\in C(\bar x,\bar y)\).
special_cases_latex: If the multiplier is unique, multiplier-dependent sufficiency reduces to the ordinary critical-cone SOSC at that unique KKT pair.
immediate_consequences_latex: Existence of the selected multiplier implies quadratic growth and strict local minimality.
Only one successful multiplier is required; other multipliers may fail the same curvature test.
boundary_notes: Selecting a different multiplier for each direction is not this condition.
A multiplier and a cone generated from different multipliers must not be mixed in the test.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((\bar x,\bar y)\) be a KKT pair, let \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)\), and suppose the relevant critical directions form a linear subspace \(S=\ker A\). Let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) have full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}Z=S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth NLP in a regime where the critical cone reduces to a subspace, such as strict complementarity with a regular active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The reduced second-order representation associated with \((A,H)\) is
\[
H_R:=Z^THZ\in\mathbb R^{r\times r},
\qquad d=Zu\in S.
\]
It represents constrained curvature because
\[
d^THd=u^TH_Ru
\qquad\forall u\in\mathbb R^r.
\]
Consequently,
\[
d^THd\geq0\ \forall d\in S
\iff H_R\succeq0,
\]
and
\[
d^THd>0\ \forall d\in S\setminus\{0\}
\iff H_R\succ0.
\]
A change of null-space basis \(\widetilde Z=ZM\), with \(M\) nonsingular, produces \(\widetilde H_R=M^TH_RM\), so definiteness is basis independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced second-order representation restricts the Lagrangian Hessian to the null space of the active-constraint Jacobian. A basis \(Z\) converts every admissible direction to coordinates \(u\), and the full quadratic form becomes the reduced quadratic form with matrix \(Z^THZ\). Positive semidefiniteness or definiteness of constrained curvature is exactly the corresponding property of this smaller matrix and does not depend on the chosen basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constrained quadratic form on \(S=\operatorname{range}Z\) is represented exactly by \(H_R=Z^THZ\), preserving positive semidefiniteness and positive definiteness.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(H|_S\succeq0\iff Z^THZ\succeq0\).
\(H|_S\succ0\iff Z^THZ\succ0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(Z\) has orthonormal columns, \(ZZ^T\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(S\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Only an \(r\times r\) matrix must be tested when the tangent subspace has dimension \(r\).
The inertia of the reduced quadratic form is invariant under any nonsingular change of null-space coordinates.
boundary_notes: For a genuinely nonpolyhedral critical cone, a single subspace basis may enlarge the direction set and yield a stronger test.
The reduced matrix is not generally the same as a principal submatrix of the full Hessian.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent-Normal Block Form of a Projected Hessian
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In orthogonal tangent-normal coordinates, the projected Hessian consists of the reduced tangent Hessian and a zero normal block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\), and let \(Z\) and \(Y\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker A\) and \(\operatorname{range}A^T\), respectively. For \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(U=[Z\;Y]\), \[U^T(PHP)U=\begin{bmatrix}Z^THZ&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}.\] Consequently, the restriction of \(PHP\) to the tangent space is represented by \(Z^THZ\), while \(\operatorname{range}A^T\subseteq\ker(PHP)\).
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U^TPHPU=\operatorname{diag}(Z^THZ,0)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Projected Lagrangian Hessian
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pseudoinverse formula produces the tangent projector without a row-rank assumption and preserves the Hessian quadratic form on tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For arbitrary \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), let \(A^\dagger\) be its Moore--Penrose inverse and define \(P:=I-A^\dagger A\). Then \(P=P^T=P^2\), \(\operatorname{range}P=\ker A\), and, for every \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), \[d^TPHPd=d^THd\qquad(d\in\ker A).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=I-A^\dagger A\) projects orthogonally onto \(\ker A\), and \(d^TPHPd=d^THd\) on \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal tangent projection when the active-constraint Jacobian has dependent rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Lagrangian Hessians
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sandwiching the Lagrangian Hessian by the tangent-space projector preserves its quadratic form on every linearized feasible direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\), and let the full-row-rank matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) contain the gradients of equality constraints and the active constraints treated as equalities. The orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\) is \[P=I-A^\top(AA^\top)^{-1}A.\] The projected Lagrangian Hessian is \(H_P=PHP\). For every tangent direction \(d\in\ker A\), \(Pd=d\) and hence \[d^\top H_Pd=d^\top Hd.\] Thus positivity of Lagrangian curvature on the tangent space is equivalent to positivity of \(H_P\) restricted to \(\operatorname{range}P\).
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^\top PHPd=d^\top Hd\) for every \(d\in\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal projection of Lagrangian curvature onto the linearized active tangent space.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)\), let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the relevant tangent subspace, and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided projection of smooth Lagrangian curvature onto a linear tangent or critical subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The coordinate projected Lagrangian Hessian is
\[
H_{\mathrm{proj}}:=Z^THZ.
\]
The corresponding ambient-space projected operator is
\[
P_SH P_S=ZZ^THZZ^T,
\qquad P_S:=ZZ^T.
\]
For every \(d\in S\), writing \(d=Zu\),
\[
d^THd=u^TH_{\mathrm{proj}}u.
\]
Thus the second-order necessary and sufficient curvature tests on \(S\) are, respectively,
\[
H_{\mathrm{proj}}\succeq0
\quad\text{and}\quad
H_{\mathrm{proj}}\succ0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected Lagrangian Hessian is the two-sided restriction of the full Lagrangian Hessian to a tangent subspace. With an orthonormal basis \(Z\), its coordinate matrix is \(Z^THZ\), while the equivalent ambient operator is \(P_SHP_S\). Its quadratic form agrees exactly with the full Hessian on tangent directions, so its definiteness encodes the corresponding constrained second-order test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_{\mathrm{proj}}=Z^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)Z\) exactly represents Lagrangian curvature on \(S\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The nonzero restricted action of \(P_SHP_S\) on \(S\) has coordinate matrix \(Z^THZ\).
\(H_{\mathrm{proj}}\succ0\iff d^THd>0\) for every \(0\neq d\in S\).
special_cases_latex: When \(S=\mathbb R^n\), one may take \(Z=I\), so \(H_{\mathrm{proj}}=H\).
When \(S=\{0\}\), the projected matrix has dimension \(0\times0\) and the strict curvature test is vacuous.
immediate_consequences_latex: Negative eigenvalues of \(H_{\mathrm{proj}}\) identify negative-curvature tangent directions.
The projected test removes curvature components normal to the feasible manifold.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of tangent curvature from the artificial normal-space kernel introduced by projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\), let the columns of \(Z\) and \(Y\) be orthonormal bases of \(\ker A\) and \(\operatorname{range}A^T\), respectively, and let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\). Then, with \(U=[Z\;Y]\), \[U^T(PHP)U=\begin{bmatrix}Z^THZ&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}.\] Hence the nonzero tangent block of \(PHP\) is \(Z^THZ\), while every normal vector lies in \(\ker(PHP)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In tangent-normal coordinates, a projected Hessian is the reduced Hessian plus a zero normal block.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U^TPHPU=\operatorname{diag}(Z^THZ,0)\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) be an active-constraint Jacobian of rank \(m\), let \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)\), and put \(r=n-m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebra representation of equality-constrained or active-manifold second-order curvature under full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A null-space–reduced-Hessian representation pair is a pair \((Z,H_R)\) satisfying
\[
Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r},\qquad AZ=0,
\qquad\operatorname{rank}Z=r,
\qquad H_R=Z^THZ.
\]
The columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\), so every tangent direction has the unique coordinate form \(d=Zu\), and
\[
d^THd=u^TH_Ru.
\]
If \(\widetilde Z=ZM\) for a nonsingular \(M\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\), then the paired reduced Hessian is
\[
\widetilde H_R=M^TH_RM.
\]
Hence the pair is basis-dependent as a matrix representation but basis-invariant as a quadratic form on \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The representation pair consists of a full-rank basis \(Z\) for the null space of the active Jacobian and the reduced Hessian \(H_R=Z^THZ\) expressed in those coordinates. Every tangent direction is represented uniquely by a reduced vector, and its full Lagrangian curvature equals the reduced quadratic form. Changing the null-space basis changes the matrix by congruence but preserves the represented curvature and definiteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((Z,H_R)\) represents \(H\) on \(\ker A\) exactly through \(d=Zu\) and \(d^THd=u^TH_Ru\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(H_R\succeq0\iff d^THd\geq0\) for all \(d\in\ker A\).
\(H_R\succ0\iff d^THd>0\) for all \(0\neq d\in\ker A\).
special_cases_latex: A QR factorization \(A^T=[Q_1\ Q_2]\begin{bmatrix}R\\0\end{bmatrix}\) permits the orthonormal choice \(Z=Q_2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced Hessian has dimension \((n-m)\times(n-m)\).
Eigenvalue or Cholesky tests on \(H_R\) certify curvature on the active tangent space.
boundary_notes: If \(A\) is rank deficient, \(r=n-\operatorname{rank}A\) and a rank-revealing factorization is required.
The null-space representation treats the selected active constraints as equalities and therefore matches a cone test only when the relevant cone is that subspace.

notation.meaning: Null-space basis matrix paired with the reduced Hessian.
Dimension of the null space under the full-row-rank assumption.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-rank null-space basis gives unique coordinates for every direction satisfying the linearized active constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(m<n\), and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(AZ=0\). Then \(\operatorname{range}Z=\ker A\), and every solution of the linearized feasibility equation \(Ad=0\) has a unique representation \[d=Zp,\qquad p\in\mathbb R^{n-m}.\] If the columns of \(Z\) are orthonormal, then \(Z^\top Z=I\), the tangent-space projector is \(ZZ^\top\), and the coordinates satisfy \(p=Z^\top d\).
assumptions_latex: \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) has full column rank and satisfies \(AZ=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker A=\{Zp:p\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\}\), with unique \(p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate representation of linearized feasible directions by a null-space basis.

notation.meaning: basis matrix for the null space of the active Jacobian

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced Hessian is the matrix of the Lagrangian quadratic form in null-space coordinates and exactly preserves tangent-space definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). The reduced Hessian associated with \(Z\) is \[R=Z^\top HZ.\] Under the unique null-space representation \(d=Zp\), the tangent quadratic form satisfies \[d^\top Hd=p^\top Rp.\] Consequently, \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\setminus\{0\}\) if and only if \(R\) is positive definite on \(\mathbb R^{n-m}\setminus\{0\}\).
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^\top Hd=p^\top Z^\top HZp\) whenever \(d=Zp\), and tangent positivity is equivalent to \(Z^\top HZ\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction of Lagrangian curvature to null-space coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Invariance Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing a null-space basis transforms the reduced Hessian by congruence, so its inertia, nonsingularity, and definiteness remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_1,Z_2\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) be full-column-rank matrices with \(\operatorname{range}Z_1=\operatorname{range}Z_2=\ker A\). There is a unique nonsingular matrix \(T\in\mathbb R^{(n-m)\times(n-m)}\) such that \(Z_2=Z_1T\). For any symmetric \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), the associated reduced Hessians obey \[R_2=Z_2^\top HZ_2=T^\top R_1T,\qquad R_1=Z_1^\top HZ_1.\] Hence Sylvester's law of inertia gives \(\operatorname{inertia}(R_2)=\operatorname{inertia}(R_1)\); in particular, nonsingularity and positive definiteness are independent of the selected null-space basis.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_1\) and \(Z_2\) are bases of the same null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_2=T^\top R_1T\) for some nonsingular \(T\), so \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) have identical inertia.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Congruence invariance of reduced curvature under changes of null-space basis.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(m\le n\), and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(AZ=0\). Define the symmetric bordered KKT matrix \(K(H,A)=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\). For a symmetric matrix \(M\), write \(\operatorname{In}(M)=(n_+(M),n_-(M),n_0(M))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained quadratic and local smooth-NLP models with a full-row-rank active-constraint Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The bordered-KKT inertia certificate system associated with \((H,A)\) is the pair consisting of \(K(H,A)\) and its inertia test. It certifies positive definiteness of the quadratic form on feasible tangent directions precisely through \[d^THd>0\quad\text{for every }d\ne0\text{ with }Ad=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{In}(K(H,A))=(n,m,0).\] More generally, \[\operatorname{In}(K(H,A))=\operatorname{In}(Z^THZ)+(m,m,0).\] Thus the certificate records simultaneously the number of positive, negative, and zero reduced-curvature directions without explicitly requiring a particular null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a symmetric Hessian matrix and a full-row-rank active-constraint Jacobian, form the symmetric bordered KKT matrix. Its inertia equals the inertia of the reduced Hessian plus one positive and one negative eigenvalue for each independent constraint. Consequently, the reduced Hessian is positive definite exactly when the bordered matrix has \(n\) positive, \(m\) negative, and no zero eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{In}(K(H,A))=\operatorname{In}(Z^THZ)+(m,m,0),\qquad Z^THZ\succ0\iff\operatorname{In}(K(H,A))=(n,m,0).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The certificate condition is equivalent to \(d^THd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker A\).
Under the certificate, \(K(H,A)\) is nonsingular and the associated equality-constrained KKT linear system has a unique primal-dual solution.
special_cases_latex: If \(m=0\), then \(K(H,A)=H\), and the certificate reduces to \(H\succ0\).
If \(n=m\), then \(\ker A=\{0\}\) and \(\operatorname{In}(K)=(n,n,0)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any symmetric-indefinite factorization that reveals \(\operatorname{In}(K)=(n,m,0)\) supplies a basis-independent reduced-curvature certificate.
A zero eigenvalue of \(K\) invalidates the strict positive-definiteness certificate.
boundary_notes: Full row rank is essential for the stated inertia shift; redundant active constraints require rank reduction or a different certificate.
The certificate concerns curvature on \(\ker A\), not positive definiteness of \(H\) on all of \(\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix
basis matrix for the null space of the constraint Jacobian

knowledge_statements.title: Bordered KKT Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bordered KKT matrix combines the symmetric Hessian and active-constraint Jacobian into a linear system for primal and multiplier corrections, with explicitly dimensioned dual and feasibility residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and define the bordered KKT matrix \[K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^\top\\A&0\end{pmatrix}.\] For a dual residual \(r_d\in\mathbb R^n\) and a primal feasibility residual \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\), the Newton or equality-constrained quadratic-programming equations for a primal correction \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) and multiplier correction \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) have the representation \[K\begin{pmatrix}d\\y\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}r_d\\r_p\end{pmatrix}.\] This system is equivalent to \(Hd+A^\top y=-r_d\) and \(Ad=-r_p\). Its quadratic form satisfies \[(d,y)^\top K(d,y)=d^\top Hd+2y^\top Ad,\] displaying curvature and linearized feasibility in one symmetric system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bordered system is equivalent to \(Hd+A^\top y=-r_d\) and \(Ad=-r_p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric saddle-point representation of equality-constrained second-order systems.

notation.meaning: dual or stationarity residual in R^n

knowledge_statements.title: Inertia-Test Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bordered KKT matrix has the reduced Hessian's inertia plus exactly m positive and m negative eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(Z\) be any basis matrix for \(\ker A\), and set \(R=Z^\top HZ\) and \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^\top\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\). With inertia ordered as numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues, \[\operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(R)+(m,m,0).\] Therefore \(R\succ0\) is certified by \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)\). Likewise, the zero count of \(K\) equals that of \(R\), so an inertia-revealing factorization tests both reduced positive definiteness and degeneracy without explicitly constructing \(Z\).
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
The columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\succ0\) if and only if \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inertia certificate relating a bordered KKT matrix to its reduced Hessian.

notation.meaning: positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts of a symmetric matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Border Forces Singularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent constraint rows make the bordered KKT matrix singular through a purely dual null vector, regardless of the Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^\top\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\). If \(\operatorname{rank}A<m\), then some \(y\ne0\) satisfies \(A^\top y=0\), and \[K\begin{pmatrix}0\\y\end{pmatrix}=0.\] Hence \(K\) is singular independently of \(H\). Together with the full-row-rank reduced-Hessian criterion, \(K\) is nonsingular exactly when \(A\) has full row rank and \(Z^\top HZ\) is nonsingular for a basis \(Z\) of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}A<m\Longrightarrow K\text{ is singular}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singularity caused by dependent constraint rows.

notation.meaning: nonzero vector in the null space of A transpose

knowledge_statements.title: Bordered-System Singularity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a full-rank active Jacobian, the bordered KKT system becomes singular exactly when tangent curvature has a null direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and let \(Z\) span \(\ker A\). For \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^\top\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\) and \(R=Z^\top HZ\), the bordered system is singular exactly when the reduced Hessian is singular: \[\det K=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\det R=0.\] Equivalently, singularity occurs precisely when there exists \(d\ne0\) with \(Ad=0\) and \(Hd\in\operatorname{range}(A^\top)\); then some \(y\) satisfies \(Hd+A^\top y=0\), producing a nonzero null vector \((d,y)\) of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is singular if and only if \(Z^\top HZ\) is singular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact degeneracy boundary for full-rank equality-constrained bordered systems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), and let \(\bar x\in\Omega\). For a parametric regime, let \(\Omega(p)\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(f(\cdot,p)\), and a selected solution \(\bar x(p)\) be defined for \(p\) near \(\bar p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local minimization; both single-problem and locally uniform parametric growth are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The point \(\bar x\) has local quadratic growth on \(\Omega\) if there exist \(\alpha>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \[f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|x-\bar x\|^2\qquad\forall x\in\Omega\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar x).\] It has uniform parametric quadratic growth at \(\bar p\) if neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar p\), radii \(\varepsilon>0\), and one modulus \(\alpha>0\) exist such that \[f(x,p)\ge f(\bar x(p),p)+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|x-\bar x(p)\|^2\] for every \(p\in U\) and every \(x\in\Omega(p)\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar x(p))\). These inequalities define isolation regimes because equality in the relevant neighborhood is possible only at the selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic growth means that every nearby feasible point has objective value at least the reference value plus a positive constant times squared distance from the reference minimizer. In the uniform parametric regime, the same positive growth modulus and neighborhood radius work for every nearby parameter.
assumptions_latex: For the uniform regime, \(\bar x(p)\in\Omega(p)\) for every parameter under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists\alpha,\varepsilon>0\ \forall x\in\Omega\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar x):\quad f(x)-f(\bar x)\ge\frac{\alpha}{2}\|x-\bar x\|^2.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The pointwise condition is equivalent to \(\liminf_{x\to\bar x,\,x\in\Omega,\,x\ne\bar x}\frac{2(f(x)-f(\bar x))}{\|x-\bar x\|^2}>0\).
special_cases_latex: For an unconstrained twice continuously differentiable problem, positive definiteness of \(\nabla^2f(\bar x)\) together with \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\) yields this regime.
For a smooth NLP satisfying second-order sufficient conditions, the inequality is restricted to nearby feasible points.
immediate_consequences_latex: Quadratic growth makes \(\bar x\) the unique minimizer within a sufficiently small feasible neighborhood.
Quadratic growth is stronger than strict local minimality; a strict minimizer can fail to have a quadratic modulus.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert global optimality.
Uniform parametric growth is stronger than having a possibly vanishing modulus separately for each parameter.

notation.meaning: open Euclidean ball of radius epsilon about x

knowledge_statements.title: Isolation Does Not Imply Quadratic Growth
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The isolated minimizer of x to the fourth has quartic rather than quadratic growth, so isolation alone does not provide a positive quadratic-growth modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=x^4\) on \(\mathbb R\), \(\bar x=0\) is an isolated strict global minimizer, but there are no \(\alpha>0\) and \(r>0\) such that \[x^4\ge \alpha x^2\qquad\text{for every }|x|<r.\] Thus isolated strict local optimality does not imply quadratic growth.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=x^4\) and the feasible set is \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\) is an isolated strict minimizer at which every positive quadratic-growth modulus fails.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of isolated strict minimality from the stronger isolated quadratic-growth property.

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated Local-Growth Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic growth from one feasible point forces that point to be the unique nearby minimizer and hence locally isolated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set and let \(\bar x\in F\). The isolated quadratic-growth condition at \(\bar x\) is the existence of constants \(\alpha>0\) and \(r>0\) such that \[f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\alpha\|x-\bar x\|^2\qquad\text{for all }x\in F\cap B_r(\bar x).\] This condition implies that \(\bar x\) is the unique minimizer of \(f\) over \(F\cap B_r(\bar x)\), after possibly reducing \(r\), and therefore is an isolated strict local minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The displayed inequality holds for some \(\alpha,r>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is an isolated strict local minimizer of \(f\) on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic objective growth measured from a single feasible minimizer.

notation.meaning: open radius-r ball centered at the candidate point

knowledge_statements.title: Flat-Manifold Quadratic-Growth Example
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared distance from a flat minimizer manifold has exact set-relative quadratic growth but no point-relative quadratic growth at its nonisolated minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(u,v)=\|v\|^2\) on \(\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}\), where \(1\le k<n\), the global minimizer set is \(S=\mathbb R^k\times\{0\}\), and \[f(u,v)=\operatorname{dist}((u,v),S)^2.\] Thus exact quadratic growth holds relative to the nonisolated set \(S\), although no member of \(S\) satisfies positive quadratic growth measured from that member on a neighborhood containing another point of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\text{ and }S\text{ is nonisolated}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Example separating set-relative growth from point-relative isolation.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Relative Quadratic Growth
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonisolated minimizers, growth is measured by squared distance to the whole local minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq F\) be a nonempty localized minimizer set on which \(f=f_*\). Quadratic growth relative to \(S\) holds if a neighborhood \(U\) of \(S\) and \(\alpha>0\) exist such that \[f(x)\ge f_*+\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\qquad(x\in F\cap U).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)-f_*\ge\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\text{ locally on }F.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic objective growth transverse to a localized nonisolated minimizer set.

notation.meaning: common objective value on the set
distance from x to the minimizer set

knowledge_statements.title: Square-Root Objective-Gap Error Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic growth relative to a minimizer set is equivalent to bounding distance to that set by the square root of the objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq F\) be a local minimizer set with common value \(f_*\), and suppose \(f(x)\ge f_*\) locally on \(F\). For fixed \(\alpha>0\), \[f(x)-f_*\ge\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\] holds on that neighborhood if and only if \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\alpha^{-1/2}\sqrt{f(x)-f_*}.\] Thus set-relative quadratic growth is equivalently a local square-root error bound from objective gap to the minimizer set.
assumptions_latex: S\subseteq F\text{ is nonempty and }f=f_*\text{ on }S.
f(x)\ge f_*\text{ on the localized feasible set}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)-f_*\ge\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\iff\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\alpha^{-1/2}\sqrt{f(x)-f_*}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent error-bound form of set-relative quadratic growth.

notation.meaning: common objective value on the minimizer set

knowledge_statements.title: Nonisolated-Minimizer Growth Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic growth measured relative to a local set of minimizers rather than one point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(S\subseteq F\) be a non-singleton set on which \(f\) has the constant value \(v\). The set \(S\) has local quadratic growth if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(S\) and \(\kappa>0\) such that
\[
f(x)\ge v+\kappa\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2
\quad\text{for every }x\in F\cap U.
\]
Thus quadratic growth transverse to \(S\) is compatible with a continuum of local minimizers and does not imply pointwise isolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective grows quadratically with distance from the entire minimizer set, although individual minimizers within that set need not be isolated.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and not a singleton.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is a locally quadratically stable minimizer set, while its individual points may be nonisolated.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from x to the minimizer set S.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(p\in P\subseteq\mathbb R^q\), consider \(P(p):\min_x f(x,p)\) subject to \(g(x,p)\le0\) and \(h(x,p)=0\). Let \(S(p)\) be its local solution set, \(v(p)=\inf P(p)\) its value, and \(K(p)\) its set of KKT triples \((x,\lambda,\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-dimensional perturbation behavior of values, local solutions, multipliers, and active patterns; generalized-equation full stability is not identified with every weaker stability notion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Parametric sensitivity-stability theory assigns to the family \(P(p)\) the set-valued maps \(S\) and \(K\), the extended-real value function \(v\), and the activity map \(\mathcal A(x,p)=\{i:g_i(x,p)=0\}\). At a reference \((\bar p,\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\), stability describes quantified continuity properties such as local single-valuedness and \[\|z(p_1)-z(p_2)\|\le L\|p_1-p_2\|,\qquad z=(x,\lambda,\mu),\] while sensitivity consists of directional, derivative, or subgradient descriptions of \(z(p)\) and \(v(p)\). Activity stability separately records whether \(\mathcal A(x(p),p)\) remains constant. These components are distinct: value stability need not imply a unique primal-dual branch, and primal stability need not imply multiplier uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The theory studies a parameterized nonlinear program through four objects: its optimal value, local solutions, KKT primal-dual solutions, and active constraints. Stability means quantified continuity or local Lipschitz behavior of these objects; sensitivity means their first-order response to parameter changes.
assumptions_latex: The reference problem has a finite local value and a KKT point \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\).
The selected local branch, when used, remains in a prescribed neighborhood of the reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p\longmapsto\big(v(p),S(p),K(p),\mathcal A(\cdot,p)\big)\] is the canonical collection of parametric sensitivity-stability objects.
special_cases_latex: For right-hand-side parameters, the KKT sensitivity system is obtained by differentiating stationarity and the active constraints.
Under active-gradient independence, strict complementarity, and a suitable second-order sufficient condition, the local primal-dual branch is differentiable.
immediate_consequences_latex: A differentiable primal-dual branch is locally Lipschitz.
Activity persistence requires additional sign separation for active multipliers and inactive slacks.
boundary_notes: This definition does not equate continuity, calmness, metric regularity, strong regularity, and differentiability.
Global solution mappings may remain set-valued even when one local branch is stable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal Value Function and Its Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P(p)\) be a parameterized minimization problem with feasible set \(X(p)\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and objective \(f(x,p)\), where \(p\in P\subseteq\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real value functions for finite-dimensional parametric optimization; smooth derivatives and convex subgradients are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The optimal value function is \[v(p):=\inf\{f(x,p):x\in X(p)\},\qquad \inf\varnothing:=+\infty.\] Its directional sensitivity at \(\bar p\) in direction \(d\) is the one-sided limit \[v'(\bar p;d):=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{v(\bar p+td)-v(\bar p)}{t},\] when this limit exists. If one vector \(s\) satisfies \(v'(\bar p;d)=\langle s,d\rangle\) for every direction, then \(v\) is differentiable at \(\bar p\) with gradient \(s\). In the convex regime, sensitivity may instead be set-valued through \[\partial v(\bar p)=\{s:v(p)\ge v(\bar p)+\langle s,p-\bar p\rangle\ \forall p\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The value function maps each parameter to the infimum objective value of its feasible problem, assigning positive infinity when the problem is infeasible. Sensitivity is its directional derivative, gradient when differentiable, or convex subdifferential when nonsmooth and convex.
assumptions_latex: Directional derivatives are considered only along parameter directions for which \(\bar p+td\) remains in the parameter domain for small \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[v(p)=\inf_{x\in X(p)}f(x,p),\qquad v'(\bar p;d)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{v(\bar p+td)-v(\bar p)}{t}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For finite convex \(v\), \(s\in\partial v(\bar p)\) exactly when \(v(p)-v(\bar p)\ge\langle s,p-\bar p\rangle\) for every \(p\).
special_cases_latex: For convex right-hand-side perturbations with strong duality, the subdifferential is the signed set of optimal multipliers.
Under a smooth stable primal-dual branch, the value gradient follows from the parameter derivative of the Lagrangian.
immediate_consequences_latex: A singleton convex subdifferential at an interior point yields differentiability there under the usual finite-dimensional regularity.
Nondifferentiability permits multiple first-order marginal values.
boundary_notes: The infimum need not be attained.
The directional derivative may fail to exist, and its existence does not by itself imply full differentiability.

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of the value function
