knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Right-Hand-Side Envelope Formula
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For constraints written as constraint functions minus their right-hand sides, the local value derivatives equal the negatives of the corresponding KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \[v_{\mathrm{loc}}(b,c)=f(x(b,c))\] for the constraints \(g(x)\le b\) and \(h(x)=c\). Suppose a differentiable local primal-dual KKT branch \((x(b,c),\lambda(b,c),
u(b,c))\) exists near \(( ar b, ar c)\). With \[L(x,\lambda,
u;b,c)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(g(x)-b)+
u^{\mathsf T}(h(x)-c),\] the local value is differentiable and satisfies \[
abla_bv_{\mathrm{loc}}( ar b, ar c)=- ar\lambda,\qquad 
abla_cv_{\mathrm{loc}}( ar b, ar c)=- ar
u.\]
assumptions_latex: A differentiable local primal-dual KKT branch exists near \((\bar b,\bar c)\).
The Lagrangian uses the displayed constraint-minus-right-hand-side convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(
abla_bv_{\mathrm{loc}}=- ar\lambda\) and \(
abla_cv_{\mathrm{loc}}=- ar
u\) at the reference right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-value derivatives for equality and inequality right-hand-side perturbations under an explicit sign convention.

notation.meaning: value along the selected local minimizer branch

knowledge_statements.title: Right-Hand-Side Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order value sensitivity to equality and inequality right-hand sides under a differentiable local KKT solution branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(b\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\), \(d\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\), and
\[
v(b,d)=\min_x\{f(x):c(x)=b,\ g(x)\le d\}.
\]
Use the Lagrangian
\[
L(x,\lambda,\mu;b,d)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(c(x)-b)+\mu^{\mathsf T}(g(x)-d),
\qquad \mu\ge0.
\]
Suppose that near \((\bar b,\bar d)\) the relevant local KKT solution and its multipliers are unique and differentiable, and let \((\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) be the reference multipliers. Then, for every \((\Delta b,\Delta d)\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\times\mathbb R^{m_i}\),
\[
Dv(\bar b,\bar d)[\Delta b,\Delta d]
=-\bar\lambda^{\mathsf T}\Delta b-\bar\mu^{\mathsf T}\Delta d.
\]
Hence \(\nabla_bv(\bar b,\bar d)=-\bar\lambda\) and \(\nabla_dv(\bar b,\bar d)=-\bar\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a differentiable, locally unique KKT solution branch, the negative reference multipliers give the first-order value changes caused by equality and inequality right-hand-side perturbations.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c,g\) are continuously differentiable near the reference solution.
A constraint qualification and second-order regularity yield a locally unique differentiable primal-dual solution branch.
The displayed Lagrangian and inequality sign conventions are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Dv(\bar b,\bar d)[\Delta b,\Delta d]=-\bar\lambda^{\mathsf T}\Delta b-\bar\mu^{\mathsf T}\Delta d\).

notation.meaning: Local optimal-value function for the right-hand sides.
Equality and inequality KKT multipliers at the reference problem.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\le b\) and \(h(x)=c\), with reference data \((b^0,c^0)\), local solution \(x^0\), and multipliers \((\lambda^0,\mu^0)\). Let \(A\) collect gradients of the active inequalities and equalities using the chosen sign convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Twice continuously differentiable finite-dimensional NLPs with a locally persistent active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Right-hand-side sensitivity is the first-order response of a selected local KKT branch \(z(b,c)=(x(b,c),\lambda(b,c),\mu(b,c))\) to perturbations of the constraint levels. When differentiable, its derivative is defined by the linearized active KKT system \[J^0Dz(b^0,c^0)=R,\qquad J^0= egin{bmatrix}
abla_{xx}^2L(x^0,\lambda^0,\mu^0)&A^T\A&0\end{bmatrix},\] where \(R\) inserts the inequality and equality right-hand-side increments in the active feasibility equations. With the convention \(g(x)\le b\), \(h(x)=c\), and \(L=f+\lambda^T(g-b)+\mu^T(h-c)\), value sensitivity satisfies \[
abla_bv(b^0,c^0)=-\lambda^0,\qquad 
abla_cv(b^0,c^0)=-\mu^0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Right-hand-side sensitivity differentiates the local primal solution, multipliers, and optimal value with respect to the levels appearing in inequality and equality constraints. The derivative of the primal-dual point solves the bordered linearized KKT system; with the stated Lagrangian signs, the value derivatives are the negatives of the multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(g_i\), and \(h_j\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^0\).
The gradients of the active constraints are linearly independent at \(x^0\).
Active inequality multipliers are positive and a suitable second-order sufficient condition holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[J^0Dz=R,\qquad \nabla_bv=-\lambda^0,\qquad \nabla_cv=-\mu^0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The columns of \(Dz\) are obtained by solving the same bordered KKT matrix with different right-hand sides.
special_cases_latex: For a single perturbed active inequality, \(dv/db=-\lambda^0\).
Inactive constraints with a positive slack remain inactive under sufficiently small perturbations and have zero local marginal value.
immediate_consequences_latex: Nonsingularity of \(J^0\) makes the local derivative unique.
Multiplier magnitude measures the first-order value change per unit right-hand-side relaxation, subject to the sign convention.
boundary_notes: Changing the inequality or Lagrangian sign convention changes the displayed signs.
At weakly active or degenerate points, the branch or value function may be nondifferentiable.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the active KKT equations at the reference point
right-hand-side injection matrix for active constraint perturbations

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D=(f,g,h)\) denote the data of \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\le0\) and \(h(x)=0\). A perturbation family is a map \(p\mapsto D_p=(f_p,g_p,h_p)\) on a neighborhood of \(0\in\mathbb R^q\), with \(D_0=D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth NLP data perturbations, classified by which components of the optimization model vary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An optimization-data perturbation regime is specified by a parameterized data map \(p\mapsto(f_p,g_p,h_p)\), a topology or norm in which \(D_p\to D_0\), and the induced feasible, value, solution, multiplier, and activity maps. The right-hand-side regime has \(f_p=f_0\), \(g_p(x)=g_0(x)-b(p)\), and \(h_p(x)=h_0(x)-c(p)\). The objective regime varies \(f_p\) while fixing the constraints. The coefficient or functional regime permits derivatives of \(f_p,g_p,h_p\) to vary. A full-data regime permits all components to vary simultaneously. Local \(C^r\) perturbation means that on a fixed neighborhood \(U\), \[\|D_p-D_0\|_{C^r(U)}\to0\quad\text{as }p\to0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A data-perturbation regime records exactly which objective and constraint data vary, how closeness of perturbed models is measured, and which induced optimization maps are studied. Right-hand-side, objective-only, functional-coefficient, and full-data perturbations are distinct regimes.
assumptions_latex: All perturbed functions share a common local decision-space neighborhood.
A specified \(C^r\) norm or another explicit topology is used to compare models.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p\mapsto D_p=(f_p,g_p,h_p),\qquad D_p\to D_0,\] together with the declared varying components, defines the perturbation regime.
special_cases_latex: Additive tilt perturbation: \(f_p(x)=f_0(x)-\langle p,x\rangle\).
Right-hand-side perturbation: \(g_p=g_0-b(p)\) and \(h_p=h_0-c(p)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Sensitivity conclusions are meaningful only relative to the declared data topology.
Stability under right-hand-side perturbations alone does not automatically establish stability under full functional perturbations.
boundary_notes: The supplied sources inspect right-hand-side perturbations but do not provide a single canonical definition covering this entire four-regime taxonomy.
Infinite-dimensional function-space perturbations require an explicitly chosen function-space topology.

notation.meaning: objective and constraint data at parameter p
local norm controlling derivatives through order r

Multiple-Minimizer Nondifferentiability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different parameter slopes at multiple current minimizers can make an objective-only value function nondifferentiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{-1,1\}\) and \(f(x,p)=px\). Then \(v(p)=\min_{x\in F}px=-|p|\). At \(p=0\), both feasible points minimize, their parameter derivatives are \(-1\) and \(1\), and \(v\) is not differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(p)=-|p|\) is directionally differentiable but not differentiable at \(p=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of ordinary differentiability when reference minimizers have different objective-data derivatives.

notation.meaning: minimum value over the fixed feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Danskin Formula for Objective-Only Perturbations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For objective-only perturbations over a fixed compact feasible set, the directional value derivative is the least parameter derivative among current minimizers; uniqueness gives the usual envelope gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact, let \(P\subset\mathbb R^m\) be open, and let \(f:F	imes P	o\mathbb R\) be continuous with continuous parameter gradient \(
abla_pf\) near \(F	imes\{ ar p\}\). Define \(v(p)=\min_{x\in F}f(x,p)\) and \(S( ar p)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x, ar p)\). Then \[v'( ar p;d)=\min_{x\in S( ar p)}
abla_pf(x, ar p)^{\mathsf T}d.\] If \(S( ar p)=\{ ar x\}\), then \(v\) is differentiable at \( ar p\) and \(
abla v( ar p)=
abla_pf( ar x, ar p)\).
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is nonempty, compact, and independent of \(p\).
\(f\) is continuous and has a continuous parameter gradient near the reference parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(v'( ar p;d)=\min_{x\in S( ar p)}
abla_pf(x, ar p)^{\mathsf T}d\), with \(
abla v( ar p)=
abla_pf( ar x, ar p)\) when \(S( ar p)=\{ ar x\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional value sensitivity over a fixed compact feasible set, including nonunique minimizers.

notation.meaning: directional derivative of the minimum-value function

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Data Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Envelope formula when only objective data vary and the feasible set remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be open, let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact, and define
\[
v(p)=\min_{x\in F}f(x,p).
\]
Assume that \(f\) is continuous on \(F\times P\), that \(\nabla_pf\) exists and is continuous near \(F\times\{\bar p\}\), and that the minimizer at \(\bar p\) is unique, denoted by \(\bar x\). Then, for every \(q\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[
Dv(\bar p)[q]=\nabla_pf(\bar x,\bar p)^{\mathsf T}q.
\]
For \(f(x,p)=f_0(x)+p^{\mathsf T}\phi(x)\), this gives \(\nabla v(\bar p)=\phi(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed compact feasible set and a unique reference optimizer, the first-order value change equals the objective's parameter derivative at that optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is open and \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and compact.
\(f\) is continuous on \(F\times P\), and \(\nabla_pf\) is continuous near \(F\times\{\bar p\}\).
The minimizer of \(f(\cdot,\bar p)\) over \(F\) is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Dv(\bar p)[q]=\nabla_pf(\bar x,\bar p)^{\mathsf T}q\) for every \(q\in\mathbb R^m\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector in a linear objective perturbation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Danskin Directional Formula for Objective-Only Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional value sensitivity when objective data vary over a fixed compact feasible set and minimizers need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact, let \(f:F\times P\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and suppose \(D_pf(x,\bar p)d\) exists and depends continuously on \(x\in F\) for every direction \(d\). Define \(v(p)=\min_{x\in F}f(x,p)\) and \(S(\bar p)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x,\bar p)\). Then \[v'(\bar p;d)=\min_{x\in S(\bar p)}D_pf(x,\bar p)d.\] In particular, if \(S(\bar p)=\{\bar x\}\) and \(f\) is differentiable in \(p\), then \(v\) is differentiable at \(\bar p\) with \(\nabla v(\bar p)=\nabla_pf(\bar x,\bar p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For objective-only perturbations over a fixed compact feasible set, the directional value derivative is the minimum parameter derivative among current minimizers; uniqueness yields the usual envelope gradient.
assumptions_latex: For every direction \(d\), \(D_pf(x,\bar p)d\) exists and is continuous in \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v'(\bar p;d)=\min_{x\in S(\bar p)}D_pf(x,\bar p)d\), with \(\nabla v(\bar p)=\nabla_pf(\bar x,\bar p)\) when the minimizer is unique.

notation.meaning: set of minimizers at the reference parameter
directional derivative of the minimum-value function

knowledge_statements.title: Danskin Directional Formula for Objective-Only Perturbations
Constraint-Data Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a differentiable branch of local minimizers and KKT multipliers, the derivative of the branch value caused solely by constraint-data perturbations equals the multiplier-weighted parameter derivative of the constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\), \(g:\mathbb R^n	imes P	o\mathbb R^r\), and \(h:\mathbb R^n	imes P	o\mathbb R^s\) be continuously differentiable near \(( ar x, ar p)\). Consider the constraints \(g(x,p)\leq 0\) and \(h(x,p)=0\). Suppose that, for every \(p\) near \( ar p\), there is a differentiable branch of local minimizers \(x(p)\), with \(x( ar p)= ar x\), and differentiable KKT multiplier branches \(\lambda(p)\in\mathbb R_+^r\) and \(
u(p)\in\mathbb R^s\); assume its active set is locally constant. Define the local value branch by \(v_{\mathrm{loc}}(p)=f(x(p))\) and the Lagrangian by \(L(x,\lambda,
u,p)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x,p)+
u^{\mathsf T}h(x,p)\). Then, for every \(d\in\mathbb R^m\), \[v_{\mathrm{loc}}'( ar p;d)=\lambda( ar p)^{\mathsf T}D_pg( ar x, ar p)d+
u( ar p)^{\mathsf T}D_ph( ar x, ar p)d.\]
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(g:\mathbb R^n\times P\to\mathbb R^r\), and \(h:\mathbb R^n\times P\to\mathbb R^s\) are continuously differentiable near \((\bar x,\bar p)\).
A differentiable local-minimizer branch \(x(p)\) and differentiable KKT multiplier branches \((\lambda(p),\nu(p))\) exist near \(\bar p\).
The active set is locally constant along the branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{loc}}'(\bar p;d)=\lambda(\bar p)^{\mathsf T}D_pg(\bar x,\bar p)d+\nu(\bar p)^{\mathsf T}D_ph(\bar x,\bar p)d\) for every \(d\in\mathbb R^m\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), \(f:\mathbb R^n	imes P	o\mathbb R\), \(g:\mathbb R^n	imes P	o\mathbb R^r\), and \(h:\mathbb R^n	imes P	o\mathbb R^s\) be continuously differentiable near \(( ar x, ar p)\). Suppose that the program with constraints \(g(x,p)\leq0\) and \(h(x,p)=0\) has, near \( ar p\), a differentiable branch of local minimizers and KKT multipliers \((x(p),\lambda(p),
u(p))\), with \(x( ar p)= ar x\), \(\lambda( ar p)= ar\lambda\), and \(
u( ar p)= ar
u\), and suppose its active set is locally constant. Define \(v_{\mathrm{loc}}(p)=f(x(p),p)\) and \(L(x,\lambda,
u,p)=f(x,p)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x,p)+
u^{\mathsf T}h(x,p)\). Then, for every \(d\in\mathbb R^m\), \[v_{\mathrm{loc}}'( ar p;d)=D_pf( ar x, ar p)d+ ar\lambda^{\mathsf T}D_pg( ar x, ar p)d+ ar
u^{\mathsf T}D_ph( ar x, ar p)d=D_pL( ar x, ar\lambda, ar
u, ar p)d.\]

A differentiable local-minimizer and KKT-multiplier branch \((x(p),\lambda(p),\nu(p))\) exists near \(\bar p\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Sensitivity Interpretations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For constraints written as constraint data minus right-hand side, the KKT multipliers are the negatives of the local branch-value derivatives with respect to those right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(b\in\mathbb R^r\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^s\), and consider the constraints \(g(x)\leq b\) and \(h(x)=c\). Suppose that near \(( ar b, ar c)\) there is a differentiable branch of local minimizers and KKT multipliers \((x(b,c),\lambda(b,c),
u(b,c))\), with reference values \(( ar x, ar\lambda, ar
u)\). Define \(v_{\mathrm{loc}}(b,c)=f(x(b,c))\) and \(L(x,\lambda,
u;b,c)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(g(x)-b)+
u^{\mathsf T}(h(x)-c)\). Then \[
abla_bv_{\mathrm{loc}}( ar b, ar c)=- ar\lambda,\qquad 
abla_cv_{\mathrm{loc}}( ar b, ar c)=- ar
u.\] Thus, under this sign convention, each multiplier is the negative marginal value of increasing its corresponding right-hand side along the selected local solution branch.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(g\), and \(h\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
A differentiable branch of local minimizers and KKT multipliers \((x(b,c),\lambda(b,c),\nu(b,c))\) exists near \((\bar b,\bar c)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(
abla_bv_{\mathrm{loc}}( ar b, ar c)=- ar\lambda\) and \(
abla_cv_{\mathrm{loc}}( ar b, ar c)=- ar
u\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(v(b,c)\) be the value of \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\le b\) and \(h(x)=c\), and use \(L(x,\lambda,\mu;b,c)=f(x)+\lambda^T(g(x)-b)+\mu^T(h(x)-c)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth local sensitivity and convex subgradient interpretations under a fixed right-hand-side and Lagrangian sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The multiplier sensitivity interpretation associates each optimal multiplier pair \((\lambda,mu)\) with a marginal value vector for the constraint right-hand sides. In the differentiable regime, \[\nabla_bv(\bar b,bar c)=-\bar\lambda,qquad \nabla_cv(bar b,bar c)=-\barmu.\] In the convex possibly nonsmooth regime, the interpretation is set-valued: the signed optimal-dual solution set equals the convex subdifferential of the value function, \[\partial v(bar b,bar c)=-\{(lambda,mu):(lambda,mu)\text{ is dual optimal at }(bar b,bar c)}.\] Thus a unique multiplier produces a unique marginal value, while multiplier multiplicity produces a family of valid supporting slopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the displayed sign convention, an inequality or equality multiplier is the negative marginal change of the optimal value with respect to its right-hand side. In convex nonsmooth problems, the entire signed optimal-multiplier set is the value function's subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: The primal value at \((\bar b,\bar c)\) is finite.
For the subgradient formula, the problem is convex and the stated dual representation is exact.
For the gradient formula, the local value function is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(-\bar\lambda,-\bar\mu)=\nabla v(\bar b,\bar c)\quad\text{or, in the convex set-valued regime,}\quad \partial v(\bar b,\bar c)=-\Lambda^*(\bar b,\bar c).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A vector \((-\lambda,-\mu)\) is a convex subgradient exactly when it defines a supporting affine lower bound for \(v\) at the reference right-hand side.
special_cases_latex: An inactive inequality has multiplier zero and hence zero first-order marginal value while it remains inactive.
For one active inequality, relaxing its upper bound by \(db>0\) changes the value to first order by \(-\lambda\,db\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Multiplier nonuniqueness is compatible with a nondifferentiable value function.
The minimum-norm multiplier corresponds to the minimum-norm subgradient under the signed identification.
boundary_notes: The sign reverses if constraints or the Lagrangian are written with the opposite convention.
A multiplier is a local marginal quantity, not generally an exact finite-change price.

notation.meaning: set of optimal inequality and equality multipliers

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a parameterized NLP, let \(K(p)\) be the set of KKT triples \(z=(x,\lambda,\mu)\), and fix \((\bar p,\bar z)\) with \(\bar z\in K(\bar p)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local finite-dimensional stability of a selected KKT solution, not global uniqueness of all optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The reference KKT point \(\bar z\) is locally primal-dual stable if there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar p\) and \(V\) of \(\bar z\) such that the localized mapping \[K_V(p):=K(p)\cap V\] is nonempty for every \(p\in U\), remains close to \(\bar z\), and obeys a declared continuity modulus. It is locally single-valued Lipschitz stable if \(K_V(p)=\{z(p)\}\) and \[\|z(p_1)-z(p_2)\|\le L\|p_1-p_2\|\qquad\forall p_1,p_2\in U.\] It is differentiably stable when this selection is differentiable at \(\bar p\). The definition jointly controls primal variables and multipliers; stability of \(x(p)\) alone is only primal stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-dual stability means that nearby parameter values possess nearby KKT points and that the localized KKT mapping has a specified continuity property. The strongest classical smooth regime used here is a unique locally Lipschitz or differentiable branch of both primal variables and multipliers.
assumptions_latex: Localization is performed in a fixed neighborhood \(V\) of the reference primal-dual point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K(p)\cap V=\{z(p)\},\qquad \|z(p_1)-z(p_2)\|\le L\|p_1-p_2\|\] defines local single-valued Lipschitz primal-dual stability.
special_cases_latex: For smooth right-hand-side perturbations under active-gradient independence, strict complementarity, and second-order sufficiency, the branch is differentiable.
If only \(x(p)\) is unique while multipliers are multiple, primal-dual single-valued stability fails.
immediate_consequences_latex: Local Lipschitz stability implies continuity of the selected primal and multiplier components.
Differentiability supplies first-order expansions for both components.
boundary_notes: The definition is local and does not preclude remote KKT points.
Existence stability, set-valued Lipschitz stability, and single-valued Lipschitz stability are distinct.

notation.meaning: KKT solution mapping localized to V

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated Calmness Without a Single-Valued Localization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Isolated calmness permits multiple perturbed branches: x=±p obey the same linear bound and meet at one isolated reference solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(S:\mathbb R\rightrightarrows\mathbb R\) by \(S(0)=\{0\}\) and \(S(p)=\{-p,p\}\) for \(p\ne0\). Its graph is closed, and every \(x\in S(p)\) satisfies \(|x|\le|p|\). Hence \(S\) is isolated calm at \((0,0)\) with modulus one, although every sufficiently small nonzero \(p\) has two localized solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is isolated calm at }(0,0),\qquad |S(p)|=2\text{ for }p\ne0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A multifunction with two nearby perturbed solutions but one isolated reference solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated Calmness of a Localized Solution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reference solution is locally isolated at the reference parameter, and every localized perturbed solution remains linearly close to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) is isolated calm at \((\bar p,\bar x)\in\operatorname{gph}S\) if neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar p\) and \(V\) of \(\bar x\), and \(\kappa\ge0\), exist such that \[S(\bar p)\cap V=\{\bar x\},\qquad S(p)\cap V\subseteq \bar x+\kappa\|p-\bar p\|\mathbb B\quad(p\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is isolated calm at }(\bar p,\bar x)\text{ exactly when the displayed localization and linear bound hold}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical graph-point definition of isolated solution stability.

notation.meaning: closed unit ball in the solution space

knowledge_statements.title: Graphical-Derivative Criterion for Isolated Calmness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally closed finite-dimensional graph, isolated calmness is equivalent to the absence of a nonzero solution tangent at zero parameter velocity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) have locally closed graph at \((\bar p,\bar x)\in\operatorname{gph}S\). Then \(S\) is isolated calm at \((\bar p,\bar x)\) if and only if \[DS(\bar p\mid\bar x)(0)=\{0\}.\]
assumptions_latex: P\text{ and }X\text{ are finite-dimensional normed spaces}.
\operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed at }(\bar p,\bar x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is isolated calm at }(\bar p,\bar x)\iff DS(\bar p\mid\bar x)(0)=\{0\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinitesimal characterization of isolated calmness for a locally closed finite-dimensional solution mapping.

notation.meaning: Graphical derivative of the solution mapping

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated-Solution Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local single-valued Lipschitz stability of a parameterized primal-dual solution branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S:P\rightrightarrows Z\) be a solution mapping, with \(\bar z\in S(\bar p)\). The solution \(\bar z\) is locally isolated and Lipschitz stable if there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar p\) and \(V\) of \(\bar z\), and \(L\ge0\), such that \(S(p)\cap V=\{z(p)\}\) for every \(p\in U\), \(z(\bar p)=\bar z\), and
\[
\lVert z(p)-z(q)\rVert\le L\lVert p-q\rVert
\quad\text{for all }p,q\in U.
\]
For primal-dual stability, \(z\) contains both the primal variable and its multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reference solution is isolated and stable when nearby parameters determine one nearby solution that varies Lipschitz continuously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localization \(p\mapsto S(p)\cap V\) is single-valued and Lipschitz near \(\bar p\).

knowledge_statements.title: Mordukhovich Coderivative Criterion for the Aubin Property
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally closed finite-dimensional solution mapping is Lipschitz-like exactly when its limiting coderivative has no nonzero parameter covector at zero solution covector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) have locally closed graph at \((\bar p,\bar x)\). Then \(S\) has the Aubin property at \((\bar p,\bar x)\) if and only if \[D^*S(\bar p\mid\bar x)(0)=\{0\}.\] Equivalently, \(S^{-1}\) is metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar p)\).
assumptions_latex: P\text{ and }X\text{ are finite-dimensional normed spaces}.
\operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed at }(\bar p,\bar x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ has the Aubin property at }(\bar p,\bar x)\iff D^*S(\bar p\mid\bar x)(0)=\{0\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional infinitesimal test for a Lipschitz-like solution mapping.

knowledge_statements.title: Calmness Need Not Imply Isolation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant non-singleton solution set is calm but not isolated calm at an interior reference solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S(p)=[-1,1]\) for every \(p\in\mathbb R\). At \((0,0)\), \(S\) is calm with modulus zero because \(S(p)\cap V\subseteq S(0)\). It is not isolated calm there, since \(S(0)\cap V\) contains points other than zero for every neighborhood \(V\) of zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is calm at }(0,0)\text{ but not isolated calm there}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of calmness from isolated calmness.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Regularity Need Not Be Strong Metric Regularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two-branch map is metrically regular but lacks the unique inverse branch required for strong metric regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F:\mathbb R\rightrightarrows\mathbb R\) by \(F(x)=\{x,-x\}\). Then \(F^{-1}(y)=\{y,-y\}\). The inverse has the Aubin property at \((0,0)\), so \(F\) is metrically regular there. However, \(F^{-1}(y)\) has two localized values for every sufficiently small nonzero \(y\); hence \(F\) is not strongly metrically regular at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is metrically regular but not strongly metrically regular at }(0,0).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation caused by a multivalued localized inverse.

knowledge_statements.title: Calmness Need Not Imply the Aubin Property
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oscillatory map is linearly bounded relative to the reference parameter and hence calm, but it is not Lipschitz-like between arbitrary nearby parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(S:\mathbb R\rightrightarrows\mathbb R\) by \(S(0)=\{0\}\) and \(S(p)=\{p\sin(1/p)\}\) for \(p\ne0\). Since \(|p\sin(1/p)|\le|p|\), \(S\) is calm at \((0,0)\) with modulus one. Its single-valued representative is differentiable for \(p\ne0\), with derivative \(\sin(1/p)-(1/p)\cos(1/p)\), which is unbounded arbitrarily close to zero. A Lipschitz function has derivative bounded by its Lipschitz constant wherever differentiable, so this localization is not Lipschitz on any neighborhood of zero and \(S\) lacks the Aubin property at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is calm at }(0,0)\text{ but does not have the Aubin property there}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A single-valued continuous map with a linear reference bound but no locally uniform Lipschitz bound.

notation.meaning: single-valued mapping represented as a multifunction

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Metric Regularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric regularity is metric regularity with a locally unique Lipschitz inverse branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set-valued mapping \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\) if neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\) exist such that \(y\mapsto F^{-1}(y)\cap U\) is single-valued on \(V\) and Lipschitz continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U,V:\;F^{-1}(y)\cap U=\{s(y)\}\text{ with }s\text{ Lipschitz on }V.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse formulation of a unique Lipschitz localization.

knowledge_statements.title: Localized Solution-Mapping Regularity Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aubin regularity compares arbitrary nearby parameters, calmness compares only with the reference parameter, and isolated calmness also isolates the reference solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) and \((\bar p,\bar x)\in\operatorname{gph}S\), the Aubin property requires neighborhoods \(U,V\) and \(\kappa\ge0\) such that \[S(p_1)\cap V\subseteq S(p_2)+\kappa\|p_1-p_2\|\mathbb B\quad(p_1,p_2\in U).\] Calmness requires \[S(p)\cap V\subseteq S(\bar p)+\kappa\|p-\bar p\|\mathbb B\quad(p\in U).\] Isolated calmness additionally localizes \(S(\bar p)\) to \(\{\bar x\}\) and replaces the reference set on the right by \(\{\bar x\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Aubin, calmness, and isolated calmness are distinguished by the displayed two-point, reference-point, and isolated-reference bounds}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct graph-point definitions of the Aubin property, calmness, and isolated calmness.

notation.meaning: closed unit ball in the solution space

knowledge_statements.title: Aubin–Metric-Regularity Equivalence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution mapping is locally Lipschitz-like exactly when its inverse satisfies the corresponding local error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) have locally closed graph at \((\bar p,\bar x)\). Then \(S\) has the Aubin property at \((\bar p,\bar x)\) with modulus \(\kappa\) if and only if \(S^{-1}:X\rightrightarrows P\) is metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar p)\); equivalently, for all nearby \((p,x)\), \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S(p))\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(p,S^{-1}(x)).\]
assumptions_latex: S:P\rightrightarrows X\text{ acts between finite-dimensional normed spaces}.
\operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed at }(\bar p,\bar x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ has the Aubin property at }(\bar p,\bar x)\iff S^{-1}\text{ is metrically regular at }(\bar x,\bar p).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct inverse-mapping equivalence between the Aubin property and metric regularity.

notation.meaning: Parameters whose solution set contains x

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Subregularity–Inverse Calmness Equivalence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity is the fixed-reference error bound dual to calmness of the inverse mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). The mapping \(F\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if locally \[\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(\bar y))\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x)).\] This holds if and only if \(F^{-1}\) is calm at \((\bar y,\bar x)\), with the same local modulus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is metrically subregular at }(\bar x,\bar y)\iff F^{-1}\text{ is calm at }(\bar y,\bar x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-reference inverse equivalence corresponding to calmness.

notation.meaning: solution set of the reference inclusion

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Mapping Regularity Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Localized Lipschitz regularity notions for set-valued solution mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) and \((\bar p,\bar x)\in\operatorname{gph}S\), the Aubin property holds if neighborhoods \(U,V\) and \(\kappa\ge0\) satisfy \(S(p_1)\cap V\subseteq S(p_2)+\kappa\lVert p_1-p_2\rVert\mathbb B\) for all \(p_1,p_2\in U\). Calmness replaces \(S(p_2)\) by \(S(\bar p)\) and fixes \(p_2=\bar p\). Isolated calmness additionally requires \(S(\bar p)\cap V=\{\bar x\}\) and replaces \(S(\bar p)\) by \(\{\bar x\}\). A single-valued localization that is Lipschitz implies all three properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aubin regularity compares any two nearby parameter values; calmness compares with the reference value; isolated calmness also isolates the reference solution.
assumptions_latex: \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) is a set-valued mapping between finite-dimensional normed spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A locally Lipschitz single-valued localization of \(S\) has the Aubin, calmness, and isolated-calmness properties.

notation.meaning: closed unit ball in the solution space

knowledge_statements.title: MFCQ Allows Bounded Nonunique Multipliers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant active inequalities can satisfy MFCQ while producing a bounded continuum of KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}-x\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_1(x)=x\le0,\qquad g_2(x)=2x\le0.\] At \(\bar x=0\), MFCQ holds because \(d=-1\) strictly decreases both active constraints. The KKT multiplier set is \[M(\bar x)=\{(\mu_1,\mu_2)\in\mathbb R_+^2:\mu_1+2\mu_2=1\},\] a nontrivial compact line segment. Thus MFCQ ensures boundedness here but not multiplier uniqueness or a single-valued localization.
assumptions_latex: The inequality convention is g_i(x)\le0 with multipliers \mu_i\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{MFCQ}(\bar x)\text{ holds},\qquad M(\bar x)\text{ is bounded and non-singleton}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary of local multiplier boundedness under MFCQ.

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier set at the reference solution

knowledge_statements.title: Pair-Indexed KKT Multiplier Mapping and Calmness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mapping assigns all KKT multipliers to each feasible primal-parameter pair; calmness gives a one-sided local linear bound relative to the reference multiplier set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a smooth parametric NLP, let \[M(p,x):=\{(\lambda,\mu):x\text{ is primal feasible and }(x,\lambda,\mu)\text{ satisfies KKT stationarity, multiplier signs, and complementarity at }p\}.\] At \(((\bar p,\bar x),\bar m)\in\operatorname{gph}M\), the mapping is calm if neighborhoods \(U,V\) and \(\kappa\ge0\) exist such that \[M(p,x)\cap V\subseteq M(\bar p,\bar x)+\kappa\|(p,x)-(\bar p,\bar x)\|\mathbb B\quad((p,x)\in U).\]
assumptions_latex: The derivatives defining the KKT system exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is calm at }((\bar p,\bar x),\bar m)\text{ exactly when the displayed localized bound holds}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier multifunction indexed consistently by the parameter and primal point.

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier set at a primal-parameter pair
combined equality and inequality multiplier vector
closed unit ball in multiplier space

knowledge_statements.title: LICQ Gives a Unique Multiplier at a Fixed KKT Point
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ makes the KKT multiplier unique at a fixed primal KKT point but does not alone establish Lipschitz dependence under perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a smooth NLP at a KKT point \(x\), suppose the equality gradients together with the active-inequality gradients are linearly independent. Then the stationarity equation has at most one multiplier vector supported on the active inequalities. Consequently, whenever a KKT multiplier exists, the multiplier set \(M(x)\) is a singleton.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint gradients exist at \(x\).
LICQ holds for the equality and active-inequality gradients at \(x\).
At least one KKT multiplier exists at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{LICQ}(x)\Rightarrow |M(x)|=1.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise multiplier uniqueness from independence of equality and active-inequality gradients.

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier set at the fixed primal point

knowledge_statements.title: MFCQ Gives Local Boundedness of KKT Multipliers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFCQ prevents nearby KKT multipliers from diverging and makes their cluster points valid reference multipliers, without ensuring uniqueness or Lipschitz dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-dimensional smooth parametric NLP, let \((p_k,x_k)\to(\bar p,\bar x)\) be KKT points with associated multipliers \((\lambda_k,\mu_k)\). If MFCQ holds at \((\bar p,\bar x)\), then nearby multiplier sets are locally bounded. Every cluster point of \((\lambda_k,\mu_k)\) is a KKT multiplier at \((\bar p,\bar x)\). Thus the multiplier mapping is locally bounded and outer semicontinuous there, although it need not be single-valued or Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint gradients are continuous in \((p,x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \limsup_{(p,x)\to(\bar p,\bar x)}M(p,x)\subseteq M(\bar p,\bar x),\quad M\text{ is locally bounded}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer stability of multiplier sets along convergent parametric KKT points.

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier set at a primal-parameter pair
Outer limit of nearby multiplier sets

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Mapping Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Lipschitz stability of KKT multiplier sets along a parameterized primal solution branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x(p)\) be a localized primal solution and let \(M(p)\) denote its set of KKT multiplier vectors. For \(\bar y\in M(\bar p)\), the multiplier mapping is locally stable at \((\bar p,\bar y)\) if there exist neighborhoods \(U,V\) and \(L\ge0\) such that \(M(p)\cap V\ne\varnothing\) and
\[
M(p)\cap V\subseteq M(q)+L\lVert p-q\rVert\mathbb B
\quad\text{for all }p,q\in U.
\]
If every localized set \(M(p)\cap V\) is a singleton, this condition is ordinary Lipschitz continuity of the unique multiplier branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearby problem parameters have nearby KKT multipliers; with local uniqueness, the multiplier vector follows a Lipschitz continuous branch.
assumptions_latex: A localized primal solution branch \(x(p)\) and associated KKT systems are defined near \(\bar p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localized multiplier mapping has the Aubin property; under uniqueness it is single-valued Lipschitz.

notation.meaning: Set of KKT multipliers associated with the localized primal solution.
Closed unit ball in multiplier space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Regularity of the KKT Generalized Equation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Write the KKT system as the generalized equation \(0\in F(z,p)+N_C(z)\), where \(z\in\mathbb R^d\), \(p\in\mathbb R^q\), \(F\) is differentiable in \(z\), \(C\) is a closed convex set encoding sign or complementarity structure, and \(N_C\) is its normal-cone mapping.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional generalized equations and their use as a local interface for NLP KKT stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The generalized equation is strongly regular at \((\bar z,\bar p)\) for \(0\) if \(0\in F(\bar z,\bar p)+N_C(\bar z)\) and there are neighborhoods \(V\) of \(\bar z\), \(W\) of \(0\), and a constant \(L\) such that, for every \(r\in W\), the partially linearized equation \[r\in F(\bar z,\bar p)+D_zF(\bar z,bar p)(z-\bar z)+N_C(z)\] has exactly one solution \(z(r)\in V\), and \[\|z(r_1)-z(r_2)\|\le L\|r_1-r_2\|.\] The Robinson interface consists of representing the NLP KKT conditions in this form so that strong regularity yields a locally unique Lipschitz primal-dual response to small residual or parameter perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong regularity requires the inverse of the linearized generalized equation to be locally single-valued and Lipschitz. The NLP interface is obtained by expressing stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity as one generalized equation in the primal-dual variables.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable with respect to \(z\) at \((\bar z,\bar p)\).
\(C\) is closed and convex, so \(N_C\) is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[r\mapsto\{z\in V:r\in F(\bar z,\bar p)+D_zF(\bar z,\bar p)(z-\bar z)+N_C(z)\}\] is single-valued and Lipschitz near \(r=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Strong regularity is local single-valued Lipschitz invertibility of the partially linearized generalized equation.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, the normal-cone term disappears and strong regularity reduces to nonsingularity of the bordered KKT Jacobian.
For polyhedral \(C\), the linearized system is a piecewise-linear generalized equation.
immediate_consequences_latex: Small residual perturbations admit a unique nearby primal-dual solution.
With suitable parameter smoothness, parameter perturbations inherit a locally Lipschitz KKT selection.
boundary_notes: Metric regularity without single-valued localization is weaker than strong regularity.
The inspected local source states Robinson-type stability and metric regularity but not this exact strong-regularity definition.

notation.meaning: normal cone to C at z
Jacobian of F with respect to the generalized-equation variable

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Regularity of the KKT Generalized Equation
LICQ Alone Does Not Give Strong Stability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quartic stationary problem has vacuous LICQ but only cube-root parameter dependence, showing that curvature nonsingularity is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\;\frac14x^4-px.\] LICQ is vacuous. Stationarity gives \(x^3=p\), hence the unique stationary solution is \(x(p)=\sqrt[3]{p}\). At \((p,x)=(0,0)\), the solution is isolated, but \(|x(p)|=|p|^{1/3}\) admits no local bound \(|x(p)|\le\kappa|p|\). Thus LICQ without nonsingular curvature does not imply strong regularity or Lipschitz solution stability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{LICQ}\not\Rightarrow\text{ strong regularity or local Lipschitz solution stability}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of isolated Lipschitz stability when curvature is singular.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Without LICQ Does Not Stabilize Multipliers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant equalities preserve a unique primal minimizer but create infinitely many multipliers, so curvature alone cannot give primal-dual strong stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\frac12x^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad h_1(x)=x=0,\qquad h_2(x)=2x=0.\] The unique feasible primal solution is \(x=0\) and the objective has positive curvature, but LICQ fails. Stationarity is \(\lambda_1+2\lambda_2=0\), so the multiplier set is a line. Thus positive primal curvature without independent active gradients does not yield a unique localized primal-dual solution or strong regularity of the KKT system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla_{xx}^2L=1>0,\qquad\{\lambda:\lambda_1+2\lambda_2=0\}\text{ is non-singleton}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of primal-dual uniqueness under redundant equality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Fixed-Activity Implicit-Function Package
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ, strict complementarity, and positive reduced curvature yield a unique smooth primal-dual branch with persistent activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a twice continuously differentiable parametric NLP, let \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) be a KKT point. Suppose LICQ holds, every active inequality multiplier is strictly positive, and the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on the null space of the active-constraint Jacobian. Then the fixed-active-set KKT Jacobian is nonsingular. Under sufficiently small smooth perturbations there is a unique nearby primal-dual KKT point with the same active set, depending continuously differentiably on the perturbation.
assumptions_latex: The NLP data are twice continuously differentiable in primal variables and continuously differentiable in parameters.
d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d>0\text{ for all }0\ne d\in\ker A(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a unique }C^1\text{ local KKT branch with constant active set}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth primal-dual stability package under strict complementarity.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of equalities and active inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Strong-Regularity Package
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full equality-constraint rank plus a nonsingular reduced Hessian gives a unique smooth local KKT branch; positive reduced curvature additionally preserves strict local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a twice continuously differentiable equality-constrained NLP, let \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) satisfy KKT, let \(A=\nabla h(\bar x)\) have full row rank, and let \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\). The KKT Jacobian \[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular if and only if \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) is nonsingular for a basis \(Z\) of \(\ker A\). Under this condition, sufficiently small smooth canonical perturbations admit a unique \(C^1\) local primal-dual KKT branch. If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\), its primal points are strict local minimizers.
assumptions_latex: The objective and equality constraints are twice continuously differentiable in x and smoothly parameterized.
A=\nabla h(\bar x)\text{ has full row rank}.
Z\text{ is a basis matrix for }\ker A.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ nonsingular}\iff Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\text{ nonsingular};\qquad K\text{ nonsingular}\Rightarrow\text{a unique local }C^1\text{ KKT branch}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact smooth-equation package for an equality-constrained KKT system.

notation.meaning: null-space basis of the equality Jacobian

knowledge_statements.title: LICQ–Strong-SOSC Package for Robinson Strong Regularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ and positive Lagrangian curvature on the KKT critical cone give Robinson strong regularity and a unique local Lipschitz primal-dual branch, even with zero active multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) be a KKT point of a twice continuously differentiable NLP. Assume LICQ and \[d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d>0\qquad(0\ne d\in C(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)),\] where \(C\) is the KKT critical cone: equality-linearized directions, zero derivative on positive-multiplier active inequalities, nonpositive derivative on zero-multiplier active inequalities, and zero first-order objective change. Then the canonically perturbed KKT generalized equation is strongly regular at the reference primal-dual point. It therefore has a unique localized Lipschitz primal-dual solution mapping. Strict complementarity is not required.
assumptions_latex: The NLP data are twice continuously differentiable.
The displayed strong second-order sufficient condition holds on the multiplier-dependent KKT critical cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The KKT generalized equation is strongly regular at }(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth mixed-constraint KKT strong regularity without strict complementarity.

notation.meaning: KKT critical cone for the reference multiplier

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a twice continuously differentiable NLP at a KKT point \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\). Let \(A\) be the active-constraint Jacobian, \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\), and \(Z\) span \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical smooth NLP package ensuring a differentiable local branch under persistent activity; it is not asserted to be the weakest possible package.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The classical regularity package for strong local primal-dual stability is the conjunction of: \[(i)\ \operatorname{rank}A=\text{number of active constraints},\qquad (ii)\ \bar\lambda_i>0\ \text{for every active inequality},\qquad (iii)\ Z^THZ\succ0.\] These are respectively active-gradient linear independence, strict complementarity, and the strong second-order sufficient condition on the active tangent space. The package makes the active KKT Jacobian \[J=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\] nonsingular, separates active multipliers and inactive slacks from zero, and supports a locally unique differentiable primal-dual branch for sufficiently small right-hand-side perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard smooth package combines independent active gradients, positive multipliers on every active inequality, and positive-definite Lagrangian curvature on the null space of the active Jacobian. It gives a nonsingular active KKT Jacobian and separates the current activity pattern from transition boundaries.
assumptions_latex: All objective and constraint functions are twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{rank}A=m_a,\quad \bar\lambda_{\mathcal A_I}>0,\quad Z^THZ\succ0\] defines the classical smooth strong-stability package.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under full row rank of \(A\), \(Z^THZ\succ0\) is equivalent to \(\operatorname{In}(J)=(n,m_a,0)\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, strict complementarity is vacuous.
For an unconstrained problem, the package reduces to \(\nabla^2f(\bar x)\succ0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The active KKT Jacobian is nonsingular.
Active inequalities and inactive inequalities retain their sign classification under sufficiently small perturbations along the local branch.
boundary_notes: Without strict complementarity, differentiable stability may require a generalized-equation analysis and activity need not persist.
The package is sufficient in the cited smooth regime, not claimed necessary in every NLP class.

notation.meaning: Lagrangian Hessian at the reference KKT point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Activity Persistence Along a Stable KKT Branch
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(z(p)=(x(p),\lambda(p),\mu(p))\) be a locally unique continuous KKT branch near \(\bar p\). For inequalities \(g_i(x,p)\le0\), define \(\mathcal A(p)=\{i:g_i(x(p),p)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional NLPs; persistence is separated from strong regularity alone by explicit slack and multiplier separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The activity-persistence property at \(\bar p\) holds if there is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar p\) such that \[\mathcal A(p)=\mathcal A(\bar p)\qquad\forall p\in U.\] A strong-regularity activity-persistence regime consists of a locally unique continuous primal-dual branch together with strict sign separation at the reference point: \[\lambda_i(\bar p)>0\quad(i\in\mathcal A(\bar p)),\qquad g_i(x(\bar p),\bar p)<0\quad(i\notin\mathcal A(\bar p)).\] Continuity then preserves positivity of active multipliers and negativity of inactive slacks locally, while the KKT complementarity relations preserve equality for the positively multiplied constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activity persists when the same inequality indices remain binding throughout a neighborhood of the reference parameter. A stable continuous KKT branch yields this persistence when active multipliers are strictly positive and inactive constraints have strictly negative slack at the reference point.
assumptions_latex: A locally unique continuous KKT selection \(z(p)\) exists.
Active multipliers and inactive slacks are strictly separated from zero at \(\bar p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists U\ni\bar p\ \forall p\in U:\quad \mathcal A(p)=\mathcal A(\bar p).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The active-set indicator vector is locally constant along the selected KKT branch.
special_cases_latex: The smooth package of active-gradient independence, strict complementarity, and strong second-order sufficiency supplies a differentiable branch with persistent activity.
With equality constraints only, the activity statement is vacuous.
immediate_consequences_latex: The local KKT equations may be written using a fixed active set.
No inequality enters or leaves the active set inside the persistence neighborhood.
boundary_notes: Strong regularity without strict complementarity need not force a constant active set.
Weakly active constraints lie on activity-transition boundaries and are excluded from this persistence regime.

notation.meaning: active inequality set along the selected branch

knowledge_statements.title: LICQ–Strong-Second-Order Characterization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth NLP, LICQ and positive Lagrangian curvature on the strong critical subspace characterize strong regularity of the primal-dual KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a twice continuously differentiable NLP at a KKT pair \(( ar x, ar\lambda, ar
u)\), the primal-dual KKT generalized equation is strongly regular under canonical perturbations if and only if LICQ holds and \[d^{\mathsf T}
abla_{xx}^2L( ar x, ar\lambda, ar
u)d>0\] for every nonzero \(d\) satisfying \(D h( ar x)d=0\) and \(D g_i( ar x)d=0\) for every active inequality with \( ar\lambda_i>0\). Consequently, the localized primal-dual KKT solution mapping is single-valued and Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraints are twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
Strong regularity is taken for the canonical primal-dual KKT generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{strong regularity}\iff\text{LICQ plus the stated strong second-order condition}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical smooth-NLP characterization of strong regularity of the primal-dual KKT generalized equation.

notation.meaning: direction in the strong critical subspace

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Regularity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robinson strong regularity for a parameterized finite-dimensional generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the KKT system be represented by \[0\in F(z,p)+N_K(z),\] where \(K\) is closed and convex and \(F\) is differentiable in \(z\). The system is in a strong-regularity regime at \((\bar z,\bar p)\) if \(0\in F(\bar z,\bar p)+N_K(\bar z)\) and there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar z\) and \(V\) of \(0\) such that, for every \(v\in V\), the partially linearized equation \[v\in F(\bar z,\bar p)+D_zF(\bar z,\bar p)(z-\bar z)+N_K(z)\] has exactly one solution \(z(v)\in U\), and \(v\mapsto z(v)\) is Lipschitz continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong regularity means the localized inverse of the linearized KKT generalized equation is single-valued and Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^q\times\mathbb R^s\to\mathbb R^q\) is differentiable in \(z\) at \((\bar z,\bar p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localized solution mapping \(v\mapsto z(v)\) is single-valued and Lipschitz near \(v=0\).

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to K at z

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical smooth-NLP sufficient regime for strong regularity of the KKT generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program at a KKT pair \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\nu)\). If the gradients of the equality constraints and active inequalities are linearly independent and the strong second-order sufficient condition holds at the KKT pair, then the associated KKT generalized equation is strongly regular there. Consequently, sufficiently small canonical perturbations admit a unique nearby primal-dual KKT solution depending locally Lipschitz continuously on the perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ together with the strong second-order sufficient condition is a classical smooth-NLP regime guaranteeing a unique Lipschitz-localized KKT response.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint functions are twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
The strong second-order sufficient condition holds at \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\nu)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KKT generalized equation is strongly regular at \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\nu)\), and its localized solution mapping is single-valued and Lipschitz.

notation.meaning: linear independence constraint qualification for equality and active-inequality gradients

knowledge_statements.title: LICQ–Strong-Second-Order Sufficient Regime
Strong-Regularity Activity Persistence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz strongly regular KKT system with strict complementarity has a locally constant inequality active set along its unique nearby primal-dual branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a parameterized smooth NLP with inequalities \(g_i(x,p)\le 0\), and let \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\nu)\) be a KKT point at \(\bar p\). Suppose the KKT generalized equation is strongly regular at this point, its parameter dependence is locally Lipschitz, and strict complementarity holds: \(\bar\lambda_i>0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p)\). Then the unique localized KKT branch \((x(p),\lambda(p),\nu(p))\) exists for all nearby \(p\), is continuous, and satisfies \[\mathcal A(x(p),p)=\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p)\] for every sufficiently near parameter. Reference-active multipliers remain positive, while reference-inactive inequalities retain negative slack.
assumptions_latex: The NLP data are continuously differentiable in the primal variables and locally Lipschitz in the parameter.
The KKT generalized equation is strongly regular at \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\nu,\bar p)\).
Strict complementarity holds at the reference KKT point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(x(p),p)=\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p)\) for all sufficiently near \(p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local constancy of the complete inequality active set along the strongly regular KKT branch under strict complementarity.

notation.meaning: indices of inequalities active at the parameterized point

knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Persistence Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence of the complete inequality active set along a continuous strongly regular KKT branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x,p)\) subject to \(h(x,p)=0\) and \(g(x,p)\le0\), where \(p\in\mathbb R^s\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^s\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuous. Suppose strong regularity at \(\bar p\) supplies a continuous local KKT branch \(p\mapsto(x(p),\lambda(p),\mu(p))\). If every reference-active inequality is strictly complementary, so that \(g_i(x(\bar p),\bar p)=0\) implies \(\mu_i(\bar p)>0\), then there is a neighborhood \(P\) of \(\bar p\) such that \[\{i:g_i(x(p),p)=0\}=\{i:g_i(x(\bar p),\bar p)=0\}\quad\text{for every }p\in P.\] After possibly shrinking \(P\), every reference-active multiplier remains positive and every reference-inactive inequality remains strictly inactive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a continuous strongly regular KKT branch, strict complementarity preserves the complete inequality active set and the positivity of its active multipliers locally.
assumptions_latex: \(p\mapsto(x(p),\lambda(p),\mu(p))\) is a continuous local KKT branch at \(\bar p\).
\(g_i(x(\bar p),\bar p)=0\) implies \(\mu_i(\bar p)>0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality active set is locally constant, and \(\mu_i(p)>0\) for every reference-active index and all sufficiently near \(p\).

notation.meaning: parameter neighborhood of the reference value

knowledge_statements.title: Orthant-Projection Strong-Regularity Counterexample Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthant projection is a strongly regular generalized equation whose weakly active inequalities change status across coordinate hyperplanes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\in\mathbb R^n\), consider \[\min_{x\ge0}\ \tfrac12\|x\|^2-p^\top x.\] Its KKT generalized equation is \(p\in x+N_{\mathbb R_+^n}(x)\). The inverse of \(x\mapsto x+N_{\mathbb R_+^n}(x)\) is the globally single-valued nonexpansive map \(p\mapsto P_{\mathbb R_+^n}(p)=p_+\); hence the generalized equation is strongly regular at \((x,p)=(0,0)\). With inequalities \(-x_i\le0\), \(\lambda(p)=(-p)_+\). At \(p=0\), every inequality is weakly active, while index \(i\) is inactive when \(p_i>0\) and active when \(p_i<0\). Thus strong regularity without strict complementarity does not imply local constancy of the active set.
assumptions_latex: The normal cone is the convex-analysis normal cone to \(\mathbb R_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Strong regularity at }(0,0)\text{ holds, but the active set is not locally constant in }p.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong regularity does not preserve weakly active inequalities.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the nonnegative orthant
normal-cone mapping of the nonnegative orthant

knowledge_statements.title: Only Weakly Active Indices Can Change on a Continuous KKT Branch
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a continuous KKT branch, strict inactivity and positive active multipliers persist; only weakly active constraints can switch status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\mapsto(x(p),\mu(p))\) be a continuous local KKT branch for \(g_i(x,p)\le0\). Every strictly inactive index at \(\bar p\) remains inactive nearby by continuity. Every active index with \(\mu_i(\bar p)>0\) remains active, because continuity gives \(\mu_i(p)>0\) and complementarity forces \(g_i(x(p),p)=0\). Therefore any local activity change can involve only indices satisfying \(g_i(x(\bar p),\bar p)=0\) and \(\mu_i(\bar p)=0\).
assumptions_latex: p\mapsto(x(p),\mu(p))\text{ is continuous and satisfies KKT complementarity locally}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A(x(p),p)\triangle A(x(\bar p),\bar p)\subseteq\{i:g_i(x(\bar p),\bar p)=0,\ \mu_i(\bar p)=0\}\text{ locally}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp local boundary for activity changes under continuous primal-dual stability.

knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Persistence Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A weakly active constraint can change status despite a unique Lipschitz KKT branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\tfrac12(x-p)^2\quad\text{subject to }x\le0.\] Its unique KKT solution is \[x(p)=\min\{p,0\},\qquad \mu(p)=\max\{p,0\}.\] At \(p=0\), the inequality is active but weakly complementary because \(x(0)=\mu(0)=0\). For every \(p<0\), it is inactive, whereas for every \(p>0\), it is active with positive multiplier. Thus uniqueness and Lipschitz continuity of the primal-dual branch do not ensure persistence of the active set when strict complementarity is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly active constraint may immediately become inactive on one side of a parameter change, even along a unique Lipschitz KKT branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict complementarity cannot be omitted from a general guarantee of complete active-set persistence.

notation.meaning: multiplier of the inequality x less than or equal to zero

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Only Weakly Active Indices Can Change Status on a Continuous KKT Branch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp local boundary for activity changes under continuous primal-dual stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\mapsto(x(p),\mu(p))\) be a continuous local KKT branch for inequalities \(g_i(x,p)\le0\). At the reference parameter \(\bar p\), every strictly inactive index \(i\) with \(g_i(x(\bar p),\bar p)<0\) remains inactive nearby by continuity. Every active index with \(\mu_i(\bar p)>0\) remains active nearby, because continuity gives \(\mu_i(p)>0\) and complementarity then forces \(g_i(x(p),p)=0\). Therefore any local change of the active set can involve only indices satisfying \(g_i(x(\bar p),\bar p)=0\) and \(\mu_i(\bar p)=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stable, Entering, Leaving, and Weak Activity Regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Along a KKT branch \((x(p),\lambda(p))\) for inequalities \(g_i(x,p)\le0\), define slack \(s_i(p)=-g_i(x(p),p)\ge0\), multiplier \(\lambda_i(p)\ge0\), and complementarity \(s_i(p)\lambda_i(p)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local classification of inequality activity along a parameterized or iterative primal-dual branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each inequality index \(i\), the strict inactive regime is \(s_i>0,\lambda_i=0\), and the strict active regime is \(s_i=0,\lambda_i>0\). The weakly active transition boundary is \(s_i=0,\lambda_i=0\). An entering transition at \(\bar p\) occurs if there are sequences \(p_k^I\to\bar p\) and \(p_k^A\to\bar p\) for which \(s_i(p_k^I)>0\) and \(s_i(p_k^A)=0\); a leaving transition is the reverse orientation along a specified parameter path. A persistent regime is a neighborhood on which the relevant strict classification is constant. For several constraints, an activity-transition regime is the product stratification generated by these per-index states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each inequality is strictly inactive, strictly active, or weakly active according to its slack and multiplier. Weakly active points form transition boundaries where nearby branches or parameter directions can place the constraint on either side of the active-set classification.
assumptions_latex: Primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity hold along the branch.
Slacks and multipliers are evaluated with one fixed inequality sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(s_i,\lambda_i)\in\{(s,0):s>0\}\cup\{(0,\lambda):\lambda>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}\] defines the inactive, active, and weak transition regimes.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Strict complementarity excludes the weakly active state \((s_i,\lambda_i)=(0,0)\).
special_cases_latex: A locally persistent active set contains no entering or leaving transition.
At a degenerate solution, one or more active indices may be weakly active.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only weakly active indices can change status without violating continuity of both slack and multiplier.
Strict sign margins yield a neighborhood with constant classification.
boundary_notes: A weakly active constraint need not actually change status along every perturbation direction.
Multiple simultaneous transitions may require a finer stratification than a single entering or leaving label.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Activity Need Not Persist
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-multiplier active constraint can become inactive under arbitrarily small parameter perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}(x-p)^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\le0.\] Its unique solution is \(x(p)=\min\{p,0\}\). At \(p=0\), the constraint is active with multiplier zero. It is inactive for every \(p<0\) and active for every \(p>0\). Thus reference activity need not persist without strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active set of the unique solution is not locally constant at \(p=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary parametric bound problem exhibiting loss of activity at a zero-multiplier reference point.

knowledge_statements.title: Locally Persistent Activity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is locally persistently active when it remains binding along the specified nearby solution branch; full persistence means that branch has a locally constant active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(g_i(x,p)\le0\) and a specified localized feasible solution selection \(x(p)\) with \(x(\bar p)=\bar x\), an index \(i\in\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p)\) is locally persistently active along this selection if a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar p\) exists such that \[g_i(x(p),p)=0\qquad(p\in U).\] The complete activity pattern is locally persistent when \[\mathcal A(x(p),p)=\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p)\qquad(p\in U).\]
assumptions_latex: \(x(p)\) is a specified localized feasible solution selection with \(x(\bar p)=\bar x\).
The inequality index set is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full local persistence is precisely local constancy of \(\mathcal A(x(p),p)\) along the selection.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence of individual or complete inequality activity along a specified localized solution selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Complementarity Preserves Activity along a Continuous KKT Selection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a continuous KKT branch, positive reference multipliers keep active constraints binding, while continuity preserves the strict slack of inactive constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x(p),\lambda(p))\) be a continuous local primal–inequality-multiplier KKT selection for continuous constraints \(g_i(x,p)\le0\). If every reference-active constraint is strictly complementary, \[i\in\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p)\ \Longrightarrow\ \lambda_i(\bar p)>0,\] then, after restricting the parameter neighborhood, \[\mathcal A(x(p),p)=\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p).\]
assumptions_latex: The inequality index set is finite.
Primal feasibility, dual nonnegativity, and complementarity hold along the selection.
Strict complementarity holds for every reference-active inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full active set is locally constant along the KKT selection.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient branchwise condition for locally constant activity.

notation.meaning: inequality multiplier along the KKT selection

knowledge_statements.title: Tangential Persistence and Higher-Order Exit
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two branches have identical first-order tangency, yet one retains activity and the other exits at second order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g(x)=x\le0\) at \(x=0\) with reference multiplier \(\mu=0\), consider \(x_1(t)=0\) and \(x_2(t)=-t^2\), \(t\ge0\). Along the first branch the constraint remains active; along the second it is inactive for every \(t>0\). Nevertheless, \[\left.\frac{d}{dt}g(x_1(t))\right|_{0}=\left.\frac{d}{dt}g(x_2(t))\right|_{0}=0.\]
assumptions_latex: The reference multiplier for g(x)=x\le0 is zero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Paired feasible branches showing that zero first derivative does not decide activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Exit from Weak Activity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative directional constraint derivative makes a weakly active constraint immediately inactive; continued activity requires first-order tangency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t\mapsto(x(t),p(t))\) be a differentiable feasible branch for \(g_i(x,p)\le0\), with \(g_i(x(0),p(0))=0\) and KKT multiplier \(\mu_i(0)=0\). Set \(\phi_i(t)=g_i(x(t),p(t))\). Feasibility gives \(\phi_i'(0)\le0\). If \(\phi_i'(0)<0\), then \(g_i(x(t),p(t))<0\) for every sufficiently small \(t>0\), so index \(i\) becomes inactive. Persistence of activity along the branch requires \(\phi_i'(0)=0\).
assumptions_latex: x(\cdot),p(\cdot),g_i\text{ are differentiable along the branch}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi_i'(0)<0\Rightarrow i\notin A(x(t),p(t))\text{ for all sufficiently small }t>0;\quad i\in A(x(t),p(t))\Rightarrow\phi_i'(0)=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order diagnostic for a weakly active constraint along a differentiable one-sided feasible branch.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Exit Test at a Weakly Active Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first nonzero higher-order derivative decides finite-order exit; flat contact remains inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi(t)=g_i(x(t),p(t))\) along a one-sided feasible \(C^r\) branch for \(g_i\le0\), with \(\phi(0)=0\), \(\mu_i(0)=0\), and \(\phi^{(j)}(0)=0\) for \(1\le j<r\). If \(\phi^{(r)}(0)<0\), then \(\phi(t)<0\) for all sufficiently small \(t>0\), so index \(i\) becomes inactive. If \(\phi^{(r)}(0)>0\), such a one-sided feasible branch cannot exist. If all available derivatives vanish, finite-order information need not decide persistence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi^{(r)}(0)<0\Rightarrow\phi(t)<0\text{ locally for }t>0;\qquad \phi^{(r)}(0)>0\Rightarrow\text{one-sided feasibility is impossible}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order refinement when the first directional constraint derivative vanishes.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Active Transition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate KKT parameters at which a reference weakly active index changes activity or multiplier-positivity status arbitrarily nearby.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\mapsto(x(p),\lambda(p),\mu(p))\) be a local KKT selection for an inequality-constrained parametric NLP, with \(p\in\mathbb R^s\), and define \[I^0(p)=\{i:g_i(x(p),p)=0,\ \mu_i(p)=0\}.\] A parameter \(\bar p\) is a weakly active transition boundary along this selection if \(I^0(\bar p)\ne\varnothing\) and every neighborhood \(P\) of \(\bar p\) contains a parameter \(p\in P\) and an index \(i\in I^0(\bar p)\) for which either \(g_i(x(p),p)<0\) or \(\mu_i(p)>0\). Thus a reference weakly active index becomes inactive or becomes active with a positive multiplier arbitrarily near \(\bar p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly active transition boundary is a KKT parameter where some zero-multiplier active constraint becomes inactive or gains a positive multiplier arbitrarily nearby along the selected branch.
assumptions_latex: A local KKT selection \(p\mapsto(x(p),\lambda(p),\mu(p))\) is defined near \(\bar p\).
The inequalities use the convention \(g_i(x,p)\le0\) with multipliers \(\mu_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Some index in \(I^0(\bar p)\) changes activity or multiplier-positivity status arbitrarily near \(\bar p\).

notation.meaning: weakly active inequality indices along the selected KKT branch
an arbitrary neighborhood of the reference parameter
