knowledge_statements.title: Model-Error Activity Transfer
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modeled activity margin is reliable only when it exceeds the model error on the valid step region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(|m_i(x;d)-g_i(x+d)|\le\kappa_i\Delta^{q_i}\) whenever \(\|d\|\le\Delta\). Then \(m_i(x;d)<-\tau-\kappa_i\Delta^{q_i}\) certifies \(g_i(x+d)<-\tau\), while \(g_i(x+d)=0\) implies \(m_i(x;d)\ge-\kappa_i\Delta^{q_i}\). Thus the activity threshold must be calibrated to the model-error order and validity radius.
assumptions_latex: The displayed model-error bound holds on the validity region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |m_i(x;d)-g_i(x+d)|\le\kappa_i\Delta^{q_i}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy condition transferring modeled thresholds to actual trial-point residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Interpolation Alone Does Not Ensure Predictive Activity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two interpolating models can make opposite activity predictions, so zero-step interpolation is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g(x)=x\) at \(x=0\), both \(m_1(0;d)=d\) and \(m_2(0;d)=-d\) satisfy \(m_j(0;0)=g(0)=0\). For any \(d>0\) and \(0\le\tau<d\), the estimator based on \(m_1\) selects the constraint, while that based on \(m_2\) does not. Thus interpolation at \(d=0\) alone supplies no activity-prediction guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_1(0;0)=m_2(0;0)=g(0)\quad\text{but their threshold classifications disagree}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when only zero-step interpolation is imposed.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Based Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicted active set defined by general local constraint models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a point \(x\), let \(m_i(x;d)\) be a local model of the residual \(g_i(x+d)\), with \(m_i(x;0)=g_i(x)\). Given a trial step \(d\) and \(\tau\ge0\), the model-based estimator is
\[
E_{\mathrm{mod}}(x,d;\tau)=\{i\in I:m_i(x;d)\ge-\tau\}.
\]
If the model subproblem enforces \(m_i(x;d)\le0\), membership means that the predicted constraint slack is at most \(\tau\). Affine, quadratic, or surrogate constraint models yield distinct instances, so the model and its accuracy region are part of the estimator specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model-based estimator selects constraints whose modeled residuals at a trial step are close to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{\mathrm{mod}}(x,d;\tau)=\{i:m_i(x;d)\ge-\tau\}.\)

notation.meaning: local model of the i-th constraint residual

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Optimality Conditions for Constrained Optimization p. 185

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 Optimality Conditions for Constrained Optimization p. 185

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The general formula is internally consistent, but the cited optimality-conditions section is indirect and does not establish this model-based estimator convention. Because interpolation at d=0 alone is too weak to substantiate the claims about local models and accuracy regions, a direct model-based optimization source with a specific locator is needed.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Tolerance Estimator Agreement Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The estimators agree whenever each surrogate error is smaller than the exact residual's distance from the shared threshold; disagreement requires an error at least that large.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau>0\), let \(E_a=\{i:a_i\ge-\tau\}\), \(E_b=\{i:b_i\ge-\tau\}\), and \(E_c=\{i:c_i\ge-\tau\}\). If \[|a_i-b_i|<|a_i+\tau|\quad\text{and}\quad |a_i-c_i|<|a_i+\tau|\quad\forall i,\] then \(E_a=E_b=E_c\). Conversely, \(i\in E_a\triangle E_b\) implies \(|a_i-b_i|\ge|a_i+\tau|\), and analogously for \(c_i\). Taking \(a_i=g_i(x+d)\), \(b_i=g_i(x)+\nabla g_i(x)^\top d\), and \(c_i=m_i(x;d)\) gives the slack, affine, and model estimator certificate.
assumptions_latex: All estimators use the same sign convention and threshold \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{|a_i-b_i|,|a_i-c_i|\}<|a_i+\tau|\ \forall i\Rightarrow E_a=E_b=E_c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic error-versus-margin criterion for agreement of residual, affine, and model estimators.

notation.meaning: symmetric difference of estimated active sets
reference residual's distance from the threshold

knowledge_statements.title: Estimator-Agreement Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic separation criterion ensuring linearized and model-based estimates coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x\), \(d\), positive scales \(w_i\), and \(\tau\ge0\). Let \(r_i=|\ell_i(x;d)|/w_i\) and \(q_i=|m_i(x;d)|/w_i\). If \(|q_i-r_i|\le\eta\) for every \(i\in I\), where \(\eta\ge0\), and no linearized score lies in the ambiguity band \([\max\{0,\tau-\eta\},\tau+\eta]\), then
\[
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{lin}}(x;d,\tau)=\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mod}}(x;d,\tau).
\]
Thus uniform model agreement plus separation from the classification threshold ensures identical active-set decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearized and model-based estimators agree when their scores differ uniformly by at most eta and every linearized score is separated from the threshold by more than eta.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{lin}}(x;d,\tau)=\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mod}}(x;d,\tau)\).

notation.meaning: Uniform discrepancy bound between the scores.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp deterministic condition for agreement of residual, affine, and model threshold estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a common threshold \(\tau>0\), define \(E_a=\{i:a_i\ge-\tau\}\), \(E_b=\{i:b_i\ge-\tau\}\), and \(E_c=\{i:c_i\ge-\tau\}\). If, for every \(i\), \[|a_i-b_i|<|a_i+\tau|\quad\text{and}\quad |a_i-c_i|<|a_i+\tau|,\] then \(E_a=E_b=E_c\). More generally, disagreement for index \(i\) can occur only if at least one approximation error reaches the reference residual's distance from the threshold: \[i\in E_a\triangle E_b\Rightarrow |a_i-b_i|\ge|a_i+\tau|.\] Taking \(a_i=g_i(x+d)\), \(b_i=g_i(x)+\nabla g_i(x)^\top d\), and \(c_i=m_i(x;d)\) gives the corresponding slack, linearization, and model-estimator criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold estimators agree whenever every affine and model error is smaller than the exact residual's distance from the shared activity threshold.
assumptions_latex: All three estimators use the same sign convention and threshold \(\tau>0\).
No reference residual lies exactly on the threshold under the strict-margin conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{|a_i-b_i|,|a_i-c_i|\}<|a_i+\tau|\ \forall i\Rightarrow E_a=E_b=E_c.\)

notation.meaning: symmetric difference of two estimated active sets
distance of the reference residual from the activity threshold

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Identification regime for constrained nonlinear programming
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathscr P\) be a class of nonlinear programs, \(\mathscr S(P)\) a class of algorithmic sequences converging to a stationary point \(x^*\) of \(P\), \(E\) an estimator, and \(T(P,x^*,\Lambda^*)\subseteq\mathcal I\) a designated target.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A regime is a specification of structural hypotheses and identification semantics, not an identification result by itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An identification regime is a tuple \(\mathfrak R=(\mathscr P,\mathscr S,E,T,\mathcal Q,\mathcal M)\), where \(\mathcal Q\) is a list of local regularity and degeneracy conditions and \(\mathcal M\) is a convergence mode. The associated guarantee has the quantified form \(\forall P\in\mathscr P\ \forall s\in\mathscr S(P)\), if \(\mathcal Q(P,s,x^*)\) holds, then \(E(s_k)\) identifies \(T(P,x^*,\Lambda^*)\) in mode \(\mathcal M\). Regimes are distinguished by strict complementarity, multiplier degeneracy, constraint geometry, target choice, and finite, asymptotic, deterministic, or probabilistic mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An identification regime packages the precise problem class, admissible convergent sequences, estimator, target set, structural conditions, and convergence mode used by an identification statement. Strict-complementarity, degenerate-multiplier, and geometry-based settings are different regimes because their hypotheses or identifiable targets differ. Naming a regime does not itself assert that identification occurs.
assumptions_latex: The problem, sequence, estimator, target, structural conditions, and convergence mode are explicitly declared.
The target \(T\) is a subset of the inequality index set.
Multiplier-dependent targets use a stated multiplier or multiplier set \(\Lambda^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak R=(\mathscr P,\mathscr S,E,T,\mathcal Q,\mathcal M)\) uniquely specifies the domain and semantics of an identification claim.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A regime can be represented as the domain of validity of the conditional predicate \(\mathcal Q\Rightarrow G_{E,T,\mathcal M}\).
Two regime descriptions are equivalent when they generate the same admissible instances, target, estimator output, and guarantee predicate.
special_cases_latex: A strict-complementarity regime includes positivity of all active multipliers in \(\mathcal Q\).
A geometry regime may target a minimal face or active manifold rather than every active constraint label.
immediate_consequences_latex: Identification guarantees from different regimes cannot be compared solely by their convergence mode.
Changing the target from the full active set to a strongly active subset changes the regime.
boundary_notes: Constraint qualifications and strict complementarity are distinct conditions and must not be conflated.
The tuple does not prescribe an algorithm or establish that its conditional guarantee is valid.
review_flags: The regime-tuple formalization is unsourced within the supplied material and requires an exact supporting reference.
knowledge_statements.title: Identification regime for constrained nonlinear programming
Strict-Complementarity Threshold Identification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity, primal threshold accuracy, and multiplier convergence make the combined estimator equal the true active set eventually.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a strictly complementary KKT pair for finitely many locally Lipschitz inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\). Let \(x_k\to x^*\), \(\widehat\lambda_k\to\lambda^*\), and \(\tau_k,\eta_k\downarrow0\), with \(\|x_k-x^*\|=o(\tau_k)\). Define \(E_k=\{i:g_i(x_k)\ge-\tau_k,\ \widehat\lambda_{k,i}\ge\eta_k\}\). Then \(E_k=A(x^*)\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many locally Lipschitz inequalities.
\((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a strictly complementary KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\ E_k=A(x^*).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact identification by a combined primal-dual threshold estimator.

notation.meaning: active inequality set at the KKT point

knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Complementarity Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification by a primal-dual threshold rule under strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the nonlinear program \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)\ge 0\) for every index in a finite set \(I\), where \(f\) and every \(c_i\) are differentiable. Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair under the convention \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i c_i(x)\), and suppose strict complementarity holds: \(c_i(x^*)=0\) implies \(\lambda_i^*>0\). Let \((x_k,\lambda_k)\to(x^*,\lambda^*)\), and let \(\tau_k>0\) satisfy \(\tau_k\downarrow0\), \(\max_{i\in I}|c_i(x_k)-c_i(x^*)|=o(\tau_k)\), and \(\max_{i\in I}|\lambda_{k,i}-\lambda_i^*|=o(\tau_k)\). Define
\[
\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\{i\in I:c_i(x_k)\le\tau_k,\ \lambda_{k,i}\ge\tau_k\}.
\]
Then \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A(x^*)\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), where \(\mathcal A(x^*)=\{i\in I:c_i(x^*)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite smooth inequality-constrained problem, strict complementarity and primal-dual errors that vanish faster than the threshold ensure that simultaneous slack and multiplier thresholding identifies the exact active set after finitely many iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite, and \(f,c_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are differentiable.
\((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a KKT pair and \(c_i(x^*)=0\Rightarrow\lambda_i^*>0\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\in\mathbb N\ \forall k\ge K:\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A(x^*)\).

notation.meaning: Indices of constraints active at x*.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\), let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfy the KKT conditions with \(\lambda_i^*\ge0\), \(\lambda_i^*c_i(x^*)=0\), and \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0\}\). Let \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\subseteq\mathcal I\) be an estimator output.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local primal-dual identification regime at a KKT point with a specified multiplier satisfying strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is strictly complementary when \(c_i(x^*)+\lambda_i^*>0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal I\); equivalently, \(\lambda_i^*>0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal A^*\) and \(c_i(x^*)>0\) for every \(i\notin\mathcal A^*\). Strict-complementarity identification is identification of the full set \(\mathcal A^*\) by an estimator along a sequence converging to such a pair, with the guarantee mode stated separately, for example \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict-complementarity identification concerns a primal-dual KKT limit where every active inequality has a positive multiplier and every inactive inequality has positive slack. In this regime, the identification target is the full active set. The phrase must still be paired with a mode such as finite exact or asymptotic identification; strict complementarity alone is a property of the limit pair, not an estimator guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity.
The multiplier \(\lambda^*\) used in the strict-complementarity condition is specified.
The estimator sequence and its convergence mode are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime condition is \(\min_{i\in\mathcal A^*}\lambda_i^*>0\) together with \(\min_{i\notin\mathcal A^*}c_i(x^*)>0\), using \(+\infty\) for a minimum over an empty set, and its identification target is \(\mathcal A^*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under complementarity, strict complementarity is equivalent to \(c_i(x^*)+\lambda_i^*>0\) for all \(i\in\mathcal I\).
For finite \(\mathcal I\), it is equivalent to a positive separation margin \(\delta^*:=\min_i(c_i(x^*)+\lambda_i^*)>0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal A^*=\varnothing\), strict complementarity reduces to strict inactivity of all inequalities.
With a unique KKT multiplier, the regime is independent of multiplier selection.
immediate_consequences_latex: The active set equals \(\{i:\lambda_i^*>0\}\).
Positive primal-dual separation permits threshold-based classification at the limit.
boundary_notes: When multipliers are nonunique, strict complementarity may mean existence of a strictly complementary multiplier or positivity of a designated multiplier; the convention must be stated.
Strict complementarity does not itself imply finite identification for an arbitrary estimator.
review_flags: Strict complementarity is standard, but no inspected locator was established for this exact identification-regime formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-complementarity identification regime
Identification without Strict Complementarity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-multiplier active constraint can be missed forever by any estimator requiring a strictly positive multiplier threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Strict complementarity cannot be omitted from exact identification by positive multiplier thresholding. Consider
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb R} x^2\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad -x\le0.
\]
At the unique solution \(x^*=0\), the constraint is active, but the unique KKT multiplier is \(\lambda^*=0\). Hence for every \(\eta>0\), the multiplier-aware rule \(E_{\mathrm{mult}}(x^*,\lambda^*;\tau,\eta)\) excludes the active constraint, for every \(\tau\ge0\). Thus convergence of primal points and multipliers alone does not guarantee exact identification when an active constraint has zero multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(x^*)=\{1\}\) but \(E_{\mathrm{mult}}(x^*,\lambda^*;\tau,\eta)=\varnothing\) for every \(\tau\ge0\) and \(\eta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier thresholding cannot generally identify weakly active constraints.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair for inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\). Define \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0\}\), \(\mathcal A^+(\lambda^*)=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\lambda_i^*>0\}\), and \(\mathcal A^0(\lambda^*)=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\lambda_i^*=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local identification when at least one active inequality is weakly active; full-set and partial-set targets are explicitly distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Identification without strict complementarity is an identification regime satisfying \(\mathcal A^0(\lambda^*)\ne\varnothing\). A full identification claim targets \(\mathcal A^*\), whereas a strong-active identification claim targets only \(\mathcal A^+(\lambda^*)\). For an estimator \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\), finite full identification means \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A^*\); finite strong-active identification means \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\mathcal A^+(\lambda^*)\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\subseteq\mathcal A^*\). The latter leaves classification of zero-multiplier active constraints unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without strict complementarity, at least one active inequality has zero multiplier. Identification statements must then say whether the target is the entire active set or only the positively multiplied constraints. A common partial target requires all strongly active constraints to be selected and forbids inactive constraints, while allowing weakly active constraints to be either selected or omitted.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier selection is fixed when multipliers are nonunique.
The estimator and finite or asymptotic mode are explicitly stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is characterized by failure of strict complementarity and by an explicit choice between target \(\mathcal A^*\) and the partial target interval \(\{S:\mathcal A^+(\lambda^*)\subseteq S\subseteq\mathcal A^*\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Failure of strict complementarity at the specified pair is equivalent to \(\min_{i\in\mathcal A^*}\lambda_i^*=0\) when \(\mathcal A^*\ne\varnothing\).
The partial finite condition is equivalent to eventual absence of false positives and eventual inclusion of every positive-multiplier index.
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal A^+(\lambda^*)=\varnothing\), the partial condition requires only \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\subseteq\mathcal A^*\) eventually.
Additional geometric information may support full identification despite zero multipliers.
immediate_consequences_latex: A guarantee for \(\mathcal A^+(\lambda^*)\) is not automatically a guarantee for \(\mathcal A^*\).
Zero multiplier does not imply that an active constraint is geometrically redundant.
boundary_notes: The regime does not assert that full identification is impossible.
Multiplier-dependent partitions can vary with multiplier choice when the multiplier set is not a singleton.

notation.meaning: active constraints with positive specified multiplier
active constraints with zero specified multiplier

review_flags: No inspected source was verified to support the stated partial-target convention under failure of strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Identification regime without strict complementarity

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x^*\) be a KKT point and let \(\Lambda(x^*)\) be its nonempty set of KKT multipliers for inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\). Define \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification regimes with possibly nonunique multipliers; the definitions separate multiplier-invariant and multiplier-dependent targets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the uniformly strongly active set \(\mathcal A^{++}:=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)}\lambda_i>0\}\), the potentially strongly active set \(\mathcal A^{+}:=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)}\lambda_i>0\}\), and the uniformly zero-multiplier set \(\mathcal A^{00}:=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\lambda_i=0\ \forall\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)\}\). A multiplier-degenerate identification regime is one in which \(\mathcal A^{++}\ne\mathcal A^*\), or multiplier selection changes the positive-multiplier support. Its target must be declared as \(\mathcal A^*\), \(\mathcal A^{++}\), \(\mathcal A^{+}\), or the support of a selected multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When KKT multipliers are nonunique or contain zeros on active constraints, identification targets based on multiplier support can differ. Constraints may have multipliers bounded positively away from zero for every multiplier, positive for at least one multiplier, or zero for all multipliers. A multiplier-degenerate regime states which of these sets is the target and whether the estimator depends on a selected multiplier sequence.
assumptions_latex: All multipliers use the same constraint orientation and normalization.
The infimum and supremum are taken over the complete declared multiplier set or a specified normalized subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A^{++}\subseteq\mathcal A^{+}\subseteq\mathcal A^*\), \(\mathcal A^{00}=\mathcal A^*\setminus\mathcal A^{+}\), and a multiplier-degenerate identification statement must name one of these distinct targets or a selected-multiplier support.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(i\in\mathcal A^{00}\iff\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)}\lambda_i=0\), since inequality multipliers are nonnegative.
Multiplier-support invariance holds when \(\{i:\lambda_i>0\}\) is identical for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\Lambda(x^*)\) is a singleton \(\{\lambda^*\}\), then \(\mathcal A^{++}=\mathcal A^{+}=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\lambda_i^*>0\}\).
If a strictly complementary multiplier exists, then \(\mathcal A^{+}=\mathcal A^*\), although \(\mathcal A^{++}\) may still be smaller.
immediate_consequences_latex: Identification of \(\mathcal A^{++}\) is invariant under multiplier selection.
Identification of a selected multiplier's support may change when the algorithm converges to a different multiplier.
boundary_notes: The condition \(\inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)}\lambda_i>0\) can be too strong when the multiplier set is not compact; the declared multiplier set must make the infimum meaningful.
Primal activity \(\mathcal A^*\) remains defined independently of multiplier degeneracy.

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier set at the target point

review_flags: The multiplier-set partitions and the infimum-based uniformly positive convention require a precise inspected source.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-set degeneracy partitions for identification
Zero-Multiplier Indistinguishability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero multiplier is compatible with both a binding and a strictly inactive constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(P_1:\min_x x^2\) subject to \(-x\le0\), the point \(x^*=0\) is optimal, the constraint is active, and its KKT multiplier is zero. In \(P_2:\min_x x^2\) subject to \(-x-1\le0\), the same point is optimal, the constraint is inactive, and its multiplier is also zero. Thus zero multiplier data alone do not distinguish weak activity from inactivity.
assumptions_latex: Classification uses multiplier data without primal residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda^*=0\not\Rightarrow g(x^*)=0\text{ or }g(x^*)<0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal multiplier-only identification failure under weak activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Identification Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With zero-multiplier active constraints, multiplier information can identify the positive-multiplier subset but does not generally determine the full active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair with \(A_+^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0,\lambda_i^*>0\}\subsetneq A^*=A(x^*)\). Suppose \(x_k\to x^*\) and \(\widehat\lambda_k\to\lambda^*\). A multiplier-significance estimator can stably identify \(A_+^*\) when its positive threshold vanishes more slowly than multiplier-estimation error, but these assumptions do not determine membership of \(A^*\setminus A_+^*\). Consequently, without an independent primal, geometric, or algorithmic separation condition, the generally supportable guarantee is sufficient-set identification rather than exact identification of \(A^*\).
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a KKT pair with \(A_+^*\subsetneq A^*\).
The multiplier threshold dominates \(\|\widehat\lambda_k-\lambda^*\|_\infty\) and tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_+^*\) may be identified finitely, whereas exact identification of \(A^*\) requires additional separation information.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification guarantees when weak activity or multiplier degeneracy is present.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique-Multiplier Identification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With nonunique KKT multipliers, different multiplier limits may have different positive supports. Identifying one support therefore need not identify every potentially positive or geometrically active constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le 0\), and let \(x^*\) be a KKT point with nonempty multiplier set \(M(x^*)\). Define \(A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\), \(A^+=\{i:\lambda_i>0\text{ for some }\lambda\in M(x^*)\}\), and \(A^{++}=\{i:\lambda_i>0\text{ for every }\lambda\in M(x^*)\}\). Then \(A^{++}\subseteq A^+\subseteq A^*\). If multipliers are nonunique, the support \(\{i:\lambda_i>0\}\) may depend on the selected multiplier; hence convergence to one multiplier can identify its support without identifying every member of \(A^+\) or all geometrically active constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every \(g_i\) are continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{++}\subseteq A^+\subseteq A^*\), while multiplier-support identification may depend on the selected element of \(M(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes geometric activity from the support associated with a selected KKT multiplier.

notation.meaning: set of KKT multiplier vectors at the solution
indices positive for some, respectively every, KKT multiplier

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicated-Constraint Selection Counterexample
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating an active inequality gives multiplier representatives with different positive supports at the same primal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x\) subject to \(-x\le0\) and \(-x\le0\). The unique minimizer is \(x^*=0\), and \(M(0)=\{(t,1-t):0\le t\le1\}\). The multipliers \((1,0)\), \((0,1)\), and \((1/2,1/2)\) have positive supports \(\{1\}\), \(\{2\}\), and \(\{1,2\}\), respectively.
assumptions_latex: The duplicate inequalities remain distinct indexed constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{supp}_+(\lambda)\text{ is not constant on }M(0).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal fixed-primal example with representative-dependent positive support.

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier set at the optimizer

knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Support Stability and Selection Invariance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thresholding eventually recovers the positive support of the selected multiplier limit; classifications are invariant exactly when all admissible limits have the same positive support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda^k\to\bar\lambda\in M(x^*)\), let \(\tau_k\downarrow0\), and define \(D_k=\{i:\lambda_i^k>\tau_k\}\). If \(\max_{i:\bar\lambda_i=0}(\lambda_i^k)_+=o(\tau_k)\), then \(D_k=\operatorname{supp}_+(\bar\lambda)\) eventually. Consequently, among admissible multiplier limits, eventual thresholded support is selection-invariant exactly when \(\operatorname{supp}_+(\lambda)\) is constant on the set of admissible limits.
assumptions_latex: Positive errors on zero limit components are \(o(\tau_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_k=\operatorname{supp}_+(\bar\lambda)\text{ eventually}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold stability for a chosen multiplier limit and the exact boundary for representative sensitivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Selection Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar parametric example exhibits nonsmooth dependence of a canonical multiplier selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem of minimizing \(\varepsilon x\) subject to \(x\le 0\) and \(-x\le 0\), the unique feasible point is \(\bar x=0\), and its multiplier set is \[\Lambda(\varepsilon)=\{(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\in\mathbb R_+^2:\varepsilon+\lambda_1-\lambda_2=0\}.\] The minimum-Euclidean-norm selection is \[\lambda^{\min}(\varepsilon)=\begin{cases}(0,\varepsilon),&\varepsilon\ge 0,\\(-\varepsilon,0),&\varepsilon<0.\end{cases}\] Thus this natural selection is continuous and Lipschitz but not differentiable at \(\varepsilon=0\); moreover, its positive-multiplier index changes across zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a minimum-norm multiplier selection can be nondifferentiable under smooth problem perturbations, and its positive-support set can change abruptly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^{\min}\) is not differentiable at \(0\), and its positive support changes there.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{x:c_i(x)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\ c_i(x)\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal I)\}\), let \(x^*\in\Omega\), and let \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0\}\). Assume the active constraints are differentiable at \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local geometric identification based on tangent and normal objects; it distinguishes geometric structure from a particular constraint representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linearized tangent cone is \(T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*):=\{d:\nabla c_i(x^*)^Td=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\ \nabla c_i(x^*)^Td\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal A^*)\}\), and its polar is the linearized normal cone \(N_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*):=T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)^\circ\). A constraint-geometry identification regime declares as its target a representation-invariant local object—such as \(T_\Omega(x^*)\), \(N_\Omega(x^*)\), a minimal face, or an active manifold—and defines identification by eventual equality or convergence of estimated geometric objects to that target. Label identification is a separate, representation-dependent target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint-geometry regime identifies local feasible geometry rather than merely a list of constraint labels. Its target can be the tangent cone, normal cone, minimal face, or active manifold at the limit point. The corresponding estimator must output a geometric object of the same type and the equality or convergence notion must be stated. Different constraint lists can describe the same geometry, so geometric identification and label identification are not equivalent without additional assumptions.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(\Omega\) and target point \(x^*\) are fixed.
The chosen geometric target and topology or equality criterion are explicitly declared.
If \(T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)\) is identified with \(T_\Omega(x^*)\), an appropriate constraint qualification is separately assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A geometry-based estimator identifies the target \(G^*\) when \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\widehat G_k=G^*\), or when \(\operatorname{dist}_{\mathfrak G}(\widehat G_k,G^*)\to0\) in a declared metric on geometric objects.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a polyhedral feasible set, identifying the minimal face containing \(x^*\) in its relative interior is a representation-invariant face-identification target.
Under an exact tangent-cone constraint qualification, \(T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)=T_\Omega(x^*)\).
special_cases_latex: For affine inequalities, \(T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)\) equals the feasible tangent cone.
Redundant active constraints may change \(\mathcal A^*\) without changing the tangent cone or minimal face.
immediate_consequences_latex: Geometric identification can remain meaningful under redundant or duplicated constraints.
Exact label recovery requires representational information beyond equality of tangent or normal cones.
boundary_notes: The polar convention must be fixed; here \(C^\circ=\{v:v^Td\le0\ \forall d\in C\}\).
Nonpolyhedral sets may lack a locally constant face structure, so an active-manifold target needs separate regularity.
review_flags: Standard cone definitions are used, but no inspected source supports the complete identification-regime formulation and listed target objects.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-geometry identification regime
Polyhedral-Constraint Identification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a polyhedron eventually identifies the solution’s minimal face when the limiting projection residual lies in the relative interior of its normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, let \(F\) be a face of \(C\), and suppose \(x^*\in\operatorname{ri}F\). Let \(z^k\to z^*=x^*+v^*\), where \(v^*\in\operatorname{ri}N_C(x^*)\), and set \(x^k=P_C(z^k)\). Then, for all sufficiently large \(k\), the projection \(x^k\) belongs to \(\operatorname{ri}F\). Consequently the minimal face of \(C\) containing \(x^k\) equals \(F\), so every inequality defining that face is identified after finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\in\operatorname{ri}F\) and \(\operatorname{face}_C(x^k)=F\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification of a polyhedral face by nearby projection pairs under normal nondegeneracy.

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to the polyhedron at x
relative interior of the face F

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold-Rate Failure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the activity threshold shrinks faster than the residual of a limiting active constraint, that constraint can be missed forever along feasible iterates converging to the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(g(x)=x\le0\), \(x^*=0\), \(x^k=-1/k\), and \(\varepsilon_k=1/k^2\). Then \(x^k\to x^*\), \(A^*=\{1\}\), and \(g(x^k)\to0\). Nevertheless, for \(A_k=\{1:g(x^k)\ge-\varepsilon_k\}\), one has \(-1/k<-1/k^2\) for every \(k>1\), so \(A_k=\varnothing\) for every \(k>1\). Thus convergence and vanishing active residuals do not suffice when \(|g(x^k)|\) is not \(o(\varepsilon_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A^*=\{1\}\quad\text{but}\quad A_k=\varnothing\ \text{for every }k>1.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of primal threshold identification when the threshold shrinks faster than the residual of a limiting active constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear-Constraint Identification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many continuous nonlinear inequalities, a shrinking primal threshold eventually identifies the exact active set when residuals of the limiting active constraints shrink faster than the threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite index set, let \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuous for every \(i\in I\), and let \(x^k\to x^*\) with \(g_i(x^*)\le 0\) for every \(i\in I\). Define \(A^*=\{i\in I:g_i(x^*)=0\}\). For \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), set \(A_k=\{i\in I:g_i(x^k)\ge-\varepsilon_k\}\). If \(\max_{i\in A^*}|g_i(x^k)|=o(\varepsilon_k)\), with the maximum over the empty set interpreted as \(0\), then \(A_k=A^*\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and every \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
\(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\) and \(\max_{i\in A^*}|g_i(x^k)|=o(\varepsilon_k)\), with the empty-set maximum interpreted as \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_k=A^*\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold identification for finitely many continuous nonlinear inequalities using primal residual accuracy and inactive slack separation.

notation.meaning: active inequality set at the limiting feasible point

knowledge_statements.title: Convergence Without Face Identification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence can converge to a polyhedral boundary point while alternating forever between the boundary and the relative interior, so convergence alone does not imply identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[0,\infty)\), let \(x^*=0\), and define \(x^{2j}=0\) and \(x^{2j+1}=1/(2j+1)\). Then \(x^k\to x^*\), but the minimal face containing \(x^k\) alternates between the boundary face \(\{0\}\) and the full half-line \(C\). Thus convergence to a boundary point alone does not imply finite stabilization of the identified face or active set.
assumptions_latex: \(C=[0,\infty)\) and activity means membership in its boundary face \(\{0\}\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^k\to0,\qquad x^{2j}\in\{0\},\qquad x^{2j+1}\notin\{0\},
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence to a polyhedral boundary point without finite stabilization of boundary-face activity.

notation.meaning: Sequence whose boundary-face classification does not stabilize.

knowledge_statements.title: Topological Boundary Obstruction to Identification from Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a common boundary of a stratum and its complement, a convergent sequence can alternate labels forever.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a metric space, \(S\subseteq C\), and \(x^*\in\overline S\cap\overline{C\setminus S}\). Then there exists a sequence \(x^k\to x^*\) for which membership in \(S\) changes infinitely often. Hence primal convergence alone cannot guarantee finite identification of \(S\) at a common boundary point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x^k\to x^*\text{ such that }\mathbf 1_S(x^k)\text{ does not stabilize}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry-independent obstruction to stabilization of a geometric stratum from primal convergence alone.

notation.meaning: face, active manifold, or other geometric stratum being identified

knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Stratum Isolation Criterion for Universal Identification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every admissible state sequence converging to the limit eventually has the desired label exactly when competing labels are locally excluded around that limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Gamma\) be a metric space, let \(\Gamma_S\subseteq\Gamma\), and let \(q^*\in\Gamma_S\). Every sequence \(q^k\to q^*\) in \(\Gamma\) eventually belongs to \(\Gamma_S\) if and only if \(q^*\) is an interior point of \(\Gamma_S\) relative to \(\Gamma\): \[\exists r>0:\ B_r(q^*)\cap\Gamma\subseteq\Gamma_S.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\forall q^k\to q^*,\ \exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\ q^k\in\Gamma_S\bigr]\iff\bigl[\exists r>0:\ B_r(q^*)\cap\Gamma\subseteq\Gamma_S\bigr].
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact topological boundary for identification from convergence of admissible algorithmic states.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Dependent Identification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curved convex geometry defeats the finite face-identification conclusion valid for polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\|x\|_2\le1\}\), choose distinct boundary points \(x_k\to\bar x\), and set \(v_k=x_k\) and \(\bar v=\bar x\). Then \(v_k\in N_C(x_k)\), \((x_k,v_k)\to(\bar x,\bar v)\), and \(\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}N_C(\bar x)\). Nevertheless, every boundary point of the strictly convex disk is its own minimal face, so \[F(x_k)=\{x_k\}\ne\{\bar x\}=F(\bar x)\] for every \(k\). Normal convergence and relative-interior nondegeneracy therefore do not ensure finite face identification outside polyhedral geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a curved strictly convex set, normals may converge nondegenerately while the minimal face changes forever, so polyhedral finite identification does not extend directly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_k)\ne F(\bar x)\) for every \(k\), despite convergent relative-interior normals.

notation.meaning: Normal cone to C at x.
Minimal face of C containing x.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k,\widehat{\mathcal A}_k)\) contain available primal, dual, and classification information for inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\). When evaluation data include a target, write \(\mathcal A^*\subseteq\mathcal I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional diagnostic interface; observable run-time diagnostics and target-dependent evaluation diagnostics are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An identification diagnostic is a map \(D:\mathcal Z\times2^{\mathcal I}\to\mathbb R_+^q\) whose components quantify primal activity, dual complementarity, set stability, or classification error. A canonical vector is \(D_k=(r_k^{\mathrm{pri}},r_k^{\mathrm{comp}},r_k^{\mathrm{stab}},e_k^{\mathrm{FP}},e_k^{\mathrm{FN}})\), where \(r_k^{\mathrm{pri}}\) measures selected and unselected slacks, \(r_k^{\mathrm{comp}}=\|\lambda_k\odot c(x_k)\|\), \(r_k^{\mathrm{stab}}=|\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\triangle\widehat{\mathcal A}_{k-1}|\), and the last two components compare with \(\mathcal A^*\). A diagnostic is observable when it does not use \(\mathcal A^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An identification diagnostic maps the current primal-dual state and estimated set to nonnegative quantities measuring evidence for correct classification. Typical components monitor primal slack, complementarity, changes in the estimated set, false positives, and false negatives. Diagnostics using the unknown target active set are evaluation measures, while those computed only from current iterates are observable during a run.
assumptions_latex: All diagnostic components have explicitly declared norms, scales, and empty-set conventions.
Multiplier components use a fixed sign convention consistent with \(c_i(x)\ge0\).
Target-dependent errors are used only when \(\mathcal A^*\) is available for evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_k\in\mathbb R_+^q\) is an identification diagnostic precisely when each component is a declared nonnegative residual or classification statistic tied to primal activity, dual complementarity, estimator stability, or target error.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A vector diagnostic may be scalarized as \(d_k=\|W_kD_k\|\) for a declared nonnegative scaling matrix \(W_k\).
Set stability can be represented by the Hamming distance between incidence vectors.
special_cases_latex: A purely primal diagnostic uses only \(x_k\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\).
An offline benchmark diagnostic may use the known solution set \(\mathcal A^*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A zero classification-error pair means exact equality with the target.
A zero stability residual means only that two successive estimates agree, not that either is correct.
boundary_notes: Small complementarity residuals do not uniquely determine active labels near degeneracy.
Diagnostics are measurements and do not by themselves constitute identification guarantees.

notation.meaning: false-positive and false-negative counts or rates

knowledge_statements.title: Diagnostic interface for active-set identification
Primal Activity Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal diagnostics classify constraints by violation, near-zero residual, or negative slack. Reliable identification requires thresholds between active residual error and inactive slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), a primal diagnostic with feasibility tolerance \(\eta_k\ge0\) and activity tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\ge\eta_k\) assigns index \(i\) the label violated if \(g_i(x^k)>\eta_k\), approximately active if \(-\varepsilon_k\le g_i(x^k)\le\eta_k\), and inactive if \(g_i(x^k)<-\varepsilon_k\). The associated estimates are \(A_k^{\mathrm p}=\{i:-\varepsilon_k\le g_i(x^k)\le\eta_k\}\) and \(V_k=\{i:g_i(x^k)>\eta_k\}\). Exact classification requires tolerances smaller than the inactive slack margin and larger than residual error on truly active constraints.
assumptions_latex: Every inequality is written in the convention \(g_i(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The three residual regions define mutually exclusive primal labels and the estimated active set \(A_k^{\mathrm p}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-band rule for classifying inequality constraints from a primal iterate.

notation.meaning: set of constraints exceeding feasibility tolerance

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), estimated active set \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\subseteq\mathcal I\), and positive scales \(\sigma_{k,i}>0\). Define normalized interior slack \(s_{k,i}:=\max\{c_i(x_k),0\}/\sigma_{k,i}\) and normalized violation \(v_{k,i}:=\max\{-c_i(x_k),0\}/\sigma_{k,i}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable primal diagnostics that use constraint values but no multiplier or known target set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The selected-set activity residual, unselected separation residual, and feasibility residual are respectively \(r_k^{\mathrm{sel}}:=\max_{i\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_k}s_{k,i}\), \(r_k^{\mathrm{unsel}}(\tau):=\max_{i\notin\widehat{\mathcal A}_k}(\tau-s_{k,i})_+\), and \(r_k^{\mathrm{feas}}:=\max_{i\in\mathcal I}v_{k,i}\), with maxima over empty sets defined as zero. A primal activity diagnostic is any declared vector or scalarization of these quantities. It is zero exactly when selected constraints have zero interior slack, unselected constraints have normalized slack at least \(\tau\), and no inequality is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal activity diagnostics use scaled constraint values to check whether selected constraints lie near their boundaries, whether unselected constraints are separated from their boundaries, and whether the current point is feasible. Empty index sets contribute zero. These quantities can be computed without knowing the true active set, but their interpretation depends on the selected threshold and scaling.
assumptions_latex: Maximum-over-empty-set values are fixed as zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_k^{\mathrm{pri}}=(r_k^{\mathrm{sel}},r_k^{\mathrm{unsel}}(\tau),r_k^{\mathrm{feas}})\in\mathbb R_+^3\) is the primal activity diagnostic vector.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(r_k^{\mathrm{sel}}=\|P_{\widehat{\mathcal A}_k}s_k\|_\infty\), where \(P_S\) restricts a vector to indices in \(S\).
\(r_k^{\mathrm{unsel}}(\tau)=0\iff s_{k,i}\ge\tau\) for every \(i\notin\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\).
special_cases_latex: At a feasible point, \(r_k^{\mathrm{feas}}=0\).
For \(\tau=0\), the unselected separation residual is identically zero and carries no separation information.
Unscaled diagnostics use \(\sigma_{k,i}=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If all three residuals vanish with \(\tau>0\), selected and unselected constraints are separated by a positive normalized primal margin.
Vanishing selected slack does not distinguish strongly active from zero-multiplier active constraints.
boundary_notes: When iterates are infeasible, interior slack alone must be accompanied by the violation residual.
Constraint rescaling changes unnormalized diagnostics, motivating explicit \(\sigma_{k,i}\).

notation.meaning: maximum normalized slack among selected constraints
failure of unselected constraints to attain threshold separation

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\), take a primal-dual pair \((x_k,\lambda_k)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^{\mathcal I}\), with estimated set \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\). Let \(s_{k,i}:=\max\{c_i(x_k),0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable primal-dual diagnostics for activity classification; stationarity is outside this interface unless added as a separate residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define dual infeasibility \(r_k^{\mathrm{dual}}:=\|(-\lambda_k)_+\|_\infty\), complementarity \(r_k^{\mathrm{comp}}:=\|\lambda_k\odot c(x_k)\|_\infty\), selected dual weakness \(r_k^{\mathrm{weak}}(\gamma):=\max_{i\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_k}(\gamma-\lambda_{k,i})_+\), and unselected dual leakage \(r_k^{\mathrm{leak}}:=\max_{i\notin\widehat{\mathcal A}_k}(\lambda_{k,i})_+\), with empty maxima equal to zero. The dual-complementarity diagnostic interface returns these residuals together with optional primal slacks \(s_{k,i}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual-complementarity interface measures negative multipliers, complementarity products, insufficient multiplier strength on selected constraints, and positive multiplier leakage onto unselected constraints. A declared positive margin can test evidence for strict complementarity. The interface may be combined with primal slack information, but small residuals alone do not resolve zero-multiplier active constraints.
assumptions_latex: Constraint orientation is \(c_i(x)\ge0\), so feasible inequality multipliers are nonnegative.
Norms, scales, and maximum-over-empty-set conventions are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_k^{\mathrm{dc}}=(r_k^{\mathrm{dual}},r_k^{\mathrm{comp}},r_k^{\mathrm{weak}}(\gamma),r_k^{\mathrm{leak}})\in\mathbb R_+^4\) is the dual-complementarity diagnostic vector.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(r_k^{\mathrm{comp}}=0\iff\lambda_{k,i}c_i(x_k)=0\) for every \(i\).
\(r_k^{\mathrm{weak}}(\gamma)=0\iff\lambda_{k,i}\ge\gamma\) for every selected index.
\(r_k^{\mathrm{leak}}=0\) and dual feasibility imply \(\lambda_{k,i}=0\) for every unselected index.
special_cases_latex: With \(\gamma=0\), selected dual weakness detects only negative selected multipliers and does not test strict complementarity.
At an exactly complementary, dual-feasible pair, the first two residuals vanish.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\gamma>0\) and both weakness and leakage vanish, the positive multiplier support is contained in the selected set and every selected multiplier exceeds the margin.
Complementarity residuals should be interpreted with primal and dual feasibility residuals.
boundary_notes: A small product \(\lambda_i c_i\) may result from small multiplier, small slack, or both.
The interface does not establish uniqueness of multipliers or correctness of the estimated set.

notation.meaning: failure of selected multipliers to reach the declared margin
positive multiplier mass on unselected constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-dual complementarity diagnostic interface
Dual Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual diagnostics use multiplier sign and magnitude to flag infeasibility, positive support, and weak activity. With separated multiplier limits, the positive-support classification stabilizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\) with KKT multipliers \(\lambda_i\ge0\), choose tolerances \(\delta_k^{\mathrm d},\tau_k^{\mathrm d}\ge0\). At an approximate primal-dual pair \((x^k,\lambda^k)\), declare index \(i\) dual-infeasible if \(\lambda_i^k<-\delta_k^{\mathrm d}\), dual-positive if \(\lambda_i^k>\tau_k^{\mathrm d}\), and dual-weak otherwise. Thus \(A_k^{\mathrm d}=\{i:\lambda_i^k>\tau_k^{\mathrm d}\}\). If \(\lambda^k\to\lambda^*\), the threshold tends to zero, and zero-component errors are little-o of the threshold, then \(A_k^{\mathrm d}\) eventually equals the positive support of \(\lambda^*\).
assumptions_latex: Inequalities use \(g_i(x)\le0\) and nonnegative KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_k^{\mathrm d}=\{i:\lambda_i^k>\tau_k^{\mathrm d}\}\) is the dual-active estimate, with negative components beyond tolerance flagged as dual-infeasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-sign and magnitude diagnostics for inequality activity under the nonnegative-multiplier convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementarity diagnostics measure products of nonnegative multipliers and slacks. A large product signals inconsistency; a small product alone cannot determine whether slack or multiplier is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible inequality pair satisfying \(g_i(x^k)\le0\) and \(\lambda_i^k\ge0\), define the complementarity residual \(c_i^k=\lambda_i^k[-g_i(x^k)]\) and aggregate residual \(c_k=\|c^k\|_\infty\). Given \(\kappa_k\ge0\), approximate complementary slackness holds when \(c_k\le\kappa_k\). A scale-aware alternative tests \(c_i^k\le\kappa_k(1+|g_i(x^k)|+|\lambda_i^k|)\) for every \(i\). A large product identifies an incompatibility between appreciable positive slack and appreciable positive multiplier, but a small product alone does not decide which factor should be classified as zero.
assumptions_latex: Constraints use \(g_i(x)\le0\), so feasible slack is \(-g_i(x)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approximate complementarity is certified by \(\max_i\lambda_i^k[-g_i(x^k)]\le\kappa_k\), subject to the chosen scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled residual test for approximate complementary slackness of inequality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual–Complementarity Consistency Checks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal slack, multiplier sign, and complementarity must agree. If the product of inactivity and dual thresholds exceeds complementarity tolerance, conflicting labels are certifiably inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_i^k=-g_i(x^k)\), and choose nonnegative tolerances \(\eta_k\), \(\delta_k\), and \(\kappa_k\). The pair \((x^k,\lambda^k)\) passes the dual-complementarity consistency check when \(s_i^k\ge-\eta_k\), \(\lambda_i^k\ge-\delta_k\), and \(|\lambda_i^ks_i^k|\le\kappa_k\) for every \(i\). If an index also satisfies \(s_i^k>\varepsilon_k>0\), then consistency with a dual-positive label \(\lambda_i^k>\tau_k>0\) requires \(\varepsilon_k\tau_k\le\kappa_k\). Thus \(\varepsilon_k\tau_k>\kappa_k\) is a directly verifiable certificate that the primal-inactive and dual-positive labels cannot both be accepted.
assumptions_latex: Inequalities are written as \(g_i(x)\le0\) with slack \(s_i=-g_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever \(s_i^k>\varepsilon_k\), \(\lambda_i^k>\tau_k\), and \(\varepsilon_k\tau_k>\kappa_k\), the complementarity check must fail for index \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint certificate aligning primal slack, multiplier sign, and approximate complementary slackness.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal I\) be a finite inequality index set, \(\mathcal A^*\subseteq\mathcal I\) a known evaluation target, and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\subseteq\mathcal I\) an estimated active set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Target-dependent offline or benchmark diagnostics for finite-set classification; these are not generally observable during optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathrm{FP}_k:=\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\setminus\mathcal A^*\), \(\mathrm{FN}_k:=\mathcal A^*\setminus\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\), counts \(e_k^{\mathrm{FP}}:=|\mathrm{FP}_k|\), \(e_k^{\mathrm{FN}}:=|\mathrm{FN}_k|\), and total Hamming error \(e_k^{\Delta}:=|\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\triangle\mathcal A^*|=e_k^{\mathrm{FP}}+e_k^{\mathrm{FN}}\). Define rates \(q_k^{\mathrm{FP}}:=e_k^{\mathrm{FP}}/|\mathcal I\setminus\mathcal A^*|\) and \(q_k^{\mathrm{FN}}:=e_k^{\mathrm{FN}}/|\mathcal A^*|\), assigning rate zero when its denominator is zero. These quantities form the activity-classification error diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classification diagnostics compare an estimated set with a known target. False positives are inactive constraints incorrectly selected, and false negatives are active constraints omitted. Their counts add to the symmetric-difference or Hamming error. Normalized rates divide by the number of truly inactive or active constraints, with an explicit zero-denominator convention.
assumptions_latex: The target \(\mathcal A^*\) is available and fixed.
The zero-denominator convention for normalized rates is explicitly adopted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_k^{\mathrm{class}}=(e_k^{\mathrm{FP}},e_k^{\mathrm{FN}},e_k^{\Delta},q_k^{\mathrm{FP}},q_k^{\mathrm{FN}})\) is the activity-classification error vector, and \(e_k^{\Delta}=0\iff\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A^*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(e_k^{\Delta}=\|\mathbf1_{\widehat{\mathcal A}_k}-\mathbf1_{\mathcal A^*}\|_1\).
Exact classification is equivalent to the conjunction \(e_k^{\mathrm{FP}}=0\) and \(e_k^{\mathrm{FN}}=0\).
Precision and recall, when their denominators are nonzero, are \(|\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\cap\mathcal A^*|/|\widehat{\mathcal A}_k|\) and \(1-q_k^{\mathrm{FN}}\), respectively.
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal A^*=\varnothing\), every selected index is a false positive and the false-negative rate is defined as zero.
If \(\mathcal A^*=\mathcal I\), every omitted index is a false negative and the false-positive rate is defined as zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: Finite exact identification is equivalent to \(e_k^{\Delta}=0\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
For finite \(\mathcal I\), convergence \(e_k^{\Delta}\to0\) implies eventual exact classification because the error is integer-valued.
boundary_notes: These diagnostics require the target and therefore are usually unavailable as run-time stopping tests.
When only a multiplier-dependent partial target is identifiable, errors must be defined relative to that target rather than silently using the full active set.
review_flags: The finite-set metrics are explicit, but no inspected source was verified for this optimization-specific diagnostic package and its conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: False-positive and false-negative activity diagnostics
Inactive-Slack Certificate for Absence of False Activity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: False activity is impossible when threshold plus constraint-value error is smaller than the minimum true inactive slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\), \(\widehat A_k=\{i:g_i(x^k)\ge-\varepsilon_k\}\), and \(\sigma^*=\min_{i\notin A^*}[-g_i(x^*)]\), with \(\sigma^*=+\infty\) if every constraint is active. If \(e_k=\max_i|g_i(x^k)-g_i(x^*)|\) satisfies \(e_k+\varepsilon_k<\sigma^*\), then \(\widehat A_k\subseteq A^*\), so the false-activity set is empty.
assumptions_latex: The inequality index set is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_k+\varepsilon_k<\sigma^*\implies\widehat A_k\setminus A^*=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative sufficient condition excluding truly inactive constraints from a primal threshold estimate.

notation.meaning: minimum slack among constraints inactive at the reference point
maximum constraint-value error relative to the reference point

knowledge_statements.title: False-Activity Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: False activity consists of estimated-active constraints that are inactive at the reference solution. Its persistence indicates excessive thresholds, iterate error, or an uncertain reference set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\) be the reference active set and let \(\widehat A_k\) be an estimated active set. The false-activity set and rate are \(F_k=\widehat A_k\setminus A^*\) and \(r_k^{\mathrm{false}}=|F_k|/\max\{1,|\widehat A_k|\}\). If the estimator is primal-threshold based, \(\widehat A_k=\{i:g_i(x^k)\ge-\varepsilon_k\}\), each false-active index satisfies \(g_i(x^*)<0\) but \(g_i(x^k)\ge-\varepsilon_k\). Persistent false activity therefore signals that the threshold has not fallen below the inactive slack margin, the iterate error remains too large, or the reference classification is uncertain.
assumptions_latex: A reference feasible point \(x^*\) and estimated set \(\widehat A_k\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_k=\widehat A_k\setminus A^*\), and exact identification requires \(F_k=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-based diagnostic for constraints incorrectly declared active.

source_witnesses.locator: 10.3 Active Set Methods p. 236

knowledge_statements.title: Missed-Activity Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Missed activity consists of truly active constraints absent from the estimate. A primal threshold has no misses once it dominates every residual error on the active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\) and let \(\widehat A_k\) be an estimated active set. The missed-activity set and rate are \(M_k=A^*\setminus\widehat A_k\) and \(r_k^{\mathrm{miss}}=|M_k|/\max\{1,|A^*|\}\). For the primal rule \(\widehat A_k=\{i:g_i(x^k)\ge-\varepsilon_k\}\), an active index is missed exactly when \(g_i(x^k)<-\varepsilon_k\). Thus \(M_k=\varnothing\) whenever \(\max_{i\in A^*}|g_i(x^k)|\le\varepsilon_k\). Persistent misses indicate a threshold smaller than active residual error, an inaccurate iterate, or an incorrect reference active set.
assumptions_latex: A reference feasible point \(x^*\) and estimated set \(\widehat A_k\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_k=A^*\setminus\widehat A_k\); for the stated primal rule, \(\max_{i\in A^*}|g_i(x^k)|\le\varepsilon_k\) implies \(M_k=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-based diagnostic for truly active constraints omitted by an estimator.

source_witnesses.locator: 10.3 Active Set Methods p. 236

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation-Robust Activity Labels
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slack label is robust when the entire admissible slack interval lies in its definite classification region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact slack be \(s_i\ge0\), let \(\widetilde s_i\) satisfy \(|\widetilde s_i-s_i|\le\rho_i\), and let \(0\le\varepsilon^-<\varepsilon^+\). If \(\widetilde s_i+\rho_i\le\varepsilon^-\), every admissible exact slack is in the active region. If \(\widetilde s_i-\rho_i\ge\varepsilon^+\), every admissible exact slack is in the inactive region. Otherwise the error interval is not contained in either definite region, so the error bound alone certifies neither label.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde s_i+\rho_i\le\varepsilon^-\) certifies activity, while \(\widetilde s_i-\rho_i\ge\varepsilon^+\) certifies inactivity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certification of activity labels when computed slacks have bounded error.

knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Classification Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two ordered slack thresholds define mutually exclusive active, inactive, and ambiguous regions; the open region between the thresholds is the ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), let \(s_i^k=-g_i(x^k)\) and choose thresholds \(0\le\varepsilon_k^-<\varepsilon_k^+\). Classify index \(i\) as active if \(s_i^k\le\varepsilon_k^-\), inactive if \(s_i^k\ge\varepsilon_k^+\), and ambiguous if \(\varepsilon_k^-<s_i^k<\varepsilon_k^+\). The ambiguity set is \(U_k=\{i:\varepsilon_k^-<s_i^k<\varepsilon_k^+\}\). These three labels are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k=\{i:\varepsilon_k^-<s_i^k<\varepsilon_k^+\}\) contains precisely the indices not classified as active or inactive by the primal band.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three-way primal classification retaining an unresolved band between active and inactive slack thresholds.

notation.meaning: measured primal slack of constraint i
inner active and outer inactive slack thresholds

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider the convex quadratic program \(\min_x q(x)=\tfrac12x^TGx+c^Tx\) subject to \(a_i^Tx=b_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\), where \(G\succeq0\). Let \(\mathcal A(x)=\mathcal E\cup\{i\in\mathcal I:a_i^Tx=b_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth quadratic models with affine constraints; this is the navigation-level interface, not a particular factorization, pivot rule, or SQP implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An active-set working-set method interface is an iteration state \(s_k=(x_k,\mathcal W_k)\), with \(\mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal W_k\subseteq\mathcal A(x_k)\), together with (i) the equality-constrained subproblem \[\min_p\ \tfrac12p^TGp+(Gx_k+c)^Tp\quad\text{subject to}\quad a_i^Tp=0\quad(i\in\mathcal W_k),\] and (ii) an update map \(\mathcal U\) that returns \((x_{k+1},\mathcal W_{k+1})\) by admitting blocking constraints or releasing working inequalities whose subproblem multipliers violate dual feasibility. The working gradients are required to be linearly independent whenever the subproblem solver uses a full-row-rank constraint representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quadratic program, the interface state is a point \(x_k\) and a working set \(\mathcal W_k\) containing all equalities and selected active inequalities. The method solves the quadratic model with working constraints imposed as equalities, then updates the point and working set by adding blocking constraints or dropping constraints with dual-infeasible multipliers. Linear independence of represented working gradients is part of the interface when required by the subproblem solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_k=(x_k,\mathcal W_k)\longmapsto (p_k,\lambda_k)\longmapsto s_{k+1}=\mathcal U(s_k,p_k,\lambda_k),\qquad \mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal W_k\subseteq\mathcal A(x_k).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(Z_k\) spans \(\ker A_{\mathcal W_k}\), the subproblem may equivalently be represented in reduced coordinates by \(p=Z_kz\) and \(\min_z\tfrac12z^TZ_k^TGZ_kz+(Gx_k+c)^TZ_kz\).
special_cases_latex: For a primal-feasible method, every \(x_k\) satisfies all original constraints.
For a strictly convex quadratic, \(G\succ0\) makes every equality-constrained working-set subproblem uniquely solvable when its constraints are consistent.
immediate_consequences_latex: If the subproblem returns \(p_k=0\) and all working inequality multipliers are nonnegative, the convex-QP KKT conditions hold.
A nonworking inequality that limits the feasible step becomes a candidate for admission.
boundary_notes: The working set need not equal the complete active set when several constraints are simultaneously active.
The definition does not prescribe a linear-algebra realization or a tie-breaking rule.

notation.meaning: Active-constraint index set at the point.
Working constraints treated as equalities at iteration \(k\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min_x\tfrac12x^TGx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\ge b\), introduce multipliers \(\lambda\ge0\), primal residual \(r_p=Ax-b\), and dual residual \(r_d=Gx+c-A^T\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A classification of finite-dimensional active-set methods by the feasibility invariant maintained during their iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasibility-oriented active-set family is a class of working-set iterations classified by which part of the KKT feasibility system it preserves before termination: \[\mathfrak M_P:\ r_p^k\ge0;\qquad \mathfrak M_D:\ r_d^k=0,\ \lambda^k\ge0;\qquad \mathfrak M_{PD}:\ (r_p^k,r_d^k,\lambda^k)\ \text{are updated jointly under an explicitly declared primal-dual regime}.\] Every member also carries a working set \(\mathcal W_k\) that selects the complementarity pairs provisionally treated as active. The family label concerns an iteration invariant, not merely whether the final solution is primal and dual feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility-oriented active-set methods are classified by the KKT feasibility conditions they maintain along the iteration. A primal family keeps \(Ax_k-b\ge0\); a dual family keeps stationarity and nonnegative multipliers; and a primal-dual family updates both sides under a declared joint regime. Each method uses a working set to select provisional complementarity pairs. The classification concerns intermediate iterates, since every successful method seeks both primal and dual feasibility at termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\{\text{feasibility-oriented active-set methods}\}=\mathfrak M_P\cup\mathfrak M_D\cup\mathfrak M_{PD},\] where membership is determined by the stated iteration invariant.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using slacks \(y=Ax-b\), primal feasibility is \(y\ge0\), dual feasibility is \(Gx+c-A^T\lambda=0\) with \(\lambda\ge0\), and complementarity is \(y_i\lambda_i=0\).
special_cases_latex: The classical primal convex-QP active-set method belongs to \(\mathfrak M_P\).
The Goldfarb–Idnani convex-QP method belongs to \(\mathfrak M_D\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A method may begin infeasible on the side it does not preserve and restore that feasibility through working-set changes.
The three labels do not imply different terminal KKT systems.
boundary_notes: Interior-point methods that keep all complementarity pairs interior are outside this active-set classification.
An algorithm that preserves neither primal nor dual feasibility requires an additional regime specification before it can be classified as primal-dual.

notation.meaning: Primal-feasible, dual-feasible, and joint primal-dual method families.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized Tangency Need Not Preserve Nonlinear Feasibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direction tangent to a curved active constraint can leave the feasible set immediately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:c(x)=1-\|x\|^2\ge0\}\), take \(x=(1,0)\), and choose \(p=(0,1)\). Then \(c(x)=0\) and \(\nabla c(x)^\top p=0\), but \(c(x+\alpha p)=-\alpha^2<0\) for every \(\alpha>0\). Thus a straight tangent step may admit no positive feasibility-preserving step length on a curved boundary.
assumptions_latex: The step follows the straight path x+\alpha p.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla c(x)^\top p=0\quad\text{but}\quad c(x+\alpha p)<0\ \text{for every }\alpha>0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature boundary for feasible active-set steps along a straight line.

notation.meaning: closed unit disk represented by c(x)>=0

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Feasible Active-Set Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a feasible point, each step preserves feasibility, admits newly blocking constraints, and releases constraints with incorrect multiplier signs until the working-set KKT conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)\ge 0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Given a feasible \(x_0\), choose \(W_0\subseteq\{i:c_i(x_0)=0\}\). At iteration \(k\), compute a direction \(p_k\) from a local subproblem imposing \(\nabla c_i(x_k)^\top p=0\) for \(i\in W_k\). Select \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\) so that \(x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) remains feasible and satisfies the chosen decrease test. Add constraints attaining the limiting feasible step; when \(p_k=0\), remove a working constraint having an inadmissible multiplier. Stop when \(p_k=0\) and all working-set multipliers satisfy the KKT sign condition; output \(x_k\).
assumptions_latex: The direction subproblem and line search are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted iterate is feasible, and termination under the stated test yields the working-set KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-iterate active-set scheme for smooth inequality-constrained nonlinear programs.

notation.meaning: indices treated as active at iteration k

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G\succeq0\) and consider \(\min_x q(x)=\tfrac12x^TGx+c^Tx\) subject to \(a_i^Tx=b_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical primal active-set iterations for convex quadratic programs, initialized at a primal-feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal-feasible active-set method is a sequence \((x_k,\mathcal W_k)\) such that, for every \(k\), \[a_i^Tx_k=b_i\ (i\in\mathcal E),\qquad a_i^Tx_k\ge b_i\ (i\in\mathcal I),\qquad \mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal W_k\subseteq\mathcal A(x_k).\] It computes \(p_k\) from the equality-constrained working-set subproblem and sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), where \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\) is the largest admissible step preserving every inequality. A blocking inequality attaining this bound may be admitted; when \(p_k=0\), a working inequality with negative multiplier may be released.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-feasible active-set method starts from a feasible point and keeps every iterate feasible for the original quadratic program. Its working constraints are active and are imposed as equalities in the step subproblem. The step is truncated at the largest value that preserves all inequalities. A constraint that blocks the step may enter the working set, while a working inequality with a negative multiplier may leave when the current point minimizes over the working face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_0\in\mathcal F\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_k\in\mathcal F\ \text{for every generated }k,\qquad \mathcal F=\{x:A_{\\mathcal E}x=b_{\mathcal E},\ A_{\mathcal I}x\ge b_{\mathcal I}\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With slacks \(y_k=Ax_k-b\), primal feasibility preservation is exactly \(y_k\ge0\) for all \(k\).
special_cases_latex: For bound constraints, working variables are fixed at their active bounds and free variables form the reduced subproblem.
If the full subproblem step is feasible, then \(\alpha_k=1\) and no blocking constraint is admitted.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every accumulation point is approached from within the primal feasible region.
At \(p_k=0\), nonnegative working inequality multipliers complete the KKT test for a convex QP.
boundary_notes: A feasible starting point is required; a phase-I procedure may be used to obtain it.
Degeneracy can give \(\alpha_k=0\) or multiple blocking constraints and requires a safeguard or tie rule.

notation.meaning: Largest feasible step length, capped at one.
