knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Feasible QP Active-Set Scheme
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method preserves nonnegative multipliers, changes dual faces by deleting zeroed multipliers or admitting violated primal constraints, and stops at a primal-dual KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\lambda^0\ge0\) and repeatedly solve the dual quadratic model on the face determined by the positive or free dual coordinates. If a face step would make a multiplier negative, shorten it to the first zero multiplier and delete that coordinate. At a face maximizer, if \(A^\top p(\lambda)\not\ge b\), admit an index with \(a_i^\top p(\lambda)<b_i\) and continue on the enlarged face. Stop when \(A^\top p(\lambda)\ge b\). The stopping pair satisfies stationarity by construction, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity.
assumptions_latex: Degenerate ties use a deterministic anti-cycling rule if finite termination is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A^\top p\ge b,\quad Hp+g-A\lambda=0,\quad \lambda\ge0,\quad \lambda_i(a_i^\top p-b_i)=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set solution of the nonnegative-bound dual of a strictly convex QP.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-QP Dual-Feasibility Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible method maintains nonnegative dual variables for the bound-constrained concave QP while reconstructed primal points may violate primal constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_p\tfrac12p^\top Hp+g^\top p\) subject to \(A^\top p\ge b\), with \(H\succ0\), the Lagrange dual is \(\max_{\lambda\ge0} d(\lambda)\), where \(d(\lambda)=b^\top\lambda-\tfrac12(g-A\lambda)^\top H^{-1}(g-A\lambda)\), and the associated primal point is \(p(\lambda)=H^{-1}(A\lambda-g)\). Thus dual feasibility is exactly \(\lambda\ge0\), while \(p(\lambda)\) may remain primal infeasible until dual optimality.
assumptions_latex: Primal inequalities are written as \(A^\top p\ge b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda\ge0\text{ is dual feasibility, and }p(\lambda)=H^{-1}(A\lambda-g).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit dual representation defining the invariant maintained by dual-feasible active-set methods.

notation.meaning: primal point reconstructed from a dual vector

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Feasible Active-Set Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-feasible working-set interface for a strictly convex quadratic program with linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \tfrac12x^THx+g^Tx\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax\le b,
\]
where \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite, \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Initialize \(x_0\), a working set \(W_0\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and multipliers \(\lambda_{0,W_0}\ge0\) satisfying \(Hx_0+g+A_{W_0}^T\lambda_{0,W_0}=0\), with nonworking multipliers set to zero; primal feasibility is not required. Select a violated inequality and compute the standard working-set KKT correction while preserving stationarity. Move no farther than the first value at which a retained multiplier would become negative; at such a breakpoint, delete a zero-multiplier working constraint and resolve. When the selected violated constraint can be incorporated without violating multiplier nonnegativity, add it and continue. Stop when \(Ax_k\le b\). At termination, stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain stationarity and nonnegative working multipliers while repairing primal violations, deleting constraints at multiplier breakpoints and adding violated constraints until the quadratic-programming KKT conditions hold.
assumptions_latex: The initial working-set representation satisfies \(Hx_0+g+A_{W_0}^T\lambda_{0,W_0}=0\) and \(\lambda_{0,W_0}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When primal feasibility is attained without losing the maintained stationarity and dual-feasibility invariants, the resulting point is the unique global minimizer of the strictly convex quadratic program.

notation.meaning: multipliers of the current working inequalities

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G\succ0\) and consider \(\min_x\tfrac12x^TGx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\ge b\), with multipliers \(\lambda\ge0\) and stationarity \(Gx+c-A^T\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual active-set methods for strictly convex quadratic programs, including the Goldfarb–Idnani feasibility regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A dual-feasible active-set method is a sequence \((x_k,\lambda_k,\mathcal W_k)\) satisfying, at every iteration, \[Gx_k+c-A^T\lambda_k=0,
\qquad \lambda_k\ge0,
\qquad (\lambda_k)_i=0\quad(i\notin\mathcal W_k),\] while primal feasibility \(Ax_k\ge b\) is not required until termination. The method selects a violated primal constraint, changes \(\mathcal W_k\), and moves through stationary primal-dual pairs while retaining nonnegative multipliers; it terminates when \(Ax_k\ge b\), at which point primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and working-set complementarity give the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible active-set method for a strictly convex quadratic program maintains stationarity and nonnegative multipliers throughout. Multipliers outside the working set are zero, but the current primal point may violate constraints. The working set is changed to remove primal infeasibilities while preserving dual feasibility. Once the primal point is feasible, the maintained stationarity, multiplier signs, and working-set complementarity form the complete KKT system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Gx_k+c-A^T\lambda_k=0,\ \lambda_k\ge0\quad\text{for all }k;\qquad Ax_k\ge b\ \Longrightarrow\ (x_k,\lambda_k)\text{ satisfies the QP KKT system}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The method is a primal active-set method applied to the dual quadratic program, expressed in primal-dual variables.
special_cases_latex: With \(\mathcal W_0=\varnothing\), one may initialize \(x_0=-G^{-1}c\) and \(\lambda_0=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: No separate primal-feasible phase is required to initialize the strict-convexity regime.
If no admissible working-set release can restore a violated primal constraint, the method can certify infeasibility under its stated conditions.
boundary_notes: The stated initialization and unique primal recovery require \(G\succ0\).
A constraint made feasible need not remain feasible during later dual-feasible iterations.

notation.meaning: Indices allowed to carry nonzero multipliers.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a convex QP write the KKT variables as \((x,y,\lambda)\), where \(y=Ax-b\), and residuals \(r_p=Ax-y-b\), \(r_d=Gx+c-A^T\lambda\), and \(r_c=Y\Lambda\mathbf1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An interface definition for active-set methods that update primal and dual feasibility jointly; it excludes interior-point iterates with every complementarity pair strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A primal-dual feasibility-regime active-set method is an iteration \((x_k,y_k,\lambda_k,\mathcal W_k)\) equipped with a declared regime map \(\rho_k\) specifying which of \(r_p^k=0\), \(r_d^k=0\), \(y_k\ge0\), and \(\lambda_k\ge0\) are exact invariants and which are restoration targets. Its working set enforces the active complementarity pattern \[i\in\mathcal W_k\Rightarrow y_i^k=0,
\qquad i\notin\mathcal W_k\Rightarrow \lambda_i^k=0.\] Each update must either reduce a designated nonzero residual or change this complementarity pattern, and termination requires \(r_p=r_d=0\), \(y\ge0\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(Y\Lambda\mathbf1=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual feasibility-regime active-set method updates primal variables, slacks, multipliers, and a working set together. A regime map declares which primal or dual conditions are maintained exactly and which are being restored. Working indices have zero slack, while nonworking indices have zero multiplier. A legitimate update reduces a targeted residual or changes that complementarity pattern. Termination requires the full primal-dual KKT system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{term}(x,y,\lambda,\mathcal W)\iff r_p=0,\ r_d=0,\ y\ge0,\ \lambda\ge0,\ Y\Lambda\mathbf1=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The working set selects a complementary basis: every pair \((y_i,\lambda_i)\) has at least one component fixed to zero.
special_cases_latex: The primal-feasible regime fixes \(r_p=0\) and \(y\ge0\) throughout.
The dual-feasible regime fixes \(r_d=0\) and \(\lambda\ge0\) throughout.
immediate_consequences_latex: Primal and dual active-set methods are boundary regimes of this joint interface.
The regime declaration makes intermediate infeasibility mathematically explicit rather than treating it as an implementation detail.
boundary_notes: The source establishes the primal, dual, and primal-dual classification, but individual primal-dual algorithms may impose stronger invariants.
Perturbed complementarity \(y_i\lambda_i>0\) for every index describes an interior-point rather than an active-set state.

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrices formed from slacks and multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Method Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration jointly updates primal variables and active multipliers through a KKT system, revising the active set until feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity residuals are small.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)\ge0\), initialize \((x_0,\lambda_0)\) and an estimated active set \(W_0\). At iteration \(k\), solve a linearized KKT system on \(W_k\),
\[
\begin{bmatrix}B_k&-J_{W_k}(x_k)^\top\\J_{W_k}(x_k)&0\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}p_k\\\delta\lambda_{W_k}\end{bmatrix}
=-\begin{bmatrix}\nabla f(x_k)-J_{W_k}(x_k)^\top\lambda_{W_k}\\c_{W_k}(x_k)\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Choose a globalization step length, update \((x,\lambda)\), add sufficiently violated constraints, and delete indices with persistently negative multipliers. Stop when primal residual, stationarity residual, and complementarity residual satisfy prescribed tolerances; output \((x_k,\lambda_k,W_k)\).
assumptions_latex: Each selected KKT system is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an approximate primal-dual KKT triple at the prescribed residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set primal–dual Newton interface for smooth inequality constraints.

notation.meaning: Jacobian rows of constraints indexed by W

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic Linearized-Feasibility Variant
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic variables keep an infeasible-start linearized subproblem feasible and measure unresolved violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equalities \(h(x)=0\) and inequalities \(c(x)\ge0\), introduce nonnegative elastic variables \(u^+,u^-,s\) and impose \[h(x_k)+J_h(x_k)p=u^+-u^-,\qquad c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)p+s\ge0.\] Minimize the local objective model plus \(\rho\mathbf1^\top(u^++u^-+s)\), subject to any step bounds. If the step domain contains \(p=0\), the elastic subproblem is feasible; zero elastic variables recover ordinary linearized feasibility, while positive elastic variables quantify unresolved linearized violation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infeasible-start subproblem made feasible by penalized elastic residual variables.

notation.meaning: nonnegative equality and inequality elastic variables

knowledge_statements.title: Filter-Globalized Infeasible-Start Variant
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter accepts a trial that sufficiently improves violation or objective relative to every stored pair, without using one penalty function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a filter \(\mathcal F_k\) of violation-objective pairs. For declared margins \(\gamma_v,\gamma_f\in(0,1)\), call a trial \(y\) acceptable if for every \((v_\ell,f_\ell)\in\mathcal F_k\), \[v(y)\le(1-\gamma_v)v_\ell\quad\text{or}\quad f(y)\le f_\ell-\gamma_fv_\ell.\] Insert an accepted pair and remove pairs it dominates. If no trial satisfies this predicate and any separately declared model-agreement test, invoke the method's restoration mechanism.
assumptions_latex: Any required model-agreement test is declared separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\text{ accepted}\Rightarrow\forall(v_\ell,f_\ell)\in\mathcal F_k:\ v(y)\le(1-\gamma_v)v_\ell\ \lor\ f(y)\le f_\ell-\gamma_fv_\ell.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty-free acceptance based on nondominance in objective–violation space.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Penalty Merit Infeasible-Start Variant
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit variant accepts possibly infeasible trials through Armijo decrease of an objective-plus-violation penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(x)\ge0\) measure violation and \(\phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho v(x)\). From an admitted infeasible iterate, compute a trial direction from a selected relaxed or elastic subproblem. When \(\phi_\rho'(x_k;p_k)<0\), accept a step satisfying \[\phi_\rho(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le\phi_\rho(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_k\phi_\rho'(x_k;p_k),\qquad 0<\sigma<1.\] The accepted point need not be feasible.
assumptions_latex: The selected violation function has a finite directional derivative along \(p_k\).
Trial points remain in the functions' domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi_\rho(x_{k+1})<\phi_\rho(x_k)\text{ for every accepted nonzero step}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Merit-function globalization as one distinct infeasible-start framework.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Linearization at an Infeasible Start
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an infeasible point with zero constraint gradient, the linearized equality system can be inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(h(x)=x^2+1=0\) at \(x_k=0\). Its linearization is \(h(0)+h'(0)p=1=0\), which has no solution. Smoothness and an arbitrary starting point therefore do not ensure consistency of an unrelaxed linearized-feasibility subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{p:h(0)+h'(0)p=0\}=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an unrelaxed linearized-feasibility subproblem.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Start Method Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible-start method admits violated initial points and remains well defined there; the label specifies neither globalization nor convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An iterative constrained-optimization method is an infeasible-start method if its admissible initialization set contains at least one point outside the target feasible set and its iteration is well defined at every admitted infeasible initial point. This designation does not select a merit function, filter, elastic formulation, or restoration rule and does not by itself imply convergence.
assumptions_latex: All quantities required by the selected iteration are defined at admitted infeasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x_0\notin\mathcal F\text{ admissible with the iteration well defined at }x_0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Umbrella definition independent of globalization and feasibility mechanisms.

notation.meaning: feasible set of the target problem

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Start Method Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set method allowing initial and intermediate constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(c(x)\ge0\), accept arbitrary \(x_0\) and initialize \(W_0\). At iteration \(k\), compute a step \(p_k\) from a working-set subproblem whose linearized constraints include \(h(x_k)+J_h(x_k)p=0\) and \(c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^\top p=0\) for \(i\in W_k\). Select \(\alpha_k\) by a merit or filter test balancing objective reduction and violation reduction, then update the working set from blocking, violated, and multiplier-sign information. Stop when feasibility and KKT residuals meet tolerance; otherwise invoke restoration if no acceptable trial step exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrary initial point is allowed; globalization balances objective and violation reduction, while restoration handles failure to obtain an acceptable step.
assumptions_latex: The local subproblem supplies a direction or reports failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method defines iterates without requiring initial feasibility and outputs an approximate KKT point when its stopping test succeeds.

knowledge_statements.title: Abstract Main–Restoration Control Transfer
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration receives control after main-phase failure and returns control only after both restoration progress and main-phase admissibility are certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the main phase cannot certify an acceptable step, preserve its state and invoke a restoration solver using a declared nonnegative violation function. Resume the main phase only after the restoration phase certifies its declared progress predicate \(\mathcal P_R(x^R,y)\) and the receiving main-phase entry predicate \(\mathcal E_M(y)\). A declared restoration-stationarity result and an operational failure are distinct exits and do not authorize resumption.
assumptions_latex: The main phase has a declared step-acceptance and entry test.
The restoration phase preserves all inviolable domain restrictions and declares its progress and exit predicates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{resume}\iff\mathcal P_R(x^R,y)\land\mathcal E_M(y).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-neutral restoration invocation and classified return procedure.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Violation-Reduction Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-factor violation reduction certifies progress but not feasibility or main-phase admissibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\ge0\), let \(v(x^R)>0\), and fix \(\eta\in(0,1)\). Then \(v(y)\le\eta v(x^R)\) certifies strict relative reduction of the declared violation measure. It does not alone certify feasibility, well-posedness of a main subproblem, or permission to resume the main phase.
assumptions_latex: \(v\) is nonnegative on the restoration domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(y)\le\eta v(x^R)<v(x^R),\qquad \mathrm{resume}\text{ additionally requires }\mathcal E_M(y).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One conventional quantitative restoration-progress predicate, separate from main-phase admissibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationary Restoration Does Not Certify Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive stationary violation does not certify infeasibility because feasible points may still exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(x)\ge0\) be a differentiable constraint-violation measure. A restoration point \(\bar x\) satisfying \(v(\bar x)>0\) and \(\nabla v(\bar x)=0\) certifies only first-order stationarity for the violation problem. It does not certify infeasibility of the original constraints unless an additional global lower-bound certificate establishes \(\inf_x v(x)>0\). For example, \(v(x)=(x^2-1)^2\) has \(v(0)=1\) and \(v'(0)=0\), while \(v(\pm1)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(\bar x)>0,\ \nabla v(\bar x)=0\ \not\Rightarrow\ \inf_x v(x)>0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary of termination at a positive stationary value of a violation function.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Neutral Restoration Status Contract
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface distinguishes successful restoration, restoration stationarity, and failure without requiring transfer of solver-specific state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restoration invocation returns \((y,\sigma)\), where \(y\) respects the inviolable domain restrictions and \(\sigma\in\{\mathrm{restored},\mathrm{stationary},\mathrm{failed}\}\). The status \(\mathrm{restored}\) asserts \(\mathcal P_R(x^R,y)\land\mathcal E_M(y)\); \(\mathrm{stationary}\) asserts only the declared stationarity test for the restoration problem; and \(\mathrm{failed}\) asserts that neither successful return nor restoration stationarity was certified. Working sets, multipliers, and factorizations are optional solver-specific payloads.
assumptions_latex: The restoration and main phases declare their domain, progress, stationarity, and entry predicates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma=\mathrm{restored}\Rightarrow\mathcal P_R(x^R,y)\land\mathcal E_M(y),\qquad \sigma=\mathrm{stationary}\not\Rightarrow y\text{ is feasible}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal exit semantics without mandatory working-set or multiplier transfer.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Restoration Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restoration phase for an infeasible-start active-set or SQP method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the violation measure \(v(x)=\|h(x)\|+\|[c(x)]_-\|\), where \([z]_-\) is the componentwise negative part. Given a main-phase iterate \(x_k\) at which no acceptable step is produced, initialize \(y_0=x_k\) and approximately minimize \(v(y)\), subject to any required bounds, using restoration steps and working-set updates. Return \(y_j\) to the main phase when \(v(y_j)\le\eta v(x_k)\) for a fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\) and the main subproblem is again well posed. Otherwise terminate with a restoration-failure report or a stationary point of the violation problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the main phase cannot accept a step, restoration reduces a constraint-violation measure and returns control after sufficient reduction, or reports restoration failure.
assumptions_latex: The violation subproblem respects any inviolable bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns a point with prescribed relative violation reduction or an explicit restoration-failure status.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restoration interface is mathematically plausible, but no source is supplied for the particular violation measure, relative-reduction return test, or stated failure outcomes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed universal data contract between main and restoration phases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restoration invocation receives \(S_k=(x_k,W_k,\mu_k,\mathcal B_k)\) and returns \(R_j=(y_j,\widehat W_j,\widehat\mu_j,\sigma_j)\), after which mapping, domain, rank, and multiplier-sign checks are required before resuming the main phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed contract requires every restoration interface to transfer working sets, multipliers, bounds, and a progress status.
assumptions_latex: Constraint identities and the main phase's rank and sign conventions are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_k\longmapsto R_j\text{ is accepted only after mapping, domain, rank, and dual validation}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative progress certificate separated from the receiving main phase's admissibility test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\ge0\) be the declared constraint-violation measure, let \(x^R\) be the restoration input, and fix \(\eta\in(0,1)\). The inequality \(v(y)\le\eta v(x^R)\) certifies strict relative restoration progress whenever \(v(x^R)>0\). It certifies return to the main phase only in conjunction with that phase's entry predicate \(\mathcal E_M(y)\); violation reduction alone need not make a local subproblem well posed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-factor violation reduction certifies restoration progress, but main-phase resumption additionally requires the receiving solver's entry checks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(x^R)>0\land v(y)\le\eta v(x^R)\Rightarrow v(y)<v(x^R),\quad\text{whereas return requires also }\mathcal E_M(y).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At an iterate \(x_k\), let \(g_k=Gx_k+c\), let \(A_{W_k}\) collect the working-constraint rows, and let \(q_k(p)=\tfrac12p^TGp+g_k^Tp\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The mathematical input-output contract of a working-set subproblem, independent of its direct or iterative linear-algebra implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A working-set subproblem interface is the relation that maps \((G,g_k,A_{W_k})\) to one of the following valid outputs: (i) a stationary pair \((p_k,\lambda_k)\) satisfying \[Gp_k+g_k-A_{W_k}^T\lambda_k=0,
\qquad A_{W_k}p_k=0;\] (ii) a nonzero reduced negative-curvature direction \(d_k\in\ker A_{W_k}\) with \(d_k^TGd_k<0\); or (iii) a declared rank-deficiency or inconsistency status. When \(A_{W_k}\) has full row rank and \(Z_k^TGZ_k\succ0\) for a null-space basis \(Z_k\), output (i) is unique in \(p_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The working-set subproblem interface takes the quadratic model, its gradient, and the working-constraint matrix. It returns either a stationary step and multipliers satisfying the equality-constrained KKT equations, a feasible direction of negative reduced curvature, or an explicit rank/inconsistency status. If the working rows are independent and the reduced Hessian is positive definite, the returned step is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal S(G,g_k,A_{W_k})\in\{(p_k,\lambda_k),\ d_k,\ \mathrm{rank\_failure}\},\] with each output satisfying its stated algebraic certificate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a full-row-rank working matrix, the stationary output solves the saddle-point system \(\begin{bmatrix}G&-A_W^T\\A_W&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g\\0\end{bmatrix}\).
With \(p=Zz\), the stationary output solves \(Z^TGZz=-Z^Tg\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal W_k=\varnothing\), the interface reduces to an unconstrained quadratic subproblem.
If \(p_k=0\), the returned multipliers support the working-set optimality or release test.
immediate_consequences_latex: The outer working-set manager can be specified without selecting a factorization method.
Negative curvature is an explicit alternative output rather than a failed positive-definite solve.
boundary_notes: The interface does not determine the step length against nonworking inequalities.
Rank-deficient working sets require dependency handling not encoded by the ordinary KKT solve.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Equality Inconsistency Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A left-null-space vector having nonzero inner product with the equality right-hand side certifies inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The system \(Ap=r\) is inconsistent if and only if there exists \(y\) such that \(A^\top y=0\) and \(y^\top r\ne0\). Such a vector separates \(r\) from \(\operatorname{range}(A)\) and certifies the inconsistency status returned by the interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ap=r\text{ is inconsistent}\iff\exists y:\ A^\top y=0,\ y^\top r\ne0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable certificate that the affine working equalities admit no step.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-QP Minimizer and Uniqueness Test
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced semidefiniteness certifies global minimality, reduced positive definiteness certifies uniqueness, and reduced nonsingularity characterizes KKT nonsingularity under full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(Ap=r\) is consistent, let \(Z\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\), and let \(p^*\) satisfy the KKT equations. Then \(p^*\) is a global minimizer if and only if \(Z^\top BZ\succeq0\), and it is the unique global minimizer if and only if \(Z^\top BZ\succ0\). If \(A\) has full row rank, the bordered KKT matrix is nonsingular exactly when \(Z^\top BZ\) is nonsingular.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\) and \(Z\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*\in\arg\min_{Ap=r}q(p)\iff Z^\top BZ\succeq0,\qquad p^*\text{ is the unique minimizer}\iff Z^\top BZ\succ0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality classification of a feasible stationary point of an equality-constrained quadratic.

notation.meaning: null-space basis of the working-equality matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Equality-QP Dual
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive-definite curvature, eliminating the primal step gives a concave multiplier dual with no duality gap when the equalities are feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(B\succ0\), the Lagrange dual of
\[\min_p\;g^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Bp\quad\text{subject to }Ap=r\]
is
\[\max_\lambda\;-\tfrac12(g+A^\top\lambda)^\top B^{-1}(g+A^\top\lambda)-r^\top\lambda.\]
When \(Ap=r\) is consistent, the primal and dual optima are attained with equal values, and \(p=-B^{-1}(g+A^\top\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{Ap=r}q(p)=\max_\lambda\left[-\tfrac12(g+A^\top\lambda)^\top B^{-1}(g+A^\top\lambda)-r^\top\lambda\right].
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrange dual of the equality-constrained quadratic when the full Hessian is positive definite.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Quadratic KKT System
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality-constrained quadratic step and its multipliers satisfy a bordered KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Writing the working equalities as \(Ap=r\), a pair \((p,\lambda)\) is stationary for \(q(p)=g^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Bp\) subject to \(Ap=r\) exactly when
\[\begin{bmatrix}B&A^\top\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g\\r\end{bmatrix}.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bp+g+A^\top\lambda=0\quad\text{and}\quad Ap=r.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual system for the working-set equality QP.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Subproblem Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The current working inequalities are imposed as equalities in a quadratic model, which returns a step, multipliers, or a structured failure or negative-curvature status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x_k\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), let \(B_k\) be a symmetric Lagrangian-Hessian model, and let \(W_k\) index inequalities treated as active. The equality-constrained step interface is
\[
\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\;g_k^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top B_kp
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
h(x_k)+J_h(x_k)p=0,\qquad
c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^\top p=0\ \ (i\in W_k).
\]
The interface returns a primal step \(p_k\), associated equality multipliers, and either a success status, an inconsistency status, or a direction of negative curvature when the quadratic model is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed equality-constrained quadratic program is the local subproblem associated with \(W_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic working-set subproblem obtained by treating selected inequalities as equalities.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^m\). Consider \(\min_p\tfrac12p^THp+g^Tp\) subject to \(Ap=h\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained quadratic subproblems, including the homogeneous tangent subproblems used by active-set methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The equality-constrained subproblem interface associates the data \((H,g,A,h)\) with a primal-dual pair \((p,\lambda)\) satisfying \[Hp+g-A^T\lambda=0,
\qquad Ap=h.\] Equivalently, \((p,\lambda)\) solves \[\begin{bmatrix}H&-A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g\\h\end{bmatrix}.\] The interface is regular when \(A\) has full row rank and \(Z^THZ\succ0\) for a basis \(Z\) of \(\ker A\); under these conditions the KKT matrix is nonsingular and the subproblem has a unique primal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-constrained quadratic subproblem maps its Hessian, gradient, constraint matrix, and right-hand side to a step and multiplier satisfying stationarity and the equality constraints. These conditions form the KKT saddle-point system. The interface is regular when the constraint matrix has independent rows and the Hessian is positive definite on its null space; then the KKT matrix is nonsingular and the primal solution is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal E(H,g,A,h)=\{(p,\lambda):Hp+g-A^T\lambda=0,\ Ap=h\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(p=Yp_Y+Zp_Z\), with \([Y\ Z]\) nonsingular and \(AZ=0\), then \(AYp_Y=h\) and \(Z^THZp_Z=-Z^T(g+HYp_Y)\).
special_cases_latex: For an active-set tangent step, \(h=0\).
For \(A=0\) and nonsingular \(H\), the solution is \(p=-H^{-1}g\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive definiteness of \(Z^THZ\) is the relevant second-order condition; full positive definiteness of \(H\) is unnecessary.
The multiplier output supplies the constraint-release test.
boundary_notes: If \(Z^THZ\) is indefinite, a stationary solution can be a saddle point rather than a minimizer.
Dependent equality rows require a rank-revealing representation or removal of redundancy.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\{x:A_{[0m\mathcal E}x=b_{[0m\mathcal E},\ A_{[0m\mathcal I}x\ge b_{[0m\mathcal I}\}\) be a polyhedron, let \(x\in P\), and let \(\mathcal E\subseteq W\subseteq\mathcal A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine faces of polyhedral feasible sets and the null-space reduction used in active-set subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The face associated with the working set \(W\) is \[F_W=P\cap\{z:a_i^Tz=b_i\ \text{for every }i\in W\}.\] Its affine tangent space at \(x\in F_W\) is \[T_W=\{p:A_Wp=0\}=\ker A_W.\] If \(Z_W\) has full-column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z_W)=\ker A_W\), then every tangent displacement has a unique reduced coordinate \(u\) with \(p=Z_Wu\). Consequently, restricting a quadratic model \(\tfrac12p^THp+g^Tp\) to the working face corresponds exactly to the reduced model \(\tfrac12u^TZ_W^THZ_Wu+(Z_W^Tg)^Tu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The working set defines the portion of the feasible polyhedron on which all working constraints are equalities. The tangent displacements along this face are exactly the null space of the working-constraint matrix. Choosing a basis \(Z_W\) for that null space gives a one-to-one representation \(p=Z_Wu\), and the quadratic model restricted to the face becomes a quadratic model with reduced Hessian \(Z_W^THZ_W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[T_W=\ker A_W=\operatorname{range}(Z_W),\qquad q(Z_Wu)=\tfrac12u^TZ_W^THZ_Wu+(Z_W^Tg)^Tu.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(A_W\) has full row rank, \(\dim T_W=n-|W|\).
The face-restricted stationarity condition is \(Z_W^T(HP+g)=0\) for the relevant displacement \(p\).
special_cases_latex: At a vertex with \(\operatorname{rank}A_W=n\), the reduced space is \(\{0\}\).
With no working constraints, \(Z_W\) may be the identity and the reduced model is the original model.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive definiteness of \(Z_W^THZ_W\) characterizes strict convexity along the working face.
Adding an independent working constraint reduces the tangent-space dimension by one.
boundary_notes: If working rows are dependent, \(n-|W|\) is not the reduced dimension; rank must replace cardinality.
The affine face includes feasibility restrictions from nonworking constraints, while its tangent space records only working equalities.

notation.meaning: Polyhedral face selected by the working equalities.
Tangent space of the working affine manifold.
Basis matrix for the reduced space.

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Restricted First-Order Optimality Test
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity on the selected face is equivalent to a tangent-cone variational inequality or normal-cone inclusion; for a convex model it certifies global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y^*=x_k+p^*\in F_W\). The step \(p^*\) is first-order stationary for minimizing differentiable \(q_k\) over \(F_W\) exactly when
\[\nabla q_k(p^*)^\top d\ge0\quad\text{for every }d\in T_{F_W}(y^*),\]
equivalently \(-\nabla q_k(p^*)\in N_{F_W}(y^*)\). If \(q_k\) is convex, this condition is sufficient for global optimality on \(F_W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\nabla q_k(p^*)\in N_{F_W}(x_k+p^*),\text{ with global sufficiency when }q_k\text{ is convex.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational certificate for minimizing a differentiable model over the selected polyhedral face.

notation.meaning: tangent cone to the selected face at y
normal cone to the selected face at y

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Restricted Subproblem Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subproblem minimizes the local quadratic model while the trial point remains on the polyhedral face fixed by the working constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b\}\), let \(x_k\in P\), and let \(W\subseteq\{i:a_i^\top x_k=b_i\}\). The affine face model is \(F_W=\{x\in P:a_i^\top x=b_i\text{ for all }i\in W\}\). For a quadratic step model \(q_k(p)=g_k^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top B_kp\), the face-restricted interface solves
\[
\min_p q_k(p)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_k+p\in F_W,
\]
and returns a minimizing step, a boundary-blocking event, an unboundedness or negative-curvature certificate, or an inconsistency status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible trial points remain in \(F_W\), with all indices in \(W\) fixed at equality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic model restricted to the affine face determined by a working set.

source_witnesses.locator: 10.3 Active Set Methods p. 236

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Quadratic Solution Classification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced quadratic is solvable exactly when its Hessian is positive semidefinite and its linear coefficient lies in the Hessian range; positive definiteness gives uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_R=Z^\top BZ\) and \(g_R=Z^\top(g+Bp_0)\). The reduced quadratic \(g_R^\top z+\tfrac12z^\top H_Rz\) has a global minimizer if and only if \(H_R\succeq0\) and \(g_R\in\operatorname{range}(H_R)\). Its minimizers are exactly the solutions of \(H_Rz=-g_R\), and the minimizer is unique if and only if \(H_R\succ0\). If \(H_R\succeq0\) but \(g_R\notin\operatorname{range}(H_R)\), the model is unbounded below along one orientation of a zero-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \arg\min_z\left(g_R^\top z+\tfrac12z^\top H_Rz\right)\ne\varnothing\iff H_R\succeq0\text{ and }g_R\in\operatorname{range}(H_R).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, optimality, uniqueness, and unboundedness tests in reduced coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Space Subproblem Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible particular step plus a null-space basis converts the equality-constrained quadratic problem into an unconstrained reduced-coordinate problem with exactly the same objective values under reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the working-set equalities be \(A_Wp=r_W\), let \(p_0\) satisfy \(A_Wp_0=r_W\), and let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A_W\). Every feasible step has the form \(p=p_0+Zz\). With \(q(p)=g^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Bp\), the exact reduced representation is
\[
\min_{A_Wp=r_W} q(p)
\quad\longleftrightarrow\quad
\min_z\; q(p_0)+(Z^\top(g+Bp_0))^\top z+\tfrac12z^\top(Z^\top BZ)z.
\]
The reduced-space interface returns \(z\) and reconstructs \(p=p_0+Zz\), together with a singularity or negative-curvature status when appropriate.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A_W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full and reduced problems have corresponding feasible points and identical objective values under \(p=p_0+Zz\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space reduction of a working-set equality-constrained quadratic model.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.1. Linear Equality Constraints p. 68

knowledge_statements.title: Face-to-Reduced-Space Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A particular face point and null-space basis give unique reduced coordinates for every point on the affine face, preserving quadratic minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{p\in\mathbb R^n:A_Wp=r_W\}\) be nonempty, choose \(p_0\in F\), and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-r)}\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A_W\), where \(r=\operatorname{rank}(A_W)\). Then the map \(\phi:\mathbb R^{n-r}\to F\) defined by \(\phi(z)=p_0+Zz\) is bijective. Moreover, for \(q(p)=g^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Bp\), minimizing \(q\) on \(F\) is equivalent to minimizing \(q\circ\phi\) on \(\mathbb R^{n-r}\); local and global minimizers correspond through \(\phi\).
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A_W\) and \(Z\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(z)=p_0+Zz\) is a bijection, and \(\arg\min_{p\in F}q(p)=\phi\bigl(\arg\min_z q(\phi(z))\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine bijection between a working face and its null-space coordinates.

notation.meaning: basis matrix for the null space of A_W

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.1. Linear Equality Constraints p. 68

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced and Full-Space Negative-Curvature Equivalence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible full-space negative curvature exists exactly when the reduced Hessian has a negative direction, with lifting through the null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A_W\). There exists a nonzero \(d\) satisfying \(A_Wd=0\) and \(d^\top Bd<0\) if and only if there exists \(v\ne0\) satisfying \(v^\top(Z^\top BZ)v<0\). The directions correspond through \(d=Zv\). Thus feasible negative curvature exists exactly when the reduced Hessian has a negative eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists d\ne0:\ A_Wd=0,\ d^\top Bd<0\iff\lambda_{\min}(Z^\top BZ)<0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of negative curvature in null-space coordinates and feasible full-space directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible direction with negative quadratic curvature certifies nonconvexity; absent other restrictions, the quadratic model is unbounded below along that direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the equality-constrained quadratic model \(q(p)=g^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Bp\) with homogeneous feasible directions \(A_Wd=0\), a nonzero vector \(d\) satisfying
\[
A_Wd=0,\qquad d^\top Bd<0
\]
is a negative-curvature certificate. It is directly verifiable by matrix-vector products. For every feasible \(p_0\), both \(p_0+td\) and \(p_0-td\) satisfy the working equalities, and at least one sign of \(d\) is a descent direction whenever \(\nabla q(p_0)^\top d\ne0\). Without additional bounds or inequalities, \(q(p_0+td)\to-\infty\) as \(|t|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed \(d\) certifies negative curvature on the working-set tangent space and unboundedness of the equality-only quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced feasible direction certifying nonconvexity of a working-set quadratic model.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 Negative Curvature Direction Method p. 147

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(p)=\tfrac12p^THp+g^Tp\), let \(A_Wp=0\) define the working tangent space, and let \(Z\) span \(\ker A_W\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indefinite equality-constrained quadratic models arising inside active-set methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A negative-curvature interface returns a nonzero reduced direction \(s\) and its full-space image \(d=Zs\) satisfying \[A_Wd=0,
\qquad d^THd=s^TZ^THZs<0.\] Its sign is oriented so that \(g^Td\le0\). The outer method may then choose the largest admissible step along \(d\) until a nonworking constraint blocks the motion. If no such finite blocking step exists, the quadratic model is unbounded below along the working-feasible ray because \(q(p+\alpha d)\to-\infty\) as \(\alpha\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative-curvature interface returns a nonzero direction tangent to all working constraints whose quadratic curvature is negative. The sign is chosen to make the direction nonascending to first order. The outer active-set method follows it until a nonworking constraint blocks the step. If no finite blocker exists, the quadratic model tends to minus infinity along that feasible ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d\in\ker A_W\setminus\{0\},\quad d^THd<0,\quad g^Td\le0;\qquad \alpha_{\max}=\infty\Rightarrow q(p+\alpha d)\to-\infty.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Negative reduced curvature is equivalent to \(\lambda_{\min}(Z^THZ)<0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(Z^THZ\succeq0\), the interface reports that no strict negative-curvature direction exists.
In inertia-controlling methods, a release is arranged so that the reduced Hessian has at most one negative eigenvalue.
immediate_consequences_latex: A stationary point of the working subproblem with negative reduced curvature is not a local minimizer on the working face.
A finite blocker supplies an index that can be admitted to shrink the negative-curvature subspace.
boundary_notes: Zero curvature \(d^THd=0\) is not strict negative curvature and needs a separate recession test.
The definition concerns the model Hessian, not necessarily the exact NLP Lagrangian Hessian.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal E\subseteq W_k\subseteq\mathcal A(x_k)\), let \(B_k\subseteq\mathcal I\setminus W_k\) be eligible blocking indices, and let \(R_k\subseteq W_k\cap\mathcal I\) be eligible release indices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued management rules for active-set admission, release, and representation maintenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A working-set management family is a pair of selection maps \(\mathsf{Add}_k\subseteq B_k\) and \(\mathsf{Drop}_k\subseteq R_k\), together with the update \[W_{k+1}=(W_k\setminus\mathsf{Drop}_k)\cup\mathsf{Add}_k,\qquad \mathcal E\subseteq W_{k+1}.\] An admissible manager preserves the structural invariant required by the subproblem interface, ordinarily linear independence of \(\{a_i:i\in W_{k+1}\}\). Admission eligibility is determined by blocking or violated feasibility; release eligibility is determined by multiplier-sign or complementarity failure. Tie-breaking and cardinality rules distinguish members of the family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A working-set manager consists of an admission selector and a release selector. The next working set removes the selected release indices and adds selected blocking or violated indices, while retaining all equality constraints. An admissible manager also preserves the rank condition needed by the subproblem solver. Different tie-breaking rules and single- versus multiple-change policies define different management families.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[W_{k+1}=(W_k\setminus\mathsf{Drop}_k)\cup\mathsf{Add}_k,\quad \mathcal E\subseteq W_{k+1},\quad \operatorname{rank}A_{W_{k+1}}=|W_{k+1}|\ \text{when required}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The update can be represented by the symmetric difference \(W_{k+1}\triangle W_k=\mathsf{Add}_k\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathsf{Drop}_k\).
special_cases_latex: A single-change manager has \(|\mathsf{Add}_k|+|\mathsf{Drop}_k|\le1\).
A block manager may change several tied or jointly selected constraints.
immediate_consequences_latex: The subproblem equations and the management policy can be analyzed as separate interfaces.
Equality constraints are never eligible for release.
boundary_notes: The definition does not guarantee finite termination without anti-cycling and progress conditions.
Dependent active constraints may be active geometrically without all being represented in the working set.

notation.meaning: Eligible admission and release index sets.
Indices selected for the current update.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Working-Set Initialization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inherited working set may be reused after removing stale or rank-dependent constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_0\) be feasible and let \(\widehat W\) be inherited from a previous solve. Retain only indices in \(\widehat W\cap I_\tau(x_0)\), then delete indices as necessary until the mandatory equality gradients and retained inequality gradients are linearly independent. The resulting set \(W_0\) is an admissible warm start. If every inherited index is near-active and the combined Jacobian already has full row rank, \(W_0=\widehat W\) is admissible.
assumptions_latex: The mandatory equality gradients are linearly independent.
All tested constraint gradients exist at \(x_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_0\subseteq\widehat W\cap I_\tau(x_0)\text{ and the combined working-set Jacobian has full row rank.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation of an inherited working set at a new feasible starting point.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Set Initialization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize from active or nearly active inequalities while retaining linear independence of the combined equality and working-inequality Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(c_i(x)\ge0\), a feasible initial point \(x_0\), and an activity tolerance \(\tau\ge0\), form \(I_\tau(x_0)=\{i:0\le c_i(x_0)\le\tau\}\). Begin with all mandatory equality constraints. Select \(W_0\subseteq I_\tau(x_0)\) so that the mandatory equality gradients together with \(\{\nabla c_i(x_0):i\in W_0\}\) are linearly independent. If adding a candidate inequality gradient destroys this joint independence, omit it or replace a dependent working inequality according to a fixed priority rule. Return \((x_0,W_0)\) and a factorization of the combined working-set Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: \(x_0\) is feasible for the inequality constraints.
All relevant constraint gradients exist at \(x_0\).
The mandatory equality gradients are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned set satisfies \(W_0\subseteq I_\tau(x_0)\), and the mandatory equality gradients together with the selected working-inequality gradients are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization rule for a primal-feasible inequality active-set method.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\) be feasible for inequalities \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\), let \(W_k\) be its working set, and let \(p_k\) satisfy \(a_i^Tp_k=0\) for \(i\in W_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-feasible line-segment steps for affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonworking inequality with \(a_i^Tp_k<0\), define its blocking ratio \[\beta_i=\frac{b_i-a_i^Tx_k}{a_i^Tp_k}\ge0.\] The maximal feasible step capped by the full subproblem step is \[\alpha_k=\min\left\{1,\min_{i\notin W_k,\ a_i^Tp_k<0}\beta_i\right\}.\] The blocking set is \(B_k=\{i\notin W_k:a_i^Tp_k<0,\ \beta_i=\alpha_k\}\). Blocking-driven admission chooses a nonempty admissible subset \(J_k\subseteq B_k\) when \(\alpha_k<1\) and sets \(W_{k+1}=W_k\cup J_k\), subject to the working-rank rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a primal-feasible step, every nonworking inequality whose value decreases has a ratio at which it becomes active. The step length is the smaller of one and the least such ratio. Constraints attaining that minimum are blockers. When the step is truncated, blocking-driven admission adds one or more admissible blockers to the working set while preserving its required rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\text{ is feasible},\qquad \alpha_k<1\Rightarrow \varnothing\ne J_k\subseteq B_k,\quad W_{k+1}=W_k\cup J_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A blocker is a nonworking constraint that is inactive before the step and active at \(x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), or is already active and forces \(\alpha_k=0\).
special_cases_latex: If the inner minimum is over an empty set, \(\alpha_k=1\) and there is no blocker.
A single-admission rule selects one element of \(B_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The ratio test preserves primal feasibility exactly in exact arithmetic.
Multiple blockers can make the active set larger than the represented working set.
boundary_notes: The formula uses the convention \(Ax\ge b\); signs reverse for \(Ax\le b\).
Degenerate zero steps require anti-cycling and dependency safeguards.

knowledge_statements.title: Blocking Constraints
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A blocking constraint is an inactive affine inequality that first reaches equality along the proposed working-set-feasible direction and strictly limits the trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^\top x\ge b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(x\in P\), and let \(W\subseteq\{i:a_i^\top x=b_i\}\). Let \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(a_i^\top p=0\) for every \(i\in W\). For each inactive index \(i\notin W\) with \(a_i^\top p<0\), define
\[
\alpha_i=\frac{a_i^\top x-b_i}{-a_i^\top p}.
\]
For a trial bound \(\bar\alpha>0\), define
\[
\alpha_*=\min\left\{\bar\alpha,\min_{i\notin W,\,a_i^\top p<0}\alpha_i\right\},
\]
where the inner minimum is \(+\infty\) when its index set is empty. An inactive constraint \(i\notin W\) is blocking when \(\alpha_i=\alpha_*<\bar\alpha\); every such constraint is active at \(x+\alpha_*p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\alpha\in[0,\alpha_*]\), \(x+\alpha p\in P\), and every blocking constraint is active at \(x+\alpha_*p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First inactive affine inequalities encountered along a feasible active-set step.

notation.meaning: step at which inactive constraint i reaches equality

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized Hitting Times Need Not Preserve Nonlinear Feasibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A first-order admission test can miss a nonlinear boundary entirely; exact feasibility needs affine constraints or an additional nonlinear safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For g(x)\ge0, the inequality g(x)+\alpha\nabla g(x)^\top p\ge0 does not generally imply g(x+\alpha p)\ge0. Let g(x)=1-x^2, x=0, and p=1. Then g(x)=1 and \nabla g(x)^\top p=0, so the linearized hitting time is +\infty, whereas g(x+\alpha p)=1-\alpha^2<0 for every \alpha>1.
assumptions_latex: The prediction uses only g(x) and \nabla g(x)^\top p.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha^{\mathrm{lin}}=+\infty\not\Rightarrow g(x+\alpha p)\ge0\text{ for all }\alpha>0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for treating a first-order hitting time as an exact nonlinear admission test.

notation.meaning: first hitting time predicted by the affine linearization

otin W}\alpha_i\}\). An inactive constraint is admissible for blocking-driven insertion precisely when \(\alpha_i= ar\alpha<\alpha_{\mathrm{trial}}\), subject to the method's rank-acceptance rule for the enlarged working set.

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Blocking Events
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simultaneous event occurs when at least two inactive constraints share the minimum finite hitting time; all are blockers, though only a compatible subset need be admitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the first-hit construction, the simultaneous blocking set is \[B(x,p)=\{i
otin W:
abla g_i(x)^	op p<0,\ \alpha_i= ar\alpha<\alpha_{\mathrm{trial}}\}.\] A simultaneous blocking event occurs exactly when \(|B(x,p)|\ge 2\). Every member reaches its linearized boundary at the same accepted step: \(g_i(x)+ ar\alpha
abla g_i(x)^	op p=0\) for all \(i\in B(x,p)\). The definition identifies the tied blockers but does not require admitting all of them; admission may select a rank-compatible subset.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependent Gradients Make Multiplier Release Ambiguous
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With dependent working gradients, valid multiplier vectors can assign different signs to the same constraint, so release is ambiguous without a multiplier-selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two duplicate working gradients a_1=a_2=a and stationarity c=a, every multiplier pair satisfying \lambda_1+\lambda_2=1 is valid. Both (\lambda_1,\lambda_2)=(1,0) and (2,-1) satisfy stationarity, but only the latter presents a negative release candidate. Thus an individual multiplier sign and the identity of a most-negative candidate can depend on the selected multiplier vector.
assumptions_latex: The working-gradient matrix is rank deficient.
No canonical multiplier-selection rule is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}A_W<|W|\text{ permits nonunique individual multiplier signs}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to invariant sign-based release decisions without multiplier uniqueness.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative Multiplier Exposes Descent After Release
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under working-gradient independence, a negative multiplier certifies that releasing its inequality exposes a feasible descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let q(p)=q(0)+c^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Hp, impose a_i^\top p=0 for i\in W, and suppose p=0 satisfies c=\sum_{i\in W}\lambda_i a_i. If the working gradients are linearly independent and \lambda_j<0, then there exists d with a_i^\top d=0 for i\in W\setminus\{j\}, a_j^\top d>0, and c^\top d<0. Hence sufficiently small positive steps along d decrease q while retaining the other equalities and moving into the feasible side a_j^\top p\ge0.
assumptions_latex: The inequality convention is a_i^\top p\ge0 with stationarity c-\sum_i\lambda_i a_i=0.
The working gradients are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists d:\ a_i^\top d=0\ (i\in W\setminus\{j\}),\ a_j^\top d>0,\ c^\top d<0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local justification for releasing a working inequality at a zero-step equality-subproblem solution.

notation.meaning: descent direction exposed by releasing constraint j

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Based Constraint Release
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a zero-step iterate, stop if every working inequality multiplier is nonnegative within tolerance; otherwise release a working inequality with a most-negative multiplier and resolve. Permanent equalities are not release candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\ge 0\), let \(W\) be the current working set and let \(W_I\subseteq W\) be its inequality indices. Suppose the active-set subproblem returns a zero primal step and multipliers \(\lambda_i^W\) under the convention \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\sum_{i\in W_I}\lambda_i g_i(x)\), with any equality-multiplier terms handled separately. Given \(\tau_\lambda\ge 0\), if \(\lambda_i^W\ge-\tau_\lambda\) for every \(i\in W_I\), terminate the multiplier release test with approximate dual feasibility. Otherwise choose \(j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{i\in W_I}\lambda_i^W\), set \(W^+=W\setminus\{j\}\), and resolve the subproblem. Equality constraints are not candidates for this release rule.
assumptions_latex: \(W_I\) is the set of inequality indices in the current working set \(W\).
The current iterate satisfies every working constraint.
The working-set subproblem supplies multipliers consistent with \(L=f-\sum_{i\in W_I}\lambda_i g_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W^+=W\setminus\{j\}\) for some \(j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{i\in W_I}\lambda_i^W\) when \(\min_{i\in W_I}\lambda_i^W<-\tau_\lambda\); otherwise the multiplier release test terminates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Release rule for inequalities represented as nonnegative constraints.

notation.meaning: equality-subproblem multiplier for working inequality i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Release Is Ambiguous Without Multiplier Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-deficiency boundary for sign-based release decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the working gradients are linearly dependent, the equality-subproblem multiplier can be nonunique. Consequently the sign of an individual multiplier, and therefore the identity of a most-negative release candidate, can depend on the selected multiplier vector. For example, two duplicate working inequalities with gradient \(a\) and stationarity \(c=a\) admit every multiplier pair satisfying \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1\), including \((1,0)\) and \((2,-1)\). Thus a negative component need not be an invariant property of the primal subproblem unless a multiplier-selection or dependency-handling rule is specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With dependent working gradients, individual multiplier signs can vary across valid multiplier vectors, so a most-negative release rule is not well defined without an additional selection rule.
assumptions_latex: The working-gradient matrix is rank deficient.
No canonical multiplier-selection rule is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}A_W<|W|\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{individual multiplier signs need not be unique}.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Release Is Ambiguous Without Multiplier Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative Multiplier Supplies a Descent Direction After Release
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact local justification for releasing a working inequality at a zero-step equality-subproblem solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(p)=q(0)+c^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Hp\), let the working constraints be \(a_i^\top p=0\) for \(i\in W\), and suppose \(p=0\) satisfies \(c=\sum_{i\in W}\lambda_i a_i\). If \(\{a_i:i\in W\}\) is linearly independent and \(\lambda_j<0\), then there exists \(d\) such that \(a_i^\top d=0\) for \(i\in W\setminus\{j\}\), \(a_j^\top d>0\), and \(c^\top d<0\). Hence sufficiently small positive steps along \(d\) decrease \(q\) while satisfying the retained working equalities and moving into the feasible side of the released inequality \(a_j^\top p\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under working-gradient independence, a negative working multiplier certifies that releasing that inequality exposes a feasible descent direction.
assumptions_latex: The inequality convention is \(a_i^\top p\ge0\) with Lagrangian stationarity \(c-\sum_i\lambda_i a_i=0\).
The working gradients are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists d:\ a_{W\setminus\{j\}}^\top d=0,\ a_j^\top d>0,\ c^\top d<0.

notation.meaning: descent direction exposed by releasing constraint j

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For consecutive working sets \(W_k,W_{k+1}\), define admissions \(A_k^+=W_{k+1}\setminus W_k\), releases \(A_k^-=W_k\setminus W_{k+1}\), and change count \(\chi_k=|A_k^+|+|A_k^-|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A classification of working-set managers by how many constraint indices may change in one outer update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A working-set change cardinality regime is a bound or rule on \((|A_k^+|,|A_k^-|)\). It is single-change when \[\chi_k\le1\quad\text{for every }k,\] block-change when \(\chi_k\) may exceed one but is finite and selected from the current eligible admission and release sets, and hybrid when the manager ordinarily uses \(\chi_k\le1\) but permits block changes under declared degeneracy, dependency, or restoration conditions. Every regime must retain mandatory equalities and preserve the required working-row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cardinality regime records how many constraints may enter or leave between two working sets. A single-change method alters at most one index per update. A block-change method may alter several eligible indices. A hybrid method normally changes one index but allows blocks under stated exceptional conditions. Regardless of regime, equalities remain represented and the working-set rank condition must be preserved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\chi_k=|W_{k+1}\triangle W_k|;\qquad \text{single-change: }\chi_k\le1,\quad \text{block-change: }\chi_k\in\mathbb N_0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The ordered pair \((|A_k^+|,|A_k^-|)\) distinguishes pure admission, pure release, and exchange updates even when their total \(\chi_k\) agrees.
special_cases_latex: Classical primal convex-QP active-set iterations normally add or drop one index.
When several constraints block at the same step, a block rule may admit several while a single-change rule admits only one.
immediate_consequences_latex: Single-change regimes permit low-rank factorization updates but can require many iterations when the optimal active set differs greatly from the initial set.
Block regimes can represent tied events directly but require dependency resolution.
boundary_notes: Cardinality alone does not specify which eligible constraints are selected.
An unchanged working set has \(\chi_k=0\) and may accompany an ordinary primal step.

knowledge_statements.title: Single Working-Set Changes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transition is single-change exactly when consecutive working sets differ by one index: one admission or one release, but not a simultaneous substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W_k\) and \(W_{k+1}\) be consecutive working sets. The transition is a single working-set change when \(|W_{k+1}\triangle W_k|=1\), where \(\triangle\) denotes symmetric difference. Thus exactly one of the alternatives holds: admission, \(W_{k+1}=W_k\cup\{i\}\) for one \(i\notin W_k\); or release, \(W_{k+1}=W_k\setminus\{j\}\) for one removable inequality \(j\in W_k\). A substitution that simultaneously deletes one index and inserts another has symmetric-difference cardinality two and is not a single change under this convention.
assumptions_latex: Permanent equality indices, if present, belong to both working sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|W_{k+1}\triangle W_k|=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-index cardinality regime for active-set transitions.

source_witnesses.locator: 10.3 Active Set Methods p. 236

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Working-Set Changes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiple working-set change modifies at least two constraint indices in one transition. The cardinality definition is separate from the method-dependent decision to accept the proposed batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal I\) be a finite constraint-index set and let \(W_k,W_{k+1}\subseteq\mathcal I\) be consecutive working sets. Define the admitted and released index sets by \(A_k=W_{k+1}\setminus W_k\) and \(R_k=W_k\setminus W_{k+1}\). A multiple working-set change is a transition satisfying \(|W_{k+1}\triangle W_k|\ge 2\). Equivalently, \(A_k\cap R_k=\varnothing\), \(|A_k|+|R_k|\ge 2\), and \[W_{k+1}=(W_k\setminus R_k)\cup A_k.\] Whether such a batch is accepted is determined separately by the method's admission, release, and collective-compatibility rules.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal I\) is a finite constraint-index set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|W_{k+1}\triangle W_k|=|A_k|+|R_k|\ge 2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batched cardinality regime for consecutive working sets.

source_witnesses.locator: 10.3 Active Set Methods p. 236

knowledge_statements.title: Batched-Change Conflicts
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changes that are individually regular can conflict collectively through working-Jacobian rank loss or contradictory admission and release requests, so the batch must be reduced, regularized, rejected, or ordered.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Individually regular working-set changes need not form a regular batch. For example, in \(\mathbb R^2\) at a point with \(x_1=0\), the active constraints \(g_1(x)=x_1\ge 0\) and \(g_2(x)=2x_1\ge 0\) each have a nonzero one-row Jacobian, but admitting both into an initially empty working set gives a two-row working Jacobian of rank one. More generally, a proposed batch conflicts when the resulting working Jacobian violates the rank condition required by the subproblem solver or when the proposal requests both admission and release of the same index. The full batch must then be rejected, reduced to a compatible subset, regularized when the solver permits it, or implemented through separate working-set transitions.
assumptions_latex: The working-set solver imposes a declared rank condition on the working Jacobian.
Selected active inequalities are treated as equalities in the local subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under a full-row-rank requirement, \(\operatorname{rank}J_{W^+}(x)<|W^+|\) is sufficient to make the proposed batch conflict with the solver's working-set regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collective incompatibilities that invalidate individually eligible or individually regular working-set changes.

notation.meaning: Jacobian whose rows are gradients of constraints in the proposed working set
working set proposed after the batch

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal P(\theta)\) be a parameterized constrained problem and let \(S(\theta)=(x(\theta),\lambda(\theta),W(\theta),F(\theta))\) denote a solution state containing primal-dual variables, a working set, and reusable factorization data.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-start and parametric reuse between related finite-dimensional constrained optimization instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reoptimization lifecycle interface is a pair of maps \[\mathsf{Seed}:(S(\theta),\theta')\mapsto S_0(\theta'),\qquad \mathsf{Repair}:S_0(\theta')\mapsto S^*(\theta'),\] where \(S_0(\theta')\) reuses any valid components of the previous point, multipliers, working partition, or factors. The repair stage first restores whichever of primal feasibility, dual feasibility, complementarity, and rank regularity are not preserved by the parameter change, then resumes optimality iterations. The completed state \(S^*(\theta')\) must satisfy the KKT termination test for \(\mathcal P(\theta')\), independently of whether the reused working set was correct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reoptimization interface transfers a solved state from one problem instance to a related instance. A seed map reuses valid primal, dual, working-set, and factorization information. A repair map restores any feasibility, complementarity, or rank conditions invalidated by the data change and then resumes optimality iterations. The resulting state must satisfy the new problem's KKT test; reuse does not assume that the old active set remains optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[S^*(\theta')=\mathsf{Repair}(\mathsf{Seed}(S(\theta),\theta')),\qquad \operatorname{KKT}_{\theta'}(S^*(\theta'))=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The lifecycle can be decomposed into transfer, feasibility restoration, active-set correction, optimality restoration, and state export.
special_cases_latex: A warm start uses a nearby estimated solution and its working set.
Parametric programming changes \(A\), \(b\), or \(c\) and retains the previous basis or partition whenever valid.
Adding a primal constraint corresponds to adding a dual variable and can preserve dual feasibility.
immediate_consequences_latex: A reused working set may reduce the number of active-set changes when the perturbation is small.
If transferred primal feasibility is lost but dual feasibility remains, a dual-feasible repair regime is natural.
boundary_notes: The interface does not assert differentiability of the solution map or stability of the active set.
Factorization reuse is conditional on dimension, rank, and numerical validity.
