knowledge_statements.title: Separable-Elastic Phase-I Variant
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate elastic variables produce a weighted sum-of-violations Phase I that is feasible throughout the common domain and has attained global value zero exactly at original feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(g_i(x)\ge0\) and \(h_j(x)=0\), introduce \(s_i,u_j^+,u_j^-\ge0\) and solve \[\min\ \sum_i w_i s_i+\sum_jv_j(u_j^++u_j^-)\] subject to \[g_i(x)+s_i\ge0,\qquad h_j(x)=u_j^+-u_j^-,\] where \(w_i,v_j>0\). Every \(x\) in the common domain admits feasible elastic variables. An attained global objective value of zero is equivalent to feasibility of the original constraints; a positive local value is not an infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: The constraint functions have a nonempty common domain.
Any claimed infeasibility conclusion uses a certified global auxiliary optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\Phi=0\iff\exists x:\ g_i(x)\ge0,\ h_j(x)=0\ \forall i,j,\quad\text{provided the minimum is attained}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted sum-of-violations alternative to common maximum-violation Phase I.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Slack Phase-I Lifecycle
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize the common slack from the current maximum violation, solve the Phase-I problem, hand off only a tolerance-feasible point, and claim infeasibility only from a global auxiliary certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^0\), set \(t^0\ge V(x^0):=\max\{0,\max_i[-g_i(x^0)],\max_j|h_j(x^0)|\}\) and solve the auxiliary problem \[\min_{x,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_i(x)+t\ge0,\quad -t\le h_j(x)\le t,\quad t\ge0.\] Return SUCCESS when a computed point satisfies \(t\le\tau_{\mathrm{feas}}\), passing \(x\) and a rank-compatible nearly active set to the receiving solver. Return CERTIFIED_INFEASIBLE only when a valid global certificate proves the auxiliary optimal value exceeds \(\tau_{\mathrm{feas}}\). If the auxiliary solver terminates without either condition, return PHASE_I_FAILURE or INDETERMINATE and do not infer infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The original constraint functions are defined at \(x^0\) and throughout the auxiliary solver's accepted domain.
The receiving solver's activity and rank requirements are checked before handoff.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t\le\tau_{\mathrm{feas}}\Rightarrow g_i(x)\ge-\tau_{\mathrm{feas}},\ |h_j(x)|\le\tau_{\mathrm{feas}};\qquad p_I^*>\tau_{\mathrm{feas}}\text{ may imply infeasibility only with a valid global certificate}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization, termination statuses, and handoff for the common maximum-violation auxiliary problem.

notation.meaning: global optimal value of the Phase-I auxiliary problem

knowledge_statements.title: Global Phase-I Optimal-Value Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The common-slack optimum is zero exactly when the original system is feasible; a positive value proves infeasibility only with a global auxiliary optimum certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t^*\) be the attained global optimum of \(\min t\) subject to \(g_i(x)+t\ge0\), \(-t\le h_j(x)\le t\), and \(t\ge0\). Then \(t^*=0\) if and only if the original constraints \(g_i(x)\ge0\), \(h_j(x)=0\) are feasible. Thus \(t^*>0\) certifies infeasibility only when global optimality of the auxiliary problem has been certified.
assumptions_latex: The Phase-I problem attains its global minimum.
The auxiliary constraints use the original constraint functions and one common nonnegative slack.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t^*=0\iff\{x:g_i(x)\ge0\ \forall i,\ h_j(x)=0\ \forall j\}\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and infeasibility interpretation of the common-slack Phase-I optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Compatible Phase-I Handoff Test
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Phase-I result is handed off only after satisfying the receiving solver's declared feasibility and working-set rank tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^I\) be returned by Phase I for \(g_i(x)\ge0\) and \(h(x)=0\), and choose \(W^I\subseteq\{i:|g_i(x^I)|\le\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\}\). Suppose the receiving solver admits residuals up to \(\tau_{\mathrm{feas}}\) and requires full row rank of its equality and working-inequality Jacobian. If \[r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x^I):=\max\{\|h(x^I)\|_\infty,\max_i[-g_i(x^I)]_+\}\le\tau_{\mathrm{feas}}\] and \[\operatorname{rank}\begin{bmatrix}J_h(x^I)\\J_{g_{W^I}}(x^I)\end{bmatrix}=m_h+|W^I|,\] then \((x^I,W^I)\) passes that solver's approximate-feasibility and rank handoff tests. Failure of either test requires a declared feasibility-failure or rank-repair status rather than an unqualified handoff.
assumptions_latex: The receiving solver explicitly admits feasibility residuals up to \(\tau_{\mathrm{feas}}\).
The receiving solver requires full row rank of the displayed Jacobian.
All retained constraint Jacobians exist at \(x^I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x^I)\le\tau_{\mathrm{feas}}\ \land\ \operatorname{rank}[J_h;J_{g_{W^I}}]=m_h+|W^I|\Rightarrow(x^I,W^I)\text{ passes the declared handoff tests}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Receiving-solver checks after Phase I reaches its declared feasibility tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive Local Phase-I Minimum Does Not Prove Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive local Phase-I minimum can coexist with feasible original constraints; only a certified positive global optimum proves infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(x)=(x^2+1)(x^2-4)\). The constraint \(h(x)=0\) is feasible at \(x=\pm2\), while its common-slack reduction is \(V(x)=|h(x)|\). Near zero, \(h(x)=x^4-3x^2-4<0\), so \(V(x)=4+3x^2-x^4\). Hence \(x=0\) is a strict local minimizer with \(V(0)=4\), although \(\min_xV(x)=0\).
assumptions_latex: Phase I minimizes the absolute equality violation \(V(x)=|h(x)|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V(0)=4\text{ is a strict local minimum},\qquad \min_xV(x)=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible equality system whose minimax Phase-I violation has a positive nonglobal local minimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Slack Phase I as Minimax Violation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the common slack turns Phase I into minimization of the maximum constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[V(x)=\max\left\{0,\max_i[-g_i(x)],\max_j|h_j(x)|\right\}.\] For each fixed \(x\), the smallest \(t\) satisfying \(g_i(x)+t\ge0\), \(-t\le h_j(x)\le t\), and \(t\ge0\) is \(V(x)\). Consequently, the common-slack Phase-I problem and \(\min_xV(x)\) have the same infimum; whenever minimizers exist, they have the same minimizing \(x\)-coordinates.
assumptions_latex: The constraint index sets are finite; a maximum over an absent constraint class is omitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x,t}\{t:g_i(x)+t\ge0,\ |h_j(x)|\le t,\ t\ge0\}=\inf_xV(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise elimination of the common violation variable.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex and twice continuously differentiable, and consider \(f_i(x)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) together with \(Ax=b\). Assume an initial \(x^{(0)}\) in the common domain satisfying \(Ax^{(0)}=b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The basic maximum-infeasibility phase-I construction for convex inequality systems with affine equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The phase-I feasibility interface forms the auxiliary problem \[\bar p^*=\inf_{x,s}\left\{s:f_i(x)\le s\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ Ax=b\right\}.\] Its output is classified by the optimal value: \(\bar p^*<0\) yields a strictly feasible point; \(\bar p^*>0\) certifies infeasibility; and \(\bar p^*=0\) is a boundary case distinguishing feasible-but-not-strictly-feasible systems from nonattainment. Any feasible auxiliary pair with \(s<0\) may be returned immediately as a strict-feasibility seed for phase II. For an active-set phase II, an independent subset of constraints active at the returned point supplies an initial working set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phase I minimizes a scalar upper bound on the inequality violations while retaining the affine equalities. A negative optimum yields a strictly feasible point; a positive optimum certifies infeasibility; and a zero optimum is the boundary case where attainment determines whether feasibility without strict feasibility occurs. The procedure can stop as soon as it finds a feasible auxiliary pair with negative scalar. An active-set solver can initialize its working set from independent active constraints at the returned point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bar p^*<0\Rightarrow\exists x:\ f_i(x)<0,\ Ax=b;\qquad \bar p^*>0\Rightarrow\{x:f_i(x)\le0,\ Ax=b\}=\varnothing.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A sum-of-infeasibilities variant minimizes \(\mathbf1^Ts\) subject to \(f_i(x)\le s_i\), \(s\ge0\), and \(Ax=b\); its optimum is zero exactly when the original system is feasible.
special_cases_latex: For affine inequalities, phase I is a linear program.
If \(x^{(0)}\) already satisfies every inequality strictly, phase I can be skipped.
immediate_consequences_latex: The returned feasible point separates feasibility acquisition from phase-II objective optimization.
A positive dual objective for the auxiliary problem can provide an infeasibility certificate.
boundary_notes: Numerically distinguishing an optimal value of exactly zero requires tolerances.
The stated construction assumes consistency of \(Ax=b\) at the supplied domain point; inconsistent equalities require a broader feasibility model.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the phase-I problem.

source_refs.locator: Section 11.4.1, basic phase-I problem (11.19), three optimal-value cases, and sum-of-infeasibilities problem (11.20)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable receiving-solver contract after a Phase-I point reaches feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^I\) be returned by Phase I for constraints \(g_i(x)\ge 0\) and \(h(x)=0\). Choose \(W^I\subseteq\{i:|g_i(x^I)|\le\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\}\). If \[\max\{\|h(x^I)\|_\infty,\max_i[-g_i(x^I)]_+\}\le\tau_{\mathrm{feas}}\] and the rows of \([J_h(x^I);J_{g_{W^I}}(x^I)]\) satisfy the receiving solver's rank test, then \((x^I,W^I)\) is a rank-compatible approximate-feasibility handoff. Failure of either test requires a feasibility-failure or rank-repair status rather than an unqualified handoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Phase-I point may be handed to the active-set solver only after it passes both the feasibility-residual and receiving-solver rank tests.
assumptions_latex: The receiving active-set solver declares feasibility, activity, and rank tolerances.
All retained constraint Jacobians exist at \(x^I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x^I)\le\tau_{\mathrm{feas}}\ \land\ \operatorname{rank}[J_h;J_{g_{W^I}}]=m_h+|W^I|\Rightarrow(x^I,W^I)\text{ is an admissible rank-compatible handoff}.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Compatible Phase-I Handoff Certificate

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Warm-start reuse of a preceding working set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q_k\) be the quadratic subproblem solved at major iteration \(k\), with feasible region \(C_k\), inequality-index set \(\mathcal I_k\), and final working set \(\mathcal W_k^{\mathrm{fin}}\). Let \(\mathcal W_{k+1}^{0}\) denote the working set supplied to the active-set solver for \(Q_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sequential quadratic programming or another reoptimization process in which consecutive subproblems have consistently identified constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Warm-start working-set reuse is the initialization rule \[\mathcal W_{k+1}^{0}=\operatorname{ind}\!\left(\{i\in\mathcal W_k^{\mathrm{fin}}:i\in\mathcal I_{k+1}\text{ and }i\text{ is admissible at the initial point of }Q_{k+1}\}\right),\] where \(\operatorname{ind}(S)\subseteq S\) selects an admissible subset whose constraint gradients satisfy the active-set solver's independence requirements. Exact reuse occurs when \(\mathcal W_{k+1}^{0}=\mathcal W_k^{\mathrm{fin}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a sequence of related quadratic subproblems, warm-start working-set reuse means initializing the next active-set solve with the final active or working set from the preceding solve, after deleting indices that no longer exist, are inadmissible at the new initial point, or violate the solver's independence requirements. It is exact reuse when no deletion is required. The transferred set is an initial prediction, not an assertion that every transferred constraint belongs to the new optimal active set; the ordinary add/drop tests of the active-set method remain applicable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal W_{k+1}^{0}=\operatorname{ind}(\mathcal W_k^{\mathrm{fin}}\cap\mathcal I_{k+1})\), subject to admissibility at the new subproblem's initial point.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When all constraint identities persist and \(\mathcal W_k^{\mathrm{fin}}\) remains admissible, exact reuse is \(\mathcal W_{k+1}^{0}=\mathcal W_k^{\mathrm{fin}}\).
For an SQP method, the rule uses the final active set of the quadratic program at iteration \(k\) as the initial working set for the quadratic program at iteration \(k+1\).
special_cases_latex: If no prior solve is available, the cold-start case may be represented by \(\mathcal W_0^0=\varnothing\).
If only a subset of constraint identities persists, reuse is restricted to the persistent indices.
immediate_consequences_latex: Transferred constraints may subsequently be deleted when their working-set multipliers have the wrong sign.
Constraints absent from the transferred set may subsequently be added when they block a feasible step.
boundary_notes: Reuse of a working set is distinct from reusing a primal point, multipliers, or a matrix factorization, although an implementation may transfer those objects as well.
The definition does not guarantee fewer active-set iterations; it specifies the initialization interface.

notation.meaning: Final working set returned for subproblem k.
An admissible linearly independent subset selected from S.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Information
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm start may transfer the primal point, working set, multipliers, and compatible solver state, but each component must be validated for the new problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a previously solved instance, represent warm-start information by \(\mathcal S=(x, W, \lambda_W, \sigma)\), where \(x\) is the prior primal point, \(W\) is its working set, \(\lambda_W\) contains multipliers associated with working constraints, and \(\sigma\) denotes optional solver state such as a reduced-Hessian approximation, factorization, trust-region radius, or penalty parameter. For a new instance, each component is a proposal rather than a certificate: the point must be checked for domain and feasibility, the indices for existence and near activity, and the multipliers and solver state for dimensional and sign compatibility.
assumptions_latex: The old and new instances use an identified correspondence between variables and constraints.
Transferred numerical objects have declared dimensions and sign conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal S=(x,W,\lambda_W,\sigma)\) is accepted only after componentwise validation against the new instance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reusable state transferred between nearby constrained NLP solves.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation is plausible, but the inclusion of reduced-Hessian data, factorizations, trust-region radii, and penalty parameters is solver-dependent and presently supported only by standard-field rationale. An inspectable authoritative locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Reused-Factorization Validation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stored symbolic data require index validation, while stored numerical factors require an actual new-system residual test; matrix closeness alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a mapped candidate set \(W^0\), form the new-instance KKT matrix \(\widehat K_0\). Reuse a stored symbolic ordering or sparsity analysis only when its dimensions, row identities, and permutation agree with \(W^0\). A stored numerical factorization may supply a candidate solution \(z\) for an actual new right-hand side \(b\) only if the receiving solver's rank or inertia test passes and the declared backward-residual test \[\frac{\|b-\widehat K_0z\|}{\|\widehat K_0\|\|z\|+\|b\|}\le\tau_K\] is satisfied. Otherwise numerically factor \(\widehat K_0\); failure returns the ordinary singular or unacceptable-inertia status. Closeness of \(\widehat K_0\) to the old matrix alone does not validate old numerical factors as an exact factorization of \(\widehat K_0\).
assumptions_latex: Old and new working-set rows have an explicit index correspondence.
The receiving solver declares a norm, residual tolerance, and rank or inertia requirement.
The denominator in the backward-residual test is nonzero for the tested system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{validated symbolic data may be reused; validated numerical factors may supply the tested solve; otherwise }\widehat K_0\text{ is refactored}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation of stored symbolic or numerical KKT-factorization data for the first new-instance solve.

notation.meaning: new-instance KKT matrix for the reused set
actual new right-hand side and candidate solution

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Working-Set Transfer Procedure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map and filter the old constraints, repair rank, validate optional multiplier and factorization data, then resume the ordinary active-set updates without freezing membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Map surviving constraint identities from the old instance to the new instance. Include every required equality and retain a mapped inequality only if it satisfies the receiving solver's initial-feasibility or near-activity test. Delete retained inequalities as needed to satisfy the solver's rank condition. Install only multipliers and numerical state that pass the solver's sign, dimension, rank, inertia, and residual checks; otherwise recompute or omit them. Use the resulting set \(W^0\) for the first ordinary active-set subproblem, after which the unchanged admission and release rules apply.
assumptions_latex: Old and new constraint identities have an explicit correspondence.
The permanent equalities satisfy the receiving solver's admissibility requirements.
The receiving solver specifies its feasibility, activity, rank, multiplier, and linear-solve validation tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W^0\text{ is an admissible initial hypothesis, and all later membership changes follow the base solver}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic installation of a previous working set as a revisable initial hypothesis for a compatible active-set solver.

notation.meaning: validated initial working set on the new instance

knowledge_statements.title: Correctness Invariance Under Admissible Working-Set Reuse
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admissible reuse inherits the base solver's guarantee but does not itself prove faster convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an active-set algorithm has a stated guarantee for every initial state in an admissible set \(\mathcal I\). If a warm-start transformation produces \(I^0\in\mathcal I\) and all subsequent iterations use the unchanged algorithm, then the same guarantee applies to the warm-started run. Reuse may change the trajectory and computational work but supplies no stronger correctness, convergence, or speed conclusion by itself.
assumptions_latex: The base guarantee holds for every \(I^0\in\mathcal I\).
Subsequent iterations use the unchanged base algorithm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I^0\in\mathcal I\Rightarrow\text{the base algorithm's stated guarantee applies to the warm-started run}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of a base-solver guarantee when reuse changes only admissible initialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Reuse Gives Immediate Convex-QP Certification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a reused convex-QP state already satisfies the full KKT system, active-set reuse terminates immediately at a global optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex inequality-constrained QP, suppose a feasible warm-start point \(x^0\), reused working set \(W^0\), and associated multipliers satisfy the complete QP KKT conditions. Then the equality-constrained direction for \(W^0\) is zero, no admission or release is required, and \(x^0\) is globally optimal.
assumptions_latex: The QP objective is convex and all constraints are affine.
The warm-start point is feasible and the reused primal-dual state satisfies stationarity, dual feasibility, and complementarity.
The equality-constrained working-set direction is uniquely defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_0=0,\qquad x^0\in\operatorname*{argmin}q(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate termination when a reused convex-QP state already satisfies the complete KKT system.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Set Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated reuse of a previous active set on a nearby instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a new constrained instance, an initial point \(x^0\), and a previous working set \(W^{\mathrm{old}}\), first discard indices absent from the new instance. Retain an inequality index \(i\) only when \(|g_i(x^0)|\le\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\), and include all permanent equalities. From the retained indices choose a subset \(W^0\) satisfying the rank requirement of the working-set solver; initialize compatible multipliers or factorizations when available. Solve the first local subproblem with \(W^0\), then apply the ordinary admission and release tests. Thus reuse supplies an initial hypothesis and does not freeze working-set membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter the old working set by index validity, near activity, and rank, then use it only as the initial hypothesis for ordinary admission and release updates.
assumptions_latex: Constraint identities are mapped from the old instance to the new one.
\(x^0\) lies in the domain of every retained constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W^0\subseteq W^{\mathrm{old}}\) is rank compatible and contains only mapped, nearly active inequalities together with permanent equalities.

notation.meaning: working set from the previous solve
validated initial working set for the new solve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validation-based reuse algorithm is plausible and locally well stated, but its filtering and initialization policy is method-dependent and has no cited source. A specific authoritative section, algorithm, or page is needed before the mathematical interface can be reviewed reliably.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Feasible Reuse Admissibility Conditions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-feasible solver can directly install only mapped, defined, currently active constraints satisfying its rank requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^0\) be feasible for affine inequalities \(g_i(x)\ge0\), and let \(W^{\mathrm{old}}\) be proposed for initialization. Direct unmodified installation requires every retained index to exist in the new instance, every retained function to be defined at \(x^0\), \[W^{\mathrm{old}}\subseteq\mathcal A(x^0):=\{i:g_i(x^0)=0\},\] and the retained constraint Jacobian to satisfy the rank requirement of the receiving equality-constrained subproblem solver. Failure of activity or rank admissibility requires deletion or rank repair before installation.
assumptions_latex: \(x^0\) is feasible for the new affine-inequality instance.
The receiving method requires its working set to be contained in the active set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W^{\mathrm{old}}\text{ directly installable}\Rightarrow W^{\mathrm{old}}\subseteq\mathcal A(x^0)\text{ and }J_{W^{\mathrm{old}}}(x^0)\text{ satisfies the required rank condition}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary direct-installation conditions for a primal-feasible working-set solver.

notation.meaning: geometric active set at the transferred point

knowledge_statements.title: Compatibility Checks Do Not Certify Active-Set Persistence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfect mapping, domain, activity, and rank compatibility does not certify that a nearby problem has the same optimal active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x\tfrac12(x-\theta)^2\) subject to \(x\ge0\). At \(\theta=0\), the solution is \(x^*=0\), so the constraint may be stored in the old working set. For every \(\theta>0\), however small, the new solution is \(x^*(\theta)=\theta>0\), whose active set is empty. At the transferred point \(x^0=0\), the old constraint remains mapped, defined, exactly active, and has nonzero gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W^{\mathrm{old}}=\{1\},\qquad W^*(\theta)=\varnothing\quad(\theta>0).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mapped, defined, rank-compatible, active constraints need not remain active at the new optimum.

notation.meaning: optimal active-index set at parameter value theta

knowledge_statements.title: Reuse Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set reuse can require revalidation at parameter values where activity or multiplier signs change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Working-set identity need not be stable across degenerate parameter values. For
\[
\min_{x\ge 0}\;\tfrac12(x-\theta)^2,
\]
the unique solution is \(x^*(\theta)=\max\{0,\theta\}\). The lower bound is active for \(\theta\le 0\) and inactive for \(\theta>0\); at \(\theta=0\), its multiplier and slack both vanish. Positive primal-slack margins for inactive constraints and correctly signed positive multiplier margins for active constraints provide a sufficient local safeguard for retaining a working set under small perturbations, subject to the usual regularity assumptions. When a slack or multiplier reaches zero, unchanged reuse is no longer certified by those margins, so affected constraints must be revalidated and may need to be added or deleted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive slack and multiplier margins can safeguard local reuse, but reuse must be revalidated at zero-margin boundaries; the scalar example changes its active set at parameter zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(\theta=0\), strict complementarity fails and the optimal active set changes across the parameter value.

source_refs.locator: 12 Theory of Constrained Optimization p. 304

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Active-Set Predictor–Corrector Reoptimization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predict along the differentiated KKT branch, correct at the new parameter, and validate primal feasibility and multiplier signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the fixed-active KKT equations as \(F(z,\theta)=0\), where \(z=(x,\lambda)\). From \(F(z_k,\theta_k)=0\), compute \[D_zF(z_k,\theta_k)s_k=-D_\theta F(z_k,\theta_k)(\theta_{k+1}-\theta_k),\qquad z_k^p=z_k+s_k.\] Apply Newton corrections to \(F(z,\theta_{k+1})=0\) from \(z_k^p\). Accept only after retained multipliers have the required signs and all inactive inequalities are feasible; otherwise repair the active set or invoke feasibility recovery.
assumptions_latex: The parameter change is sufficiently small for the branch and Newton correction to remain local.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(z_{k+1},\theta_{k+1})=0\text{ with valid active/inactive signs, or active-set repair is invoked}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local predictor-corrector procedure on a strongly regular KKT branch.

knowledge_statements.title: Corrected-State Active-Set Acceptance Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity, feasibility, positive inactive slacks, and positive retained multipliers certify the corrected active-set branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(L=f+
u^{\mathsf T}h-\lambda^{\mathsf T}g\), a corrected state with proposed active set \(W\) is compatible with that strict-complementarity branch when \[
abla_xL=0,\quad h=0,\quad g_i=0\ (i\in W),\quad g_i>0\ (i
otin W),\quad \lambda_i>0\ (i\in W),\quad \lambda_i=0\ (i
otin W).\] Failure of an inactive-slack or retained-multiplier test identifies an index requiring admission or release.
assumptions_latex: The inequality convention is \(g_i\ge0\) with \(L=f+\nu^{\mathsf T}h-\lambda^{\mathsf T}g\).
The proposed active set and multiplier indexing are consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Displayed conditions}\Rightarrow\text{KKT compatibility with exact active set }W\text{ and strict complementarity}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact corrected-state certificate under the convention \(g_i\ge0\).

notation.meaning: proposed active set at the new parameter

knowledge_statements.title: Rank Loss Can Destroy Parametric Solution Continuity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a parameter makes an active constraint vanish, the optimizer can jump discontinuously and KKT continuation can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_x\ \tfrac12x^2\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad \theta(x-1)=0.\] For every \(\theta\ne0\), the unique solution is \(x(\theta)=1\). At \(\theta=0\), the constraint vanishes and the unique solution is \(x(0)=0\). Thus the solution map is discontinuous and the fixed-active KKT branch cannot continue through the rank-loss parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lim_{\theta\to0,\ \theta\ne0}x(\theta)=1\ne0=x(0).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of KKT continuation when a parameter-dependent active constraint loses rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Smooth Parametric KKT Continuation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ, strict complementarity, and strong second-order sufficiency yield a unique smooth nearby KKT branch with unchanged active set; its sensitivity follows from the differentiated KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT point at \(\theta^*\). If the active-constraint Jacobian has full row rank, strict complementarity holds, and the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on the active tangent space, then a neighborhood of \(\theta^*\) admits a unique continuously differentiable nearby KKT branch \((x(\theta),\lambda(\theta))\) with the same active set. Its derivative solves the differentiated fixed-active-set KKT equations.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint functions are twice continuously differentiable jointly in \((x,\theta)\) near \((x^*,\theta^*)\).
LICQ, strict complementarity, and positive-definite reduced Lagrangian curvature hold at \((x^*,\lambda^*,\theta^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,U\ni\theta^*\text{ and a unique }C^1\text{ map }\theta\mapsto(x(\theta),\lambda(\theta))\text{ on }U\text{ with the same active set}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local persistence and differentiability of a fixed active-set KKT branch under strong regularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Predictor Accuracy and Local Newton Correction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A first-order KKT sensitivity predictor has second-order local error, after which Newton correction converges quadratically for sufficiently small parameter changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the fixed-active KKT mapping \(F\) is twice continuously differentiable near a solution branch \(z(\theta)\) and \(D_zF(z(\theta),\theta)\) is nonsingular there. The first-order sensitivity predictor for a parameter increment \(\Delta\theta\) satisfies \[z^p-z(\theta+\Delta\theta)=O(\|\Delta\theta\|^2).\] For sufficiently small \(\Delta\theta\), Newton correction at \(\theta+\Delta\theta\) is well defined and converges quadratically to the local fixed-active KKT state.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is twice continuously differentiable near the local branch.
\(D_zF\) is nonsingular along the relevant branch segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|z^p-z(\theta+\Delta\theta)\|=O(\|\Delta\theta\|^2),\qquad \|z^{j+1}-z^*\|=O(\|z^j-z^*\|^2).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local accuracy and convergence of the fixed-active predictor-corrector step.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p\). For each \(\theta\in\Theta\), define \(P(\theta):\min_x f(x,\theta)\) subject to \(h(x,\theta)=0\) and \(g(x,\theta)\leq0\), with solution set \(S(\theta)\) and KKT set \(K(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal interface for solving a sequence of nearby finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programs; no differentiability or stability of the solution map is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parametric reoptimization interface is a tuple \[\mathfrak R=(\Theta,P,\Sigma,\operatorname{Init},\operatorname{Solve},\operatorname{Export})\] such that, for every transition \((\theta^-,\sigma^-)\mapsto\theta^+\), \(\operatorname{Init}(\theta^+,\sigma^-)\) returns an admissible initial state for \(P(\theta^+)\), \(\operatorname{Solve}\) returns either a state \(\sigma^+\) whose primal-dual component lies in \(K(\theta^+)\) to the prescribed tolerance or a declared failure status, and \(\operatorname{Export}(\sigma^+)\in\Sigma\) is transferable to a subsequent problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parametric reoptimization interface consists of a parameterized nonlinear program, a state space, an initializer that converts a state from a previously solved parameter value into an admissible initial state for a new parameter value, a solver, and an exporter. The transferable state may contain a primal point, multipliers, a working set, and linear-algebra data. Correctness means that a successful solve reports a primal-dual state satisfying the new problem's stated KKT residual tolerance; transfer itself does not imply that the preceding solution or active set remains valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Solve}(P(\theta^+),\operatorname{Init}(\theta^+,\sigma^-))\in K(\theta^+)\) to the declared tolerance whenever the returned status is successful.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The interface may be viewed as a state-transition map \(T_{\theta^-,\theta^+}:\Sigma\rightrightarrows\Sigma\) together with a success certificate for \(P(\theta^+)\).
special_cases_latex: For a fixed constraint structure, the state can be \(\sigma=(x,\lambda,\mathcal W)\).
A cold start is obtained when \(\operatorname{Init}\) ignores \(\sigma^-\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A change in \(\theta\) may alter feasibility, multipliers, and the optimal active set even when the transferred state is admissible.
boundary_notes: This definition does not assert continuity, differentiability, or single-valuedness of \(S(\theta)\).
No inspected source was found that presents this exact six-component interface as a canonical definition.

notation.meaning: Primal-dual KKT set for the parameter value theta.

review_flags: The supplied sources discuss related warm starts and sensitivity but do not support this exact interface definition.
A source explicitly formalizing state transfer for parametric NLP reoptimization is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Parametric constrained-reoptimization interface
Parametric Reoptimization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT-state transfer between nearby parameter values under active-set identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x f(x;\theta)\) subject to \(g_i(x;\theta)\ge0\) and \(h(x;\theta)=0\). At parameter \(\theta_k\), expose the reoptimization state \((x_k,W_k,\lambda_k)\). For a new value \(\theta_{k+1}\), use this state as an initial guess for the KKT system restricted to \(W_k\): stationarity, \(h(x;\theta_{k+1})=0\), and \(g_i(x;\theta_{k+1})=0\) for \(i\in W_k\). Accept the predicted state only after checking all inactive inequalities and multiplier signs; otherwise invoke constraint admission, release, or Phase I.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer the previous primal-dual active-set state to the new parameter, solve the restricted KKT system, then validate feasibility and multiplier signs before acceptance.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(g_i\), and \(h\) are continuously differentiable in \(x\) near the transferred state.
Variables and constraints have consistent identities between \(\theta_k\) and \(\theta_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transferred state is accepted only if the corrected restricted KKT point is primal feasible and dual-sign compatible at \(\theta_{k+1}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Typed family of specialized active-set interfaces
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a class of finite-dimensional constrained problems and let \(\tau\in\{\mathrm{BND},\mathrm{GP},\mathrm{QP},\mathrm{SQP}\}\) identify a specialized active-set regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Umbrella interface joining bound-constrained, gradient-projection, quadratic-programming, and SQP working-set mechanisms without identifying them as one algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A specialized active-set interface is a tagged tuple \[\mathfrak A_\tau=(\mathcal D_\tau,\Sigma_\tau,\operatorname{Model}_\tau,\operatorname{Step}_\tau,\operatorname{Update}_\tau,\operatorname{Cert}_\tau),\] where \(\mathcal D_\tau\subseteq\mathcal P\), the state contains a primal point and a working set, \(\operatorname{Step}_\tau\) solves the regime-specific reduced or equality-constrained model, \(\operatorname{Update}_\tau\) adds blocking constraints or deletes constraints failing the multiplier test, and \(\operatorname{Cert}_\tau\) evaluates the regime-appropriate first-order conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A specialized active-set interface is a typed mathematical contract rather than a single iteration formula. Its tag selects a problem domain, a state representation, a model or reduced subproblem, a step operator, an add/drop update, and an optimality certificate. Bound-constrained and gradient-projection interfaces classify coordinates at their bounds; convex-QP interfaces operate on linear working constraints; SQP interfaces use the active set of a linearized quadratic subproblem as an estimate of the nonlinear problem's active set. Each specialization must define its own feasibility and multiplier sign conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each tag \(\tau\), \(\operatorname{Cert}_\tau(\sigma)=0\) means that the state satisfies the first-order certificate defined on \(\mathcal D_\tau\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The family is the disjoint union \(\bigsqcup_\tau \mathfrak A_\tau\), so operations from different tags are not implicitly interchangeable.
special_cases_latex: For \(\tau=\mathrm{BND}\), the working set is a set of coordinates fixed at lower or upper bounds.
For \(\tau=\mathrm{QP}\), the step is an equality-constrained quadratic-programming step over the current working set.
immediate_consequences_latex: A multiplier test meaningful for one sign convention must be translated before it is used by another specialization.
boundary_notes: The definition does not include feasibility restoration or parametric state transfer unless a specialization adds those operations.
No inspected source states this tagged umbrella object as a canonical mathematical definition.
review_flags: The source node is an organizational umbrella, while the supplied sources define its child methods separately.
A source supporting a unified formal interface is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Typed family of specialized active-set interfaces
Bound-Constrained Active-Set Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound-active variables are fixed while free variables move; stationarity requires zero free gradients and inward-pointing gradient signs at lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(\ell\le x\le u\), define \(A_\ell(x)=\{i:x_i=\ell_i\}\), \(A_u(x)=\{i:x_i=u_i\}\), and \(F(x)=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus(A_\ell(x)\cup A_u(x))\). A working-set step fixes selected bound-active variables and computes a direction over the free variables. First-order stationarity is represented componentwise by \[
abla_i f(x)=0\ (i\in F(x)),\qquad 
abla_i f(x)\ge0\ (i\in A_\ell(x)),\qquad 
abla_i f(x)\le0\ (i\in A_u(x)).\] Equivalently, \(x=P_{[\ell,u]}(x-\alpha
abla f(x))\) for any \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is first-order stationary if and only if \(x=P_{[\ell,u]}(x-\alpha\nabla f(x))\) for some, equivalently every, \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set decomposition and stationarity test for box constraints.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(l\leq x\leq u\), where \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(l_i<u_i\). At iteration \(k\), let \(x_k\) be feasible and let \(q_k(x)=f(x_k)+\nabla f(x_k)^T(x-x_k)+\tfrac12(x-x_k)^TB_k(x-x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional bound-constrained optimization using a quadratic model and a coordinate working set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bound-constrained active-set interface assigns disjoint sets \[\mathcal A_k^L\subseteq\{i:x_{k,i}=l_i\},\qquad \mathcal A_k^U\subseteq\{i:x_{k,i}=u_i\},\qquad \mathcal F_k=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus(\mathcal A_k^L\cup\mathcal A_k^U),\] fixes \(p_i=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal A_k^L\cup\mathcal A_k^U\), computes the free step by minimizing the model over the remaining coordinates and bounds, and updates the sets when a free coordinate reaches a bound or a bound coordinate fails its projected-gradient sign test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a box-constrained problem, the active-set state partitions coordinates into a lower-bound set, an upper-bound set, and a free set. Coordinates in the working set are fixed while a quadratic model is minimized over the free coordinates. A free coordinate is eligible to enter the working set when it reaches a bound. A lower-bound coordinate is eligible to leave when its gradient sign permits feasible descent into the box, and an upper-bound coordinate is treated analogously. The interface therefore reduces an inequality-constrained model to a subspace problem after predicting which bounds are active.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathcal A_k^L\cup\mathcal A_k^U}=0\), while \(p_{\mathcal F_k}\) is obtained from the bound-restricted quadratic model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With projection \(P_{[l,u]}\), first-order stationarity is equivalent to \(x=P_{[l,u]}(x-\alpha\nabla f(x))\) for any fixed \(\alpha>0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal A_k^L=\mathcal A_k^U=\varnothing\), the model step is unconstrained.
A trust-region box subproblem replaces the bounds by \(\max(l,x_k-\Delta_ke)\leq x\leq\min(u,x_k+\Delta_ke)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Once the correct active bounds are fixed, only the free-coordinate subproblem remains.
boundary_notes: The interface does not apply directly to general coupled constraints because projection onto their feasible set need not be componentwise.
A predicted active bound need not be active at the solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Step Projected-Gradient Stationarity Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-step projected gradient has an order-one-over-square-root-K best-iterate stationarity residual and drives the residual to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(f\) is bounded below by \(f_{\inf}\) on a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on a neighborhood of \(C\), and \(0<\alpha<2/L\). For \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha\nabla f(x_k))\), \[\min_{0\le k<K}\|G_\alpha(x_k)\|^2\le\frac{f(x_0)-f_{\inf}}{\alpha(1-\alpha L/2)K}.\] Hence \(\sum_k\|G_\alpha(x_k)\|^2<\infty\), \(\|G_\alpha(x_k)\|\to0\), and every accumulation point is stationary.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below on \(C\) and has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient near \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{0\le k<K}\|G_\alpha(x_k)\|=O(K^{-1/2}),\qquad \lim_{k\to\infty}\|G_\alpha(x_k)\|=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global residual convergence and best-iterate complexity for fixed-step projected gradient.

notation.meaning: a finite lower bound for f on C

knowledge_statements.title: Oversized Projected-Gradient Steps Can Diverge
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a one-dimensional convex quadratic, projected gradient diverges above step 2/L and cycles at the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C=\mathbb R and f(x)=\tfrac{L}{2}x^2 with L>0. For a constant step \alpha, projected gradient gives x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha Lx_k)=(1-\alpha L)x_k. If \alpha>2/L and x_0\ne0, then |1-\alpha L|>1 and |x_k|=|1-\alpha L|^k|x_0|\to\infty. If \alpha=2/L, then x_{k+1}=-x_k, so every nonzero orbit cycles and its projected-gradient residual does not converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha>2/L\Longrightarrow |x_k|\to\infty;\qquad \alpha=2/L\Longrightarrow x_{k+1}=-x_k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of fixed-step projected-gradient convergence at and beyond the upper stepsize boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Gradient Descent Inequality and Stationarity Test
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero projected-gradient step is a feasible descent direction, and its residual vanishes exactly at first-order constrained stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z=P_C(x-\alpha
abla f(x))\), \(d=z-x\), and \(G_\alpha(x)=(x-z)/\alpha\), where \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, \(x\in C\), and \(\alpha>0\). Then \(
abla f(x)^{\mathsf T}d\le-\|d\|^2/\alpha\). Moreover, \(G_\alpha(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in
abla f(x)+N_C(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex; \(x\in C\); \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla f(x)^{\mathsf T}d\le-\alpha\|G_\alpha(x)\|^2,\qquad G_\alpha(x)=0\iff0\in\nabla f(x)+N_C(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fundamental projection inequality for a differentiable objective over a closed convex set.

notation.meaning: convex normal cone of C at x

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Optimality System Exposes Active Constraints
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projection residual is a normal vector, and projection multipliers identify active constraints supporting that normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:Az\ge b\}\) be nonempty and closed, let \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(z=P_C(y)\). Then \(y-z\in N_C(z)\). Equivalently, there exists \(\mu\ge0\) such that \[z-y-A^{\mathsf T}\mu=0,\qquad Az-b\ge0,\qquad \mu_i(A_iz-b_i)=0.\] Thus \(y-z=-A^{\mathsf T}\mu\), and \(\operatorname{supp}(\mu)\) is contained in the active constraints at \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y-z=-A^{\mathsf T}\mu\in N_C(z),\qquad \operatorname{supp}(\mu)\subseteq\{i:A_iz=b_i\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connection between Euclidean projection and polyhedral working-set information without a solver-specific face-transfer rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Projection Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected-gradient iteration over a closed convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), a feasible \(x_0\in C\), and positive trial steps, compute
\[
x_{k+1}=P_C\bigl(x_k-\alpha_k\nabla f(x_k)\bigr).
\]
Choose \(\alpha_k>0\) directly or by backtracking until the accepted projected step gives the prescribed sufficient decrease. The projection identifies binding constraints that may be passed to an active-set phase. Stop and return \(x_k\) when \(\|G_{\alpha_k}(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\), where \(G_\alpha(x)=\alpha^{-1}(x-P_C(x-\alpha\nabla f(x)))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project a gradient step onto the convex feasible set, optionally identify binding constraints, and stop when the projected-gradient mapping is small.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_\alpha(x)=0\) if and only if \(-\nabla f(x)\in N_C(x)\), the first-order stationarity condition.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the feasible set
convex normal cone to the feasible set at the point

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\) has full row rank, \(r<n\), and \(x\) is feasible. For inequalities, \(A\) denotes the matrix of gradients of the current working constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional problems with linear equalities, or an active-set local model in which the current working constraints are imposed as equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The gradient-projection interface defines the orthogonal tangent-space projector and search vector by \[P_A=I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A,\qquad u(x)=-P_A
abla f(x).\] Thus \(Au(x)=0\), and if \(u(x)
eq0\), its normalized version is the steepest-descent direction among unit vectors \(s\) satisfying \(As=0\). For inequalities, blocking constraints are added during motion, while a working constraint with an inadmissible multiplier may be removed when \(P_A
abla f(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gradient-projection interface projects the negative gradient onto the null space of the current equality or working-constraint matrix. The resulting vector is tangent to every working constraint and is the feasible steepest-descent direction within that linear subspace. In an inequality-constrained active-set method, a step follows this direction until a line-search endpoint or a new blocking constraint is reached. If the projected gradient vanishes, multipliers for the current working constraints are examined: acceptable multiplier signs certify first-order stationarity for the active model, while a wrong sign permits deletion of a constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u(x)=-\left(I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A\right)\nabla f(x)\) and \(Au(x)=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(P_A\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\).
The normalized direction solves \(\min\{\nabla f(x)^Ts:As=0,\ \|s\|=1\}\).
\(P_A\nabla f(x)=0\) is equivalent to \(\nabla f(x)+A^T\lambda=0\) for an appropriate sign convention.
special_cases_latex: If \(A\) has no rows, then \(P_A=I\) and \(u=-\nabla f(x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For every \(\alpha\), \(A(x+\alpha u)=b\) whenever \(Ax=b\).

If \(u
eq0\), then \(
abla f(x)^Tu=-\|P_A
abla f(x)\|^2<0\).
boundary_notes: The inverse formula requires full row rank; rank-deficient working constraints require a pseudoinverse or an independent subset.
For nonlinear constraints, the direction preserves only linearized feasibility unless a correction is applied.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(f\) is bounded below on a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on a neighborhood of \(C\), and \(0<\alpha<2/L\). For \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha\nabla f(x_k))\), \(f(x_k)\) is nonincreasing, \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\|G_\alpha(x_k)\|^2<\infty\), and \(\|G_\alpha(x_k)\|\to0\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a sufficiently small fixed step and Lipschitz gradient, projected gradient drives its stationarity residual to zero.

Convex-QP KKT Global-Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility, stationarity, nonnegative multipliers, and complementarity certify global optimality for a convex QP; strict convexity gives uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(H\succeq0\) and affine inequalities \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\), any feasible \(x\) admitting \(\lambda_i\ge0\) such that \(Hx+c-\sum_i\lambda_i a_i=0\) and \(\lambda_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i)=0\) is a global minimizer. If \(H\succ0\), the minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in\operatorname*{argmin}q;\qquad H\succ0\Longrightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}q=\{x\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global interpretation of the terminal primal working-set test.

notation.meaning: inequality multiplier under the greater-than constraint convention

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Working-Set Termination Under Nonrepetition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If no nonterminal working set is ever reused, the finite collection of at most 2^m working sets gives finite termination at the convex-QP KKT certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the accepted feasible primal active-set algorithm for a convex QP with m inequalities. Partition its execution into phases, each beginning with the equality-constrained solve associated with one working set W\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\} and ending in termination, admission, or release. Assume exact arithmetic, every required phase is well defined, and no working set that begins a nonterminal phase begins any other phase. Then at most 2^m nonterminal phases occur, followed by at most one terminal phase. The method therefore terminates at its KKT test and hence at a global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The QP and all phase subproblems satisfy the assumptions of the accepted primal active-set interface.
All computations are exact, and each nonterminal phase produces a valid admission or release.
No working set beginning a nonterminal phase begins another phase.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{phases}}\le 2^m+1,\qquad x_{\mathrm{final}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}q.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state termination guarantee for an exact feasible convex-QP active-set implementation with genuine working-set nonrepetition.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Programming Active-Set Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the equality-constrained QP defined by the working set. At a zero direction, stop if all working-set multipliers are nonnegative and otherwise delete a most-negative multiplier; at a nonzero direction, take the longest feasible step up to one and add a blocking constraint when the step is truncated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=	frac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n	imes n}\) is symmetric positive semidefinite, and consider \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\geq b_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Starting from a feasible \(x_k\) and a working set \(W_k\subseteq\{i:a_i^{\mathsf T}x_k=b_i\}\), let \(A_{W_k}\) have rows \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\) for \(i\in W_k\), and solve \(Hp_k+
abla q(x_k)-A_{W_k}^{\mathsf T}\lambda_k=0\) and \(A_{W_k}p_k=0\). If \(p_k=0\) and \(\lambda_k\geq0\), return \(x_k\). If \(p_k=0\) and some component of \(\lambda_k\) is negative, delete an index attaining \(\min_{i\in W_k}(\lambda_k)_i\). If \(p_k
eq0\), define \(B_k=\{i
otin W_k:a_i^{\mathsf T}p_k<0\}\) and \(\alpha_k=\min\{1,\min_{i\in B_k}(a_i^{\mathsf T}x_k-b_i)/(-a_i^{\mathsf T}p_k)\}\), using the convention \(\min\varnothing=+\infty\). Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\); when \(\alpha_k<1\), add at least one index in \(B_k\) attaining the blocking minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is symmetric positive semidefinite and positive definite on \(\ker A_{W_k}\) whenever a working-set subproblem is solved.
\(x_k\) is feasible and every index in \(W_k\) is active at \(x_k\).
Equality-constrained working-set subproblems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(p_k=0\) and \(\lambda_k\geq0\), then \(x_k\) satisfies the KKT conditions; every nonzero-step update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) is feasible.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal working-set interface for a convex quadratic program
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^TGx+c^Tx\), where \(G\succeq0\), subject to \(a_i^Tx=b_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(a_i^Tx\geq b_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). Let \(x_k\) be feasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional primal active-set methods for convex quadratic programs; the working-set gradients are maintained as linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A QP active-set interface maintains \(\mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal W_k\subseteq\mathcal A(x_k)\) and computes \[p_k\in\arg\min_p\left\{\tfrac12p^TGp+(Gx_k+c)^Tp:a_i^Tp=0\ \forall i\in\mathcal W_k\right\}.\] If \(p_k\neq0\), it takes \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), where \[\alpha_k=\min\left(1,\min_{i\notin\mathcal W_k,\ a_i^Tp_k<0}\frac{b_i-a_i^Tx_k}{a_i^Tp_k}\right),\] and adds a blocking constraint when \(\alpha_k<1\). If \(p_k=0\), it computes working-set multipliers, terminates when all inequality multipliers have the admissible sign, and otherwise deletes an index with an inadmissible multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal active-set interface for a convex quadratic program maintains a feasible iterate and a linearly independent working set containing every equality constraint. It minimizes the quadratic over directions tangent to the working constraints. A nonzero direction is followed as far as feasibility permits; a constraint attaining the limiting step is a blocking constraint and may be added. When the tangent subproblem has zero solution, the method checks the working-set multipliers. Admissible signs give the KKT certificate, while a wrong sign causes deletion of a working inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface is determined by the equality-constrained step, maximal feasible step length, blocking-constraint addition, and multiplier-sign deletion rules.
equivalent_formulations_latex: At \(p_k=0\), stationarity of the working-set subproblem is \(Gx_k+c=\sum_{i\in\mathcal W_k}\lambda_i a_i\).
special_cases_latex: If \(G\succ0\), every equality-constrained working-set subproblem has a unique minimizer.
If \(\mathcal I=\varnothing\), the interface reduces to one equality-constrained QP solve.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every accepted iterate remains feasible.
For \(G\succeq0\), satisfaction of the QP KKT conditions certifies global optimality.
boundary_notes: Indefinite QPs require additional negative-curvature safeguards not included here.
Degeneracy may produce zero step lengths and cycling unless an anti-cycling rule is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: SQP Working-Set Handoff
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP active-set solver returns a step, multipliers, and a QP endpoint working set. After globalization, that set is warm-start information and must be reconciled with the accepted nonlinear iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At x_k, form the SQP quadratic subproblem with linearized constraints, solve it for a primal-dual point (p_k,\nu_k,\lambda_k) and terminal QP working set W_k^{\mathrm{QP}}, and globalize the trial step to x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k. The set W_k^{\mathrm{QP}} describes the QP endpoint p_k. It may initialize the next QP solve, but its members may be declared active at x_{k+1} only after the next working-set feasibility, activity, and rank tests are applied. No solver-independent SQP rule requires blind transfer of every member of W_k^{\mathrm{QP}}.
assumptions_latex: f, h, and g are continuously differentiable.
B_k is symmetric and the quadratic subproblem supplies a primal-dual solution or a declared failure status.
The next working set is subjected to the method's activity and regularity tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_k^{\mathrm{QP}}\text{ is valid warm-start metadata, but }W_{k+1}=W_k^{\mathrm{QP}}\text{ is not a universal SQP identity}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent handoff between an SQP quadratic subproblem and the accepted nonlinear iterate.

notation.meaning: terminal working set of the current SQP quadratic subproblem

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP termination must check stationarity, equality and inequality feasibility, complementarity, and multiplier signs; a small step alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \min f(x) subject to h(x)=0 and g(x)\le0, let L(x,
u,\lambda)=f(x)+
u^	op h(x)+\lambda^	op g(x). An approximate KKT certificate checks \|
abla_xL(x,
u,\lambda)\|\le\varepsilon_d, \|h(x)\|\le\varepsilon_h, \|[g(x)]_+\|\le\varepsilon_g, \|\lambda\odot g(x)\|\le\varepsilon_c, and \lambda\ge-\varepsilon_\lambda\mathbf1.

knowledge_statements.title: Shortened SQP Steps Break Blind Working-Set Transfer
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint active at the full QP step can be inactive after globalization shortens the SQP step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let g(x)=x\le0, x_k=-1, p_k=1, and \alpha_k=1/2. The QP endpoint satisfies g(x_k)+\nabla g(x_k)^\top p_k=0, but the accepted point satisfies g(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)=-1/2<0. Thus QP-endpoint activity does not imply activity after a shortened step, even for an affine constraint.
assumptions_latex: The counterexample uses the affine inequality g(x)=x\le0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g_i(x_k)+\nabla g_i(x_k)^\top p_k=0\not\Rightarrow g_i(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample separating QP-endpoint activity from activity at a globalized nonlinear iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: SQP Working-Set Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Working-set QP interface for sequential quadratic programming with nonlinear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\). For minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(c(x)\ge0\), form at \(x_k\) the QP
\[
\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\;\nabla f(x_k)^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
h(x_k)+J_h(x_k)p=0,\quad c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)p\ge0.
\]
Initialize its working set from mapped constraints retained from the preceding SQP subproblem, solve it by additions and deletions of linearized active constraints, and obtain a step and multiplier estimate \((p_k,\lambda_{k+1})\). Select a globalization step length \(\alpha_k\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), update \(B_k\), and repeat. Stop when nonlinear feasibility and KKT residuals meet their prescribed tolerances. If the QP is infeasible, unbounded, or cannot be solved reliably, report that status and invoke the solver's restoration or regularization mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each SQP iteration warm-starts an active-set solver for the linearized-constraint QP, globalizes a successful step, and transfers its multipliers and working set; unsuccessful QPs are reported for restoration or regularization.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h,c\) are continuously differentiable near the iterates, and \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric.
A merit function, filter, or trust region supplies globalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns an SQP step, multiplier estimate, and updated working set, or reports a QP failure requiring restoration or regularization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Working-set interface for sequential quadratic programming
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\geq0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). At \((x_k,\lambda_k)\), let \(B_k\) approximate \(\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional SQP using an inequality-constrained quadratic subproblem and an active-set QP solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The SQP working-set interface forms \[\min_p\ 
abla f(x_k)^Tp+	frac12p^TB_kp\] subject to \[c_i(x_k)+
abla c_i(x_k)^Tp=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\qquad c_i(x_k)+
abla c_i(x_k)^Tp\geq0\ (i\in\mathcal I).\] Its working-set output \(\mathcal W_k^{\mathrm{QP}}\) is the set imposed as equalities at the selected QP solution, and therefore serves as the current estimate of the nonlinear optimal active set. The QP step and multipliers provide the primal and dual SQP updates, possibly after globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP working-set interface constructs a quadratic model of the Lagrangian and linearizes every constraint. An active-set QP solver selects the constraints active at the subproblem solution. This QP working set is the SQP method's estimate of the nonlinear problem's optimal active set. The subproblem solution supplies the primal search direction and its multipliers supply a new multiplier estimate. A line search, trust region, or filter may modify acceptance of the step without changing the definition of the local QP working set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal W_k^{\mathrm{QP}}=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{QP}}(p_k)\) is the SQP estimate of \(\mathcal A(x^*)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The IQP form solves the full inequality-constrained QP and reads the active-set estimate from its solution.
An EQP form first predicts a working set and then solves the corresponding equality-constrained quadratic subproblem.
special_cases_latex: With only equality constraints, every constraint belongs to every SQP working set.
With the exact Lagrangian Hessian and a correctly identified active set, the local iteration is a Newton iteration for the reduced KKT system.
immediate_consequences_latex: The final QP working set can initialize the next QP solve as a warm start.
boundary_notes: The linearized subproblem may be infeasible away from a solution; restoration or relaxation is then an additional mechanism.
The QP active set need not equal the nonlinear active set before identification.

notation.meaning: Exact or approximate Hessian of the Lagrangian used in the SQP model.
Working set selected at the QP subproblem solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Globalization Breaks Blind QP Working-Set Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes activity at an SQP subproblem solution from activity at a shortened nonlinear step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an SQP subproblem be formed at \(x_k\), and suppose an inequality \(g_i(x_k)+\nabla g_i(x_k)^\top p_k\le0\) is active at its solution \(p_k\). If globalization accepts \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) with \(0<\alpha_k<1\), then QP activity alone does not imply \(g_i(x_{k+1})=0\), even for affine \(g_i\). For example, with \(g(x)=x\le0\), \(x_k=-1\), \(p_k=1\), and \(\alpha_k=1/2\), the QP endpoint is active but \(g(x_{k+1})=-1/2<0\). Therefore a transferred working set must be reconciled with the accepted point or deliberately treated only as a warm start.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint active at the full QP step can be inactive after a shortened SQP step, so the QP working set cannot automatically be declared active at the accepted nonlinear iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i\) is continuously differentiable; the counterexample uses an affine constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g_i(x_k)+\nabla g_i(x_k)^\top p_k=0\not\Rightarrow g_i(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence contract for an active-set iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an active-set method generate states \(\sigma_k=(x_k,\lambda_k,\mathcal W_k)\) for a constrained problem with solution set \(X^*\) and optimal active-set map \(\mathcal A(\cdot)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract finite-dimensional convergence interface separating global approach, finite termination, and post-identification local rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An active-set convergence interface is a tuple \[\mathfrak C=(\mathcal G,\mathcal I,\mathcal R,\mathcal T),\] where \(\mathcal G\) is a globalization predicate implying that every relevant accumulation point is stationary, \(\mathcal I\) is the identification predicate \(\exists K\ \forall k\geq K:\mathcal W_k=\mathcal A(x^*)\), \(\mathcal R\) specifies the local rate after identification, and \(\mathcal T\) is the finite-termination predicate \(\exists K:x_K\in X^*\) with termination at \(K\). Each component must state its own hypotheses; no component is implied merely by naming the interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active-set convergence interface records four logically distinct claims about a generated state sequence: a globalization claim for remote starting points, an eventual active-set identification claim, a local convergence-rate claim once the correct set is fixed, and an optional finite-termination claim. The interface is satisfied only for the components whose hypotheses and conclusions have been explicitly established. In particular, convergence to a stationary point does not by itself imply finite identification, and identification does not by itself imply superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface exposes the separately quantified predicates \(\mathcal G\), \(\mathcal I\), \(\mathcal R\), and \(\mathcal T\) on the sequence \(\{\sigma_k\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Identification can be written as eventual constancy of the working set at the target active set.
Finite termination can be written as existence of a finite first hitting time for the certified solution set.
special_cases_latex: A convex-QP active-set method may satisfy \(\mathcal T\) without requiring an asymptotic rate.
A globalized SQP method may satisfy \(\mathcal G\), \(\mathcal I\), and a quadratic local-rate predicate.
immediate_consequences_latex: Failure of strict complementarity may invalidate \(\mathcal I\) while leaving a weaker stationarity conclusion possible.
boundary_notes: This is an abstract packaging of convergence properties, not a convergence theorem.
No inspected source states this four-component object as a canonical definition.

notation.meaning: Globalization, identification, rate, and termination predicates.

review_flags: The supplied sources state the component properties separately but do not define this unified convergence interface.
A source explicitly supporting this packaging is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Convergence contract for an active-set iteration
Finite-State Cycling Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A process may alternate forever between two working sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal W=\{W^a,W^b\}\) and define \(T(W^a)=W^b\), \(T(W^b)=W^a\). Then \(W_{k+1}=T(W_k)\) uses only two states but never terminates. Hence finiteness of the working-set family alone does not imply finite termination.
assumptions_latex: No progress invariant or anti-cycling rule is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\mathcal W|<\infty\not\Rightarrow\text{ finite termination}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite-state termination reasoning without nonrecurrence.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-State Noncycling Termination Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact strictly convex QP active-set method terminates finitely when a valid anti-cycling rule excludes recurrence of its finite combinatorial states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a feasible active-set method for a strictly convex quadratic program with finitely many inequalities. Assume each working-set subproblem is solved exactly, each nonterminal transition either makes strict primal objective progress or performs a zero-displacement pivot, and an anti-cycling rule prevents recurrence of the complete finite working-set state associated with an exact subproblem solution. Then only finitely many transitions occur. If the method stops exactly when the current point is primal feasible, stationary, and has sign-feasible working-set multipliers, it terminates at the unique global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The QP is feasible and has \(H\succ0\).
There are finitely many inequalities and exact working-set solves.
The anti-cycling rule excludes recurrence of complete degenerate states.
The stopping test is the convex-QP KKT test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The method terminates after finitely many transitions at the unique KKT minimizer.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional finite termination of an exact convex-QP working-set method.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite termination of a certified active-set method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an active-set algorithm generate \((x_k,\mathcal W_k)\) and let \(C\) be its terminal certificate set, such as the KKT set of a convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic finite termination; the principal specialized case is a primal active-set method for a strictly convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The algorithm has the finite-termination property on a problem class \(\mathcal P\) if \[\forall P\in\mathcal P\ \forall\sigma_0\in\operatorname{Dom}(P)\ \exists K<\infty:\ \sigma_K\in C(P)\quad\text{and the algorithm stops at }K.\] For the strictly convex-QP active-set interface, \(C(P)\) is the QP KKT set, and the standard finite-termination regime additionally requires that every nonzero computed search direction be followed by a strictly positive step, thereby excluding a zero-movement working-set cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite termination means that every admissible run in the stated problem class reaches a state carrying the required terminal certificate after finitely many iterations and stops there. It is stronger than asymptotic convergence. For the standard primal active-set method on a strictly convex quadratic program, the terminal certificate is primal feasibility together with stationarity and admissible multiplier signs. The usual finite-termination statement assumes that a nonzero computed direction always produces a positive step; this rules out cycling in which the iterate remains fixed while working sets are repeatedly added and deleted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K<\infty\) such that \(\sigma_K\in C(P)\) and no state \(\sigma_{K+1}\) is generated.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The terminal hitting time \(\tau_C=\inf\{k:\sigma_k\in C(P)\}\) is finite for every admissible initial state.
special_cases_latex: For a strictly convex QP, the KKT point is the unique global minimizer.
If a finite-state working-set method never revisits a certified working-set minimizer and encounters such a minimizer periodically, termination is finite.
immediate_consequences_latex: Finite termination implies eventual identification only when the terminal certificate uniquely determines the optimal active set.
boundary_notes: Floating-point tolerance termination is not the exact finite-termination property.
Degenerate zero steps can permit cycling unless an anti-cycling assumption or rule is imposed.

notation.meaning: Set of terminally certified states for problem P.
First iteration at which the certificate set is reached.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Termination Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination of a noncycling primal active-set method on a strictly convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a feasible primal active-set method for a quadratic program with finitely many linear inequalities and a strictly convex objective. Suppose every nonzero step strictly decreases the objective, every equality-constrained working-set subproblem is solved exactly, and a deterministic anti-cycling rule prevents repetition during degenerate zero-length pivots. In exact arithmetic, only finitely many distinct working sets can be visited without repetition. Consequently the method terminates after finitely many additions and deletions at a feasible point \(x_*\) whose working-set multipliers have the required signs. The primal feasibility, stationarity, and multiplier-sign conditions are the KKT conditions, so \(x_*\) is the unique global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noncycling exact active-set method for a strictly convex QP visits only finitely many working sets and terminates at the unique KKT minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The QP objective has \(H\succ0\) and the linear feasible set is nonempty.
Nonzero steps strictly decrease the objective.
Degenerate pivots obey an anti-cycling rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method terminates finitely at the unique minimizer \(x_*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Post-Identification Fast-Convergence Phase
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard nondegeneracy and second-order assumptions, exact-Hessian SQP becomes equality-constrained Newton after active-set identification and converges quadratically with unit steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_*\) be a KKT point of a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program. Assume LICQ, strict complementarity, and the strong second-order sufficient condition hold at \(x_*\). If an SQP sequence converges to \(x_*\), uses the exact Lagrangian Hessian, and identifies the active inequality set after some index \(K\), then for \(k\geq K\) its subproblem is locally the equality-constrained Newton system on the identified active manifold. Once unit steps are accepted, the primal-dual iterates \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\) satisfy \(\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|\leq C\|z_k-z_*\|^2\) for all sufficiently large \(k\) and some \(C>0\).
assumptions_latex: LICQ, strict complementarity, and strong second-order sufficiency hold at \(x_*\).
The SQP sequence converges to \(x_*\) and finitely identifies its active inequalities.
Exact Lagrangian Hessians and eventually accepted unit steps are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|\leq C\|z_k-z_*\|^2\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic SQP convergence after finite identification of the strongly active constraints.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role is appropriate, but twice continuous differentiability alone generally does not supply the Lipschitz derivative condition used for a quadratic Newton rate. The multiplier update defining the primal-dual iterate is also unspecified. The broad SQP section locator does not establish the exact hypotheses and rate claimed.
